## The Induction / 引子
===Original===

There was a man named Lessingham dwelt in an old low house in Wastdale, set in a gray old garden where yew-trees flourished that had seen Vikings in Copeland in their seedling time. Lily and rose and larkspur bloomed in the borders, and begonias with blossoms big as saucers, red and white and pink and lemon-colour, in the beds before the porch. Climbing roses, honeysuckle, clematis, and the scarlet flame-flower scrambled up the walls. Thick woods were on every side without the garden, with a gap northeastward opening on the desolate lake and the great fells beyond it: Gable rearing his crag-bound head against the sky from behind the straight clean outline of the Screes.

Cool long shadows stole across the tennis lawn. The air was golden. Doves murmured in the trees; two chaffinches played on the near post of the net; a little water-wagtail scurried along the path. A French window stood open to the garden, showing darkly a dining-room panelled with old oak, its Jacobean table bright with flowers and silver and cut glass and Wedgwood dishes heaped with fruit: greengages, peaches, and green muscat grapes. Lessingham lay back in a hammock-chair watching through the blue smoke of an after-dinner cigar the warm light on the Gloire de Dijon roses that clustered about the bedroom window overhead. He had her hand in his. This was their House.

“Should we finish that chapter of Njal?” she said.

She took the heavy volume with its faded green cover, and read: “He went out on the night of the Lord’s day, when nine weeks were still to winter; he heard a great crash, so that he thought both heaven and earth shook. Then he looked into the west airt, and he thought he saw thereabouts a ring of fiery hue, and within the ring a man on a gray horse. He passed quickly by him, and rode hard. He had a flaming firebrand in his hand, and he rode so close to him that he could see him plainly. He was black as pitch, and he sung this song with a mighty voice﻿—

“Here I ride swift steed,

His flank flecked with rime,

Rain from his mane drips,

Horse mighty for harm;

Flames flare at each end,

Gall glows in the midst,

So fares it with Flosi’s redes

As this flaming brand flies;

And so fares it with Flosi’s redes

As this flaming brand flies.

===Chinese===

有一个名叫莱辛厄姆（Lessingham）的人，住在沃斯代尔（Wastdale）一栋低矮的老宅里；宅子坐落在一座灰扑扑的古园中，园里繁茂的紫杉，在幼苗时代曾见过科泛兰的维京人。
花境里百合、玫瑰、飞燕草盛开，门廊前的花床上开满花朵大如碟子的秋海棠，红的、白的、粉的、柠檬黄的。
攀缘蔷薇、忍冬、铁线莲和猩红的火焰花爬满了墙壁。园外四围是茂密的树林，东北方开出一道缺口，露出荒凉的湖和湖那边的大山：盖博山从斯克林山笔直清晰的轮廓后面，昂起它峭壁嶙峋的头颅，直指天空。

清凉的长影悄悄爬过网球草坪。空气是金色的。鸽子在树间呢喃；两只苍头燕雀在网球场近处的网柱上嬉戏；一只小鹡鸰沿小径匆匆跑过。
落地长窗向花园敞开，昏暗地映出镶着古老橡木护壁板的餐室，那张詹姆斯时代的桌子上，鲜花、银器、水晶和堆满水果的韦奇伍德瓷盘光彩熠熠：青梅、桃子和绿玫瑰香葡萄。
莱辛厄姆仰在躺椅里，透过饭后雪茄的蓝烟，望着卧室窗外攀绕成一团的第戎荣光蔷薇上的暖光。他把她的一只手握在自己手里。这是他们的居所。

「咱们把《尼雅尔萨迦》那一章读完吧？」她说。

她拿起那本绿封皮已经褪色的厚重卷册，念道：「在一个主日的夜里，离冬天还有九个星期，他走了出去；他听见一声巨响，以为天地都震动了。于是他望向西方，恍恍偬惚看见那方有一圈火色的环，环中有一个人骑着一匹灰马。那人从他身旁疾掠而过，骑得飞快。
他手里握着一支燃烧的火把，骑得离他那么近，以致他能把那人看得清清楚楚。
那人黑得像柏油，用洪亮的声音唱着这支歌——

「我骑骏马疾驰，

两胁霜痕斑斑，

鬃毛雨水淋漓，

烈马为祸人间；

两端烈焰腾腾，

中怀毒火炎炎：

弗洛西的计谋恰如此焰，

火把飞向何方它便何往；

弗洛西的计谋恰如此焰，

火把飞向何方它便何往。」

===Original===

“Then he thought he hurled the firebrand east towards the fells before him, and such a blaze of fire leapt up to meet it that he could not see the fells for the blaze. It seemed as though that man rode east among the flames and vanished there.

“After that he went to his bed, and was senseless for a long time, but at last he came to himself. He bore in mind all that had happened, and told his father, but he bade him tell it to Hjallti Skeggi’s son. So he went and told Hjallti, but he said he had seen ‘the Wolf’s Ride, and that comes ever before great tidings.’ ”

They were silent awhile; then Lessingham said suddenly, “Do you mind if we sleep in the east wing tonight?”

“What, in the Lotus Room?”

“Yes.”

“I’m too much of a lazybones tonight, dear,” she answered.

“Do you mind if I go alone, then? I shall be back to breakfast. I like my lady with me; still, we can go again when next moon wanes. My pet is not frightened, is she?”

“No!” she said, laughing. But her eyes were a little big. Her fingers played with his watch-chain. “I’d rather,” she said presently, “you went later on and took me. All this is so odd still: the House, and that; and I love it so. And after all, it is a long way and several years too, sometimes, in the Lotus Room, even though it is all over next morning. I’d rather we went together. If anything happened then, well, we’d both be done in, and it wouldn’t matter so much, would it?”

“Both be what?” said Lessingham. “I’m afraid your language is not all that might be wished.”

“Well, you taught me!” said she; and they laughed.

They sat there till the shadows crept over the lawn and up the trees, and the high rocks of the mountain shoulder beyond burned red in the evening rays. He said, “If you like to stroll a bit of way up the fell-side, Mercury is visible tonight. We might get a glimpse of him just after sunset.”

A little later, standing on the open hillside below the hawking bats, they watched for the dim planet that showed at last low down in the west between the sunset and the dark.

He said, “It is as if Mercury had a finger on me tonight, Mary. It’s no good my trying to sleep tonight except in the Lotus Room.”

Her arm tightened in his. “Mercury?” she said. “It is another world. It is too far.”

But he laughed and said, “Nothing is too far.”

===Chinese===

「随后他恍恍惚惚把火把朝东面面前的山掷去，登时腾起好大一片火光来接那火把，亮得他连山都看不见了。那人仿佛在火焰中骑向东去，就消失在那里。

「此后他上床躺下，人事不省了好一阵子，最后才缓过来。他把经过的事都记在心里，告诉了他父亲；父亲吩咐他去把这事讲给斯凯吉之子雅尔蒂听。于是他去告诉了雅尔蒂，雅尔蒂说，他看见的是『狼奔』，那总是大事件临头的前兆。」

两人静了一会；莱辛厄姆忽然说：「今晚咱们到东厢去睡，你介意吗？」

「什么，到莲花室（the Lotus Room）去？」

「嗯。」

「今晚我太懒得动了，亲爱的，」她答道。

「那我一个人去，你不介意吧？我会回来吃早饭。我喜欢有我的女伴同行；不过下弦月时咱们可以再去。我的小心肝不害怕吧？」

「不怕！」她笑着说道。可她的眼睛睁得大了些。她的手指摆弄着他的表链。「我倒宁愿，」过了片刻她说，「你过些时候再带我去。
这一切如今还这么古怪：这座居所，还有那些事；可我又这么爱它。
再说，在莲花室里，有时候那可是迢迢长路，还外带好几年呢，哪怕第二天一早就全都过去了。
我宁愿咱们一起去。万一真出了什么事，好啊，咱们俩就一起完蛋，那也就没那么要紧了，是不是？」

「一起什么？」莱辛厄姆说。「恐怕你这话可不大讲究。」

「哼，还不是你教我的！」她说；两人都笑了。

他们坐在那里，直到影子爬过草坪、爬上树梢，山那边高处山肩上的岩石在晚照里烧得通红。他说：「要是愿意到山坡上溜达一小段，今晚能看见水星（Mercury）。太阳刚落那会儿，咱们兴许能看它一眼。」

过了一会儿，两人站在开阔的山坡上，头顶是翻飞的蝙蝠，他们守候着那颗晦暗的行星；它终于在西天低处露面了，在落日与黑暗之间。

他说：「今晚水星像是有根指头按在我身上，玛丽（Mary）。今晚我不到莲花室去睡，是怎么也睡不着的。」

她的手臂在他臂弯里收紧了。「水星？」她说。「那是另一个世界。太远了。」

他却笑道：「没有什么太远的。」

===Original===

They turned back as the shadows deepened. As they stood in the dark of the arched gate leading from the open fell into the garden, the soft clear notes of a spinet sounded from the house. She put up a finger. “Hark,” she said. “Your daughter playing ‘Les Barricades.’ ”

They stood listening. “She loves playing,” he whispered. “I’m glad we taught her to play.” Presently he whispered again, “ ‘Les Barricades Mystérieuses.’ What inspired Couperin with that enchanted name? And only you and I know what it really means. ‘Les Barricades Mystérieuses.’ ”

---

That night Lessingham lay alone in the Lotus Room. Its casements opened eastward on the sleeping woods and the sleeping bare slopes of Illgill Head. He slept soft and deep; for that was the House of Postmeridian, and the House of Peace.

In the deep and dead time of the night, when the waning moon peered over the mountain shoulder, he woke suddenly. The silver beams shone through the open window on a form perched at the foot of the bed: a little bird, black, round-headed, short-beaked, with long sharp wings, and eyes like two stars shining. It spoke and said, “Time is.”

So Lessingham got up and muffled himself in a great cloak that lay on a chair beside the bed. He said, “I am ready, my little martlet.” For that was the House of Heart’s Desire.

Surely the martlet’s eyes filled all the room with starlight. It was an old room with lotuses carved on the panels and on the bed and chairs and roof-beams; and in the glamour the carved flowers swayed like water-lilies in a lazy stream. He went to the window, and the little martlet sat on his shoulder. A chariot coloured like the halo about the moon waited by the window, poised in air, harnessed to a strange steed. A horse it seemed, but winged like an eagle, and its forelegs feathered and armed with eagle’s claws instead of hooves. He entered the chariot, and that little martlet sat on his knee.

===Chinese===

影子渐浓，两人转身回去。他们站在那道从开阔山野通进园子的拱门暗影里时，宅中传来羽管键琴柔亮的声音。她竖起一根手指。「听，」她说。「你女儿在弹《藩篱》。」

两人站着听。「她真爱弹琴，」他低声说。「真高兴咱们教会了她。」过了一会儿他又低声说：「《神秘的藩篱》（Les Barricades Mystérieuses）。库泊兰是从哪里得来这个迷人名称的灵感？而它真正的意思，只有你和我知道。《神秘的藩篱》。」

---

当夜，莱辛厄姆独自躺在莲花室里。窗扉向东开着，面向沉睡的树林和伊尔吉尔山沉睡的光秃山坡。
他睡得又软又沉；因为这是午后之居，安宁之居。

夜阑更深、万籁俱寂的时候，下弦月从山肩上探出头来，他忽然醒了。
银色的月光透过敞开的窗，照在床脚栖着的一个身影上：一只小鸟，黑色，头圆喙短，翅膀长而尖，眼睛像两颗明星般闪烁。
它开口说：「时间已至。」

于是莱辛厄姆起身，裹上搭在床边椅子上的一件大擎。他说：「我准备好了，我的小无足燕（martlet）。」因为这是心之所愿之居。

无足燕的那双眼确实把满室照得星光熠熠。这是一间老屋子，护壁板上、床上、椅上和梁上都雕着莲花；在那魔法的光晕里，雕花摇曳，仿佛懒溪中的睡莲。他走到窗前，小无足燕栖在他肩上。一辆颜色如月晕般的马车停在窗边，悬在空中，套着一匹神异的骏马。那似乎是马，却生着鹰一样的翅膀，前腿披羽，不生马蹄而长着鹰爪。他登上马车，小无足燕坐在他膝上。

===Original===

With a whirr of wings the wild courser sprang skyward. The night about them was like the tumult of bubbles about a diver’s ears diving in a deep pool under a smooth steep rock in a mountain cataract. Time was swallowed up in speed; the world reeled; and it was but as the space between two deep breaths till that strange courser spread wide his rainbow wings and slanted down the night over a great island that slumbered on a slumbering sea, with lesser isles about it: a country of rock mountains and hill pastures and many waters, all a-glimmer in the moonshine.

They landed within a gate crowned with golden lions. Lessingham came down from the chariot, and the little black martlet circled about his head, showing him a yew avenue leading from the gates. As in a dream, he followed her.

===Chinese===

双翼呼喇一响，那匹野骏马腾空而起。四围的夜，就像潜泳人在山瀑下深潭中、光滑陡岩底潜水时耳边翻腾的气泡声。时间被速度吞没了；世界旋转起来；只隔了两次深呼吸的工夫，那匹神异的骏马便展开彩虹般的双翼，斜斜掠下夜空，来到一座大岛上空——岛在沉睡的海上沉睡，四围环绕着较小的岛屿：那是一片岩石高山、山地牧場和众多水泽的国土，在月光下粼粼闪动。

他们降落在一座冠着金狮的大门内。莱辛厄姆下了马车，黑色的小无足燕绕着他的头盘旋，给他引出一条从大门通进去的紫杉道。如在梦中，他随她而去。

## I / 一
===Original===

The Castle of Lord Juss

Of the rarities that were in the lofty presence chamber fair and lovely to behold, and of the qualities and conditions of the lords of Demonland: and of the embassy sent unto them by King Gorice XI, and of the answer thereto.

The eastern stars were paling to the dawn as Lessingham followed his conductor along the grass walk between the shadowy ranks of Irish yews, that stood like soldiers mysterious and expectant in the darkness. The grass was bathed in night-dew, and great white lilies sleeping in the shadows of the yews loaded the air of that garden with fragrance. Lessingham felt no touch of the ground beneath his feet, and when he stretched out his hand to touch a tree his hand passed through branch and leaves as though they were unsubstantial as a moonbeam.

The little martlet, alighting on his shoulder, laughed in his ear. “Child of earth,” she said, “dost think we are here in dreamland?”

He answered nothing, and she said, “This is no dream. Thou, first of the children of men, art come to Mercury, where thou and I will journey up and down for a season to show thee the lands and oceans, the forests, plains, and ancient mountains, cities and palaces of this world, Mercury, and the doings of them that dwell therein. But here thou canst not handle aught, neither make the folk ware of thee, not though thou shout thy throat hoarse. For thou and I walk here impalpable and invisible, as it were two dreams walking.”

===Chinese===

朱斯大人的城堡

述高厅中琳琅可观的珍异，与魔国诸王公的品性境况；及戈里斯十一世遣使来见，与魔国的答复。

东方的星辰正在晨光前褪色，莱辛厄姆（Lessingham）随引路者走在两侧爱尔兰紫杉排成的暗影行列之间的草径上，那些紫杉像一列神秘而待动的士兵立在黑暗里。草上浸满夜的露水，沉睡在紫杉影中的大朵白百合，把满园的空气熏得馥郁。莱辛厄姆脚不沾地；他伸手去碰一棵树，手竟穿过枝叶而过，仿佛它们同月光一样并非实体。

小无足燕（martlet）落在他肩上，在他耳边笑道：「地之子，你以为我们这是在梦境吗？」

他没有作声。她说：「这不是梦。你，人类的孩子中的第一人，来到了水星（Mercury）。你和我要在此间游历一段时间，把这个世界——水星——的陆地与海洋、森林、平原与古老的山脉、城池与宫殿，以及住在其中之人的行事，指给你看。但在这里你拿不动任何东西，也不能叫人察觉你，哪怕你喊破喉咙。因为你我在此间行走，无形无质，就像两个行走的梦。」

===Original===

They were now on the marble steps which led from the yew walk to the terrace opposite the great gate of the castle. “No need to unbar gates to thee and me,” said the martlet, as they passed beneath the darkness of that ancient portal, carved with strange devices, and clean through the massy timbers of the bolted gate thickly riveted with silver, into the inner court. “Go we into the lofty presence chamber and there tarry awhile. Morning is kindling the upper air, and folk will soon be stirring in the castle, for they lie not long abed when day begins in Demonland. For be it known to thee, O earthborn, that this land is Demonland, and this castle the castle of Lord Juss, and this day now dawning his birthday, when the Demons hold high festival in Juss’s castle to do honour unto him and to his brethren, Spitfire and Goldry Bluszco; and these and their fathers before them bear rule from time immemorial in Demonland, and have the lordship over all the Demons.”

===Chinese===

这时他们已在那从紫杉径通往城堡正门对面平台的玉石阶上。「这样的门，用不着为你我而开，」无足燕说着，他们已穿过那古老门廊的黑暗——门上刻着奇异的纹样——又径直穿过上了闩的大门那厚重的木料——门上密密铆着白银——进了内院。「我们进高厅去，在那里盘桓片刻。晨光正点燃高处的空气，城堡里的人很快就要起来了；在魔国（Demonland），天一亮，人们是不长卧不起的。要知道，地生的啊，这地方是魔国，这座城堡是朱斯大人（Lord Juss）的城堡，今天这个正在破晓的日子是他的生日：魔人们在朱斯的城堡里大设庆典，向他、也向他的兄弟斯皮特法厄（Spitfire）与戈尔德里·布卢斯科（Goldry Bluszco）致敬；他们和他们的列祖列宗，自太古以来就在魔国执掌权柄，统辖全体魔人。」

===Original===

She spoke, and the first low beams of the sun smote javelin-like through the eastern windows, and the freshness of morning breathed and shimmered in that lofty chamber, chasing the blue and dusky shades of departed night to the corners and recesses, and to the rafters of the vaulted roof. Surely no potentate of earth, not Croesus, not the great King, not Minos in his royal palace in Crete, not all the Pharaohs, not Queen Semiramis, nor all the Kings of Babylon and Nineveh had ever a throne room to compare in glory with that high presence chamber of the lords of Demonland. Its walls and pillars were of snow-white marble, every vein whereof was set with small gems: rubies, corals, garnets, and pink topaz. Seven pillars on either side bore up the shadowy vault of the roof; the rooftree and the beams were of gold, curiously carved, the roof itself of mother-of-pearl. A side aisle ran behind each row of pillars, and seven paintings on the western side faced seven spacious windows on the east. At the end of the hall upon a dais stood three high seats, the arms of each composed of two hippogriffs wrought in gold, with wings spread, and the legs of the seats the legs of the hippogriffs; but the body of each high seat was a single jewel of monstrous size: the left-hand seat a black opal, a-sparkle with steel-blue fire, the next a fire-opal, as it were a burning coal, the third seat an alexandrite, purple like wine by night but deep sea-green by day. Ten more pillars stood in semicircle behind the high seats, bearing up above them and the dais a canopy of gold. The benches that ran from end to end of the lofty chamber were of cedar, inlaid with coral and ivory, and so were the tables that stood before the benches. The floor of the chamber was tesselated, of marble and green tourmaline, and on every square of tourmaline was carven the image of a fish: as the dolphin, the conger, the catfish, the salmon, the tunny, the squid, and other wonders of the deep. Hangings of tapestry were behind the high seats, worked with flowers, snake’s-head, snapdragon, dragon-mouth, and their kind; and on the dado below the windows were sculptures of birds and beasts and creeping things.

===Chinese===

她说话时，太阳最初低低的光束像标枪一样穿过东窗刺进来，清晨的清新气息在这高厅里呼吸、闪烁，把昨夜蓝暗的阴影赶到角落与凹处、赶到拱顶的椽上。的确，地上的任何君王——不是克罗伊斯，不是那位大王，不是克里特王宫里的弥诺斯，不是所有的法老，不是塞弥拉弥斯女王，也不是巴比伦与尼尼微的诸王——都不曾有过一座殿堂，能与魔国诸王公这座高厅的荣耀相比。厅壁与廊柱皆雪白大理石，柱上每一道纹路里都嵌着细小的宝石：红宝石、珊瑚、石榴石与粉红托帕石。两侧各七根柱子撑起屋顶幽暗的拱顶；屋脊与梁是黄金的，雕刻精奇，屋顶本身则是珠母的。每排柱子背后各有一条侧廊；西面七幅绘画，正对东面七扇宽敞的窗。大厅尽头一座高台上立着三张高座，每座的扶手由两只金铸的鹫马（hippogriff）构成，双翼大展；座腿即鹫马之腿；而每张高座的座身是一整块硕大无朋的宝石：左首一座是黑欧泊，闪烁着钢蓝色的火；旁边一座是火欧泊，仿佛一块燃着的炭；第三座是紫翠玉，夜里酒红如葡萄酒，白日里却是深深的海绿。高座之后又有十根柱子排成半圆，在座与高台上方撑起一顶黄金华盖。纵贯高厅两端的长凳是杉木的，嵌着珊瑚与象牙，立在凳前的长桌也是如此。厅地用大理石与绿碧玺拼镶而成，每一方碧玺上都刻着一种鱼的形像：海豚、康吉鳗、鲇鱼、鲑鱼、金枪鱼、鱿鱼，以及深海里的其他奇物。高座之后悬着花毯，绣着龙头花、金鱼草、龙口花之类的花卉；窗下的墙裙上则是飞禽走兽与爬虫的雕像。

===Original===

But a great wonder of this chamber, and a marvel to behold, was how the capital of every one of the four-and-twenty pillars was hewn from a single precious stone, carved by the hand of some sculptor of long ago into the living form of a monster: here was a harpy with screaming mouth, so wondrously cut in ochre-tinted jade it was a marvel to hear no scream from her: here in wine-yellow topaz a flying firedrake: there a cockatrice made of a single ruby: there a star sapphire the colour of moonlight, cut for a cyclops, so that the rays of the star trembled from his single eye: salamanders, mermaids, chimaeras, wild men o’ the woods, leviathans, all hewn from faultless gems, thrice the bulk of a big man’s body, velvet-dark sapphires, chrysolite, beryl, amethyst, and the yellow zircon that is like transparent gold.

To give light to the presence chamber were seven escarbuncles, great as pumpkins, hung in order down the length of it, and nine fair moonstones standing in order on silver pedestals between the pillars on the dais. These jewels, drinking in the sunshine by day, gave it forth during the hours of darkness in a radiance of pink light and a soft effulgence as of moonbeams. And yet another marvel, the nether side of the canopy over the high seats was encrusted with lapis lazuli, and in that feigned dome of heaven burned the twelve signs of the zodiac, every star a diamond that shone with its own light.

---

===Chinese===

但这厅堂里的一大奇观、一件可惊可叹的事，是那二十四根柱子中每一根的柱顶，都由一整块宝石凿成，出自远古某位雕刻家之手，刻成活生生的怪物之形：这里有尖声嘶叫的鸟身女妖，以赭色软玉雕得如此神妙，竟叫人惊怪听不见她的嘶叫；这里在酒黄色的托帕石里有一条飞腾的火龙；那里有一只整块红宝石雕成的蛇鸡；那里有一块月光色的星光蓝宝石，凿成独眼巨人之首，星形的辉光便从他独眼中颤动而出；还有火蜥蜴、美人鱼、喀迈拉、林中野人、利维坦，都凿自无瑕的宝石，每块都有大汉身躯三倍之大：天鹅绒般深暗的蓝宝石、橄榄石、绿柱石、紫晶，还有那像透明黄金的黄锆石。

为高厅照明的，是七颗红焰宝石（escarbuncles），大如南瓜，沿厅依次悬挂；另有九颗皎洁的月长石，依次立在台前柱间的白银座上。这些宝石白日饮足阳光，到黑夜的时辰便放出光来：粉红的辉光，加上月光一般柔和的莹亮。还有一奇：高座之上华盖的底面镶满青金石，在那仿造的天穹里燃着黄道十二宫，每一颗星都是一颗钻石，各自放光。
