And all countries of the world and the rulers thereof, so many as the sun doth spread his beams over, shall do me obeisance, and call me King and Lord.”

All they shouted assent, praising the King and bowing down before him.

Then said the King, “Imagine not that oaths sworn unto the Demons by Gorice XI of memory ever glorious bind me any whit. I will not be at peace with this Juss and his brethren, but do account them all mine enemies. And this night have I made a sending to take them on the waste of waters as they sail homeward to many-mountained Demonland.”

Corund said, “Lord, your words are as wine unto us. And well we guessed that the principalities of darkness were afoot last night, seeing all Carcë rocked and the foundations thereof rose and fell as the breast of the large earth a-breathing.”

When they were come into the banqueting hall, the King said, “Gro shall sit at my right hand this night, since manfully hath he served me.” And when they scowled at this, and spake each in the other’s ear, the King said, “Whoso among you shall so serve me and so water the growth of this Witchland as hath Gro in this night gone by, unto him will I do like honour.” But unto Gro he said, “I will bring thee home to Goblinland in triumph, that wentest forth an exile. I will pluck Gaslark from his throne, and make thee king in Zajë Zaculo, and all Goblinland shalt thou hold for me in fee, exercising dominion over it.”

===Chinese===

其时，巫国众勋贵正聚在院中，准备赴大宴厅饮宴；王身穿召灵法袍，从碉楼下面的门中出来，走到他们跟前。王以其赫赫威仪立于彼处，巫国铁冠上的宝石在他沉重的眉骨、颧骨和刚愎之唇上方灿然生光；格罗与仪仗立在门影里。王说：「科伦德、科苏斯（Corsus）、科里尼厄斯、加兰杜斯（Gallandus）诸位大人，科苏斯与科伦德的众位公子，还有你们众巫国人：看哪，你们的王，第十二位戈里斯，在喀尔刻受此冠加冕，为巫国与魔国之王。世上万国及其君长，凡日光所照临的，都要向我臣服，称我为王、为主。」

众人齐声欢呼应命，颂赞王，向他俯伏。

王又说：「休以为功业永耀的戈里斯十一世向魔族起的誓缚得住我分毫。我绝不与这贾斯及其兄弟讲和，我要把他们全数当作我的仇敌。今夜我已遣出一物，要在他们渡海归返多山魔国的荒波之上拿住他们。」

科伦德说：「主上，您的话于我们如美酒。昨夜我们也就猜到了黑暗的诸权势出动了——整个喀尔刻都在摇晃，地基一起一伏，像大地宽广的胸膛在呼吸。」

进了大宴厅，王说：「今夜格罗坐我右手，因为他以大丈夫气概侍奉了我。」众人闻之变色，交头接耳；王便说：「你们中间，谁若也能像格罗昨夜那样侍奉我、那样浇灌巫国的生长，我也必给他同样的尊荣。」又对格罗说：「我要使你凯旋荣归哥布林国（Goblinland）——你当年是被放逐出去的。我要把加斯拉克从王座上掠下来，立你为扎伊·扎库洛之王；整个哥布林国由你为我采邑领有，行使统治。」

## V / 五
===Original===

King Gorice’s Sending

Of King Gaslark, and of the coming of the sending upon the demons on the high seas; with how the Lord Juss by the egging on of his companions was persuaded to an unadvised rashness.

The next morning following that night when King Gorice XII sat crowned in Carcë as is aforesaid, was Gaslark a-sailing on the middle sea, homeward from the east. Seven ships of war he had, and they steered in column southwestward close hauled on the starboard tack. Greatest and fairest among them was she who led the line, a great dragon of war painted azure of the summer sea with towering head of a worm, plated with gold and wrought with overlapping scales, gaping defiance from her bows, and a worm’s tail erect at the poop. Seventy and five picked men of Goblinland sailed on that ship, clad in gay kirtles and byrnies of mail and armed with axes, spears, and swords. Their shields, each with his device, hung at the bulwarks. On the high poop sat King Gaslark, his sturdy hands grasping the great steering paddle. Goodly of mien and well knit were all they of Goblinland that went on that great ship, yet did Gaslark outdo them all in goodliness and strength and all kingliness. He wore a silken kirtle of Tyrian purple. Broad wristlets of woven gold were on his wrists. Dark-skinned was he as one that hath lived all his days in the hot sunshine: clean-cut of feature, somewhat hooky-nosed, with great eyes and white teeth and tight-curled black moustachios. Nought restful was there in his presence and bearing, but rashness and impetuous fire; and he was wild to look on, swift and beautiful as a stag in autumn.

Teshmar, that was the skipper of his ship, stood at his elbow. Gaslark said to him, “Is it not one of the three gallant spectacles of the world, a good ship treading the hastening furrows of the sea like a queen in grace and beauty, scattering up the wave-crests before her stem in a glittering rain?”

“Yea, Lord,” answered he; “and what be the other two?”

“One that I most unhappily did miss, whereof but yesterday we had tidings: to behold such a battling of great champions and such a victory as Lord Goldry obtained upon yonder vaunting tyrant.”

===Chinese===

戈里斯王的遣送

述加斯拉克王事，及那遣送如何临到公海上的魔人；并朱斯大人如何被同伴们撺掇，被劝入一场失算的鲁莽。

如前所述、戈里斯十二世（King Gorice XII）在喀尔刻加冕的那一夜之后的次日早晨，加斯拉克正航行在大海之中，自东而返。他有七艘战船，成列紧抢右舷风朝西南行驶。其中最大最美的，是领队的那艘：一条大海蓝色的战龙，夏季海色的蓝，高昂着蠕虫形的船首，包金为鳞、叠甲成纹，自船首张着大口作势威吓，船尾竖着蠕虫的尾。七十五名哥布林国（Goblinland）的精选之士乘在那船上，穿鲜色的短衣与锁子甲，执斧、矛、剑。他们的盾，各绘各章，悬在舷墙上。高高的船尾座上坐着加斯拉克王，健壮的双手握着大舵桨。那大船上所有的哥布林人都仪表堂堂、筋骨匀称，而加斯拉克在英伟、膂力与一切王者气度上又超过他们所有人。他穿一件推罗紫的绸短衣，腕上戴着织金的宽腕环。他皮肤黝黑，像终生在烈日下生活的人：轮廓分明，鼻梁微钩，大眼睛，白牙齿，黑色髭须紧紧卷曲。他的风仪气度里没有一丝安闲，全是鲁莽与烈火；他望之桀骜，迅疾而美，像秋天的一头牡鹿。

特什马尔——他船上的船长——立在他肘边。加斯拉克对他说：「一艘好船，像王后一般雍容美丽，踏着大海疾驰的犁沟，船首把浪峰碎成一场晶亮的雨撒开去——这岂不是世上三大壮观的奇景之一么？」

「是的，主上，」他答道；「那另外两大是什么？」

「有一件我不幸错过了，昨天我们才得了消息：亲眼看那样的豪杰对决、看戈尔德里大人赢得对那边那个夸口暴君的那场大胜。」

===Original===

“The third shall be seen, I think,” said Teshmar, “when the Lord Goldry Bluszco shall in your royal palace of Zajë Zaculo, amid pomp and high rejoicing, wed the young princess your cousin: most fortunate lord, that must be lord of her whom all just censure doth acknowledge the ornament of earth, the model of heaven, the queen of beauty.”

“Kind Gods hasten the day,” said Gaslark. “For truly ’tis a most sweet lass, and those kinsmen of Demonland my dearest friends. But for whose great upholding time and again, Teshmar, in days gone by, where were I today and my kingdom, and where thou and all of you?” The king’s brow darkened a little with thought. After a time he began to say, “I must have more great action: these trivial harryings, spoils of Nevria, chasing of Esamocian black-a-moors, be toys not worthy of our great name and renown among the nations. Something I would enact that shall embroil and astonish the world, even as the Demons when they purged earth of the Ghouls, ere I go down into silence.”

Teshmar was staring toward the southern bourne. He pointed with his hand: “There rideth a great ship, O king. And methinks she hath a strange look.”

Gaslark gazed earnestly at her for an instant, then straightway shifted his helm and steered towards her. He spake no more, staring ever as he sailed, marking ever as the distance lessened more and more particulars of that ship. Her silken sail fluttered in tatters from the yard; she rowed feebly, as one groping in darkness, with barely strength to stay her from drifting stern-foremost before the wind. So hung she on the sea, as one struck stupid by some blow, doubting which way her harbour lay or which way her course. As a thing which hath been held in the flame of a monstrous candle, so seemed she, singed and besmirched with soot. Smashed was her proud figurehead, and smashed was her high forecastle, and burned and shattered the carved timbers of the poop and the fair seats that were thereon. She leaked, so that a score of her crew must be still a-baling to keep her afloat. Of her fifty oars, half were broken or gone adrift, and many of the ship’s company lay wounded and some slain under her thwarts.

===Chinese===

「第三件嘛，我想我们看得见，」特什马尔说，「等戈尔德里·布卢斯科大人，在您扎杰·扎库洛的王宫里，在盛大的庆典与欢腾之中，娶您那位年轻的堂妹公主的时候：最蒙福的贵人，他必作她的夫君——一切公正的舆论都承认她是地的妆饰、天的典范、美的王后。」

「愿仁慈的诸神催促那日子，」加斯拉克说。「她实在是个顶甜美的姑娘，而魔国那几位族人，是我最亲爱的朋友。若不是他们一再大力扶持，特什马尔，往日那些关口，今天我在哪里、我的王国在哪里？你、还有你们所有人，又在哪里？」王的眉宇因沉思微微阴沉下来。过了一阵他开口说：「我必须再有更大的作为：这些琐碎的劫掠——抢点内夫里亚、追追埃萨莫西亚的黑摩尔人——都是玩具，配不上我们在列国中间的大名与声威。我要做一件搅动世界、震骇世界的事，像魔人们扫荡食尸鬼那样，然后才下到寂默里去。」

特什马尔正望着南方的天际。他抬手指着：「那边驶来一艘大船，王啊。我看它的样子有些古怪。」

加斯拉克凝神看了一瞬，随即转舵朝它驶去。他不再说话，一面行驶一面盯着看，随着距离缩短，那船的细节越来越多地看在眼里。它的绸帆破碎成条，在桁上飘动；它划桨划得虚弱，像人在黑暗里摸索，几乎没了力气阻止自己被风推着船尾朝前漂。它那样悬在海上，像被什么一击打傻了的东西，疑疑惑惑不知港口在哪边、航路在哪边。它像一件在巨烛火焰里燎过的东西：燎焦了，蒙满烟灰。它高傲的船首像撞碎了，高高的船楼撞碎了，船尾的雕木和上面华美的座席烧灼崩裂。它漏水，二十来个水手不得不一直戽水才叫它浮着。五十支桨，一半折断或漂失；许多船员带着伤、有的死了，躺在桨座下面。

===Original===

And now was King Gaslark ware as he drew near that here was the Lord Juss on her ruined poop a-steering, and by him Spitfire and Brandoch Daha. Their jewelled arms and gear and rich attire were black with most stinking soot, and it was as though admiration and grief and anger were so locked and twined within them that none of these passions might win forth to outward showing on their frozen countenances.

When they were within hailing distance, Gaslark hailed them. They answered him not, only beholding him with alien eyes. But they stopped the ship, and Gaslark lay aboard of her and came on board and went up on the poop and greeted them. And he said, “Well met in an ill hour. What’s the matter?”

The Lord Juss made as if to speak, but no word came. Only he took Gaslark by both hands and sat down with a great groan on the poop, averting his face. Gaslark said, “O Juss, for so many a time as thou hast borne part in my evils and succoured me, surely right requireth I have part of thine?”

But Juss answered in a thick, strange voice all unlike himself, “Mine, sayest thou, O Gaslark? What in the stablished world is mine, that am thus in a moment reived of him that was mine own heartstring, my brother, the might of mine arm, the chiefest citadel of my dominion?” And he burst into a great passion of weeping.

King Gaslark’s rings were driven into the flesh of his fingers by the grip of Juss’s strong hands on his. But he scarce wist of the pain, such agony of mind was in him for the loss of his friend, and for the bitterness and wonder that it was to behold these three great lords of Demonland weep like frightened women, and all their ship’s company of tried men of war weeping and wailing besides. And Gaslark saw well that their lordly souls were unseated for a season because of some dreadful fact, the havoc whereof his eyes most woefully beheld, while its particulars were yet dark to him, yet with a terror in darkness that might well make his heart to quail.

===Chinese===

加斯拉克驶近了，这才看见：朱斯大人（Lord Juss）在那毁坏的船尾掌着舵，他旁边是斯皮特法厄（Spitfire）和布兰多赫·达哈大人（Lord Brandoch Daha）。他们镶宝的臂钏、装具与华服，都黑满了一层极臭的烟灰；赞叹、悲恸与忿怒仿佛在他们里面绞锁缠结成一团，哪一个也挣不到那凝住的脸上来。

船到可呼喊的距离，加斯拉克向他们喊话。他们不答，只用陌生的眼睛看他。但船停了，加斯拉克靠帮登船，走上船尾问安。他说：「不幸的时辰里幸会。出了什么事？」

朱斯大人像要说话，却一个字也出不来。他只握住加斯拉克双手，一声长呻在船尾坐下，把脸转开。加斯拉克说：「朱斯啊，你多少次分担我的患难、救助我；如今你遭了事，我岂不义当有分？」

朱斯用一种滞重陌生的、全然不像他的声音答道：「我的？你说我的，加斯拉克？在这立定的世界上，还有什么算是我的？一转瞬，我就被夺去了他——我的心弦、我的兄弟、我臂上的伟力、我疆土的首座坚城。」他放声大哭起来。

加斯拉克王的戒指被朱斯有力的双手攥进指肉里。他几乎不觉得疼：为丧友而生的剧痛在心里，也为目睹这桩奇祸而生的苦楚与惊愕——魔国这三位大人在他眼前哭得像惊惶的妇人，满船久经战阵的汉子也都在啼哭哀号。加斯拉克看得分明：他们的贵族之魂被某个骇人的事实一时震离了本位；那事实的荼毒他已亲眼最悲惨地看见，其细节却还暗着——而黑暗中有一种恐怖，足以叫他心里发颤。

===Original===

By much questioning he was at last well advertised of what had befallen: how they the day before, in broad noon, on such a summer sea, had heard a noise like the flapping of wings outstretched from one edge of the sky to another, and in a moment the calm sea was lifted up and fell again and the whole sea clashed together and roared, yet was the ship not sunken. And there was a tumult about them of thunder and raging waters and black night and wildfire in the night; which presently passing away and the darkness lifting, the sea lay solitary as far as eye might reach. “And nothing is more certain,” said Juss, “than that this is a sending of King Gorice XII spoken of by the prophets as a great clerk of necromancy beyond all other this world hath seen. And this is his vengeance for the woes we wrought for Witchland in the Foliot Isles. Against such a peril I had provided certain amulets made of the stone alectorian, which groweth in the gizzard of a cock hatched on a moonless night when Saturn burneth in a human sign and the lord of the third house is in the ascendant. These saved us, albeit sorely buffeted, from destruction: all save Goldry alone. He, by some cursed chance, whether he neglected to wear the charm I gave him, or the chain of it was broken in the plunging of the ship, or by some other means ’twas lost: when daylight came again, we stood but three on this poop where four had stood. More I know not.”

“O Gaslark,” said Spitfire, “our brother that is stolen from us, with us it surely lieth to find him and set him free.”

But Juss groaned and said, “In which star of the unclimbed sky wilt thou begin our search? Or in which of the secret streams of ocean where the last green rays are quenched in oozy darkness?”

Gaslark was silent for a while. Then he said, “I think nought likelier than this, that Gorice hath caught away Goldry Bluszco into Carcë, where he holdeth him in duress. And thither must we straightway to deliver him.”

===Chinese===

他细细盘问，终于问明白了遭了什么：昨天正午，在那样一片夏日的海上，他们听见一声巨响，像双翼从天这边一路展拍到天那边；顷刻间，平静的海被掀起来又落下，整个海面相击咆哮，船却没有沉。他们四围是雷霆、狂涛与黑夜，以及黑夜里的野火；不多时这些过去、黑暗揭起，放眼望去，海上一片孤寂。「再没有比这更确实的了，」朱斯说，「这是戈里斯十二世王的一次遣送；先知们说过，他是谙死灵之学的大法师，超出这世上所见的一切。这是他对我们在福略特群岛加给巫国之祸的报复。为防这样的凶险，我原备有几件阿勒克托利亚石做的护符——那石头生在一只鸡的胗里，那鸡须在无月之夜孵出，其时土星燃于人宫、第三宫主升在东天。这些护符救了我们，尽管我们被击打得够呛：唯独戈尔德里（Goldry）没能得救。他，不知撞了什么霉运——也许忘了戴我给他的护符，也许是船颠簸时链子断了，也许另有缘故丢了——天再亮时，昨日四人站的这船尾，只剩我们三人站着。其余的我不知道了。」

「加斯拉克啊，」斯皮特法厄说，「我们兄弟被人偷走，寻他、救他，这担子当然落在我们身上。」

但朱斯呻吟道：「你要从没攀过的天上哪一颗星开始找？还是从大洋哪一条隐秘的流里——那绿光最后在泥泞的黑暗里熄灭的地方？」

加斯拉克沉默了一会儿，说：「我看再没有比这更可能的了：戈里斯把戈尔德里·布卢斯科摄进了喀尔刻（Carcë），囚在那里。我们必须立刻去那里救他。」

===Original===

Juss answered no word. But Gaslark seized his hand, saying, “Our ancient love and your oft succouring of Goblinland in days gone by make this my quarrel. Hear now my rede. As I fared from the east through the Straits of Rinath I beheld a mighty company of forty sail, bound eastward to the Beshtrian sea. Well it was they marked us not as we lay under the isles of Ellien in the dusk of evening. For touching later at Norvasp in Pixyland we learned that there sailed Laxus with the whole Witchland fleet, being minded to work evil deeds among the peaceful cities of the Beshtrian seaboard. And as well met were an antelope with a devouring lion, as I and my seven ships with those ill-doers in such strength on the high seas. But now, behold how wide standeth the door to our wishes. Laxus and that great armament are safe harrying eastward-ho. I make question whether at this moment more than nine score or ten score fighting men be left in Carcë. I have here of mine own nigh on five hundred. Never was fairer chance to take Witchland with his claws beneath the table, and royally may we scratch his face ere he get them forth again.” And Gaslark laughed for joy of battle, and cried, “O Juss, smiles it not to thee, this rede of mine?”

“Gaslark,” said Lord Juss, “nobly and with that open hand and heart that I have loved in thee from of old hast thou made this offer. Yet not so is Witchland to be overcome, but after long days of labour only, and laying of schemes and building of ships and gathering of hosts answerable to the strength we bare of late against the Ghouls when we destroyed them.”

Nor for all his urging might Gaslark move him any whit.

But Spitfire sat by his brother and spake privately to him: “Kinsman, what ails thee? Is all high heart and swiftness to action crushed out of Demonland, and doth but the unserviceable juiceless skin remain to us? Thou art clean unlike that thou hast ever been, and could Witchland behold us now well might he judge that base fear had ta’en hold upon us, seeing that with the odds of strength so fortunately of our side we shrink from striking at him.”

===Chinese===

朱斯一言不答。但加斯拉克抓住他的手说：「我们旧日的情谊，加上你们往日屡屡驰援哥布林国，这就也是我的事。听我的主意。我从东边来，过里纳特海峡时，看见一支四十艘的大舰队，往东去贝什特里亚海。亏得薄暮时我们伏在埃利恩群岛下，没被他们看见。后来我们在精灵国（Pixyland）的诺瓦斯普停靠，才听说那是拉克苏斯（Laxus）率着巫国全部舰队，要去贝什特里亚沿海那些和平的城池行凶作恶。我和我的七艘船，在公海上撞见那样实力的恶徒，就好比羚羊撞上吞人的狮子。可现在你看，通往我们心愿的门开得多宽：拉克苏斯和那支大军正安安稳稳往东抢。我算此时喀尔刻留下的战夫，多不过一百八或二百。我这里自己带了将近五百人。再没有比这更好的机会，趁巫国的爪子还藏在桌子底下时拿住他；趁他爪子再伸出来之前，我们尽可以体面地抓花他的脸。」加斯拉克为战而喜，大笑起来，喊道：「朱斯啊，我这个主意，你听着不笑开怀么？」

「加斯拉克，」朱斯大人说，「你这提议提得高贵，还是我素来爱你的那副敞开的手与心。但巫国不是这样能克制的：要制服它，只有经过长日的操劳——设谋、造船、聚集一支与我们前番灭食尸鬼时所率相当的大军。」

任凭他怎样劝说，加斯拉克也撼不动他分毫。

但斯皮特法厄坐到兄弟身旁，私下对他说：「兄弟，你怎么了？魔国的一切豪情与雷厉风行都被碾灭了，只剩一张无用无汁的皮给我们么？你全然不像你一向的样子了；巫国若此刻看见我们，满可以断定我们被卑怯攫住了——明明兵力之势这样侥幸在我们这边，我们却缩着不敢打他。」

===Original===

Juss said in Spitfire’s ear, “This it is, that I do misdoubt me of the steadfastness of the Goblins. Too like to fire among dead leaves is the sudden flame of their valour, a poor thing to rely on if once they be checked. So do I count it folly trusting in them for our main strength to go up against Carcë. Also it is but a wild fancy that Goldry hath been transported into Carcë.”

But Spitfire leaped up a-cursing, and cried out, “O Gaslark, thou wert best fare home to Goblinland. But we will sail openly to Carcë and crave audience of the great King, entreating him suffer us to kiss his toe, and acknowledging him to be our King and us his ill-conditioned, disobedient children. So may he haply restore unto us our brother, when he hath chastised us, and haply of his mercy send us home to Demonland, there to fawn upon Corsus or vile Corinius, or whomsoever he shall set up in Galing for his Viceroy. For with Goldry hath all manliness departed out of Demonland, and we be milksops that remain, and objects of scorn and spitting.”

Now while Spitfire spake thus in wrath and sorrow of heart, the Lord Brandoch Daha fared fore and aft on the gangway about and about, as a caged panther fareth when feeding time is long overdue. And at whiles he clapped hand to the hilt of his long and glittering sword and rattled it in the scabbard. At length, standing over against Gaslark, and eyeing him with a mocking glance, “O Gaslark,” he said, “this that hath befallen breedeth in me a cruel perturbation which carries my spirits outwards, stirring up a tempest in my mind and preparing my body to melancholy, and madness itself. The cure of this is only fighting. Wherefore if thou love me, Gaslark, out with thy sword and ward thyself. Fight I must, or this passion will kill me quite out. ’Tis pity to draw upon my friend, but sith we be banned from fighting with our enemies, what choice remaineth?”

Gaslark laughed and seized him playfully by the arms, saying, “I will not fight with thee, how prettily soe’er thou ask it, Brandoch Daha, that savedst Goblinland from the Witches”; but straight grew grave again and said to Juss, “O Juss, be ruled. Thou seest what temper thy friends are in. All we be as hounds tugging against the leash to be loosed against Carcë in this happy hour, that likely cometh not again.”

===Chinese===

朱斯在斯皮特法厄耳边说：「我心里犯疑的，是哥布林人的心志不坚。他们那骤起的勇烈，太像死叶堆上的火，一受挫折便不足倚仗。所以我把倚他们为主力去攻打喀尔刻看作愚事。而且说戈尔德里被摄进了喀尔刻，也不过是瞎猜。」

但斯皮特法厄跳起来咒骂，喊道：「加斯拉克啊，你最好还是回哥布林国去吧。我们要大大方方开到喀尔刻，求见大王，恳求他许我们亲他的脚趾，承认他是我们的王、我们是他忤逆不肖的儿女。这样，等他责罚了我们，他说不定肯把我们兄弟还给我们；再发发慈悲，遣送我们回魔国，去巴结科苏斯（Corsus）或卑劣的科里尼厄斯，或他将来派去坐镇加灵（Galing）的哪一位总督。因为戈尔德里一去，魔国的丈夫气全数离场，剩下的我们全是奶面团，是被人嗤笑唾弃的东西。」

斯皮特法厄这样悲愤说着的时候，布兰多赫·达哈大人在舷道上来回踱步，转了又转，像一头喂食迟迟不来的笼中豹。他不时按住那柄修长雪亮的剑柄，把剑在鞘里拨得锿锵。末了他站到加斯拉克对面，眼光带着讥诮：「加斯拉克啊，」他说，「这场变故在我里面生了一场酷烈的扰乱，把我的精气都掀到外面去：在我心里掀起一场风暴，叫我的身子趋向忧郁、直趋向癫狂。这病唯一的治法就是打架。所以你若爱我，加斯拉克，拔出剑来，保护好你自己。我必须打，否则这股激情要把我整个杀死。对朋友拔剑实在抱歉；可既然不许我们同敌人打，还有什么可选择？」

加斯拉克大笑，嬉闹地抓住他的双臂说：「我不跟你打，任你求得再妙也不打——布兰多赫·达哈，你救过哥布林国的人。」随即又正色对朱斯说：「朱斯啊，听劝吧。你看见你的朋友们都在什么火候上。我们个个像拽着皮带要扑向喀尔刻的猎犬，趁着这千载难逢的好时辰；这时机怕不会再来了。」

===Original===

Now when Lord Juss perceived them all against him, and hot-mouthed for that attempt, he smiled scornfully and said, “O my brother and my friends, what echoes and quail-pipes are you become who seem to catch wisdom by imitating her voice? But ye be mad like March hares, every man of you, and myself too. Break ice in one place, ’twill crack in more. And truly I care not greatly for my life now that Goldry is gone from me. Cast we lots, then, which of us three shall fare home to Demonland with this our ship, that is but a lame duck since this sending. And he on whom the lot shall fall must fare home to concert the raising of a mighty fleet and armament to carry on our war against the Witches.”

So spake Lord Juss, and all they who had but a short hour ago felt themselves in such point that there was in them no hope of convalescence nor of life, had now their spirits raised in a seeming drunkenness, and thought only on the gladness of battle.

The lords of Demonland marked each his lot and cast it in the helm of Gaslark, and Gaslark shook the helm, and there leapt forth the lot of the Lord Spitfire. Right wrathful was he. So the lords of Demonland did off their armour and their costly apparel that was black with soot, and let cleanse it. Sixty of their fighting men that were unscathed by the sending went aboard one of Gaslark’s ships, and the crew of that ship manned the ship of Demonland, and Spitfire took the steering paddle, and the Demons that were hurt lay in the hold of the hollow ship. They brought forth a spare sail and hoisted it in place of that that was destroyed; so in sore discontent, yet with a cheerful countenance, the Lord Spitfire set sail for the west. And Gaslark the king sat by the steering paddle of his fair dragon of war, and by him the Lord Juss and the Lord Brandoch Daha, who was like a warhorse impatient for battle. Her prow swung north and so round eastaway, and her sail broidered with flower-de-luces smote the mast and filled to the northwest wind, and those other six fared after her in line ahead with white sails unfurled, striding majestic over the full broad billows.

===Chinese===

朱斯大人见他们都反对他、都热切催着这一趟冒险，便冷冷一笑，说：「我的兄弟，我的朋友们，你们都成了什么回声与鹌鹑笛了？只学智慧的嗓音，就想捉住智慧么？可你们真是一群疯得像三月野兔的人，一个一个都是，连我自己也是。一处破了冰，处处都要裂。说真的，如今戈尔德里去了，我这条命我也不大在乎了。那么我们掷签吧，看我们三人谁驾着这条船——自那遣送之后它已是只瘸腿鸭——回魔国去。签落在谁身上，谁就回家去，筹办一支大舰队大军，接续我们对巫人的战争。」

朱斯大人这样说；于是，方才还自觉伤得连痊愈与活命的指望都没有的那些人，此刻都精神陡振，像醺醺然醉了，一心只想着战斗的欢乐。

魔国诸大人各做了签，投进加斯拉克的头盔；加斯拉克摇了摇头盔，跳出来的是斯皮特法厄大人的签。他大为忿然。于是魔国诸大人脱下被烟灰熏黑的甲胄与华服，叫人洗净。六十名未被遣送所伤的战士上了加斯拉克的一艘船，那船的水手过来操纵魔国的船；斯皮特法厄接过舵桨，伤者躺进空舱里。他们取出一面备用帆，升起换掉毁掉的那面；斯皮特法厄大人就这样满心郁郁、面上却欢然地扬帆西去。加斯拉克王坐在他那条美丽战龙的舵桨旁，身边是朱斯大人和布兰多赫·达哈大人——后者像一匹等不得上阵的战马。船首转北，又向东转；绣着鸢尾花的帆打上桅杆，吃满了西北风；另外六艘白帆尽张，鱼贯相随，在那宽阔的涌浪上雄壮地破浪而行。

## VI / 六
===Original===

The Claws of Witchland

Of King Gaslark’s leading in the attempt on Carcë in the dark, and how he prospered therein, and of the great stand of Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha.

On the evening of the third day, whenas they drew near to within sight of the Witchland coast, they brailed up their sails and waited for the night, that so they might make the landfall after dark; for little to their mind it was that the King should have news of their farings. This was their plan, to beach their ships on the lonely shore some two leagues north of Tenemos, whence it was but two hours’ march across the fen to Carcë. So when the sun set and all the ways were darkened they muffled their oars and rowed silently to the low shore that showed strangely near in the darkness, yet ever seemed to flee and keep its distance as they rowed toward it. Coming at length ashore, they drew their ships up on the beach. Some fifty men of the Goblins they left to guard the ships, while the rest took their weapons. And when they were marshalled they marched inland over the sand-dunes and so on to the open fen; and seeing that the most of them by far were of Goblinland, it was agreed between those three, Juss, Brandoch Daha, and Gaslark, that Gaslark should have command of this emprise. So fared they silently across the marshes, that were firm enough for marching so it were done circumspectly, rounding the worst moss-hags and the small lochs that were scattered here and there. For the weather had been fine for a season, and little new water stood on the marsh. But as they drew near to Carcë the weather worsened and fine rain began to fall. And albeit there was little comfort marching through the drizzling murk of night towards that fortress of evil name, yet was Lord Juss glad at the rain, since it favoured surprise, and on surprise hung all their hopes.

===Chinese===

巫国的爪子

述加斯拉克王如何乘黑进击喀尔刻及其顺利；及朱斯大人与布兰多赫·达哈大人的苦战。

第三天傍晚，他们将将望得见巫国海岸时，便收帆停桨等天黑，好黑夜登陆；因为万不可叫王得到他们行踪的消息。他们的计划是：把船靠上特内莫斯（Tenemos）以北约二里格的荒岸，从那里过沼泽到喀尔刻（Carcë）不过两小时路程。日落路暗之后，他们裹住桨，悄悄划向那低低的岸——黑暗里那岸显得异样地近，却又仿佛总在后退，与他们划近的距离始终不缩。终于登了岸，他们把船拖上沙滩。留下五十来个哥布林人守船，其余的执了兵刃。整好队，他们便越过沙丘向内陆行进，走上开阔的沼泽；他们中绝大多数既是哥布林国人，朱斯（Lord Juss）、布兰多赫·达哈（Lord Brandoch Daha）与加斯拉克三人便议定：这次行动由加斯拉克统率。他们就这样悄悄穿过沼泽——只要走得小心，沼泽尽可通行——绕开最坏的泥沼和四散的小湖。原来天时已晴了一阵，沼上积的新水不多。但临近喀尔刻时天转坏，下起了细雨。在夜里潘湿的昏暗中向那恶名昭彰的堡垒行进，固然没有什么舒服可言，朱斯大人却为这雨欢喜：雨利于奇袭，而他们的全部指望都悬在奇袭上。

===Original===

About the middle night they halted within four hundred paces of the outer walls of Carcë, that loomed ghostly through the watery curtain, silent as it had been a tomb where Witchland lay in death, rather than the mailed shell wherein so great a power sat waiting. The sight of that vast bulk couched shadowy in the rain lighted the fire of battle in the breast of Gaslark, nor would aught please him save that they should go forthwith up to the walls with all their force, and so march round them seeking where they might break suddenly in and seize the place. Nor would he listen to the counsel of Lord Juss, who would send forth detachments to select a spot for assault and bring back word before the whole force advanced. “Be sure,” said Gaslark, “that they within are all foxed and cupshotten the third night with swilling of wine, in honour of such triumph as he hath gotten by his sending, and but a sorry watch is kept on such a night. For who, say they, shall come up against Carcë now that the power of Demonland is stricken in pieces? The scorned Goblins, ha? A motion for laughter and derision. But thine advance guard might give them warning or ever our main force could seize the occasion. Nay, but as the Ghouls in an evil day coming suddenly upon me in Zajë Zaculo gat my palace taken ere we were well ware of their coming, so must we take this hold of Carcë. And if thou fearest a sally, right hotly do I desire it. For if they open the gate we are enough to force an entry in despite of any numbers they are like to have within.”

Now Juss thought ill of this counsel, yet, for a strange languor that still hung about his wits, he would not gainsay Gaslark. So crept they in stealth near to the great walls of Carcë. Softly ever fell the rain, and breathless stood the cypresses within the outer ward, and blank and dumb and untenanted frowned the black marble walls of that sleeping castle. And dour midnight waited over all.

===Chinese===

午夜前后，他们在离喀尔刻外墙四百步的地方停了下来；那堡垒隔着水雾的帷幕影影绰绰，沉寂得像一座巫国仰卧在其中的坟墓，不像一座甲壳，里面坐着这样一股大权势在等候。那庞大黑影伏在雨里的景象，点燃了加斯拉克胸中的战火；他只肯一件事：立刻全军直追到墙下，沿墙搜行，找一处可以突然冲入夺下堡垒的地方。他不听朱斯大人的主意——朱斯主张先派分队去选定突破口，回报之后再全军压上。「你放心，」加斯拉克说，「里面的人正为着他那遣送得来的大捷，酗酒灌到第三个夜晚，个个烂醉如泥；这样的夜，哨备也稀松。他们说：魔国的势力既已被击得粉碎，还有谁敢来碰喀尔刻？被人燋不起的哥布林人，哈？笑话罢了。可你的先锋倒可能给他们报了信，误了我们主力抓住时机。不，就像当年食尸鬼倒雾的日子，在扎杰·扎库洛突然扑到我头上，我们还不大醒悟，宫就被他们夺了；我们也必这样夺下喀尔刻这座堡。你若怕他们出城反击——我正求之不得！他们若开门，凭他们里面可能有的任何人数，我们也尽够杀进去。」

朱斯觉得这主意不妥；然而一种奇怪的倦怠仍缠着他的心智，他不愿驳加斯拉克。他们就这样潜行到喀尔刻大墙近处。雨轻轻落着，外院里的柏树屏息而立，那沉睡城堡的黑大理石墙荒芜、嘻哑、无人，阴沉地雔伏着。顽钝的午夜笼罩着一切。

===Original===

Now Gaslark issued command, bidding them march warily round the walls northward, for no way was betwixt the lofty walls and the river on the south and east, but to the northeast was he hopeful to find a likely place to win into the hold. In such order went they that Gaslark with an hundred of his ablest men led the van, and after him came the Demons. The main strength of the Goblins followed after, with Teshmar for their captain. Warily they marched, and now were they on the rising ground that ran back north and west from the bluff of Carcë to the fen. Full eager were they of Goblinland and flown with the intoxication of impending battle, and they of the vanguard fared apace, outstripping the Demons, so that Juss was fain to hasten after them lest they should lose touch and fall to confusion. But Teshmar’s men feared greatly to be left behind, nor might he hold them back, but they must run betwixt the Demons and the walls, meaning to join with Gaslark. Juss swore under his breath, saying, “See the unruly rabble of Goblinland. And they will yet be our undoing.”

===Chinese===

加斯拉克传令：沿墙小心向北绕行——南面与东面，高墙与河之间没有路，唯有东北方他有望找到一处可以攻进堡去的地方。行军的次序是：加斯拉克率百名最精锐的作先锋，魔人居后，哥布林主力再随其后，由特什马尔统领。他们小心行进，这时已走上从喀尔刻陡坎向西北折回沼泽的那片高地。哥布林人求战心切，都被将临之战的醉意熏腾着；先锋走得飞快，把魔人甩在后面，朱斯只得赶紧追赶，惟恐失了联络乱作一团。特什马尔的人又极怕落在后头，拦也拦不住，竟从魔人与城墙之间奔跑起来，要去与加斯拉克会合。朱斯低声咒骂：「瞧哥布林国这帮没规矩的暴民。他们早晚要坏了我们的事。」

===Original===

In such case stood they, nor were Teshmar’s folk more than twenty paces from the walls, when, sudden as night-lightning, flares were kindled along the walls, dazzling the Goblins and the Demons and brightly lighting them for those that manned the walls, who fell a-shooting at them with spears and arrows and a-slinging of stones. In the same moment opened a postern gate, whence sallied forth the Lord Corinius with an hundred and fifty stout lads of Witchland, shouting, “He that would sup of the crab of Witchland must deal with the nippers ere he essay the shell”; and charging Gaslark’s army in the flank he cut them clean in two. As one wood fared forth Corinius, smiting on either hand with a two-edged axe with heft lapped with bronze; and greatly though the folk of Gaslark outnumbered him, yet were they so taken at unawares and confounded by the sudden onslaught of Corinius that they might not abide him but everywhere gave ground before his onslaught. And many were wounded and some were slain; and with these Teshmar of Goblinland, the master of Gaslark’s ship. For smiting at Corinius and missing of his aim he louted forward with the blow, and Corinius hewed at him with his axe and the blow came on Teshmar’s neck and so hewed off his head. Now Gaslark with the best of his fighting men was come some way past the postern, but whenas they fell to fighting he turned back straightway to meet Corinius, calling loudly on his men to rally against the Witches and drive them back within the walls. So when Gaslark was gotten through the press to within reach of Corinius, he thrust at Corinius with a spear, wounding him in the arm. But Corinius smote the spear-shaft asunder with his axe, and leapt upon Gaslark, giving him a great wound on the shoulder. And Gaslark took to his sword, and many blows they bandied that made either stagger, till Corinius struck Gaslark on the helm a great downstroke of his axe, as one driveth a pile with a wooden mallet. And because of the good helm he wore, given by Lord Juss in days gone by as a gift of love and friendship, was Gaslark saved and his head not cloven asunder; for on that helm Corinius’s axe might not bite. Yet with that great stroke were Gaslark’s senses driven forth of him for a season, so that he fell senseless to the earth. And with his fall came dismay upon them of Goblinland.

===Chinese===

正当此时——特什马尔的人离墙不过二十步——骤然如夜里的闪电，沿墙一齐燃起火炬，照得哥布林人和魔人睁不开眼，却把他们的身影清清楚楚照给了守墙的人；墙上的人朝他们撒下矛、箭，投下石弹。同一瞬间，一道边门开处，科里尼厄斯（Corinius）大人率一百五十名巫国壮士冲出，大吼道：「想吃巫国螃蟹的，先对付螯，再碰壳！」他侧击加斯拉克的军队，一刀把它剁成两断。科里尼厄斯像一片扫倒的树林冲杀过来，双手抡一柄铜篐柄的双刃斧，左右开弓；加斯拉克的人虽然远多于他，却被这笑袭弄得措手不及、心胆俱乱，挡他不住，在他的冲击前处处后退。许多人带伤，一些人被杀；其中有哥布林国的特什马尔，加斯拉克船上的船长。他一斧劈向科里尼厄斯却劈了个空，身子随斧前倾；科里尼厄斯挥斧砍他，正中脖颈，割下了他的头。加斯拉克和最棒的一批战士这时已走过边门一段路，厮杀一起，他立刻回身来战科里尼厄斯，大声呼叫部下向巫人集结、把他们赶回墙里去。加斯拉克挤过人群，够到科里尼厄斯跟前，挺矛刺去，伤了他的手臂。科里尼厄斯一斧砍断矛杆，扑向加斯拉克，在他肩上重重砍了一道大口。加斯拉克拔出剑来，两人一来一往对了多少斧剑，杀得彼此踉跄；末了科里尼厄斯抢圆斧头朝加斯拉克的头盔猛劈下来，像用木槌打桩一般。多亏他戴的那顶好盔——往日朱斯大人赠他作情谊之礼的——加斯拉克才保住了头没有劈作两半；科里尼厄斯的斧在那盔上咬不住。然而这一记重击仍把他打得神志离体，昏迷倒地。他一倒，哥布林人顿时惶遽。

===Original===

All this befell in the first brunt of the battle, nor were the lords of Demonland yet fully joined in the mellay, for the great press of Gaslark’s men were between them and the Witches; but now Juss and Brandoch Daha went forth mightily with their following, and took up Gaslark that lay like one dead, and Juss bade a company of the Goblins bear him to the ships, and there was he bestowed safe and sound. But the Witches shouted loudly that King Gaslark was slain; and at this chosen time Corund, that was come privily forth of a hidden door on the western side of Carcë with fifty men, took the Goblins mightily in the rear. So they, still falling back before Corinius and Corund, and their hearts sick at the supposed slaying of Gaslark, waxed full of doubt and dejection; for in the watery darkness they might nowise perceive by how much they outwent in numbers the men of Witchland. And panic took them, so that they broke and fled before the Witches, that came after them resolute, as a stoat holdeth by a rabbit, and slew them by scores and by fifties as they fled from Carcë. Scarce three score men of that brave company of Goblinland that went up with Gaslark against Carcë won away into the marshes and came to their ships, escaping pitiless destruction.

But Corund and Corinius and their main force turned without more ado against the Demons, and bitter was the battle that befell betwixt them, and great the clatter of their blows. And now were the odds clean changed about with the putting of the Goblins out of the battle, since but few of Witchland were fallen, and they were as four to one against the Demons, hemming them in and having at them from every side. And some shot at them from the wall, until a chance shot came that was like to have stove in Corund’s helm, who straightway sent word that when the rout was ended he would make lark-pies of the cow-headed doddipole whosoever he might be that had set them thus a-shooting, spoiling sport for their comrades and dangering their lives. Therewith ceased the shooting from the wall.

===Chinese===

这一切都发生在战斗的头一击里，魔国诸大人尚未完全卷入混战，因为加斯拉克的大队人马正隔在他们与巫人中间；这时朱斯与布兰多赫·达哈率部猛进，抬起死人似的加斯拉克，朱斯点了一队哥布林人把他送回船上，安顿妥当。巫人却大声欢呼，说加斯拉克王被杀了；乘着这个时机，科伦德（Corund）带五十人从喀尔刻西面一道暗门里悄悄出来，狠狠兜到哥布林人背后。哥布林人被科里尼厄斯与科伦德前后夹着，又心痛加斯拉克阵亡的讹传，疑惧清沉到了极点：在水雾的黑暗里，他们全然看不出自己在人数上怎样远远压过巫人。恐悦攫住了他们，他们在巫人面前溃败奔逃；巫人穷追不舍，像鼬鼠咬住兔子不放，在他们逃出喀尔刻的路上成十成五十地宰杀。随加斯拉克攻喀尔刻的那支哥布林国勇士之队，逃进沼泽、回到船上的，还不满六十人，才算躲过了无情的屠戮。

科伦德与科里尼厄斯随即率主力掉头对付魔人，一场恶战在他们中间展开，斧剑相击铮然震响。哥布林人一垮，形势整个倒了过来：巫人阵亡的寥寥，如今四比一围住魔人，四面八方攻他们。还有人从墙上放箭，直到一发流箭差点砸瘪了科伦德的盔，他立刻传话：等收拾完这股溃兵，他要把那个下令放箭的牛头蠢货剁成云雀馅饼——这样乱射，坏了袍泽的兴致还险他们性命。墙上的箭这才停了。

===Original===

And now grim and woundsome grew the battle, for the Demons mightily withstood the onset of the Witches, and the Lord Brandoch Daha rushed with an onslaught ever and anon upon Corund or upon Corinius, nor might either of those great captains bear up long against him, but every time gave back before Lord Brandoch Daha; and bitterly cursed they one another as each in turn was fain to save himself amid the press of their fighting men. Nor could one hope in one night’s space to behold such deeds of derring-do as were done that night by Lord Brandoch Daha, that played his sword lightly as one handleth a willow wand; yet death sat on the point thereof. In such wise that eleven stout sworders of Witchland were slain by him, and fifteen besides were sorely wounded. And at the last, Corinius, stung by Corund’s taunts as by a gadfly, and well nigh bursting for grief and shame at his ill speeding, leapt upon Lord Brandoch Daha as one reft of his wits, aiming at him a great two-handed blow that was apt enough to cleave him to the brisket. But Brandoch Daha slipped from the blow lightly as a kingfisher flying above an alder-shadowed stream avoideth a branch in his flight, and ran Corinius through the right wrist with his sword. And straight was Corinius put out of the fight. Nor had they greater satisfaction that went against Lord Juss, who mowed at them with great swashing blows, beheading some and hewing some asunder in the midst, till they were fain to keep clear of his reaping. So fought the Demons in the glare and watery mist, greatly against great odds, until all were smitten to earth save those two lords alone, Juss and Brandoch Daha.

Now stood King Gorice on the outer battlements of Carcë, all armed in his black armour inlaid with gold; and he beheld those twain how they fought back to back, and how the Witches beset them on every side yet nowise might prevail against them. And the King said unto Gro that was by him on the wall, “Mine eyes dazzle in the mist and torchlight. What be these that maintain so bloody an advantage upon my kemperie-men?”

Gro answered him, “Surely, O King, these be none other than Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha of Krothering.”

===Chinese===

战局愈来愈凶险酷烈：魔人顽强地抵挡着巫人的冲击，布兰多赫·达哈大人一次次猛扑向科伦德或科里尼厄斯；那两位大统帅谁也撑不住他多久，每次都在他面前败退，在自家兵马的乱丛里各自逃命时，彼此恶声咒骂。一夜之间，人休想再见到布兰多赫·达哈大人那晚所立的武功：他的剑在他手里轻灵如挥柳条，剑尖上却坐着死亡。那一夜，巫国十一员健壮的剑手被他杀死，另有十五人重伤。末了，科里尼厄斯被科伦德的奚落蚊虻似地叮着，又因受挫而悲愤欲狂，像失了魂一样扑向布兰多赫·达哈大人，双手抡起狠劈一记，那力道尽够把他劈到胸口。布兰多赫·达哈轻轻闪过那一斧，轻得像翠鸟掠过赤杨荫下的溪面避开一根枝子，随剑刺穿科里尼厄斯右腕。科里尼厄斯当下就退出了战团。扑向朱斯大人的那些人也没讨到更多便宜：他挥剑大扫大砍，削头的削头，断腰的断腰，杀得他们巴不得离他这收割的镰刀远些。魔人就这样在火光与水雾里，以寡敌众，杀到最后，除了朱斯与布兰多赫·达哈两位大人，尽数倒地。

戈里斯王这时站在喀尔刻的外垛口上，全副黑金嵌饰的甲胄；他看着那两人背靠背厮杀，看着巫人四面围困却奈何他们不得。王对身旁墙上的格罗（Gro）说：「我眼睛在雾与火把光里发花。这些在我武士头上占着血腥上风的，是什么人？」

格罗答道：「王啊，这必是朱斯大人和克罗瑟林（Krothering）的布兰多赫·达哈大人，不是别人。」

===Original===

The King said, “So by degrees cometh my sending home to me. For by my art I have intelligence, albeit not certainly, that Goldry was taken by my sending; so have I my desire on him I hold most in hate. And these, saved by their enchantments from like ruin, have been driven mad to rush into the open mouth of my vengeance.” And when he had gazed awhile, the King sneered and said unto Gro, “A sweet sight, to behold an hundred of my ablest men flinch and duck before these twain. Till now methought there was a sword in Witchland, and methought Corinius and Corund not simple braggarts without power or heart, as here appeareth, since like boys well birched they do cringe from the shining swords of Juss and the vile upstart from Krothering.”

But Corinius, who stood no longer in the battle but by the King, full of spleen and his wrist all bloody, cried out, “You do us wrong, O King. Juster it were to praise my great deed in ambushing this mighty company of our enemies and putting them all to the slaughter. And if I prevailed not against this Brandoch Daha your majesty needs not to marvel, since a greater than I, Gorice X of memory ever glorious, was lightly conquered by him. Wherein methinks I am the luckier, to have but a gored wrist and not my death. As for these twain, they be stick-frees, on whom no point or edge may bite. And nought were more to be looked for, since we deal with such a sorcerer as this Juss.”

“Rather,” said the King, “are ye all grown milksops. But I have no further stomach for this interlude, but straight will end it.”

Therewith the King called to him the old Duke Corsus, bidding him take nets and catch the Demons therein. And Corsus, faring forth with nets, by sheer weight of numbers and with the death of near a score of the Witches at length gat this performed, and Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha well tangled in the nets, and lapped about as silkworms in their cocoons, and so drawn into Carcë. Soundly were they bumped along the ground, and glad enow were the Witches to have gotten those great fighters scotched at last. For utterly spent were Corund and his men, and fain to drop for very weariness.

===Chinese===

王说：「我的遣送就这样一笔一笔给我送回账来。凭我的法术，我得了消息（虽不十分确凿）：戈尔德里已被我的遣送摄去；这样，我最恨的那人已落我手。而这两个，靠他们的邪术免了同样的下场，却疯得撞进我复仇的嘴里来。」他注目看了一阵，嗤笑一声，对格罗说：「好看的景象：我一百名最健的武士，在这两人面前点头哈腰、躲躲闪闪。到今夜之前，我还当巫国有剑，还当科里尼厄斯与科伦德不是无勇无胆的吹牛匠；照眼前这样子，他们倒像挨了鞭子的小学生，见了朱斯和克罗瑟林那个卑贱暴发户的亮剑就发抖。」

科里尼厄斯这时已不在战阵，立在王旁，一肚子怨气，手腕鲜血淋漓。他喊道：「王啊，您冤枉我们了。更公道些，该夸我伏击这股敌人劲旅、把他们送去屠场的大功。我若胜不过这个布兰多赫·达哈，陛下也不必诧异：比我更伟大的、那永远光荣的戈里斯十世，不也轻易败在他手下么？这么想，我倒是运气好的：只挂了彩腕，没送命。至于那两位，他们是有免刀免枪之体的，刀尖斧刃咬他们不动。这也没什么可奇怪的，我们对付的是朱斯这样的大巫师。」

「倒不如说，」王说，「你们全成了奶面团。这出插戏我看够了，马上就收场。」

于是王唤来老公爵科苏斯（Corsus），命他取网来捉魔人。科苏斯带人张网而上，凭着人多势众，又赔上巫人近二十条性命，才终于把这事办成：朱斯大人与布兰多赫·达哈大人被紧紧缠在网里，像茧中的蚕，被拖进了喀尔刻。他们在地上被拖得砰砰作响；巫人们好不欢喜，总算把这两头猛兽制住了。科伦德和他的部下已彻底脱力，累得只想倒下。

===Original===

So when they were gotten into Carcë, the King let search with torches and bring in them of Witchland that lay hurt before the walls; and any Demons or Goblins that were happed upon in like case he let slay with the sword. And the Lord Juss and the Lord Brandoch Daha, still lapped tightly in their nets, he let fling into a corner of the inner court of the palace like two bales of damaged goods, and set a guard upon them until morning.

As the lords of Witchland were upon going to bed they beheld westward by the sea a red glow, and tongues of fire burning in the night. Corinius said unto Lord Gro, “Lo where thy Goblins burn their ships, lest we pursue them as they flee shamefully homeward in the ship they keep from the burning. One ship sufficeth, for most of them be dead.”

And Corinius betook him sleepily to bed, pausing on the way to kick at the Lord Brandoch Daha, that lay safely swathed in his net powerless as then to do him harm.

===Chinese===

他们既被弄进喀尔刻，王便命人打着火把搜索，把倒在墙外带伤的巫国人都抬进来；撞见的魔人或哥布林人，一律用剑杀却。朱斯大人与布兰多赫·达哈大人仍被网子紧紧裹着，王命人把他们像两捆破损的货一样，扬进宫内院的一个角落，派人看守到天明。

巫国诸大人正要就寝，望见西边海边一片红光，火舌在夜里熊熊烧着。科里尼厄斯对格罗大人说：「瞧，你的哥布林人在烧他们的船呢，免得我们在他们可耻逃回家去时追击——他们从火里只留了一条船。一条船尽够了，他们大部分都死了。」

科里尼厄斯便瞑腾腾去睡了，半路上还停下来，朝布兰多赫·达哈大人踢了一脚——那人裹在网里，此时奈何他不得，安全得很。

## VII / VII
===Original===

Guests of the King in Carcë

Of the two banquet halls that were in Carcë, the old and the new, and of the entertainment given by King Gorice XII in the one hall to Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha and in the other to the prince La Fireez; and of their leave-taking when the banquet was done.

The morrow of that battle dawned fair on Carcë. Folk lay long abed after their toil, and until the sun was high nought stirred before the walls. But toward noon came forth a band sent by King Gorice to bring in the spoil; and they took up the bodies of the slain and laid them in howe on the right bank of the river Druima half a mile below Carcë, Witches, Demons, and Goblins in one grave together, and raised up a great howe over them.

Now was the sun’s heat strong, but the shadow of the great keep rested still on the terrace without the western wall of the palace. Cool and redolent of ease and soft repose was that terrace, paved with flagstones of red jasper, with spleenwort, asafoetida, livid toadstools, dragons’ teeth, and bitter moonseed growing in the joints. On the outer edge of the terrace were bushes of arbor vitae planted in a row, squat and round like sleeping dormice, with clumps of choke-pard aconite in the interspaces. Many hundred feet in length was the terrace from north to south, and at either end a flight of black marble steps led down to the level of the inner ward and its embattled wall.

===Chinese===

王之贵宾在喀尔刻

记喀尔刻新旧两座宴厅；戈里斯十二世（King Gorice XII）如何在一厅中「款待」朱斯大人（Lord Juss）与布兰多赫·达哈大人（Lord Brandoch Daha），在另一厅中款待拉·菲里兹（La Fireez）亲王；及宴罢辞别诸事。

那场大战的次日，喀尔刻天朗气清。人们劳乏之后高卧不起，直到日头高照，城墙外还没什么动静。将近正午，戈里斯王派出一队人马去收拾战场；他们收殓阵亡者的尸首，抬到喀尔刻下游半里、德鲁伊马河右岸，巫国人、魔族、哥布林人同穴而埋，在上面堆起一座大琛。

此时日光已烈，但大碉楼的影子还罩在宫墙西外的平台上。那平台凉爽宜人，满溢着安逸闲适的气息，铺着红碧玉的石板，石缝里长着铁角蕨、阿魏、灰白的毒蕈、龙齿草和苦味的蝙蝠葛。平台外缘成行种着侧柏，矮墩墩圆滚滚，像睡着的小鞘；树空隙间丛生着舟形乌头。平台自北而南长几百尺，两端各有一道黑大理石阶梯，通到内苑的地面和那带雉埞的围墙。

===Original===

Benches of green jasper massily built and laden with velvet cushions of many colours stood against the palace wall facing to the west, and on the bench nearest the Iron Tower a lady sat at ease, eating cream wafers and a quince tart served by her waiting-women in dishes of pale gold for her morning meal. Tall was that lady and slender, and beauty dwelt in her as the sunshine dwells in the red floor and gray-green trunks of a beech wood in early spring. Her tawny hair was gathered in deep folds upon her head and made fast by great silver pins, their heads set with anachite diamonds. Her gown was of cloth of silver with a knotted cord-work of black silk embroidery everywhere decked with little moonstones, and over it she wore a mantle of figured satin the colour of the wood-pigeon’s wing, tinselled and overcast with silver threads. White-skinned she was, and graceful as an antelope. Her eyes were green, with yellow fiery gleams. Daintily she ate the tart and wafers, sipping at whiles from a cup of amber, artificially carved, white wine cool from the cellars below Carcë; and a maiden sitting at her feet played on a seven-stringed lute, singing very sweetly this song:

“Aske me no more where Jove bestowes,

When June is past, the fading rose;

For in your beautie’s orient deepe,

These flowers, as in their causes, sleepe.

Aske me no more whether doth stray

The golden atomes of the day;

For in pure love heaven did prepare

Those powders to inrich your haire.

Aske me no more whether doth hast

The nightingale when May is past;

For in your sweet dividing throat

She winters and keepes warme her note.

Aske me no more where those starres light,

That downewards fall in dead of night;

For in your eyes they sit, and there

Fixed become as in their sphere.

Aske me no more if east or west

The Phenix builds her spicy nest;

For unto you at last shee flies,

And in your fragrant bosome dyes.”

“No more,” said the lady; “thy voice is cracked this morning. Is none abroad yet thou canst find to tell me of last night’s doings? Or are all gone my lord’s gate, that I left sleeping still as though all the poppies of all earth’s gardens breathed drowsiness about his head?”

“One cometh, madam,” said the damosel.

The lady said, “The Lord Gro. He may resolve me. Though were he in the stour last night, that were a wonder indeed.”

===Chinese===

厚重碧绿的碧玉长凳靠着宫墙面西而设，堆满各色天鹅绒坐垫；离铁塔最近的那张长凳上，一位贵妇悠然而坐，用着她的早点——侍女们用淡金盘子端上来的奶油薄脆和榅桲塔。那位贵妇高挑苗条，美在她身上驻留，如初春的阳光驻留在山毛榉林的红色地衣和灰绿树干上。她赤褐色的头发叠成厚厚的发望盘在头上，用大银簪固定，簪头嵌着阿那奇特钻石。她的长裙是银线锦缎，满绣黑色丝线结成的绳纹，绳纹上缀满小月光石；外面罩一件木鸽翅色提花缎斗篷，闪着银线织就的光。她肌肤雷白，体态轻盈如羚羊。眼睛是绿色的，闪着火黄的光。她雅致地吃着塔和薄脆，不时啜一口琥珀杯中的酒——那是喀尔刻地窖里的冷白葡萄酒；一个侍女坐在她脚边，弹七弦鲁特琴，甜美地唱着这支歌：

「别再问我，六月过后，朱庇特把那凋残的玫瑰藏向何处；

因为在你的美所居的东方深处，

这些花儿如藏在种因里一般安睡。

别再问我，白昼那金色的原子飘向何处；

因为纯粹的爱里，上天备下了

那些香粉，好富饰你的头发。

别再问我，五月过后，夜莺为何匆匆离去；

因为在你那甜蜜婉转的喉咙里，

她安度寒冬，把她的歌音煊得暖暖的。

别再问我，夜半坠落的星星在何处发光；

因为它们坐在你眼里，在那里

固定不动，如在自己的天球上。

别再问我，长生鸟在东方还是西方筑它那香巢；

因为它终究要向你飞来，

在你芬芳的怀抱里死去。」

「别唱了，」贵妇说；「今早你的嗓子哑了。外面就没个人，能给我讲讲昨夜的事？还是都去了我夫君的门上？我离开时他还在睡，仿佛全天下花园的罂粟都朝他头顶吐着倦意。」

「有人来了，夫人。」侍女说。

贵妇说：「是格罗勋爵。他能解我心头的疑问。虽然，他若真在昨夜的混战里，那倒真是奇事了。」

===Original===

Therewith came Gro along the terrace from the north, clad in a mantle of dun-coloured velvet with a collar of raised work of gold upon silver purl; and his long black curly beard was perfumed with orange-flower water and angelica. When they had greeted one another and the lady had bidden her women stand apart, she said, “My lord, I thirst for tidings. Recount to me all that befell since sundown. For I slept soundly till the streaks of morning showed through my chamber windows, and then I awoke from a flying dream of sennets sounding to the onset, and torches in the night, and war’s alarums. And there were torches indeed in my chamber lighting my lord to bed, that answered me no word but straightway fell asleep as in utter weariness. Some slight scratches he hath, but else unhurt. I would not wake him, for balm is in slumber; also is he ill to do with if one wake him so. But the tattle and wild surmise of the servants bloweth as ever to all points of wonder: as that a great armament of Demonland is disembarked at Tenemos, and all routed last night by my lord and by Corinius, and Goldry Bluszco slain in single combat with the King. Or that Juss hath set a charm on Laxus and all our fleet, making them sail like parricides against this land, Juss and the other Demons leading them; and all slain save Laxus and Goldry Bluszco, but these brought bound into Carcë, stark mad and frothing at the lips, and Corinius dead of his wounds after slaying of Brandoch Daha. Or, foolishly,” and her green eyes lightened dangerously, “that it was my brother risen in revolt to wrest Pixyland from the overlordship of Gorice, and joined with Gaslark to that end, and their army overthrown and both ta’en prisoner.”

Gro laughed and said, “Surely, O my Lady Prezmyra, truth masketh in many a strange disguise when she rideth rumour’s broomstick through kings’ palaces. But somewhat of herself hath she shown thee, if thou conclude that an event was brought to birth betwixt dark and sunrise to stagger the world, and that the power of Witchland bloomed forth this night into unbeholden glory.”

“Thou speakest big, my lord,” said the lady. “Were the Demons in it?”

“Ay, madam,” he said.

“And triumphed on? and slain?”

“All slain save Juss and Brandoch Daha, and they taken,” said Gro.

“Was this my lord’s doing?” she asked.

说话间格罗从平台北头走来，披一件暗褐色天鹅绒斗篷，领子是用金线在银辫上凸起绣成；他长长的黑色卷须上熏着橙花水和当归香。两人见礼之后，贵妇命侍女们退开，说：「大人，我渴望消息。把日落后发生的一切都讲给我听。我一觉睡到晨光透进卧室窗户才醒，醒来时正从一个乱梦里挣脱：号角吹响冲锋，火把在夜里摇曳，战事的惊呼。我的闺房里倒真是有火把，照着我夫君上床；他一句话也不答我，倒头便睡，像裹尽了疲惫。他受了几处轻伤，其余无恙。我不忍叫醒他，睡里有香膏；何况这样叫醒他，他也不会好相与。可仆人们的闲话和瞎猜照例吹向一切可惊之处：说魔国的大军马在特内莫斯（Tenemos）登陆，昨夜被我夫君和科里尼厄斯（Corinius）全歼，戈尔德里·布卢斯科（Goldry Bluszco）在与王单挑中被杀。或者说朱斯施法迷了拉克苏斯（Laxus）和我们整个舰队，叫他们弑亲一般反戈打向本国，朱斯和其他魔族率领他们；除拉克苏斯和戈尔德里全都死了，这两个被捆进喀尔刻，赤裸裸地疯着，嘴吐白沫，科里尼厄斯杀了布兰多赫·达哈之后伤重而死。或者说——愚不可及，」她的绿眼睛危险地闪着光，「说是我兄弟起兵造反，要从戈里斯的宗主权下夺回精灵国（Pixyland），为此与加斯拉克合兵，兵败被俘。」

格罗笑道：「千真万确，我的普雷兹米拉夫人（Prezmyra），当真理骑着谣言的扫帚穿过王宫时，总是戴着千百种奇怪的假面。但她也向你露了几分真容，只要你想到：黑夜与日出之间降生了一件震动世界的大事，而巫国的权势今夜绽放出了前所未见的光荣。」

「大人说得盛大，」贵妇说。「魔族人也在其中？」

「在，夫人。」他说。

「他们打胜了？被杀了？」

「除朱斯和布兰多赫·达哈，全部被杀，那两个被俘了。」格罗说。

「这是我夫君的功劳？」她问。

“Greatly, as I think,” said Gro; “though Corinius claimeth for himself, as commonly, the main honour of it.”

Prezmyra said, “He claimeth overmuch.” And she said, “There were none in it save Demons?”

Gro, knowing her thought, smiled and made answer, “Madam, there were Witches.”

“My Lord Gro,” she cried, “thou dost ill to mock me. Thou art my friend. Thou knowest the Prince my brother proud and sudden to anger. Thou knowest it chafeth him to have Witchland over him. Thou knowest the time is many days overpast when he should bring his yearly tribute to the King.”

Gro’s great ox-eyes were soft as he looked upon the Lady Prezmyra, saying, “Most assuredly am I thy friend, madam. Belike, if truth were told, thou and thy lord are all the true friends I have in waterish Witchland: you two, and the King: but who sleepeth safe in the favour of kings? Ah, madam, none of Pixyland stood in the battle yesternight. Therefore let thy soul be at ease. But my task it was, standing on the battlements beside the King, to smile and smile while Corinius and our fighting men made a bloody havoc of four or five hundred of mine own kinsfolk.”

Prezmyra caught her breath and was silent a moment. Then, “Gaslark?”

“The main force was his, it appeareth,” answered Lord Gro. “Corinius braggeth himself his banesman, and certain it is he felled him to earth. But I am secretly advertised he was not among the dead taken up this morning.”

“My lord,” she said, “my desire for news drinks deep while thou art fasting. Some, bring meat and wine for my Lord Gro.” And two damosels ran and returned with sparkling golden wine in a beaker, and a dish of lampreys with hippocras sauce. So Gro sat him down on the jasper bench and, while he ate and drank, rehearsed to the Lady Prezmyra the doings of the night.

When he had ended she said, “How hath the King dealt with those twain, Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha?”

Gro answered, “He hath them clapped up in the old banqueting hall in the Iron Tower.” And his brow darkened, and he said, “ ’Tis pity thy lord lay thus long abed, and so came not to the council, where Corsus and Corinius, backed by thy stepsons and the sons of Corsus, egged on the King to use shamefully these lords of Demonland. 普雷兹米拉倒抽一口气，沉默片刻。然后问：「加斯拉克呢？」

and little for my health, and little gain withal, had it been had I then openly withstood them. Corinius is ever watchful to fling Goblin in my teeth. But Corund weigheth in their councils as his hand weigheth in battle.”

Corund sat by his lady on the bench and drank. “If that be all, madam,” said he, “then have I little to charge my conscience withal. For nought lies readier than strike off their heads, and so bring all to a fit and happy ending.”

“La Fireez?” she said.

“Mine eyes be strong enow and clear enow,” said Corund, “but thou’dst scarce require me swear to mine own brother at three miles’ distance. And as for thine, I leave thee the swearing.”

They found the King on the topmost battlements above the water-gate with his lords about him, gazing eastaway toward the long low hills beyond which lay Pixyland. But when Corund began to open his mind to the King, the King said, “Thou growest old, O Corund, and like a good-for-nothing chapman bringest not thy wares to market ere the market be done. I have already ta’en order for this, and straitly charged my people that nought befell last night save a faring of the Goblins against Carcë, and their overthrow, and my chasing of them with a great slaughter into the sea. Whoso by speech or sign shall reveal to La Fireez that the Demons were in it, or that these enemies of mine are thus entertained by me to their discomfort in the old banquet hall, he shall lose nothing but his life.”

Corund said, “It is well, O King.”

The King said, “Captain general, what is our strength?”

Corinius answered, “Seventy and three were slain, and the others for the most part hurt: I among them, that am thus one-handed for the while. I will not engage to find you, O King, fifty sound men in Carcë.”

“My Lord Corund,” said the King, “thine eyes pierced ever a league beyond the best among us, young or old. How many makest thou yon company?”

Corund leaned on the parapet and shaded his eyes with his hand that was broad as a smoked haddock and covered on the back with yellow hairs growing somewhat sparsely, as the hairs on the skin of a young elephant. “He rideth with three score horse, O King. One or two more I give you for good luck, but if a have a horseman fewer than sixty, never love me more.”

Now was the afternoon wearing to evening when the Prince La Fireez was come in with all his company, and greetings done, and the tribute safe bestowed, and sleeping room appointed for him and his. And now were all gathered together in the great banquet hall that was built by Gorice XI, when he was first made King, in the southeast corner of the palace; and it far exceeded in greatness and magnificence the old hall where Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha were held in duress. Seven equal walls it had, of dark green jasper, specked with bloody spots. In the midst of one wall was the lofty doorway, and in the walls right and left of this and in those that enclosed the angle opposite the door were great windows placed high, giving light to the banquet hall. In each of the seven angles of the wall a caryatide, cut in the likeness of a three-headed giant from ponderous blocks of black serpentine, bowed beneath the mass of a monstrous crab hewn out of the same stone. The mighty claws of those seven crabs spreading upwards bare up the dome of the roof, that was smooth and covered all over with paintings of battles and hunting scenes and wrastling bouts in dark and smoky colours answerable to the gloomy grandeur of that chamber. On the walls beneath the windows gleamed weapons of war and of the chase, and on the two blind walls were nailed up all orderly the skulls and dead bones of those champions which had wrastled aforetime with King Gorice XI or ever he appointed in an evil hour to wrastle with Goldry Bluszco. Across the innermost angle facing the door was a long table and a carven bench behind it, and from the two ends of that table, set square with it, two other tables yet longer and benches by them on the sides next the wall stretched to within a short space of the door. Midmost of the table to the right of the door was a high seat of old cypress wood, great and fair, with cushions of black velvet broidered with gold, and facing it at the opposite table another high seat, smaller, and the cushions of it sewn with silver. In the space betwixt the tables five iron braziers, massive and footed with claws like an eagle’s, stood in a row, and behind the benches on either side were nine great stands for flamboys to light the hall by night, and seven behind the cross bench, set at equal distances and even with the walls.

===Chinese===

到下午特近日暮时，拉·菲里兹亲王一行人等进了城；见礼已毕，贡品入库，也给他和他的一行人安排了寝室。众人齐聚在大宴厅——那是戈里斯十一世初次登基时建的，在宫殿东南角；无论宏丽都远远超过囚禁朱斯大人和布兰多赫·达哈大人的老厅。厅堂七面墙等长，都是墨绿碧玉，斑点如血。正中一面墙开高门；门左右两墙及门对角的两墙上，高处开大窗，给宴厅采光。厅的七个墙角，各立一尊女像柱——用整块沉重的黑蛇纹岩雕成三头巨人之形——在一头同石凿成的巨蟹之下屈身负重。那七只巨蟹的大螯向上张开，托住穹顶；顶面平滑，满绘战役、狩猎和角力之图，用色幽暗如烟，正配那厅堂阴沉的壮丽。窗下的墙上挂着兵器猎具，两面临墙上整整齐齐钉着昔年与戈里斯十一世角力过的各位豪杰的头骨枯骨——直到他那个凶时辰择定与戈尔德里·布卢斯科角力为止。正对门的内角横一张长桌，桌后一条雕花长凳；从长桌两端各引出一张更长的条桌，与主桌成直角，两侧靠墙各配长凳，一直延伸到离门不远的地方。门右条桌正中，设一张柏木高椅，宽大华美，铺着金线绣的黑天鹅绒坐垫；对面条桌上对着它另设一张较小的高椅，坐垫缝银。两桌之间的空地里，五只铁火盆一字排开，厚重墩实，盆足作鹰爪形；两侧长凳后各立九座大火把架，供夜间照厅，横凳后还有七座，间距相等，与墙齐平。

The floor was paved with steatite, white and creamy, with veins of rich brown and black and purple and splashes of scarlet. The tables resting on great trestles were massy slabs of a dusky polished stone, powdered with sparks of gold as small as atoms.

The women sat on the cross-bench, and midmost of them the Lady Prezmyra, who outwent the rest in beauty and queenliness as Venus the lesser planets of the night. Zenambria, wife to Duke Corsus, sat on her left, and on her right Sriva, daughter to Corsus, strangely fair for such a father. On the upper bench, to the right of the door, the lords of Witchland sat above and below the King’s high seat, clad in holiday attire, and they of Pixyland had place over against them on the lower bench. The high seat on the lower bench was set apart for La Fireez. Great plates and dishes of gold and silver and painted porcelain were set in order on the tables, laden with delicacies. Harps and bagpipes struck up a barbaric music, and the guests rose to their feet, as the shining doors swung open and Gorice the King followed by the Prince his guest entered that hall.

Like a black eagle surveying earth from some high mountain the King passed by in his majesty. His byrnie was of black chain mail, its collar, sleeves, and skirt edged with plates of dull gold set with hyacinths and black opals. His hose were black, cross-gartered with bands of sealskin trimmed with diamonds. On his left thumb was his great signet ring fashioned in gold in the semblance of the worm Ouroboros that eateth his own tail: the bezel of the ring the head of the worm, made of a peach-coloured ruby of the bigness of a sparrow’s egg. His cloak was woven of the skins of black cobras stitched together with gold wire, its lining of black silk sprinkled with dust of gold. The iron crown of Witchland weighed on his brow, the claws of the crab erect like horns; and the sheen of its jewels was many-coloured like the rays of Sirius on a clear night of frost and wind at Yuletide.

===Chinese===

地面铺着皂石，白润如脂，纹理是浓棕、黑、紫各色，间有猩红斑痕。搁在大支架上的桌面，是一块块暗色磨光的厚重石板，上面金屑细如原子，星星点点。

女眷们坐在横长凳上，居中是普雷兹米拉夫人；论美貌与王后气度，她压倒全场女眷，如维纳斯压倒诸小行星。科苏斯公爵之妻泽南布丽亚（Zenambria）坐在她左手，右手是科苏斯之女丝莉瓦（Sriva）——那样的父亲竟生得出这样的美人，真是奇事。门右的高凳上，巫国众勋贵分坐在王的高椅上下，个个盛装；精灵国人坐在对面低凳上。低凳的高椅留给拉·菲里兹。金、银和彩瓷的大盘大碟在桌上排开，满盛佳肴。竖琴和风笛奏起粗犷的乐声；宾客们纷纷起身——锃亮的大门开启，戈里斯王领着亲王贵宾步入大厅。

王以其威仪鱼贯穿行而过，如一头黑鹰自高山之巅俯瞰大地。他的锁子甲是黑铁环链，领、袖、下摆都镶着乌金甲片，嵌风信子石和黑蛋白石。他的裤袜是黑色的，十字绑腿，绑带是饰钻的海豹皮。左手拇指上是他的大图章戒指，金铸衔尾蛇之形——那吞吃自己尾巴的蛇：戒面就是蛇头，用一枚桃色红宝石琢成，大如雀卵。他的斗篷用黑眼镜蛇的皮缀成，金线缝缀，里子是黑丝，洒着金屑。巫国的铁冠压在他眉上，蟹螯竖起如双角；冠上宝石的光泽五彩变幻，如隆冬风夜清空中的天狼星光。

===Original===

The Prince La Fireez went in a mantle of black sendaline sprinkled everywhere with spangles of gold, and the tunic beneath it of rich figured silk dyed deep purple of the Pasque flower. From the golden circlet on his head two wings sprung aloft exquisitely fashioned in plates of beaten copper veneered with jewels and enamels and plated with precious metals to the semblance of the wings of the oleander hawk-moth. He was something below the common height, but stout and strong and sturdily knit, with red crisp curly hair, broad-faced and ruddy, clean-shaved, with high wide-nostrilled nose and bushy red heavy eyebrows, whence his eyes, most like his lady sister’s, sea-green and fiery, shot glances like a lion’s.

When the King was come into his high seat, with Corund and Corinius on his left and right in honour of their great deeds of arms, and La Fireez facing him in the high seat on the lower bench, the thralls made haste to set forth dishes of pickled grigs and oysters in the shell, and whilks, snails, and cockles fried in olive oil and swimming in red and white hippocras. And the feasters delayed not to fall to on these dainties, while the cupbearer bore round a mighty bowl of beaten gold filled with sparkling wine the hue of the yellow sapphire, and furnished with six golden ladles resting their handles in six half-moon shaped nicks in the rim of that great bowl. Each guest when the bowl was brought to him must brim his goblet with the ladle, and drink unto the glory of Witchland and the rulers thereof.

Somewhat greenly looked Corinius on the Prince, and whispering Heming, Corund’s son, in the ear, who sat next him, he said, “True it is that La Fireez is the showiest of men in all that belongeth to gear and costly array. Mark with what ridiculous excess he affecteth Demonland in the great store of jewels he flaunteth, and with what an apish insolence he sitteth at the board. Yet this lobcock liveth only by our sufferance, and I see a hath not forgot to bring with him to Witchland the price of our hand withheld from twisting of his neck.”

===Chinese===

拉·菲里兹亲王披一件黑闪色绸斗篷，满缀金色亮片；里面的紧身衣是华贵的提花丝织，染成白头翁花那样的深紫。他头上的金环两侧，高高挺出一对翅膀，用镶宝石珐琅、包贵重金属的紫铜薄片精工打成夹竹桃天蛾翅之形。他比常人略矮，却壮实强健，筋骨结实；一头火红卷发，宽脸红润，脸剃得干净，鼻梁高阔，浓密火红的重眉下，一双极像他姐妹的眼睛——海绿色带火光——目光如狮。

王升了高座，科伦德与科里尼厄斯以殊勋侍立左右；拉·菲里兹坐在对面低凳的高椅上。奴仆们赶紧端上腾渍的小鱼、带壳牡蛎，还有油燅的油螺、蜗牛和海扇贝，泡在红白两种希波克拉斯酒里。宾客们立刻大啖这些美味；司酒捧着一只打制的黄金巨碗巡行，碗中盛满起泡的酒，色如黄蓝宝石，碗沿六个半月形凹口上架着六只金勺。巨碗捧到每位客人面前，各人须用勺把酒杯斟满，为巫国及其君主的荣光而饮。

科里尼厄斯带着几分青眼看待亲王，凑到坐在旁边的科伦德之子赫明（Heming）耳边说：「拉·菲里兹确是天下最炫的人，凡关行头和排场的事。看他那一大堆炫耀的珠宝，可笑地学魔国的样学到了何等过火的地步；再看他坐在席上那副猴似的倡傲相。可这条傻大个儿活着全凭我们容让；我看他倒没忘记给巫国带来买命钱——买下我们那只没去拧断他脖子的手。」

===Original===

Now were borne round dishes of carp, pilchards, and lobsters, and thereafter store enow of meats: a fat kid roasted whole and garnished with peas on a spacious silver charger, kid pasties, plates of neats’ tongues and sweetbreads, sucking rabbits in jellies, hedgehogs baked in their skins, hogs’ haslets, carbonadoes, chitterlings, and dormouse pies. These and other luscious meats were borne round continually by thralls who moved silent on bare feet; and merry waxed the talk as the edge of hunger became blunted a little, and the cockles of men’s hearts were warmed with wine.

“What news in Witchland?” asked La Fireez.

“I have heard nought newer,” said the King, “than the slaying of Gaslark.” And the King recounted the battle in the night, setting forth as in a frank and open honesty every particular of numbers, times, and comings and goings; save that none might have guessed from his tale that any of Demonland had part or interest in that battle.

La Fireez said, “Strange it is that he should so attack you. An enemy might smell some cause behind it.”

“Our greatness,” said Corinius, looking haughtily at him, “is a lamp whereat other moths than he have been burnt. I count it no strange matter at all.”

Prezmyra said, “Strange indeed, were it any but Gaslark. But sure with him no wild sudden fancy were too light but it should chariot him like thistledown to storm heaven itself.”

“A bubble of the air, madam: all fine colours without and empty wind within. I have known other such,” said Corinius, still resting his gaze with studied insolence on the Prince.

Prezmyra’s eye danced. “O my Lord Corinius,” said she, “change first thine own fashion, I pray thee, ere thou convince gay attire of inward folly, lest beholding thee we misdoubt thy precept﻿—or thy wisdom.”

===Chinese===

接着端上来鲤鱼、沙丁鱼和龙虾，然后是够多的肉食：整只烤肥羔羊配豌豆，装在阔大的银盘里；羔羊馅饼、牛舌牛杂拼盘、果冻乳兔、连皮燅的猬子、猪杂、炭烤肉、猪肠，还有睡鼠派。这些和别的肥甘美味由赤脚无声走动的奴仆川流不息地端上来；饥饿的锋芒稍钝，酒暖了众人的心窝，谈话热闹起来。

「巫国有什么新闻？」拉·菲里兹问。

「我听到的最新消息，」王说，「就是加斯拉克被杀。」王讲述了夜里的战事，以一种坦率诚实的姿态，把人数、时刻、往来调动一一摆出；只是任谁也听不出，魔国人在那场战斗里有过任何参与或干系。

拉·菲里兹说：「他竟这样来攻打你们，真是奇怪。敌手或许能嗅出背后有些缘由。」

「我们的伟大，」科里尼厄斯傲然望着他说，「是一盏灯，在他之前已有别的飞蛾扑过火。我一点也不觉得奇怪。」

普雷兹米拉说：「若是别人自然奇怪，可他是加斯拉克。对他来说，再狂再突然的念头都不嫌轻，都能像蓟花冠毛一样载着他直捣天宫。」

「空气里的一个泡儿，夫人：外头五颜六色，里头一场空风。这样的人我见得多啦。」科里尼厄斯说，目光依旧刻意倡傲地盯着亲王。

普雷兹米拉的眼光闪动起来。「科里尼厄斯大人哪，」她说，「你要想叫人相信华丽衣着等于内心愚毝，还是先改了你自己的行头吧，免得大家看着你，反倒怀疑你的教条——或者你的智慧。」

===Original===

Corinius drank his cup to the drains and laughed. Somewhat reddened was his insolent handsome face about the cheeks and shaven jowl, for surely was none in that hall more richly apparelled than he. His ample chest was cased in a jerkin of untanned buckskin plated with silver scales, and he wore a collar of gold that was rough with smaragds and a long cloak of sky-blue silk brocade lined with cloth of silver. On his left wrist was a mighty ring of gold, and on his head a wreath of black bryony and sleeping nightshade. Gro whispered Corund in the ear, “He bibbeth it down apace, and the hour is yet early. This presageth trouble, since ever with him indiscretion treadeth hard on the heels of surliness as he waxeth drunken.”

Corund grunted assent, saying aloud, “To all peaks of fame might Gaslark have climbed, but for this same rashness. Nought more pitiful hath been heard to tell of than his great sending into Impland, ten years ago, when, on a sudden conceit that a should lay all Impland under him and become the greatest king in all the world, he hired Zeldornius and Helteranius and Jalcanaius Fostus﻿—”

“The three most notable captains found on earth,” said La Fireez.

“Nothing is more true,” said Corund. “These he hired, and brought ’em ships and soldiers and horses and such a clutter of engines of war as hath not been seen these hundred years, and sent ’em﻿—whither? To the rich and pleasant lands of Beshtria? No. To Demonland? Not a whit. To this Witchland, where with a twentieth part the power a hath now risked all and suffered death and doom? No! but to yonder hell-besmitten wilderness of Upper Impland, treeless, waterless, not a soul to pay him tribute had he laid it under him save wandering bands of savage Imps, with more bugs on their bodies than pence in their purses, I warrant you. Or was he minded to be king among the divels of the air, ghosts, and hob-thrushes that be found in that desert?”

“Without controversy there be seventeen several sorts of divels on the Moruna,” said Corsus, very loud and sudden, so that all turned to look on him; “fiery divels, divels of the air, terrestrial divels, as you may say, and watery divels, and subterranean divels. Without controversy there be seven seen sorts, seventeen several sorts of hob-thrushes, and several sorts of divels, and if the humour took me I could name them all by rote.”

科里尼厄斯把杯中酒一饮而尽，哈哈大笑。他那张倡傲的俊脸，两颊和剃光的下巴都有些泛红了——这厅里确实没有谁比他穿得更华贵。他宽阔的胸膛裹着未鞮鹿皮镶银鳞片的紧身衣，戴着缀满祖母绿的粗金项圈，外面一袭天青色丝锦长斗篷，衬银线呢。他左腕上套一只粗大的金环，头上戴黑泻根和沉睡的龙葵编成的花环。格罗悄声对科伦德说：「他灌得急，天还早呢。这是要出事的兆头：他一醉，无礼总是紧跟倡慢的脚后跟。」

科伦德哼了一声算是同意，高声说：「加斯拉克要不是这股子狂性，天下名声的顶峰哪个爬不上去。他的事迹里再没有比十年前大举进军妖国（Impland）更可悲的了：他忽发奇想，要把整个妖国踩在脚下，做全天下最伟大的君王，于是雇了泽尔多尼厄斯（Zeldornius）、赫尔特拉尼厄斯（Helteranius）和贾尔卡奈厄斯·福斯图斯（Jalcanaius Fostus）——」

「普天之下最著名的三员大将。」拉·菲里兹说。

「一点不错，」科伦德说。「他雇了他们，给他们船只、兵员、马匹，还有百年未见的一大批战争器械，然后把他们送去——送去哪里？去富饶膏腴的贝什特里亚（Beshtria）？不。去魔国？一点也不。去这个巫国——拿他现在兵力的二十分之一他敢来冒险送死的地方？不！而是去妖国上省那片鬼哭神愁的荒原：没树，没水，就算他拿下了它，也没一个魂灵给他上贡，只有游荡的野妖人，身上的臭虫比钱袋里的铜板还多，我敢担保。再不然，他是想去做那荒原上空中群魔、幽灵和家宅小妖的王？」

「毫无疑问，莫鲁纳荒原上有十七种不同的魔鬼，」科苏斯突然扯着大嗓门说，众人都转头看他；「火魔、风魔、地魔——你可以这么说——还有水魔、地下魔。毫无疑问，有七种可见的魔、十七种不同的家宅小妖、若干种魔鬼；我要是高兴，能一口气把它们全数出来。」

Wondrous solemn was the heavy face of Corsus, his eyes, baggy underneath and somewhat bloodshed, his pendulous cheeks, thick blubber underlip, and bristly gray moustachios and whiskers. He had eaten, mainly to provoke thirst, pickled olives, capers, salted almonds, anchovies, fumadoes, and pilchards fried with mustard, and now awaited the salt chine of beef to be a pillow and a resting place for new potations.

The Lady Zenambria asked, “Knoweth any for certain what fate befell Jalcanaius and Helteranius and Zeldornius and their armies?”

“Heard I not,” said Prezmyra, “that they were led by Will-o’-the-Wisps to the regions Hyperborean, and there made kings?”

“Told thee by the madge-howlet, I fear me, sister,” said La Fireez. “Whenas I fared through Impland the More, six years ago, there was many a wild tale told me hereof, but nought within credit.”

Now was the chine served in amid shallots on a great dish of gold, borne by four serving men, so weighty was the dish and its burden. Some light there glowed in the dull eye of Corsus to see it come, and Corund rose up with brimming goblet, and the Witches cried, “The song of the chine, O Corund!” Great as a neat stood Corund in his russet velvet kirtle, girt about with a broad belt of crocodile hide edged with gold. From his shoulders hung a cloak of wolf’s skin with the hair inside, the outside tanned and diapered with purple silk. Daylight was nigh gone, and through a haze of savours rising from the feast the flamboys shone on his bald head set about with thick grizzled curls, and on his keen gray eyes, and his long and bushy beard. He cried, “Give me a rouse, my lords! and if any fail to bear me out in the refrain, I’ll ne’er love him more.” And he sang this song of the chine in a voice like the sounding of a gong; and all they roared in the refrain till the piled dishes on the service tables rang:

“Bring out the Old Chyne, the Cold Chyne to me,

And how Ile charge him come and see,

Brawn tusked, Brawn well sowst and fine,

With a precious cup of Muscadine:

*How shall I sing, how shall I look,*

*In honour of the Master-Cook?*

The Pig shall turn round and answer me,

Canst thou spare me a shoulder? a wy, a wy.

The Duck, Goose, and Capon, good fellows all three,

Shall dance thee an antick, so shall the Turkey:

But O! the Cold Chyne, the Cold Chyne for me:

*How shall I sing, how shall I look,*

泽南布丽亚夫人问：「有谁知道贾尔卡奈厄斯、赫尔特拉尼厄斯和泽尔多尼厄斯他们那几路人马的下落么？」

「我不是听说，」普雷兹米拉说，「他们被鬼火引到了极北之邦，在那里封了王么？」

「只怕是夜猫子告诉你的，姐，」拉·菲里兹说。六年前我走大妖国时，听过许多这方面的胡话，没一句可信。」

这时腌脊肉上来了，盛在金大盘里垫着小葱，四个仆人抬着——盘和肉沉得很。科苏斯呆滞的眼睛见它上来，竟有了几分光。科伦德起身，杯中斟满，巫国众人喊道：「脊肉之歌，科伦德！」科伦德穿着栗色天鹅绒短袍立在席前，高大如牛，腰束一条宽宽的鳄鱼皮腰带，镶着金边。肩上一领狼皮斗篷，毛朝里，外皮鞣过，绣着紫色丝线菱纹。天光将尽，透过筵席上升腾的香雾，火把照在他那秃顶上——四周一圈浓密的灰白鬈发——照在他犀利的灰眼睛和长而蓬乱的大胡子上。他喊：「诸位，给我喝个彩！谁要是在副歌上不替我撑住，我从此不再疼他。」于是他用锣一般的声音唱起这支脊肉歌；众人轰然应和副歌，震得桌上叠着的盘碟铮铮作响：

瞧我怎么向它发起冲锋：

腌好的公猪獠牙长，腌猪一身好肉香，

*我该怎样唱，该怎样看，*

猪会转过身来答我话：

鸭、雁和阔鸡，三位好兄弟，

可是啊！我要的是冷脊肉，冷脊肉：

*我该怎样唱，该怎样看，*

*In honour of the Master-Cook?*

When the chine was carved and the cups replenished, the King issued command saying, “Call hither my dwarf, and let him act his antick gestures before us.”

Therewith came the dwarf into the hall, mopping and mowing, clad in a sleeveless jerkin of striped yellow and red mockado. And his long and nerveless tail dragged on the floor behind him.

“Somewhat fulsome is this dwarf,” said La Fireez.

“Speak within door, Prince,” said Corinius. “Know’st not his quality? A hath been envoy extraordinary from King Gorice XI of memory ever glorious unto Lord Juss in Galing and the lords of Demonland. And ’twas the greatest courtesy we could study to do them, to send ’em this looby for our ambassador.”

The dwarf practised before them to the great content of the lords of Witchland and their guests, save for his japing upon Corinius and the Prince, calling them two peacocks, so like in their bright plumage that none might tell either from other; which somewhat galled them both.

And now was the King’s heart waxen glad with wine, and he pledged Gro, saying, “Be merry, Gro, and doubt not that I will fulfil my word I spake unto thee, and make thee king in Zajë Zaculo.”

“Lord, I am yours forever,” answered Gro. “But methinks I am little fitted to be a king. Methinks I was ever a better steward of other men’s fortunes than of mine own.”

Whereat the Duke Corsus, that was sprawled on the table well nigh asleep, cried out in a great voice but husky withal, “A brace of divels broil me if thou sayst not sooth! If thine own fortunes come off but bluely, care not a rush. Give me some wine, a full weeping goblet. Ha! Ha! whip it away! Ha! Ha! Witchland! When wear you the crown of Demonland, O King?”

“How now, Corsus,” said the King, “art thou drunk?”

But La Fireez said, “Ye sware peace with the Demons in the Foliot Isles, and by mighty oaths are ye bound to put by forever your claims of lordship over Demonland. I hoped your quarrels were ended.”

“Why so they are,” said the King.

可是啊！我要的是老脊肉，冷脊肉：

*我该怎样唱，该怎样看，*
