===Original===

On that ninth day of their journey from Salapanta they came through waste lands of stone and living rock, where not so much as an earth-louse stirred with life. Gorges split the earth here and there: rock-walled labyrinths of gloom, unvisited forever by sunbeam or moonbeam, turbulent in their depths with waters that leaped and churned forever, never still and never silent. So was that day’s journey tortuous, turning now up now down along those river banks to find crossing places.

When they were halted at noon by the deepest rift they had yet beheld, there came one hastening to them and fell down by Juss and lay panting face to earth as breathless from long running. And when they raised him up, behold Mivarsh Faz, harnessed in the gear of a black rider of Jalcanaius Fostus and armed with axe and sword. Great was his agitation, and he speechless for lack of breath. They used him kindly, and gave him to drink from a great skin of wine, Zeldornius’s gift, and anon he said, “He hath armed countless hundreds of our folk with weapons taken from Salapanta field. These, led by the devils his sons, with Philpritz cursed of the gods, be gone before to hold all the ways be-east of you. Night and day have I ridden and run to warn you. Himself, with his main strength of devils ultramontane, rideth hot on your tracks.”

They thanked him well, marvelling much that he should be at such pains to advertise them of their danger. “I have eat your salt,” answered he, “and moreover ye are against this naughty wicked baldhead that came over the mountains to oppress us. Therefore I would do you good. But I can little. For I am poor, that was rich in land and fee. And I am alone, that had formerly five hundred spearmen lodging in my halls to do my pleasure.”

“There’s need to do quickly that we do,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “How great start of him hadst thou?”

“He must be upon you in an hour or twain,” said Mivarsh, and fell a-weeping.

“To cope him in the open,” said Juss, “were great glory, and our certain death.”

===Chinese===

离开萨拉潘塔的第九天，他们穿过石头和山岩的荒地，那里连一只土虱都不见动一动。峡谷四处裂开大地：岩壁夹峙的幽暗迷宫，日辉月影永世不到，谷底的湍流永远翻腾搅卷，永不停，永不静。那一天的行程便曲曲折折，沿河岸忽上忽下地找渡口。

正午，他们停在迄今所见最深的裂谷边，有一人急奔而来，倒在朱斯身边，脸伏在地上喘个不停，像跑了长路的人。扶起来一看，竟是米瓦尔什·法兹：穿着贾尔卡奈厄斯·福斯图斯（Jalcanaius Fostus）黑骑士的甲胄，带斧和剑。他激动万分，气得说不出话。他们好意待他，拿泽尔多尼厄斯（Zeldornius）所赠的一大皮囊酒给他喝；缓过来后他说：「他用萨拉潘塔战场上缴的兵器武装了我们成百上千的族人，由他那群魔鬼儿子率领，加上那个遭神咒的菲尔普里茨，先一步去封锁你们以东的所有道路。我日夜骑马又跑路，赶来警告你们。他本人，带着他山外来的魔鬼主力，正紧紧追着你们的踪迹。」

他们好好地谢了他，很惊论他竟肯这般辛劳来报信。「我吃过你们的盐，」他答，「再说，你们反对的是那个翻山来压迫我们的秃头恶棍。所以我愿对你们好。可我能力有限。因为我穷了——从前我有的是土地采邑。我孤身一人——从前我厅堂里住着五百矛兵，听我使唤。」

「我们的事得赶紧办了。」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「你比他先行多远？」

「他至多一两个钟头就到你们。」米瓦尔什说完，哭了起来。

「在开阔地同他对垒，」朱斯说，「是莫大的荣耀，也是必死无疑。」

===Original===

“Give me to think, but a minute’s while,” said Brandoch Daha. And while they busked them he walked musing by the lip of that ravine, switching pebbles over the edge with his sword. Then he said, “This is without doubt that stream Athrashah spoken of by Gro. O Mivarsh, runneth not this flood of Athrashah south to the salt lakes of Ogo Morveo, and was there not thereabout a hold named Eshgrar Ogo?”

Mivarsh answered, “This is so. But never heard I of any so witless as go thither. Here where we stand is the land fearsome enough; but Eshgrar Ogo standeth at the very edge of the Moruna. No man hath harboured there these hundred years.”

“Standeth it yet?” said Brandoch Daha.

“For all I wot of,” answered Mivarsh.

“Is it strong?” he asked.

“In old times it was thought no place stronger,” answered Mivarsh. “But ye were as well die here by the hand of the devils ultramontane, as there be torn in pieces by bad spirits.”

Brandoch Daha turned him about to Juss. “It is resolved?” said he. Juss answered, “Yea;” and forthwith they started at a great pace south along the river.

“Methought you should have been gotten clean away ere this,” said Mivarsh as they went. “This is but nine or ten days’ journey, and ’tis now the sixteenth day since ye did leave me on Salapanta Hills.”

Brandoch Daha laughed. “Sixteenth!” said he. “Thou’lt be rich, Mivarsh, if thou reckon gold pieces o’ this fashion thou dost days. This is but our ninth day’s journey.”

But Mivarsh stood stoutly to it, saying that was the seventh day after their departure when Corund first came to Salapanta, “And I fleeing now nine days before his face chanced on your tracks, and now out of all expectation on you.” Nor for all their mocking would he be turned from this. And when, as they still pressed through the desert southward, the sun declined and set in a clear sky, behold the moon a little past her full: and Juss saw that she was seven days older than on that night she was when they came to Ishnain Nemartra. So he showed this wonder to Brandoch Daha and Spitfire, and much they marvelled.

“You are much to thank me,” said Brandoch Daha, “that I kept you not a full year awaiting of me. Beshrew me, but that seven days’ space seemed to me but an hour!”

“Likely enow, to thee,” said Spitfire somewhat greenly. “But all we slept the week out on the cold stones, and I am half lamed yet with the ache on’t.”

===Chinese===

「给我一分钟想想。」布兰多赫·达哈说。趁众人整装的工夫，他沿着裂谷的唇沿蹰独行，用剑尖把碎石一块块挑下崖去。然后他说：「这无疑就是格罗（Gro）说过的那条阿斯拉沙（Athrashah）河。米瓦尔什，这条阿斯拉沙洪流不是向南流入奥戈·莫尔维奥（Ogo Morveo）的盐湖么？那一带不是有座要塞叫埃什格拉·奥戈（Eshgrar Ogo）么？」

米瓦尔什答：「是这样。可我从没听说有谁蠢到要去那里。咱们站的这地方已经够吓人了；埃什格拉·奥戈却立在莫鲁纳的边上。一百年没人敢在那儿安身了。」

「它还立着么？」布兰多赫·达哈说。

「就我所知还立着。」米瓦尔什答。

「它坚固么？」他问。

「古时候它被认为是最坚固的地方。」米瓦尔什答。「可你们与其在那里被恶灵撕成碎片，还不如就在这里死在山外魔鬼的手里。」

布兰多赫·达哈转向朱斯。「就这么定了？」他说。朱斯答：「定了；」于是他们立刻沿着河向南疾行。

「我原以为你们早就走远了。」米瓦尔什边走边说。「这段路不过九天十天的行程，可你们离开我在萨拉潘塔山上，今天已是第十六天了。」

布兰多赫·达哈大笑。「第十六天！」他说。「米瓦尔什，你要是数金币也这么个数法，可就发财了。这才是我们行程的第九天。」

可米瓦尔什坚持己见，说科伦德到萨拉潘塔那天，才是他们启程后的第七天，「我如今在他前面逃了九天，碰巧撞见你们的踪迹，又万想不到撞见了你们本人。」任他们怎么笑，他也不改口。当他们还在荒漠里向南赶路时，太阳在晴空里西沉了；看哪，月亮已过盈圆：朱斯看出，它比他们到伊斯内恩·内马尔特拉那晚的月亮老了七天。他把这件奇事指给布兰多赫·达哈和斯皮特法厄看，两人都大为惊异。

「你们真该好好谢我，」布兰多赫·达哈说，「幸亏我没让你们等上整整一年。老天爷，那七天在我竟像一个钟头！」

「对你，恐怕是。」斯皮特法厄有点酸酸地说。「可我们全体在冷石头上睡了整整一礼拜，我至今还半边身子酸得不能动呢。」

===Original===

“Nay,” said Juss, laughing; “I will not have thee blame him.”

The moon was high when they came to the salt lakes that lay one a little above the other in rocky basins. Their waters were like rough silver, and the harsh face of the wilderness was black and silver in the moonlight; and it was as a country of dead bones, blind and sterile beneath the moon. Betwixt the lakes a rib of rock rose monstrous to an eminence crag-begirt on every side, with dark walls ringing it round above the cliffs. Thither they hastened, and as they climbed and stumbled among the crags a she-owl squeaked on the battlements and took wing ghostlike above their heads. The teeth of Mivarsh Faz chattered, but right glad were the Demons as they won up the rocks and entered at last into that deserted burg. Without, the night was still; but fires were burning in the desert eastward, and others as they watched were kindled in the west, and soon was the circle joined of twinkling points of red round about Eshgrar Ogo and the lakes.

Juss said, “By an hour have we forestalled them. And behold how he ringeth us about as men ring a scorpion in flame.”

So they made all sure, and set the guard, and slept until past dawn. But Mivarsh slept not, for terror of hob-thrushes from the Moruna.

===Chinese===

「不，」朱斯笑道；「我不许你们怪他。」

他们到达盐湖时，月亮已高。湖一层比一层略高，嵌在岩石的盆地里。湖水如粗砺的白银，荒野粗砺的脸在月光下黑白分明，像一片死骨之国，在月下盲然而荒瘠。两湖之间，一道岩脊隆起，高耸成四面峭壁环围的孤峰，峭壁之上又环着一圈黑墙。他们直奔那里；在乱岩间攀爬趑趄时，一只母鸮在雉埞上尖叫一声，鬼影似的掠过他们头顶飞起。米瓦尔什·法兹的牙齿捉对儿打颤，魔族（Demonland）众人却欢欢喜喜地登上了岩顶，终于进了那座荒堡。外面，夜静悄悄；可东面荒漠里已燃起火，他们观看间，西面又起了几处，不多时，闪烁的红点便围成了一圈，把埃什格拉·奥戈和盐湖团团围住。

朱斯说：「我们抢在他们前面一个钟头。看哪，他这样围住我们，就像人用火圈困住一只塱子。」

于是他们把一切安顿妥当，设了岗哨，一觉睡过了黎明。只有米瓦尔什睡不着——他怕莫鲁纳来的家宅小妖。

## XI / XI
===Original===

The Burg of Eshgrar Ogo

Of the Lord Corund’s besieging of the burg above the lakes of Ogo Morveo, and what befell there betwixt him and the demons; wherein is also an example how the subtle of heart standeth at whiles in great danger of his death.

When the Lord Corund knew of a surety that he held them of Demonland shut up in Eshgrar Ogo, he let dight supper in his tent, and made a surfeit of venison pasties and heath-cocks and lobsters from the lakes. Therewith he drank nigh a skinful of sweet dark Thramnian wine, in such sort that an hour before midnight, becoming speechless, he was holpen by Gro to his couch and slept a great deep sleep till morning.

Gro watched in the tent, his right elbow propped on the table, his cheek resting on his hand, his left hand reaching forward with delicate fingers toying now with the sleek heavy perfumed masses of his beard, now with the goblet whence he sipped ever and anon pale wine of Permio. His thoughts inconstant as insects in a summer garden flitted ever round and round, resting now on the scene before him, the great form of his general wrapt in slumber, now on other scenes sundered by great gulfs of time or weary leagues of perilous ways. So that in one instant he saw in fancy that lady in Carcë welcoming her lord returned in triumph, and him, may be, crowned king of new-vanquished Impland; and in the next, swept from the future to the past, beheld again the great sending-off in Zajë Zaculo, Gaslark in his splendour on the golden stairs saying adieu to those three captains and their matchless armament foredoomed to dogs and crows on Salapanta Hills; and always, like a gloomy background darkening his mind, loomed the yawning void, featureless and vast, beyond the investing circle of Corund’s armies: the blind blasted emptiness of the Moruna.

===Chinese===

埃什格拉·奥戈之堡

记科伦德大人围攻奥戈·莫尔维奥湖畔的城堡，及他与魔族之间所生的事；其中亦是一例：心机深沉者，有时也会大满杀身之祸。

科伦德大人确知自己已把魔国诸人关死在埃什格拉·奥戈之后，便命人在帐中备下晚餐，饕餮了一顿鹿肉馅饼、松鸡和湖里的龙虾，又灌下近一皮囊的特拉姆尼安甜黑酒，结果半夜前一个钟头便说不出话来，由格罗扶上床，一觉沉沉睡到天亮。

格罗在帐中守夜，右肘支在桌上，脸颊倚着手，左手伸在前面，纤细的手指一会儿捻着胡须那油亮浓香的一大把，一会儿捻着酒杯——杯里是佩尔米奥淡酒，他不时啜上一口。他的思绪如夏日花园里的虫豸般无常，绕来绕去：一会儿停在眼前的景象——他的主帅那庞大的身躯沉在睡乡里；一会儿又飞到别的景象上，隔着时间的深壑和艰险路途的漫长里格。这一瞬间，他恍惚看见喀尔刻那位夫人迎接凯旋的夫君，而他，或许，做了新灭妖国的王；下一瞬间，又从未来扫回过去，重见扎伊·扎库洛那盛大的出征——加斯拉克辉煌地立在金阶上，向那三员大将和那支无匹的大军道别，而那支大军命里注定要喂萨拉潘塔山上的狗和乌鸦；而这一切之下，始终像一片阴沉的底色压暗他的心：科伦德大军合围之外那 gaping 的虚空，无形无状而浩瀚——莫鲁纳那盲目荒芜的空旷。

===Original===

With such fancies, melancholy like a great bird settled upon his soul. The lights flickered in their sockets, and for very weariness Gro’s eyelids closed at length over his large liquid eyes; and, too tired to stir from his seat to seek his couch, he sank forward on the table, his head pillowed on his arms. The red glow of the brazier slumbered ever dimmer and dimmer on the slender form and black shining curls of Gro, and on the mighty frame of Corund where he lay with one great spurred booted leg stretched along the couch, and the other flung out sideways resting its heel on the ground.

---

It wanted but two hours of noon when a sunbeam striking through an opening in the hangings of the tent shone upon Corund’s eyelids, and he awoke fresh and brisk as a youth on a hunting morn. He waked Gro, and giving him a clap on the shoulder, “Thou wrongest a fair morn,” he said. “The devil damn me black as buttermilk if it be not great shame in thee; and I, that was born this day six and forty years as the years come about, busy with mine affairs since sunrise.”

Gro yawned and smiled and stretched himself. “O Corund,” he said, “counterfeit a livelier wonder in thine eyes if thou wilt persuade me thou sawest the sunrise. For I think that were as new and unexampled a sight for thee as any I could produce to thee in Impland.”

Corund answered, “Truly I was seldom so uncivil as surprise Madam Aurora in her nightgown. And the thrice or four times I have been forced thereto, taught me it is an hour of crude airs and mists which breed cold dark humours in the body, an hour when the torch of life burns weakest. Within there! bring me my morning draught.”

The boy brought two cups of white wine, and while they drank, “A thin ungracious drink is the wellspring,” said Corund: “a drink for queasy-stomached skipjacks: for sand-levericks, not for men. And like it is the dayspring: an ungrateful sapless hour, an hour for stab-i’-the-backs and cold-blooded betrayers. Ah, give me wine,” he cried, “and noonday vices, and brazen-browed iniquities.”

“Yet there’s many a deed of profit done by owl-light,” said Gro.

===Chinese===

怀着这些幻想，忧郁像一只巨鸟栖上他的魂。灯火在灯盏里摇曳，格罗疲极，大而水灵的眼皮终于合上；他累得连起身到床榻的力气也没有，向前伏在桌上，头枕着双臂睡了。火盆的红光越来越暗，照着格罗纤瘦的身形和黑亮的卷发，照着科伦德庞大的身躯——他一只穿马刺长靴的大腿直伸在榻上，另一条甩在榻边，脚跟搁在地上。

---

离正午还有两个钟头时，一线阳光穿过帐帘的缝隙照在科伦德的眼皮上，他醒了，精神抖擞，像狩猎之晨的少年。他叫醒格罗，在他肩上一拍：「你喜负了一个好早晨。」他说。「见鬼，要是这不怪你那才怪；我呢——今天我满四十六了——日出起就忙我自己的事。」

格罗打着哈欠伸着懒腰笑道：「科伦德哪，你要让我信你看见了日出，眼睛里的惊奇得装得再活一些。我看那景象对你，同我在妖国能变给你看的任何奇景一样，新鲜而无先例。」

科伦德答：「我这辈子很少那么失礼，去撞见黎明女神穿睡袍。被迫撞见过三四回，教我明白了：那是个寒气未退、雾气沉沉的时辰，专在人身子里生寒冷阴湿的体液，是生命之火烧得最弱的时辰。来人！给我拿晨酒来。」

侍童端来两杯白葡萄酒；两人喝着，科伦德说：「井泉水是种寡淡无礼的饮料：给反胃的跳跳佬喝的东西：给沙百灵，不是给人。就像那黎明：一个不领情的、无汁无水的时辰，一个属于背后捅刀和冷血背叛的时辰。啊，给我酒，」他喊，「给我正午的恶行和厚颜无耻的罪衍！」

「可猫头鹰的光下也办成过许多有利可图的事。」格罗说。

===Original===

“Ay,” said Corund: “deeds of darkness: and there, my lord, I’m still thy scholar. Come, let’s be doing.” And taking his helm and weapons, and buckling about him his great wolfskin cloak, for the air was eager and frosty without, he strode forth. Gro wrapped himself in his fur mantle, drew on his lambskin gloves, and followed him.

“If thou wilt take my rede,” said Lord Gro, as they looked on Eshgrar Ogo stark in the barren sunlight, “thou’lt do this honour to Philpritz, which I question not he much desireth, to suffer him and his folk take first knock at this nut. It hath a hard look. Pity it were to waste good Witchland blood in a first assault, when these vile instruments stand ready to our purpose.”

Corund grunted in his beard, and with Gro at his elbow paced in silence through the lines, his keen eyes searching ever the cliffs and walls of Eshgrar Ogo, till in some half-hour’s space he halted again before his tent, having made a complete circuit of the burg. Then he spake: “Put me in yonder fighting-stead, and if it were only but I and fifty able lads to man the walls, yet would I hold it against ten thousand.”

Gro held his peace awhile, and then said, “Thou speakest this in all sadness?”

“In sober sadness,” answered Corund, squaring his shoulders at the burg.

“Then thou’lt not assault it?”

Corund laughed. “Not assault it, quotha! That were a sweet tale ’twixt the boiled and the roast in Carcë: I’d not assault it!”

“Yet consider,” said Gro, taking him by the arm. “So shapeth the matter in my mind: they be few and shut up in a little place, in this far land, out of reach and out of mind of all succour. Were they devils and not men, the multitude of our armies and thine own tried qualities must daunt them. Be the place never so cocksure, doubt not some doubts thereof must poison their security. Therefore before thou risk a repulse which must dispel those doubts use thine advantage. Bid Juss to a parley. Offer him conditions: it skills not what. Bribe them out into the open.”

“A pretty plan,” said Corund. “Thou’lt merit wisdom’s crown if thou canst tell me what conditions we can offer that they would take. And whilst thou riddlest that, remember that though thou and I be masters hereabout, another reigns in Carcë.”

===Chinese===

「那倒是，」科伦德说；「黑暗中的勾当：那方面，大人，我还是你的学生。走，办事去。」他取了盔和兵器，裹上他那领大狼皮斗篷——外面空气凛冽刺骨——大步出门。格罗裹上皮裘，戴上羊皮手套，跟上他。

「你要是肯听我的主意，」格罗勋爵望着荒瘠日光中嶙峋的埃什格拉·奥戈说，「就把这份体面给菲尔普里茨——我毫不怀疑他极想要：让他和他的人先来磕这颗核桃。这核桃看着硬。既然这些贱工具现成可用，何苦头一轮强攻就浪费巫国的好血。」

科伦德在胡子里哼了一声，让格罗跟在肘边，默默穿过各条战线，犀利的眼睛始终搜索着埃什格拉·奥戈的岩壁和城墙；约莫半个钟头，他绕堡一周，又回到自己帐前站住，才开口：「把我放进那边的阵地，哪怕只有我和五十条好汉守墙，我也能挡它一万。」

格罗沉默了一会儿，说：「你这话是当真的？」

「板板正正的当真。」科伦德答，向那城堡挺了挺肩膀。

「那你不打算强攻？」

科伦德笑了。「不攻，亏你说得出！这话传回喀尔刻，够不冷不热的笑话听了：我不攻！」

「可是想想，」格罗挽住他的手臂，「我心里是这样盘算的：他们人少，关在一个小地方，在这远隔之地，一切救援都够不着、想不着。他们就算是魔鬼不是人，我们大军之众、你身经百战之才，也必叫他们胆寒。地方再牢靠，那些疑虑也必然毒害他们的安全感。所以，在冒险吃一个必会驱散他们疑虑的败仗之前，先用手里的优势。召朱斯来会谈。开条件给他们：什么条件都无所谓。把他们诱到开阔地来。」

「好一个妙计，」科伦德说。「你要能说出我们能开出什么他们肯接受的条件，就算你配戴智慧的冠冕。你猜这个谜的时候，记住：你我在这里是当家，可在喀尔刻当家的另有一位。」

===Original===

Lord Gro laughed gently. “Leave jesting,” he said, “O Corund, and never hope to gull me to believe thee such a babe in policy. Shall the King blame us though we sign away Demonland, ay and the wide world besides, to Juss to lure him forth? Unless indeed we were so neglectful of our interest as suffer him, once forth, to elude our clutches.”

“Gro,” said Corund, “I love thee. But hardly canst thou receive things as I receive them that have dealt all my days in great stripes, given and taken in the open field. I sticked not to take part in thy notable treason against these poor snakes of Impland that we trapped in Orpish. All’s fair against such dirt. Besides, great need was upon us then, and hard it is for an empty sack to stand straight. But here is far other matter. All’s won here but the plucking of the apple: it is the very main of my ambition to humble these Demons openly by the terror of my sword: wherefore I will not use upon them cogs and stops and all thy devilish tricks, such as should bring me more of scorn than of glory in the eyes of aftercomers.”

So speaking, he issued command and sent an herald to go forth beneath the battlements with a flag of truce. And the herald cried aloud and said: “From Corund of Witchland unto the lords of Demonland: thus saith the Lord Corund, ‘I hold this burg of Eshgrar Ogo as a nut betwixt the crackers. Come down and speak with me in the batable land before the burg, and I swear to you peace and grith while we parley, and thereto pledge I mine honour as a man of war.’ ”

So when the due ceremonies were performed, the Lord Juss came down from Eshgrar Ogo and with him the lords Spitfire and Brandoch Daha and twenty men to be their bodyguard. Corund went to meet them with his guard about him, and his four sons that fared with him to Impland, Hacmon, namely, and Heming and Viglus and Dormanes: sullen and dark young men, likely of look, of a little less fierceness than their father. Gro, fair to see and slender as a racehorse, went at his side, muffled to the ears in a cloak of ermine; and behind came Philpritz Faz helmed with a winged helm of iron and gold. A gilded corselet had Philpritz, and trousers of panther’s skin, and he came a-slinking at Corund’s heel as the jackal slinks behind the lion.

===Chinese===

格罗勋爵轻轻笑了。「别打趣了，」他说，「科伦德，别指望骗我相信你在权谋上是个娃娃。为了诱朱斯出洞，咱们就是把魔国签送给他——连整个世界一并奉上——王上难道还会怪罪？除非我们不小心到让他一出洞就溜出我们的手心。」

「格罗，」科伦德说，「我爱你。可你很难像我这样接事——我一辈子在开阔战场上大手笔地打，一手交一手接。那天在奥皮什围住妖国那群可怜虫，你那场漂亮叛变，我不是也入了伙吗。对那种脏东西，无所不可。再说那时我们大难当头，空口袋站不直。可现在完全是另一回事。这里万事已定，只欠摘果子：我要公开地、以我剑之威压服这些魔族人——这正是我毕生之志；所以我不会对他们用齿轮和暗栓，用你那些鬼把戏——那只会给后世留下耻笑，不是光荣。」

说着，他下令派一名传令官打着休战旗到城墙下去，高声喊道：「巫国科伦德致魔国众勋贵：科伦德大人如此说——『我视埃什格拉·奥戈这堡为夹在钳子里的核桃。下来，到堡前可争之地与我说话；我向你们立誓，会谈期间和平与安宁，我以军人之名为此作保。』」

于是仪式毕，朱斯大人下埃什格拉·奥戈而来，同来的有斯皮特法厄、布兰多赫·达哈两位大人和二十名卫士。科伦德带着卫队去迎，随行有随他来妖国的四个儿子：哈克蒙、赫明、维格卢斯和多尔马内斯：阴都都的年轻汉子，相貌堂堂，威猛略逊其父。格罗俊美纤瘦如赛马，走在他身边，裹着一件貂皮斗篷直裹到耳朵；后面跟着菲尔普里茨·法兹，戴着铁金双料的飞翼盔。菲尔普里茨穿一件镀金胸甲，豹皮裤，像豺狗溜在狮子脚后一样溜在科伦德脚跟边。

===Original===

When they were met, Juss spake and said, “This would I know first, my Lord Corund, how thou comest hither, and why, and by what right thou disputest with us the ways eastward out of Impland.”

Corund answered, leaning on his spear, “I need not answer thee in this. And yet I will. How came I? I answer thee, over the cold mountain wall of Akra Skabranth. And ’tis a feat hath not his fellow in man’s remembrance until now, with so great a force and in so short a space of time.”

“ ’Tis well enough,” said Juss. “I’ll grant thee thou hast outrun mine expectations of thee.”

“Next thou demandest why,” said Corund. “Suffice it for thee that the King hath had advertisement of your farings into Impland and your designs therein. For to bring these to nought am I come.”

“There was many firkins of wine drunk dry in Carcë,” said Hacmon, “and many a noble person senseless and spewing on the ground ere morn for pure delight, when cursed Goldry was made away. We were little minded these healths should be proved vain at last.”

“Was that ere thou rodest from Permio?” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “The merry god wrought of our side that night, if my memory cheat not.”

“Thou demandest last,” said Corund, “my Lord Juss, by what right I bar your passage eastaway. Know, therefore, that not of mine own self speak I unto you, but as vicar in wide-fronted Impland of our Lord Gorice XII, King of Kings, most glorious and most great. There remaineth no way out for you from this place save into the rigour of mine hands. Therefore let us, according to the nature of great men, agree to honourable conditions. And this is mine offer, O Juss. Yield up this burg of Eshgrar Ogo, and therewith thy sealed word in a writing acknowledging our Lord the King to be King of Demonland and all ye his quiet and obedient subjects, even as we be. And I will swear unto you of my part, and in the name of our Lord the King, and give you hostages thereto, that ye shall depart in peace whither you list with all love and safety.”

===Chinese===

两下相见，朱斯开口说：「科伦德大人，我先想知道这个：你怎么到的这里，为什么来，凭什么权利拦阻我们东出妖国的路。」

科伦德拄着长矛答：「这本不必答你。但我还是答。我怎么来的？答你：翻过阿克拉·斯卡布兰斯冰冷的石墙。带这么大的兵、这么短的时日做到这一步，人所能记的范围内没有第二例。」

「不坏，」朱斯说。「我承认你起出了我对你的预期。」

「其次你问为什么，」科伦德说。「王上已得到你们窜入妖国及图谋的消息，这于你足够了。我来，就是为把这些化为董粉。」

「可咒的戈尔德里被除掉那晚，喀尔刻喝空的酒桶数也数不清，」哈克蒙说，「多少贵人乐得人事不省、吐了一地——我们可不愿这些祝酒到头一场空。」

「那是你从佩尔米奥动身之前的事吧？」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「那晚欢乐之神若没骗我的记性，可是站在我们一边的。」

「你最后问，」科伦德说，「朱斯大人，我凭什么权利拦你们东去。那你就知道：我对你们说话，不是出于我自己，而是作为万王之王、至荣至大的戈里斯十二世陛下在大妖国的全权总督。你们从此地出去的路，只剩一条：落进我的铁手里。所以，让我们以大人物的方式，谈个体面的条件。朱斯啊，这是我的开价：交出埃什格拉·奥戈这座堡，连同你盖印的字据，承认我们的王上为魔国之王、你们全体为他恭顺的臣民，同我们一样。我则担保我这方——并以我们王上的名义，给你们人质——你们可以安宁地、随你们所愿地去任何地方，享尽亲爱与平安。」

The Lord Juss scowled fiercely on him. “O Corund,” he said, “as little as we do understand the senseless wind, so little we understand thy word. Oft enow hath gray silver been in the fire betwixt us and you Witchlanders; for the house of Gorice fared ever like the foul toad, that may not endure to smell the sweet savour of the vine when it flourisheth. So for this time we will abide in this hold, and withstand your most grievous attempts.”

“With free honesty and open heart,” said Corund, “I made thee this offer; which if thou refuse I am not thy lackey to renew it.”

Gro said, “It is writ and sealed, and wanteth but thy sign-manual, my Lord Juss,” and with the word he made sign to Philpritz Faz that went to Lord Juss with a parchment. Juss put the parchment by, saying, “No more: ye are answered,” and he was turning on his heel when Philpritz, louting forward suddenly, gave him a great yerk beneath the ribs with a dagger slipped from his sleeve. But Juss wore a privy coat that turned the dagger. Howbeit with the greatness of that stroke he staggered aback.

Now Spitfire clapped hand to sword, and the other Demons with him, but Juss loudly shouted that they should not be truce-breakers but know first what Corund would do. And Corund said, “Dost hear me, Juss? I had neither hand nor part in this.”

Brandoch Daha drew up his lip and said, “This is nought but what was to be looked for. It is a wonder, O Juss, that thou shouldst hold out to such mucky dogs a hand without a whip in it.”

“Such strokes come home or miss merely,” said Gro softly in Corund’s ear, and he hugged himself beneath his cloak, looking with furtive amusement on the Demons. But Corund with a face red in anger said, “It is thine answer, O Juss?” And when Juss said, “It is our answer, O Corund,” Corund said violently, “Then red war I give you; and this withal to testify our honour.” And he let lay hands on Philpritz Faz and with his own hand hacked the head from his body before the eyes of both their armies. Then in a great voice he said, “As bloodily as I have revenged the honour of Witchland on this Philpritz, so will I revenge it on all of you or ever I draw off mine armies from these lakes of Ogo Morveo.”

===Chinese===

朱斯大人对他狠狠皱眉。「科伦德，」他说，「我们听不懂无意义的的风，也同样听不懂你的话。我们与你们巫人之间，银子在火里炼过不止一遭了；戈里斯家的做派从来像那只肮脏的蟾蜍——葡萄长得正茂时，它受不了那香气。所以这一回，我们就守在这堡里，抵挡你们最凶猛的攻势。」

「我以坦荡的诚意和磊落的心，」科伦德说，「向你开了这个价；你若拒绝，我不是你的跟班，不会重开第二次。」

格罗说：「已写好盖印了，只欠朱斯大人的亲笔。」说着向菲尔普里茨·法兹示意；菲尔普里茨捧着一卷羊皮纸走向朱斯大人。朱斯把羊皮纸拨开，说：「不必了：你们得到了回答。」他转身要走，菲尔普里茨突然一个箭步欺身，袖中滑出七首，向朱斯肋下狠狠一刺。但朱斯里面穿着暗甲，七首滑开了。只是那一下力道太大，他踉跄后退。

斯皮特法厄即刻拔剑，其他魔族人也拔剑；朱斯却大喝一声，不许他们做破坏休战的人，先看科伦德怎么办。科伦德说：「听见没有，朱斯？此事我无份，也没参与。」

布兰多赫·达哈抵起嘴唇说：「这完全在意料之中。奇怪的是，朱斯，你对这种肮脏狗伸出去的手里，居然没藏一条鞭子。」

「这一击要么中要么空，只此而已。」格罗凑在科伦德耳边轻轻说，在斗篷底下抱着自己的胳膊，带着偷来的兴致看魔族人。科伦德却涨红了脸怒道：「这就是你们的回答，朱斯？」朱斯说：「是我们的回答，科伦德。」科伦德厉声道：「那我给你们血红的战争；还有这个，来见证我们的荣誉。」他命人拿下菲尔普里茨·法兹，亲自动手，当着两军的眼，砍下了他的头。然后他厉声说：「我在这个菲尔普里茨身上怎样血腥地为巫国报了仇，也必怎样在你们全体身上报仇，然后才从奥戈·莫尔维奥湖边撤兵。」

===Original===

So the Demons went up into the burg, and Gro and Corund home to their tents. “This was well thought on,” said Gro, “to flaunt the flag of seeming honesty, and with the motion rid us of this fellow that promised ever to grow thorns to make uneasy our seat in Impland.”

Corund answered him not a word.

In that same hour Corund marshalled his folk and assaulted Eshgrar Ogo, placing those of Impland in the van. They prospered not at all. Many a score lay slain without the walls that night; and the obscene beasts from the desert feasted on their bodies by the light of the moon.

---

Next morning the Lord Corund sent an herald and bade the Demons again to a parley. And now he spake only to Brandoch Daha, bidding him deliver up those brethren Juss and Spitfire, “And if thou wilt yield them to my pleasure, then shalt thou and all thy people else depart in peace without conditions.”

“An offer indeed,” said Lord Brandoch Daha; “if it be not in mockery. Say it loud, that my folk may hear.”

Corund did so, and the Demons heard it from the walls of the burg.

Lord Brandoch Daha stood somewhat apart from Juss and Spitfire and their guard. “Libel it me out,” he said. “For good as I now must deem thy word, thine hand and seal must I have to show my followers ere they consent with me in such a thing.”

“Write thou,” said Corund to Gro. “To write my name is all my scholarship.” And Gro took forth his ink-horn and wrote in a great fair hand this offer on a parchment. “The most fearfullest oaths thou knowest,” said Corund; and Gro wrote them, whispering, “He mocketh us only.” But Corund said, “No matter: ’tis a chance worth our chancing,” and slowly and with labour signed his name to the writing, and gave it to Lord Brandoch Daha.

Brandoch Daha read it attentively, and tucked it in his bosom beneath his byrnie. “This,” he said, “shall be a keepsake for me of thee, my Lord Corund. Reminding me,” and here his eyes grew terrible, “so long as there surviveth a soul of you in Witchland, that I am still to teach the world throughly what that man must abide that durst affront me with such an offer.”

Corund answered him, “Thou art a dapper fellow. It is a wonder that thou wilt strut in the tented field with all this womanish gear. Thy shield: how many of these sparkling baubles thinkest thou I’d leave in it were we once come to knocks?”

===Chinese===

魔族众人上了堡，格罗和科伦德回帐。「这一手想得好，」格罗说，「既要亮出诚实的大旗，又顺手除掉了这家伙——他总会长出刺来，搅得我们在妖国的位子不安生。」

科伦德一字不答。

当天那个时辰，科伦德便点齐人马强攻埃什格拉·奥戈，把妖国人摆在头阵。一无所获。当夜，墙外横尸几十具；荒漠里那些污秽的野兽就着月光飨用了他们的尸体。

---

次日晨，科伦德大人再派传令官，又召魔族人会谈。这一回他只对布兰多赫·达哈一人说话，叫他交出朱斯和斯皮特法厄兄弟二人：「你若肯把他们交给我发落，你和其余你的人便可以无条件安宁离开。」

「好一个开价，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说，「若不是拿人开玩笑的话。大点声说，让我的人也听见。」

科伦德照办，堡墙上的魔族人都听见了。

布兰多赫·达哈站得离朱斯、斯皮特法厄和卫士们稍远。「给我立下字据来。」他说。「你这话我现在虽信是好话，可要我的人在这件事上跟我一条心，我得拿出你的亲笔和印鉴给他们看。」

「你写，」科伦德对格罗说。「写自己的名字是我全部的学问。」格罗取出墨角，用一手漂亮的大字把开价写在羊皮纸上。「把你所知最可怕的誓言都写上。」科伦德说；格罗写了，悄声道：「他只是耍我们。」科伦德却说：「无所谓：值得一赔。」于是他吃力地慢慢签上名，把羊皮纸交给布兰多赫·达哈大人。

布兰多赫·达哈仔细读过，把它塞进锁子甲下的怀里。「这个，」他说，「就当是你给我的纪念品吧，科伦德大人。提醒我——」他的眼睛变得吓人，「只要巫国还剩下一个活魂，我就还得教导世人：敢拿这种开价僈我的人，得落个什么下场。」

科伦德答：「你倒是个俊俏人物。真奇怪，你居然敢带着这身娘们儿行头上战场。就说你这面盾：真动起手来，你以为我能在上头留下几颗这种亮晶晶的小玩意儿？」

===Original===

“I’ll tell thee,” answered Lord Brandoch Daha. “For every jewel that hath been beat out of my shield in battle, never yet went I to war that I brought not home an hundredfold to set it fair again, from the spoils I obtained from mine enemies. Now this will I bid thee, O Corund, for thy scornful words: I will bid thee to single combat, here and in this hour. Which if thou deny, then art thou an open and apparent dastard.”

Corund chuckled in his beard, but his brow darkened somewhat. “I pray what age dost thou take me of?” said he. “I bare a sword when thou was yet in swaddling clothes. Behold mine armies, and what advantage I hold upon you. Oh, my sword is enchanted, my lord: it will not out of the scabbard.”

Brandoch Daha smiled disdainfully, and said to Spitfire, “Mark well, I pray thee, this great lord of Witchland. How many true fingers hath a Witch on his left hand?”

“As many as on his right,” said Spitfire.

“Good. And how many on both?”

“Two less than a deuce,” said Spitfire; “for they be false fazarts to the fingers’ ends.”

“Very well answered,” said Lord Brandoch Daha.

“You’re pleasant,” Corund said. “But your fusty jibes move me not a whit. It were a simple part indeed to take thine offer when all wise counsels bid me use my power and crush you.”

“Thou’dst kill me soon with thy mouth,” said Brandoch Daha. “In sum, thou art a brave man when it comes to roaring and swearing: a big bubber of wine, as men say to drink drunk is an ordinary matter with thee every day in the week; but I fear thou durst not fight.”

“Doth not thy nose swell at that?” said Spitfire.

But Corund shrugged his shoulders. “A footra for your baits!” he answered. “I am scarce bounden to do such a kindness to you of Demonland as lay down mine advantage and fight alone, against a sworder. Your old foxes are seldom taken in springes.”

“I thought so,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “Surely the frog will have hair sooner than any of you Witchlanders shall dare to stand me.”

So ended the second parley before Eshgrar Ogo. The same day Corund essayed again to storm the hold, and grievous was the battle and hard put to it were they of Demonland to hold the walls. Yet in the end were Corund’s men thrown back with great slaughter. And night fell, and they returned to their tents.

「我告诉你，」布兰多赫·达哈大人答。「我的盾上每有一颗宝石在战斗中被砸掉，我出征归来，总能从敌人的辎重里带回百倍来补镶一新。现在，科伦德，为你这番轻蔑的话，我向你要求一件事：我邀你单挑，就在此地，就在此时。你若拒绝，你就是公开而明白的懦夫。」

科伦德在胡子里咕了一声笑，眉头却沉了沉。「请问你算我多大年纪？」他说。「你还在襁褓里时，我已经挎剑了。看看我的大军，看看我手里握着你们多大的优势。哦，我的剑是中了魔的，大人：它不肯出鞘。」

布兰多赫·达哈鄙夷地一笑，对斯皮特法厄说：「请你好好看清这位巫国的大人物。巫国人左手上有几根真手指？」

「同右手一样多。」斯皮特法厄说。

「好。两只手一共几根？」

「比两根还少两根，」斯皮特法厄说，「因为他们从指尖到指根全是假货。」

「回答得好极了。」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。

「你们真会说话，」科伦德说，「可这些发霉的嘴皮动不了我一根毛。一切明智的忠告都叫我用手里的实力压碎你们，这时偏接你的挑战，那才真是傻蛋。」

「你的嘴先把我杀死了，」布兰多赫·达哈说。「总而言之：吼叫和赌咒的时候，你是个勇士；酒桶里的大肚汉，人们说，天天喝醉对你不过是家常便饭；可我怕你不敢真打。」

「你鼻子气粗了没有？」斯皮特法厄说。

科伦德却耸耸肩。「你们这些饵，去他的！」他说。「我可没义务给魔国人行这种好：放下我的优势，单枪匹马去斗一个剑客。老狐狸很少落进陷阱里。」

「我料到了，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「青蛙长出毛来，也要比你们巫国人有一个敢站出来挨我快。」

埃什格拉·奥戈前的第二轮会谈就此收场。当天，科伦德又试图强攻此堡，战况惨烈，魔族守墙守得岌岌可危。但到头来，科伦德的人还是被击退，死伤惨重。夜幕降临，他们回帐去了。

===Original===

“Mine invention,” said Gro, when on the next day they took counsel together, “hath yet some contrivance in her purse which shall do us good, if it fall but out to our mind. But I doubt much it will dislike thee.”

“Well, say it out, and I’ll give thee my censure on’t,” said Corund.

Gro spake: “It hath been shown we may not have down this tree by hewing above ground. Let’s dig about the roots. And first give them a seven-night’s space for reckoning up their chances, that they may see morning and evening from the burg thine armies set down to invest them. Then, when their hopes are something sobered by that sight, and want of action hath trained their minds to sad reflection, call them to parley, going straight beneath the wall; and this time shalt thou address thyself only to the common sort, offering them all generous and free conditions thou canst think on. There’s little they can ask that we’d not blithely grant them if they’ll but yield us up their captains.”

“It mislikes me,” answered Corund. “Yet it may serve. But thou shalt be my spokesman herein. For never yet went I cap in hand to ask favour of the common muck o’ the world, nor I will not do it now.”

“O but thou must,” said Gro. “Of thee they will receive in good faith what in me they would account but practice.”

“That’s true enough,” said Corund. “But I cannot stomach it. Withal, I am too rough spoken.”

Gro smiled. “He that hath need of a dog,” he said, “calleth him ‘Sir Dog.’ Come, come, I’ll school thee to it. Is it not a smaller thing than months of tedious hardship in this frozen desert? Bethink thee too what honour it were to thee to ride home to Carcë with Juss and Spitfire and Brandoch Daha bounden in a string.”

Not without much persuasion was Corund won to this. Yet at the last he consented. For seven days and seven nights his armies sat before the burg without sign; and on the eighth day he bade the Demons to a parley, and when that was granted went with his sons and twenty men-at-arms up the great rib of rock between the lakes, and stood below the east wall of the burg. Bitter chill was the air that day. Powdery snow light-fallen blew in little wisps along the ground, and the rocks were slippery with an invisible coat of ice. Lord Gro, being troubled with an ague, excused himself from that faring and kept his tent.

===Chinese===

「我的发明，」次日众人合议时格罗说，「囊中还有几个妙者，能于我们有益——若天从人愿。只是我怕它不合你的胃口。」

「好，说出来，我给你评评。」科伦德说。

格罗说：「已经证明，从地面上砍是砍不倒这棵树的。咱们从根上挖。先给他们七天工夫盘点他们的胜算，叫他们从堡上朝暮看着你的大军扎下围困的营。然后，等那景象把他们的希望浇醒了一些，闲坐无聊又把他们的心思磨得阴郁了，再召他们会谈，直接走到墙下去；这一次，你只对那些普通士卒说话，开出你能想出的一切慷慨宽松的条件。只要他们肯把首领交给我们，他们提什么我们都乐意给。」

「我不喜欢这主意，」科伦德答，「但也许有用。只是讲话得你来。我这辈子没掼过帽子去求世上那群贱泥的什么好，现在也不干。」

「啊，可非你来不可，」格罗说。「由你口中说出，他们会当真心；由我口中说出，他们只会当是算计。」

「这倒不假，」科伦德说。「可我咽不下这口气。再说，我嘴笨。」

格罗笑了。「需要狗的人，」他说，「也得叫它一声『狗老爷』。来，来，我教你。这难道不比在这冰荒漠里熬上几个月轻省？再想想：骑着马回喀尔刻，朱斯、斯皮特法厄、布兰多赫·达哈用绳子串成一串——那是多大的光荣！」

劝了许久，科伦德才被说动。但他终于应允了。他的大军在堡前静坐了七天七夜，无声无息；第八天，他召魔族人会谈；得允后，带着儿子们和二十名带甲武士，登上两湖间那道大岩脊，立在堡的东墙下。那天空气酷寒。粉状的轻雪一缭一缭贴地飘，石头上蒙着一层看不见的冰，滑得很。格罗大人正犯寒热，告了假，留在帐里。

Corund stood beneath the walls with his folk about him. “I have matter of import,” he cried, “and ’tis needful it be heard both by the highest and the lowest amongst you. Ere I begin, summon them all to this part of the walls: a lookout is enow to shield you of the other parts from any sudden onslaught, which besides I swear to you is clean without my purpose.” So when they were thick on the wall above him, he began to say, “Soldiers of Demonland, against you had I never quarrel. Behold how in this Impland I have made freedom flourish as a flower. I have strook off the heads of Philpritz Faz, and Illarosh, and Lurmesh, and Gandassa, and Fax Fay Faz, that were the lords and governors here aforetime, abounding in all the bloody and crying sins, oppression, gluttony, idleness, cruelty, and extortion. And of my clemency I delivered all their possessions unto their subjects to hold and order after their own will alone, who before did put on patience and endured with much heartburning the tyranny of these Fazes, until by me they found a remedy for their more freedom. In like manner, not against you do I war, O men of Demonland; but against the tyrants that enforced you for their private gain to suffer hardship and death in this remote country: namely, against Juss and Spitfire that came hither in quest of their cursed brother whom the might of the great King hath happily removed. And against Brandoch Daha am I come, of insolence untamed, who liveth a chambering idle life eating and drinking and exercising tyranny, while the pleasant lands of Krothering and Failze and Stropardon, and the dwellers in the isles, Sorbey, Morvey, Strufey, Dalney, and Kenarvey, and they of Westmark and all the western parts of Demonland groan and wax lean to feed his luxury. To your hurt only have these three led you, as cattle to the slaughter. Deliver them to me, that I may chastise them, and I, that am great viceroy of Impland, will make you free and grant you lordships: a lordship for every man of you in this my realm of Impland.”

===Chinese===

科伦德立在墙下，众人环侍。「我有要紧话，」他喊道，「你们中最高的和最低的都必须听见。开讲之前，把他们都叫到这一段墙上来：别处留个哨就够护你们防备突袭了——何况我向你们立誓，突袭绝不在我的盘算里。」等墙上站满了人，他开始说：「魔国的士兵们，我对你们素无争端。看看我在妖国是怎样让自由之花盛开的：我砍了菲尔普里茨·法兹、伊拉罗什、卢尔梅什、甘达萨、法克斯·费·法兹的头——他们是从前这里的领主和总督，恶贯满盈，暴戾、饕餮、怠惰、残忍、横征暴敛，血泪斑斑。我又大发慈心，把他们的产业统统交还给他们的属民，任他们自行持有、自行治理；这些属民从前忍气吞声，怀着满腔怨毒忍受法兹家的暴政，直到由我手替他们争来了更多自由。同样，魔国的人们，我不是对你们开战；我是对那些驱使你们为私利在这绝远之地受苦送命的暴君开战：就是朱斯和斯皮特法厄——他们到这里来找他们那个被伟大王上的神威已除去的可咒兄弟；还有布兰多赫·达哈——一个骄纵不驯的浪子，过着吃喝嫔赌的闲荡日子，行着暴政，而克罗瑟林、法伊尔泽、斯特罗帕尔登那些膏腴之地，索尔贝、莫尔维、斯特鲁菲、达尔尼、肯纳尔维诸岛的岛民，西马克和魔国整个西部的人，都在他的奢侈下呻吟消瘦。这三人带你们走的是绝路，像把牲口赶上屠场。把他们交给我惩办；我，妖国的伟大总督，必给你们自由，赐你们领地：你们每一个人，在我这妖国里都得一份领地。」

===Original===

While Corund spake, the Lord Brandoch Daha went among the soldiers bidding them hold their peace and not murmur against Corund. But those that were most hot for action he sent about an errand preparing what he had in mind. So that when the Lord Corund ceased from his declaiming, all was ready to hand, and with one voice the soldiers of Lord Juss that stood upon the wall cried out and said, “This is thy word, O Corund, and this our answer,” and therewith flung down upon him from pots and buckets and every kind of vessel a deluge of slops and offal and all filth that came to hand. A bucketful took Corund in the mouth, befouling all his great beard, so that he gave back spitting. And he and his, standing close beneath the wall, and little expecting so sudden and ill an answer, fared shamefully, being all well soused and bemerded with filth and lye.

Therewith went up great shouts of laughter from the walls. But Corund cried out, “O filth of Demonland, this is my latest word with you. And though ’twere ten years I must besiege this hold, yet will I take it over your heads. And very ill to do with shall ye find me in the end, and very puissant, proud, mighty, cruel, and bloody in my conquest.”

“What, lads?” said Lord Brandoch Daha, standing on the battlements, “have we not fed this beast with pig-wash enow, but he must still be snuffing and snouking at our gate? Give me another pailful.”

So the Witches returned to their tents with great shame. So hot was Corund in anger against the Demons, that he stayed not to eat nor drink at his coming down from Eshgrar Ogo, but straight gathered force and made an assault upon the burg, the mightiest he had yet essayed; and his picked men of Witchland were in that assault, and he himself to lead them. Thrice by main fury they won up into the hold, but all were slain who set foot therein, and Corund’s young son Dormanes wounded to the death. And at even they drew off from the battle. There fell in that fight an hundred and fourscore Demons, and of the Imps five hundred, and of the Witches three hundred and ninety and nine. And many were hurt of either side.

===Chinese===

科伦德说话时，布兰多赫·达哈大人在士兵们中间穿行，叫他们安静，不要咒骂科伦德。那些最按捺不住的，他派去办一件差事，为他心中所想的作准备。所以科伦德大人一收声，一切已备办停当；站在墙上的朱斯大人的士兵们齐声大喊：「科伦德，这是你的话，这是我们的回答！」说着，从锅、桶和各种家什里，一股脑儿向他泼下脏水、馊汤、垃圾和一切顺手的东西。一整桶正中科伦德的嘴，把他大胡子糊了个透，他啐着直往后退。他和他的人贴墙站着，万想不到得到这样突然又这样下流的回答，人人被脏水和硷水浇了个透，糊了个满身粪污。

墙上爆起一片大笑。科伦德喊道：「魔国的脏东西，这是我给你们最后的和谈。就算围上十年，我也要把这堡从你们头顶上拿下来。到头来你们会发现我又难对付、又强大、又倡傲、又威猛、又残忍、又血腥。」

「怎么，弟兄们？」布兰多赫·达哈大人站在雉埞上说，「这条畜生泔水还没喝够，还要在我们门口哼哼嘬嘬？再给他一桶。」

巫国人含羞回帐。科伦德对魔族人恨得心头火起，下埃什格拉·奥戈回来连吃喝都顾不上，直接点兵强攻此堡，这是他迄今最猛的一击；巫国的精兵都投了进去，他亲自带队。他们凭一腔凶悍三度杀上堡去，可凡踏进堡内的全被杀死，科伦德的小儿子多尔马内斯伤重垂死。入夜，他们才收兵。那一仗，魔族人阵亡一百八十，妖人五百，巫国三百九十九。双方还有许多带伤的。

===Original===

Wrath sat like thunder on Corund’s brow at suppertime. He ate his meat savagely, thrusting great gobbets in his mouth, crunching the bones like a beast, taking deep draughts of wine with every mouthful, which yet dispelled not his black mood. Over against him Gro sat silent, shivering now and then for all that he kept his ermine cloak about him and the brazier stood at his elbow. He made but a poor meal, drinking mulled wine in little sips and dipping little pieces of bread in it.

So wore without speech that cheerless and unkindly meal, until the Lord Corund, looking suddenly across the board at Gro and catching his eye studying him, said, “That was a bright star of thine and then shined clear upon thee when thou tookest this bout of shivering fits and so wentest not with me to be soused with muck before the burg.”

“Who would have dreamed,” answered Gro, “of their using so base and shameful a part?”

“Not thou, I’ll swear,” said Corund, looking evilly upon him and marking, as he thought, a twinkling light in Gro’s eyes. Gro shivered again, sipped his wine, and shifted his glance uneasily under that unfriendly stare.

Corund drank awhile in silence, then flushing suddenly a darker red, said, leaning heavily across the board at him, “Dost know why I said ‘not thou’?”

“ ’Twas scarce needful, to thy friend,” said Gro.

“I said it,” said Corund, “because I know thou didst look for another thing when thou didst skulk shamming here.”

“Another thing?”

“Sit not there like some prim-mouthed miss feigning an innocence all know well thou hast not,” said Corund, “or I’ll kill thee. Thou plottedst my death with the Demons. And because thyself hast no shred of honour in thy soul, thou hadst not the wit to perceive that their nobility would shrink from such a betrayal as thy hopes entertained.”

Gro said, “This is a jest I cannot laugh at; or else ’tis madman’s brabble.”

“Dissembling cur,” said Corund, “be sure that I hold him not less guilty that holds the ladder than him that mounts the wall. It was thy design they should smite us at unawares when we went up to them with this proposal thou didst urge on me so hotly.”

Gro made as if to rise. “Sit down!” said Corund. “Answer me; didst not thou egg on the poor snipe Philpritz to that attempt on Juss?”

“He told me on’t,” said Gro.

===Chinese===

晚饭时，雷霆般的怒气压在科伦德眉上。他凶暴地吃着肉，大块大块往嘴里塞，像野兽一样嚼碎骨头，每一口灌一大口酒——可酒压不下他的黑心绪。对面格罗默坐，时不时发一阵抖——尽管裹着貂皮斗篷，火盆就在肘边。他吃得很勉强，一小口一小口啜着热酒，掰一小块一小块的面包蘸着吃。

这顿冷清难受的饭就这样无声地挨着，直到科伦德大人突然隔着桌子看向格罗，撞上他那正打量自己的目光：「你那颗智星可真亮，真照得你准，」他说，「叫你正赶上这场寒热病发，没跟我去堡前吃那顿粪泼。」

「谁想得到，」格罗答，「他们会用这么卑鄙无耻的手段？」

「你想不到，我敢担保。」科伦德说，恶狠狠地看着他，觉得看出格罗眼里一闪一闪的光。格罗又抖了一下，啜口酒，在那不友好的瞪视下不安地把目光挪开。

科伦德默默喝了一阵酒，忽然涨得更红，隔着桌子沉沉地探身过去：「你知道我为什么说『你想不到』么？」

「对自己的朋友，何必说这个。」格罗说。

「我说它，」科伦德道，「因为我都知道：你躲在这里装病时，你等的是另一件事。」

「另一件事？」

「别坐在那儿装什么矜持的小姐，装清白——谁都知道你没有清白，」科伦德说，「不然我杀了你。你和魔族人密谋害我。你自己灵魂里没有一丝荣誉，你就没脑子想到：人家的贵族气概会燋不起你指望的那种背叛。」

格罗说：「这个玩笑我笑不出来；不然就是疯子的胡话。」

「两面三刀的狗，」科伦德说，「你给我记住：我认定扶梯子的和爬墙的同样有罪。你那么热心撺掇我上去提这个建议，就是要他们趁我们不备下手。」

格罗作势要起身。「坐下！」科伦德说。「回答我：是不是你嗾使菲尔普里茨那可怜的沙锥鸟去刺朱斯的？」

「他告诉过我这事。」格罗说。

===Original===

“O, thou art cunning,” said Corund. “There too I see thy treachery. Had they fallen upon us, thou mightest have thrown thyself safely upon their mercy.”

“This is foolishness,” said Gro. “We were far stronger.”

“ ’Tis so,” said Corund. “When did I charge thee with wisdom and sober judgement? With treachery I know thou art soaked wet.”

“And thou art my friend!” said Gro.

Corund said in a while, “I have long known thee to be both a subtle and dissembling fox, and now I durst trust thee no more, for fear I should fall further into thy danger. I am resolved to murther thee.”

Gro fell back in his chair and flung out his arms. “I have been here before,” he said. “I have beheld it, in moonlight and in the barren glare of day, in fair weather and in hail and snow, with the great winds charging over the wastes. And I knew it was accursed. From Morna Moruna, ere I was born or thou, O Corund, or any of us, treason and cruelty blacker than night herself had birth, and brought death to their begetter and all his folk. From Morna Moruna bloweth this wind about the waste to blast our love and bring us destruction. Ay, kill me; I’ll not ward myself, not i’ the smallest.”

“ ’Tis small matter, Goblin,” said Corund, “whether thou shouldst or no. Thou art but a louse between my fingers, to kill or cast away as shall seem me good.”

===Chinese===

「哦，你真是狡猾，」科伦德说。「那里面我也看见了你的背叛。他们若真的扑上来，你就可以万无一失地投进他们的饶命里去。」

「这是蠢话，」格罗说。「我们强得多。」

「是这么回事，」科伦德说。「我几时说过你有智慧和清醒的判断？我只知道你背叛透了。」

「你还说你是我的朋友！」格罗说。

过了一会儿，科伦德说：「我早就知道你是一只狡猾而善伪装的狐狸；如今我再不敢信你，怕再掉进你的危险里。我决意杀了你。」

格罗仰回椅中，双臂一摊。「这一幕我从前经历过。」他说。「我见过它，在月光里，在白昼荒瘠的烈光里，在晴天里，在冰雹和雪里，在大风扫过荒原的时候。我早知道它是可咒的。从莫尔纳·莫鲁纳（Morna Moruna），在你我出生之前，科伦德——在我们任何人出生之前——比夜本身还黑的背叛与残忍就诞生了，给它的缔造者和他的全体族人带来了死亡。从莫尔纳·莫鲁纳刮来的这阵风扫过荒原，要摧折我们的爱，给我们带来毁灭。唉，杀了我吧；我不自卫，一根指头也不自卫。」

「自卫不自卫，哥布林，都由不得你，」科伦德说，「你不过是我指缝里的一只虱子，捏死还是掸掉，随我高兴。」

===Original===

“I was King Gaslark’s man,” said Gro, as if talking in a dream; “and between a man and a boy near fifteen years I served him true and costly. Yet it was my fortune in all that time and at the ending thereof only to get a beard on my chin and remorse at heart. To what scorned purpose must I plot against him? Pity of Witchland, of Witchland sliding as then into the pit of adverse luck, ’twas that made force upon me. And I served Witchland well: but fate ever fought o’ the other side. I it was that counselled King Gorice XI to draw out from the fight at Kartadza. Yet wanton Fortune trod down the scale for Demonland. I prayed him not wrastle with Goldry in the Foliot Isles. Thou didst back me. Nought but rebukes and threats of death gat I therefrom; but because my redes were set at nought, evil fell upon Witchland. I helped our Lord the King when he conjured and made a sending against the Demons. He loved me therefor and upheld me, but great envy was raised up against me in Carcë for that fact. Yet I bare up, for thy friendship and thy lady wife’s were as bright fires to warm me against all the frosts of their ill-will. And now, for love of thee, I fared with thee to Impland. And here by the Moruna where in old days I wandered in danger and in sorrow, it is fitting I behold at length the emptiness of all my days.”

Therewith Gro fell silent a minute, and then began to say: “O Corund, I’ll strip bare my soul to thee before thou kill me. It is most true that until now, sitting before Eshgrar Ogo, it hath been present to my heart how great an advantage we held against the Demons, and the glory of their defence, so little a strength against us so many, and the great glory of their flinging of us back, these things were a splendour to my soul beholding them. Such glamour hath ever shone to me all my life’s days when I behold great men battling still beneath the bludgeonings of adverse fortune that, howsoever they be mine enemies, it lieth not in my virtue to withhold from admiration of them and well nigh love. But never was I false to thee, nor much less ever thought, as thou most unkindly accusest me, to compass thy destruction.”

“Thou dost whine like a woman for thy life,” said Corund. “Cowardly hounds never stirred pity in me.” Yet he moved not, only looking dourly on Gro.

===Chinese===

「我本是加斯拉克王的人，」格罗像说梦话一样说；「从少年到成年，将近十五年，我为他效力，忠心而破费。可那整段日子里，直到末了，我只落得下巴上一把胡子和心里一腔悔恨。叫我谋算他，是遭人白眼的目的么？是对巫国的怜悯——它那时正滑进背运的深坑——是那怜悯逼住了我。我为巫国效力也不遗余力：可命运总是站在对面那头。劝戈里斯十一世从卡尔塔扎（Kartadza）战事中脱身的是我，可任性的命运偏偏把秤压给魔国。求他别在福廖特群岛与戈尔德里角力的也是我，你也帮了腔。我得的全是叱责和死罪的威吓；正因我的计策被踩在脚下，灾祸才落到巫国头上。王上召灵作法对付魔族时，是我侍立的。他因此爱我、抬举我，喀尔刻却因那件事对我妒火中烧。可我挺住了，因为你和你夫人的情谊是两团明火，替我挡住他们恶意的所有严寒。如今，为了对你的爱，我随你来到妖国。在这里，在这片我当年于危难忧愁中流浪过的莫鲁纳边上，我总算合该看清：我这一生，原来是一场空。」

格罗沉默了一阵，然后开口说：「科伦德，你杀我之前，我把灵魂剥给你看。千真万确，直到此刻，坐在埃什格拉·奥戈城下，我心里一直放着我们握有对魔族多大的优势；而他们防御的荣光——那么少的人对抗我们这么多的人，他们把我们一次次打回去的大光荣——这些在我灵魂里看去是一片辉光。我这一生，每逢看见伟人们在厄运的棒击下仍然战斗，眼前总有这样的魔光：无论他们是不是我的仇敌，要我不佩服他们、几乎不爱他们，我的德性办不到。可我从不曾背弃你，更从不曾如你最刻薄地指控的那样，存心谋你的命。」

「你为活命哭哭啼啼像个娘们，」科伦德说。「怯懦的狗从来不曾感动过我。」可他没动，只是阴都都地看着格罗。

===Original===

Gro plucked forth his own sword, and pushed it towards Corund hilt-foremost across the board. “Such words are worse than sword-thrusts betwixt us twain,” said he. “Thou shalt see how I’ll welcome death. The King will praise thee, when thou showest the cause. And it will be sweet news to Corinius and them that have held me in their hate, that thy love hath cast me off, and thou hast rid them of me at last.”

But Corund stirred not. After a space, he filled another cup, and drank, and sat on. And Gro sat motionless before him. At last Corund rose heavily from his seat, and pushing Gro’s sword back across the table, “Thou’dst best to bed,” said he. “But the night air’s o’er shrewd for thine ague. Sleep on my couch tonight.”

===Chinese===

格罗拔出自己的剑，捏着剑柄那一头，隔着桌子推向科伦德。「这样的话比剑刺还伤我们之间的情分。」他说。「你看着我怎么迎接死吧。等你说明缘由，王上会夸你。科里尼厄斯（Corinius）和那些一贯恨我的人听到这消息一定甜到心里：你的爱把我抛了，你终于替他们除掉了我。」

科伦德却不动。过了一阵，他又斟了一杯，喝了，坐着。格罗也在他面前一动不动。末了，科伦德沉重地从座上起身，把格罗的剑推回桌子那头。「你最好去睡。」他说。「只是夜里的空气对你那寒热病太尖利了。今夜就睡我的榻。」

===Original===

The day dawned cold and gray, and with the dawn Corund ordered his lines round about Eshgrar Ogo and sat down for a siege. For ten days he sat before the burg, and nought befell from dawn till night, from night till dawn: only the sentinels walked on the walls and Corund’s folk guarded their lines. On the eleventh day came a bank of fog rolling westward from the Moruna, chill and dank, blotting out the features of the land. Snow fell, and the fog hung on the land, and night came of such a pitchy blackness that even by torchlight a man might not see his hand stretched forth at arm’s length before him. Five days the fog held. On the fifth night, it being the twenty-fourth of November, in the darkness of the third hour after midnight, the alarm was sounded and Corund summoned by a runner from the north with word that a sally was made from Eshgrar Ogo, and the lines bursten through in that quarter, and fighting going forward in the mirk. Corund was scarce harnessed and gotten forth into the night, when a second runner came hotfoot from the south with tidings of a great fight thereaway. All was confounded in the dark, and nought certain, save that the Demons were broken out from Eshgrar Ogo. In a space, as Corund came with his folk to the northern quarter and joined in the fight, came a message from his son Heming that Spitfire and a number with him were broken out at the other side and gotten away westward, and a great band chasing him back towards Outer Impland; and therewith that more than an hundred Demons were surrounded and penned in by the shore of the lakes, and the burg entered and taken by Corund’s folk; but of Juss and Brandoch Daha no certain news, save that they were not of Spitfire’s company, but were with those against whom Corund went in person, having fared forth northaway. So went the battle through the night. Corund himself had sight of Juss, and exchanged shots with him with twirl-spears in a lifting of the fog toward dawn, and a son of his bare witness of Brandoch Daha in that same quarter, and had gotten a great wound from him.

===Chinese===

天亮了，又冷又灰。破晓时，科伦德把环埃什格拉·奥戈的各条战线布好，坐困围城。他在堡前坐了十天，从拂晓到入夜，从入夜到拂晓，毫无动静：只有哨兵在墙上走动，科伦德的人守着围线。第十一天，一团浓雾从莫鲁纳滚滚西来，又冷又湿，抹去了大地的眉目。雪落了，雾凝在原野上，夜里黑得像漆——打着火把也看不见自己伸直在面前一臂远的手。雾困了五天。第五夜，十一月二十四日，后半夜三点光景的黑暗里，警号吹响，一名信使从北面奔来急报科伦德：埃什格拉·奥戈里有人突出，那一面的围线被凿穿，黑暗中正在接战。科伦德披挂未全，刚冲进夜色，又一名信使从南面飞奔而来，报那边也大战正酣。黑暗中一切混乱，唯一确实的是：魔族人已破堡而出。不多时，科伦德率人赶到北面投入战斗，又接到他儿子赫明的口信：斯皮特法厄带一批人在另一面突围，向西去了，一支大队正追着他往外妖国方向去；另有一百多名魔族人被围死在湖岸边；堡已被科伦德的人攻入占领；可朱斯和布兰多赫·达哈没有确实消息，只知他们不在斯皮特法厄队中，而在科伦德亲自迎战的那批人里，向北去了。战事就这样打了一整夜。科伦德亲眼看见了朱斯，趁雾散时用旋枪同他对掷过一轮；他的一个儿子在同一地带目击了布兰多赫·达哈，还挨了他一大伤。

===Original===

When night was past, and the Witches returned from the pursuit, Corund straitly questioned his officers, and went himself about the battlefield hearing each man’s story and viewing the slain. Those Demons that were hemmed against the lakes had all lost their lives, and some were taken up dead in other parts, and some few alive. These would his officers let slay, but Corund said, “Since I am king in Impland, till that the King receive it of me, it is not this handful of earth-lice shall shake my safety here; and I may well give them their lives, that fought sturdily against us.” So he gave them peace. And he said unto Gro, “Better that for every Demon dead in Ogo Morveo ten should rise up against us, if but Juss only and Brandoch Daha were slain.”

“I’ll be in the tale with thee, if thou wilt proclaim them dead,” said Gro. “And nothing is likelier, if they be gone with but two or three on to the Moruna, than that such a tale should come true ere it were told in Carcë.”

“Pshaw!” said Corund, “to the devil with such false feathers. What’s done shows brave enow without them: Impland conquered, Juss’s army minced to a gallimaufry, himself and Brandoch Daha chased like runaway thralls up on the Moruna. Where if devils tear them, ’tis my best wish come true. If not, thou’lt hear of them, be sure. Dost think these can survive on earth and not raise a racket that shall be heard from hence to Carcë?”

===Chinese===

夜尽，巫国人追击回来，科伦德严询众军官，又亲赴战场，听每个人讲述、验看死者。被逼到湖边的魔族人全部战死，另有些尸首在别处收起，活捉的寥寥几个。军官们要杀这些活口，科伦德说：「既然我在妖国是王，在王上从我手里接管之前，总不是这一撮土虱子能撼动我这里的安稳；他们同我们打得那样壮勇，我尽可以饶他们的命。」于是饶了。他对格罗说：「但愿奥戈·莫尔维奥每一个死掉的魔族人换成十个来找我们报仇，只要朱斯和布兰多赫·达哈死了就好。」

「你要是肯宣布他们死了，我可以陪你把这话说圆。」格罗说。「再说，倘若他们只带两三个人上了莫鲁纳，那就再没有比这更可能的事了：这故事还没传到喀尔刻，自己就会成真。」

「咄！」科伦德说，「见鬼的假羽毛。办成的事本身够体面了，用不着装点：妖国已定，朱斯的大军剁成了杂烩，他和布兰多赫·达哈像逃奴一样被赶上莫鲁纳。魔鬼若在那里撕了他们，是我最大的心愿得偿。若没有，你放心，他们还会闹出动静来的。你以为这样的人还能活在世上，而不搅出一场从这里响到喀尔刻的喧天大锣鼓么？」

## XII / 十二
===Original===

Koshtra Pivrarcha

Of the coming of the lords of Demonland to Morna Moruna, whence they beheld the Zimiamvian Mountains, seen also by Gro in years gone by; and of the wonders seen by them and perils undergone and deeds done in their attempt on Koshtra Pivrarcha, the which alone of all earth’s mountains looketh down upon Koshtra Belorn; and none shall ascend up into Koshtra Belorn that hath not first looked down upon her.

Now it is to be said of Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha that they, finding themselves parted from their people in the fog, and utterly unable to find them, when the last sound of battle had died away wiped and put up their bloody swords and set forth at a great pace eastward. Only Mivarsh fared with them of all their following. His lips were drawn back a little, showing his teeth, but he carried himself proudly as one who being resolved to die walks with a quiet mind to his destruction. Day after day they journeyed, sometimes in clear weather, sometimes in mist or sleet, over the changeless desert, without a landmark, save here a little sluggish river, or here a piece of rising ground, or a pond, or a clump of rocks: small things which faded from sight amid the waste ere they were passed by a half-mile’s distance. So was each day like yesterday, drawing to a morrow like to it again. And always fear walked at their heel and sat beside them sleeping: clanking of wings heard above the wind, a brooding hush of menace in the sunshine, and noises out of the void of darkness as of teeth chattering. So came they on the twentieth day to Morna Moruna, and stood at even in the sorrowful twilight by the little round castle, silent on Omprenne Edge.

===Chinese===

科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡

述魔国诸大人来到莫尔纳·莫鲁纳、从那里望见齐米亚姆维亚（Zimiamvia）群山——格罗往昔也曾望见；并他们在攀加固什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡——大地群山中惟一俯瞰科什特拉·贝洛恩者——的尝试中所见的奇观、所历的凶险、所立的功业；而不先俯瞰过她的人，无一人能登上科什特拉·贝洛恩。

再说朱斯大人与布兰多赫·达哈大人：他们在雾中与部众失散、又全然寻他们不见，待战斗最后的声音消歇，便拭净收起血剑，迈开大步向东进发。随行的部众里只剩米瓦尔什一人。他嘴唇微微翻起露着牙，举止却昂然，像一个决意赴死的人、怀着安静的心走向毁灭。他们日复一日地行进，或晴或雾或雨雪，越过不变的荒原，没有地标，只有这里一条懒河、那里一片高地、一方池沼、一丛乱石：这些小东西还没走出半英里，就消失在荒芜的视野里。于是每一天都像昨天，又引向一个与之相似的明天。恐惧始终跟在他们脚跟后、睡时坐在他们身旁：风声之上有翅膀的铿锵，日光里有威胁的阴静，黑暗的虚空外有牙齿打颤般的声响。第二十天他们这样来到莫尔纳·莫鲁纳（Morna Moruna），黄昏时分立在哀愁的暮色里，在奥姆普伦崖上那座沉默的小圆堡旁。

===Original===

From their feet the cliffs dropped sheer. Strange it was, standing on that frozen lip of the Moruna, as on the limit of the world, to gaze southward on a land of summer, and to breathe faint summer airs blowing up from blossoming trees and flower-clad alps. In the depths a carpet of huge treetops clothed a vast stretch of country, through the midst of which, seen here and there in a bend of silver among the woods, the Bhavinan bore the waters of a thousand secret mountain solitudes down to an unknown sea. Beyond the river the deep woods, blue with distance, swelled to feathery hilltops with some sharper-featured loftier heights bodying cloudily beyond them. The Demons strained their eyes searching the curtain of mystery behind and above those foothills; but the great peaks, like great ladies, shrouded themselves against their curious gaze, and no glimpse was shown them of the snows.

Surely to be in Morna Moruna was to be in the death chamber of some once lovely presence. Stains of fire were on the walls. The fair gallery of open woodwork that ran above the main hall was burnt through and partly fallen in ruin, the blackened ends of the beams that held it jutting blindly in the gap. Among the wreck of carved chairs and benches, broken and worm-eaten, some shreds of figured tapestries rotted, the home now of beetles and spiders. Patches of colour, faded lines, mildewed and damp with the corruption of two hundred years, lingered to be the memorials, like the mummied skeleton of a king’s daughter long ago untimely dead, of sweet gracious paintings on the walls. Five nights and five days the Demons and Mivarsh dwelt in Morna Moruna, inured to portents till they marked them as little as men mark swallows at their window. In the still night were flames seen, and flying forms dim in the moonlit air; and in moonless nights unstarred, moans heard and gibbering accents: prodigies beside their beds, and ridings in the sky, and fleshless fingers plucking at Juss unseen when he went forth to make question of the night.

===Chinese===

悬崖从他们脚边直落。站在莫鲁纳这冻结的唇沿上，如立在世界尽头，向南凝望一片夏日之国，呼吸从花树与繁花覆坡的高山上拂上来的微弱夏风，实在奇哉。深处一层巨大的树冠铺盖着广袤的原野，巴维南河从中间穿过——在林木间这里那里露出一段银色的河湾——把千百处隐秘山荒的水载往不知名的海。河那边，深林带着远方的蔚蓝，隆起为绒羽般的峰顶，其后又有面目更峻峭的高山影影地耸出。魔人们眯眼搜寻那些山麓丘陵背后与上方的神秘帷幔；但众高峰像贵妇一样，把自己裹起来不叫人好奇地看，雪顶一线也不给他们瞧。

身在莫尔纳·莫鲁纳，就像置身于一位昔日可爱者的停灵之室。墙上有火的焦痕。主厅上方那道镂刻木作的美丽回廊烧穿了、半已坍塌，承着它的焦黑梁头在豁口里茫然戳出。雕椅长凳的残骸间，断裂虫蛀，几片织花挂毯的碎片在朽烂，如今是甲虫与蜘蛛的家。一片片颜色、一行行褪了线的痕迹，带着两百年的霉腐与潮气，流连在墙上，像一位公主久已夭折的木乃伊骸骨，作着那些甜美典雅壁画的纪念。魔人们与米瓦尔什在莫尔纳·莫鲁纳住了五夜五日，对异象惯到如人对窗前的燕子一样不再留意。静夜里有火光、有月光下朦胧的飞影；无月无星的夜里，有呻吟与呓语可闻：床边有怪异，天空有驰骋，朱斯夜里出去叩问黑暗时，有无肉的指头看不见地拉扯他。

===Original===

Cloud and mist abode ever in the south, and only the foothills showed of the great ranges beyond Bhavinan. But on the evening of the sixth day before Yule, it being the nineteenth of December when Betelgeuze stands at midnight on the meridian, a wind blew out of the northwest with changing fits of sleet and sunshine. Day was fading as they stood above the cliff. All the forest land was blue with shades of approaching night: the river was dull silver: the wooded heights afar mingled their outlines with the towers and banks of turbulent deep blue vapour that hurtled in ceaseless passage through the upper air. Suddenly a window opened in the clouds to a space of clean wan windswept sky high above the shaggy hills. Surely Juss caught his breath in that moment, to see those deathless ones where they shone pavilioned in the pellucid air, far, vast, and lonely, most like to creatures of unascended heaven, of wind and of fire all compact, too pure to have aught of the gross elements of earth or water. It was as if the rose-red light of sundown had been frozen to crystal and these hewn from it to abide to everlasting, strong and unchangeable amid the welter of earthborn mists below and tumultuous sky above them. The rift ran wider, eastward and westward, opening on more peaks and sunset-kindled snows. And a rainbow leaning to the south was like a sword of glory across the vision.

Motionless, like hawks staring from that high place of prospect, Juss and Brandoch Daha looked on the mountains of their desire.

Juss spake, haltingly as one talking in a dream. “The sweet smell, this gusty wind, the very stone thy foot standeth on: I know them all before. There’s not a night since we sailed out of Lookinghaven that I have not beheld in sleep these mountains and known their names.”

“Who told thee their names?” asked Lord Brandoch Daha.

===Chinese===

云雾始终住在南方，巴维南河外的大山脉只露出山麓。但冬至前第六天的傍晚——十二月十九日，参宿四午夜行至中天——一阵西北风带着间歇的雨雪与日光吹起。他们立在崖上时，白昼正在消退。整片林地浸着入夜的青蓝：河是暗银色：远处林木覆盖的高地，轮廓与汹涌的深蓝云涛的塔与岸混作一处，那云在高空奔腾不休。忽然，云间开了一扇窗，露出多毛山峦之上高处一块干净苍白的、被风扫过的天空。朱斯在那一刻屏住了呼吸：看见那些不死者在澄澈之气中辉耀为宫，遥远、巨大、孤绝，最像未升之天的造物，纯以风与火凝成，纯得不带地与水的浊元素。仿佛落日的玫瑰红光冻结成了水晶，而这些就是从其中凿出、存到永远的，在下界土雾的翻涌与上界天涛的喧騷之间，坚强而不改。裂缝越开越宽，向东向西，敞出更多的峰与落日点燃的雪。一道偏向南方的彩虹，像一柄荣耀之剑横在视野上。

朱斯与布兰多赫·达哈一动不动，像鹰从那高高的展望处凝望，望着他们心所愿的群山。

朱斯说话了，迟缓得像梦中人。「这甜香，这阵阵的风，你脚站着的这块石头：我全都认得。自我们驶出卢克黑文，没有一夜我不曾在睡里看见这些山、叫出它们的名字。」

「谁告诉你它们的名字？」布兰多赫·达哈大人问。

===Original===

“My dream,” Juss answered. “And first I dreamed it in mine own bed in Galing when I came home from guesting with thee last June. And they be true dreams that are dreamed there.” And he said, “Seest thou where the foothills part to a dark valley that runneth deep into the chain, and the mountains are bare to view from crown to foot? Mark where, beyond the nearer range, bleak-visaged precipices, cobweb-streaked with huge snow corridors, rise to a rampart where the rock towers stand against the sky. This is the great ridge of Koshtra Pivrarcha, and the loftiest of those spires his secret mountaintop.”

As he spoke, his eye followed the line of the eastern ridge, where the towers, like dark gods going down from heaven, plunge to a parapet which runs level above a curtain of avalanche-fluted snow. He fell silent as his gaze rested on the sister peak that east of the gap flamed skyward in wild cliffs to an airy snowy summit, soft-lined as a maiden’s cheek, purer than dew, lovelier than a dream.

While they looked the sunset fires died out upon the mountains, leaving only pale hues of death and silence. “If thy dream,” said Lord Brandoch Daha, “conducted thee down this Edge, over the Bhavinan, through yonder woods and hills, up through the leagues of ice and frozen rock that stand betwixt us and the main ridge, up by the right road to the topmost snows of Koshtra Belorn: that were a dream indeed.”

“All this it showed me,” said Juss, “up to the lowest rocks of the great north buttress of Koshtra Pivrarcha, that must first be scaled by him that would go up to Koshtra Belorn. But beyond those rocks not even a dream hath ever climbed. Ere the light fades, I’ll show thee our pass over the nearer range.” He pointed where a glacier crawled betwixt shadowy walls down from a torn snowfield that rose steeply to a saddle. East of it stood two white peaks, and west of it a sheer-faced and long-backed mountain like a citadel, squat and dark beneath the wild skyline of Koshtra Pivrarcha that hung in air beyond it.

“The Zia valley,” said Juss, “that runneth into Bhavinan. There lieth our way: under that dark bastion called by the Gods Tetrachnampf.”

===Chinese===

「我的梦，」朱斯答。「头一次是六月里我从你家做客回来、在加灵我自己床上梦见的。在那张床上做的梦都是真的。」他又说：「看见没有，山麓在哪里分开，露出一道黑谷深深切进山链，群山从顶到脚裸露在望？再看近山脊之外，苍白的绝壁上挂着蛛丝般巨大的雪廊，上升到一道埂墙，岩塔顶天而立。这就是科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡（Koshtra Pivrarcha）的大山脊，那些尖塔中最高的一座，就是它隐秘的绝顶。」

他说话时，目光沿着东山脊的线看去：那里的塔群像下凡的黑神，直坠到一道栏墙，栏墙平齐地走在一幅雪崩刻槽的雪幕之上。他默然了，目光停在姊妹峰上：它在隘口以东，以狂野的危崖燃向天空，顶着一个空灵雪白的峰顶，线条柔得像少女的面颊，比露更纯，比梦更可爱。

他们望着，落日之火在群山上熄灭，只余死亡与寂静的淡色。「你的梦，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说，「若领你走下这崖，渡过巴维南，穿过那边的林与山，攀上立在我们与主山脊之间的几里格冰岩，沿正路直上科什特拉·贝洛恩最高的雪：那才真是一个梦。」

「这一切它都给我看了，」朱斯说，「直到科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡巨大北扶壁最下面的岩壁——要先登它，才能去科什特拉·贝洛恩。但那些岩石以上，连梦也从不曾爬上去过。趁光未灭，我指给你看我们过近山脊的隘口。」他指向一道冰川，在幽暗的壁间从一片撕裂的雪原蠕下，雪原陡升到一处鞍部。鞍部以东立着两座白峰，以西是一座面平背长的山，像一座堡垒，蹲踞而黑，衬在悬于空中的科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡野性的天际线前。

「齐亚谷，」朱斯说，「通到巴维南。我们的路在那里：在那座众神称之为特特拉赫南普夫的黑堡垒之下。」

===Original===

On the morrow Lord Brandoch Daha came to Mivarsh Faz and said, “It is needful that this day we go down from Omprenne Edge. I would for no sake leave thee on the Moruna, but ’tis no walking matter to descend this wall. Art thou a cragsman?”

“I was born,” answered he, “in the high valley of Perarshyn by the upper waters of the Beirun in Impland. There boys scarce toddle ere they can climb a rock. This climb affrights me not, nor those mountains. But the land is unknown and terrible, and many loathly ones inhabit it, ghosts and eaters of men. O devils transmarine, and my friends, is it not enough? Let us turn again, and if the Gods save our lives we shall be famous forever, that came unto Morna Moruna and returned alive.”

But Juss answered and said, “O Mivarsh Faz, know that not for fame are we come on this journey. Our greatness already shadoweth all the world, as a great cedar tree spreading his shadow in a garden; and this enterprise, mighty though it be, shall add to our glory only so much as thou mightest add to these forests of the Bhavinan by planting of one more tree. But so it is, that the great King of Witchland, practising in darkness in his royal palace of Carcë such arts of grammarie and sendings magical as the world hath not been grieved with until now, sent an ill thing to take my brother, the Lord Goldry Bluszco, who is dear to me as mine own soul. And They that dwell in secret sent me word in a dream, bidding me, if I would have tidings of my dear brother, inquire in Koshtra Belorn. Therefore, O Mivarsh, go with us if thou wilt, but if thou wilt not, why, fare thee well. For nought but my death shall stay me from going thither.”

And Mivarsh, bethinking him that if the mantichores of the mountains should devour him along with those two lords, that were yet a kindlier fate than all alone to abide those things he wist of on the Moruna, put on the rope, and after commending himself to the protection of his gods followed Lord Brandoch Daha down the rotten slopes of rock and frozen earth at the head of a gully leading down the cliff.

===Chinese===

次日早晨，布兰多赫·达哈大人来到米瓦尔什·法兹跟前说：「今天我们必须下奥姆普伦崖。我不愿把你撇在莫鲁纳，可这道崖不是走路的事。你善攀岩么？」

「我生在妖国贝伦河上游、佩拉尔申的高谷里，」他答。「那里的孩子还不会走路就先会爬岩。这次攀爬吓不倒我，那些山也吓不倒我。可那地方陌生可怖，住着许多可憎的东西：鬼魂和吃人的东西。海那边的魔鬼们，我的朋友们，这还不够么？我们回去吧；若众神保住我们的命，我们将永远出名：到过莫尔纳·莫鲁纳、活着回来了的人。」

朱斯答道：「米瓦尔什·法兹，要知道：我们这一程不是为名声来的。我们的伟大已荫蔽全世界，像园中一株大香柏张开的荫影；这一事业纵然宏大，给我们荣耀添的，也不过像你往这巴维南森林再栽一棵树。可是事情是：巫国的大王在喀尔刻王宫里暗行语法与遣送之术——世上迄今未受过的祸——遣了一个恶物来摄我兄弟戈尔德里·布卢斯科大人，他于我亲如我自己的魂。那些隐秘中居住者托梦传话给我，说：我若要我兄弟的消息，到科什特拉·贝洛恩去问。所以，米瓦尔什，你愿意就跟我们来，不愿意，那就再会。因为除了我的死，没有什么能拦我去那里。」

米瓦尔什想：山里的曼提克若把他连那两位大人一并吞了，也强似独自留在莫鲁纳守着他知道的那些东西；于是他系上绳，把自己托付给他众神的保佑之后，跟着布兰多赫·达哈大人从冲沟头上那片酥石冻土的陡坡下崖去了。

===Original===

For all that they were early afoot, yet was it high noon ere they were off the rocks. For the peril of falling stones drove them out from the gully’s bed first on to the eastern buttress and after, when that grew too sheer, back to the western wall. And in an hour or twain the gully’s bed grew shallow and it narrowed to an end, whence Brandoch Daha gazed between his feet to where, a few spear’s lengths below, the smooth slabs curved downward out of sight and the eye leapt straight from their clean-cut edge to shimmering treetops that showed tiny as mosses beyond the unseen gulf of air. So they rested awhile; then returning a little up the gully forced a way out on to the face and made a hazardous traverse to a new gully westward of the first, and so at last plunged down a long fan of scree and rested on soft fine turf at the foot of the cliffs.

Little mountain gentians grew at their feet; the pathless forest lay like the sea below them; before them the mountains of the Zia stood supreme: the white gables of Islargyn, the lean dark finger of Tetrachnampf nan Tshark lying back above the Zia Pass pointing to the sky, and west of it, jutting above the valley, the square bastion of Tetrachnampf nan Tsurm. The greater mountains were for the most part sunk behind this nearer range, but Koshtra Belorn still towered above the Pass. As a queen looking down from her high window, so she overlooked those green woods sleeping in the noonday; and on her forehead was beauty like a star. Behind them where they sat, the escarpment reared back in cramped perspective, a pile of massive buttresses cleft with ravines leading upward from that land of leaves and waters to the hidden wintry flats of the Moruna.

===Chinese===

尽管他们起得早，下完岩已是正午。落石的凶险先逼他们出沟床上了东扶壁，待那边太陡，又折回西壁。一两个钟头后，沟床变浅、窄到尽头；布兰多赫·达哈从那里朝两脚之间望去：几矛之遥的下方，平滑的石板弯下去隐没不见，眼光从它们利落的边棱径直跳到闪光的小小树冠上——像苔藓，隔着看不见的空气深渊。他们歇了一阵；又回上沟里一点，从崖面强行横切，冒险横渡到西面一道新冲沟，最后顺着一长扇碎石冲下去，在崖脚细软的草皮上歇定。

小小的山龙胆开在脚边；无路的森林像海一样卧在下面；面前齐亚的群山至高无上：伊斯拉尔金的白山墙，特特拉赫南普夫·南·恰尔克那瘦黑的指岩，在齐亚隘口上方仰指着天，它以西、俯临河谷的，是特特拉赫南普夫·南·楚尔姆的方棱堡垒。更大的山大多沉在这道近山脊后面，唯有科什特拉·贝洛恩仍高耸在隘口之上。像王后从高窗俯望，她俯瞰正午沉睡的绿林；她额上有美，像一颗星。他们坐处的身后，陡崖向后收缩着耸起，一堆巨大的扶壁，裂着一道道沟壑，从那叶与水之乡向上通到莫鲁纳隐秘的冬日高台。

---

===Original===

That night they slept on the fell under the stars, and next day, going down into the woods, came at dusk to an open glade by the waters of the broad-bosomed Bhavinan. The turf was like a cushion, a place for elves to dance in. The far bank full half a mile away was wooded to the water with silver birches, dainty as mountain nymphs, their limbs gleaming through the twilight, their reflections quivering in the depths of the mighty river. In the high air day lingered yet, a faint warmth tingeing the great outlines of the mountains, and westward up the river the young moon stooped above the trees. East of the glade a little wooded eminence, no higher than a house, ran back from the river bank, and in its shoulder a hollow cave.

“How smiles it to thee?” said Juss. “Be sure we shall find no better place than this thou seest to dwell in until the snows melt and we may on. For though it be summer all the year round in this fortunate valley, it is winter on the great hills, and until the spring we were mad to essay our enterprise.”

“Why then,” said Brandoch Daha, “turn we shepherds awhile. Thou shalt pipe to me, and I’ll foot thee measures shall make the dryads think they ne’er went to school. And Mivarsh shall be a goat-foot god to chase them; for to tell thee truth country wenches are long grown tedious to me. O, ’tis a sweet life. But ere we fall to it, bethink thee, O Juss: time marcheth, and the world waggeth: what goeth forward in Demonland till summer be come and we home again?”

“Also my heart is heavy because of my brother Spitfire,” said Juss. “O, ’twas an ill storm, and ill delays.”

“Away with vain regrettings,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “For thy sake and thy brother’s fared I on this journey, and it is known to thee that never yet stretched I out mine hand upon aught that I have not taken it, and had my will of it.”

===Chinese===

当夜他们在星空下的高地宿营；次日下到林中，黄昏来到巴维南宽阔的河畔一片开阔林间草地。草皮软如坐垫，是个精灵跳舞的地方。半英里外的对岸，银桦植到水边，窈窕如山中宁芙，肢体在暮色里发亮，倒影在大河深处颤动。高空里白昼还在流连，一线微暖染着群山巨大的轮廓；河的上游以西，新月俯在树梢上。草地以东，一座林木覆盖的小丘——不过房子那么高——从河岸延展开去，丘肩上有一个洞穴。

「你看这地方如何？」朱斯说。「放心，雪化之前，我们找不到比这更好的住处了。这幸运的山谷虽四季皆夏，大山之上却是冬天；不到春天，我们去碰我们的事业就是发疯。」

「那好，」布兰多赫·达哈说，「我们且做一阵牧人。你给我吹笛，我给你跳几下舞步，叫树精们以为自己没上过学。米瓦尔什就做个羊脚神去追她们；实对你说，乡下姑娘我早腻了。啊，这日子甜。不过开工之前，你想一想，朱斯：时间在走，世界在转：夏天到来、我们回家之前，魔国那边怎么样了？」

「我也为兄弟斯皮特法厄心重，」朱斯说。「唉，那场风暴坏，那些耽搁也坏。」

「丢开无益的懊悔吧，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「为你和你兄弟的缘故我才走这一程；你知道，我从来伸手没有拿不到、没有不如愿的。」

===Original===

So they made their dwelling in that cave beside deep-eddying Bhavinan, and before that cave they ate their Yule feast, the strangest they had eaten all the days of their lives: seated, not as of old, on their high seats of ruby or of opal, but on mossy banks where daisies slept and creeping thyme; lighted not by the charmed escarbuncle of the high presence chamber in Galing, but by the shifting beams of a brushwood fire that shone not on those pillars crowned with monsters that were the wonder of the world but on the mightier pillars of the sleeping beechwoods. And in place of that feigned heaven of jewels self-effulgent beneath the golden canopy at Galing, they ate pavilioned under a charmed summer night, where the great stars of winter, Orion, Sirius, and the Little Dog, were raised up near the zenith, yielding their known courses in the southern sky to Canopus and the strange stars of the south. When the trees spake, it was not with their winter voice of bare boughs creaking, but with whisper of leaves and beetles droning in the fragrant air. The bushes were white with blossom, not with hoarfrost, and the dim white patches under the trees were not snow, but wild lilies and wood anemones sleeping in the night.

All the creatures of the forest came to that feast, for they were without fear, having never looked upon the face of man. Little tree-apes, and popinjays, and titmouses, and coalmouses, and wrens, and gentle round-eyed lemurs, and rabbits, and badgers, and dormice, and pied squirrels, and beavers from the streams, and storks, and ravens, and bustards, and wombats, and the spider-monkey with her baby at her breast: all these came to gaze with curious eye upon those travellers. And not these alone, but fierce beasts of the woods and wildernesses: the wild buffalo, the wolf, the tiger with monstrous paws, the bear, the fiery-eyed unicorn, the elephant, the lion and she-lion in their majesty, came to behold them in the firelight in that quiet glade.

“It seems we hold court in the woods tonight,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “It is very pleasant. Yet hold thee ready with me to put some firebrands amongst ’em if need befall. ’Tis likely some of these great beasts are little schooled in court ceremonies.”

===Chinese===

于是他们在巴维南深深漩流的河畔那洞里住下，在洞前吃了他们的冬至大宴——平生吃过的最奇异的一席：座位不是从前那样在红宝石或欧泊的高座上，而是在睡满雏菊与百里香的苔堤上；照明的不是加灵高厅那有魔法的红焰宝石，而是一堆柴火摇曳的光——照的不是那些冠着怪物、为世界奇观的柱子，而是沉睡山毛榉林更宏伟的柱子。代替加灵金篷下那片自放光的宝石仿造天庭的，是他们在受魔法的夏夜之下张幕而食：冬天的巨星——猎户、天狼、小犬——被举到近天顶处，让出它们在南天的旧路，给老人星与南天的陌生星群。树说话时，用的不是冬日秃枝吱嘎的嗓，而是叶的低语与甲虫在香风中的嗡鸣。灌木白的是花，不是霜；树下暗白的斑块不是雪，是夜里沉睡的野百合与林银莲。

森林里所有的生灵都来赴那席，因为它们无惧，从未见过人的脸。小小的树猿、鹦鹉、山雀、煤雀、鹪鹩、温良圆眼的狐猴、兔子、獾、睡鼠、花斑松鼠、溪边的河狸、鹳、渡鸦、鸨、怀里抱着崽的蛛猴：全都来用好奇的眼睛看这几位旅人。不止这些，林野的猛兽也来了：野牛、狼、巨爪的虎、熊、火眼的独角兽、象、雄狮与母狮之尊，都到火光里、到那片安静的草地上看他们。

「看来今晚我们在林中开御前会议，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「妙极了。不过你同我一起留神，必要时往它们中间掷几个火把。这些大兽，恐怕有几个没学过多少朝仪。」

===Original===

Juss answered, “And thou lovest me, do no such thing. There lieth this curse upon all this land of the Bhavinan, that whoso, whether he be man or beast, slayeth in this land or doeth here any deed of violence, there cometh down a curse upon him that in that instant must destroy and blast him forever off the face of the earth. Therefore it was I took away from Mivarsh his bow and arrows when we came down from Omprenne Edge, lest he should kill game for us and so a worse thing befall him.”

Mivarsh harkened not, but sat all a-quake, looking intently on a crocodile that came ponderously out upon the bank. And now he began to scream with terror, crying, “Save me! let me fly! give me my weapons! It was foretold me by a wise woman that a cocadrill-serpent must devour me at last!” Whereat the beasts drew back uneasily, and the crocodile, his small eyes wide, startled by Mivarsh’s cries and violent gestures, lurched with what speed he might back into the water.

---

Now in that place Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha and Mivarsh Faz abode for four moons’ space. Nothing they lacked of meat and drink, for the beasts of the forest, finding them well disposed, brought them of their store. Moreover, there came flying from the south, about the ending of the year, a martlet which alighted in Juss’s bosom and said to him, “The gentle Queen Sophonisba, fosterling of the Gods, had news of your coming. And because she knoweth you both mighty men of your hands and high of heart, therefore by me she sent you greeting.”

Juss said, “O little martlet, we would see thy Queen face to face, and thank her.”

“Ye must thank her,” said the bird, “in Koshtra Belorn.”

Brandoch Daha said, “That shall we fulfil. Thither only do our thoughts intend.”

“Your greatness,” said the martlet, “must approve that word. And know that it is easier to lay under you all the world in arms than to ascend up afoot into that mountain.”

“Thy wings were too weak to lift me, else I’d borrow them,” said Brandoch Daha.

But the martlet answered, “Not the eagle that flieth against the sun may alight on Koshtra Belorn. No foot may tread her, save of those blessed ones to whom the Gods gave leave ages ago, till they be come that the patient years await: men like unto the Gods in beauty and in power, who of their own might and main, unholpen by magic arts, shall force a passage up to her silent snows.”

===Chinese===

朱斯答道：「你若爱我，就别干这个。这巴维南全地带着这样的咒：无论人兽，谁在这地土里杀生、行强暴，咒诅就临到他，那一刻就要把他从地面上毁掉、烧灭。所以我先前下奥姆普伦崖时才收走米瓦尔什的弓箭，惟恐他为我们猎野味，反而遭了大祸。」

米瓦尔什没听，浑身发抖地坐着，紧盯一头从岸上笨重爬出的鳄鱼。这时他恐怖地尖叫起来，喊着：「救我！放我逃！把武器还我！有个聪明的女人给我算过命，说我末了必被一条鳄龙蛇吞掉！」众兽不安地退开；那鳄鱼瞪着小眼睛，被米瓦尔什的叫声与剧烈动作惊了，尽其可能快地一颠一颠缩回水里去了。

---

朱斯大人、布兰多赫·达哈大人与米瓦尔什·法兹在那里住了四个月。饮食一无缺乏，因为林中百兽见他们和善，运来自己的存粮。此外，约在岁末，一只无足燕从南方飞来，落进朱斯怀里，对他说：「温良的索芙妮丝芭女王（Queen Sophonisba），众神之养女（fosterling of the Gods），得了你们要来的消息。因为她知道你们两位都是手上功夫了得、心气高迈之人，便差我来向你们致意。」

朱斯说：「小无足燕，我们愿当面见你们女王，谢她。」

「你们要在科什特拉·贝洛恩谢她，」鸟说。

布兰多赫·达哈说：「那必成全。我们的心思只向着那里。」

「你们的伟大，」无足燕说，「须证实这句话。要知道：把全世界踏在兵锋之下，也容易过徒步登上那座山。」

「你的翅膀太弱，驮不动我；不然我倒要借用，」布兰多赫·达哈说。

无足燕却答：「逆日而飞的鹰，也不能落在科什特拉·贝洛恩上。没有脚能踏她——除了那些蒙众神在亘古之前赐准的有福者——直到那些坚忍的岁月所等候的人来到：像众神一样美、一样有能力的人，凭自己的膂力，不借魔法之助，强行开出一条路，登上她寂静的雪。」

===Original===

Brandoch Daha laughed. “Not the eagle?” he cried, “but thou, little flitter-jack?”

“Nought that hath feet,” said the martlet. “I have none.”

The Lord Brandoch Daha took it tenderly in his hand and held it high in the air, looking to the high lands in the south. The birches swaying by the Bhavinan were not more graceful nor the distant mountain-crags behind them more untameable to behold than he. “Fly to thy Queen,” he said, “and say thou spakest with Lord Juss beside the Bhavinan and with Lord Brandoch Daha of Demonland. Say unto her that we be they that were for to come; and that we, of our own might and main, ere spring be well turned summer, will come up to her in Koshtra Belorn to thank her for her gracious sendings.”

---

Now when it was April, and the sun moving among the signs of heaven was about departing out of Aries and entering into Taurus, and the melting of the snows in the high mountains had swollen all the streams to spate, filling the mighty river so that he brimmed his banks and swept by like a tide-race, Lord Juss said, “Now is the season propitious for our crossing of the flood of Bhavinan and setting forth into the mountains.”

“Willingly,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “But shall’s walk it, or swim it, or take to us wings? To me, that have many a time swum back and forth over Thunderfirth to whet mine appetite ere I brake my fast, ’tis a small matter of this river stream howso swift it runneth. But with our harness and weapons and all our gear, that were far other matter.”

“Is it for nought we are grown friends with them that do inhabit these woods?” said Juss. “The crocodile shall bear us over Bhavinan for the asking.”

“It is an ill fish,” said Mivarsh; “and it sore dislikes me.”

“Then here thou must abide,” said Brandoch Daha. “But be not dismayed, I will go with thee. The fish may bear us both at a draught and not founder.”

“It was a wise woman foretold it me,” answered Mivarsh, “that such a kind of serpent must be my bane. Yet be it according to your will.”

===Chinese===

布兰多赫·达哈大笑。「鹰不能？」他喊，「你倒能，小扑棱儿？」

「有脚的都不能，」无足燕说。「我就没有脚。」

布兰多赫·达哈大人把它温柔地托在手里，高举向空，望向南方的高地。巴维南河畔摇曳的银桦不及他优雅，它们背后远处的山岩也不及他难驯。「飞回你的女王那里去，」他说，「就说你在巴维南河边同朱斯大人、同魔国的布兰多赫·达哈大人说过话。告诉她：我们就是那将要来的人；凭我们自己的膂力，赶春天刚转成夏天，我们就上科什特拉·贝洛恩到她那里，谢她仁厚的馈问。」

---

到四月，太阳行在诸天宫之间、将出白羊宫入金牛宫，高山雪水融化，诸溪俱涨，灌满大河，叫它漫过堤岸、像潮流一般扫过。朱斯大人说：「现在正是我们渡巴维南洪流、出发进山的吉时。」

「乐意之至，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「可我们是走过去、游过去，还是长翅膀？在我，曾多次往返泅渡雷湾、好开早饭前开开胃口，这样一条河再急也是小事。可带上我们的甲胄兵刃和全部行装，就完全是另一回事了。」

「我们同这些林中居民交了朋友，岂是白交的？」朱斯说。「说一声，鳄鱼就驮我们过巴维南。」

「那是条恶鱼，」米瓦尔什说，「我实在不喜欢它。」

「那你只好留在这里，」布兰多赫·达哈说。「不过别怕，我陪你一起。这鱼一趟能驮我们两个，沉不了。」

「有位聪明的女人给我算过，」米瓦尔什答，「说这一类的蛇必是我的死因。但就照你们的意吧。」

===Original===

So they whistled them up the crocodile; and first the Lord Juss fared over Bhavinan, riding on the back of that serpent with all his gear and weapons of war, and landed several hundred paces down stream for the stream was very strong; and thereafter the crocodile returning to the north bank took the Lord Brandoch Daha and Mivarsh Faz and put them across in like manner. Mivarsh put on a gallant face, but rode as near the tail as might be, fingering certain herbs from his wallet that were good against serpents, his lips moving in urgent supplication to his gods. When they were come ashore they thanked the crocodile and bade him farewell and went their way swiftly through the woods. And Mivarsh, as one new loosed from prison, went before them with a light step, singing and snapping his fingers.

Now had they for three days or four a devious journey through the foothills, and thereafter made their dwelling for forty days’ space in the Zia valley, above the gorges. Here the valley widens to a flat-floored amphitheatre, and lean limestone crags tower heavenward on every side. High in the south, couched above great gray moraines, the Zia glacier, wrinkle-backed like some dragon survived out of the elder chaos, thrusts his snout into the valley. Here out of his caves of ice the young river thunders, casting up a spray where rainbows hover in bright weather. The air blows sharp from the glacier, and alpine flowers and shrubs feed on the sunlight.

Here they gathered them good store of food. And every morning they were afoot before the sunrise, to ascend the mountains and make sure their practice ere they should attempt the greater peaks.
