So they explored all the spurs of Tetrachnampf and Islargyn, and those peaks themselves; the rock peaks of the lower Nuanner range overlooking Bhavinan; the snow peaks east of Islargyn: Avsek, Kiurmsur, Myrsu, Byrshnargyn, and Borch Mehephtharsk, loftiest of the range, by all his ridges, dwelling a week on the moraines of the Mehephtharsk glacier above the upland valley of Foana; and westward the dolomite group of Burdjazarshra and the great wall of Shilack.

===Chinese===

于是他们唤来鳄鱼；朱斯大人先渡巴维南，带着全副甲胄兵刃骑在那蛇的背上，因水流太急，在下游几百步处登了岸；随后鳄鱼回到北岸，照样把布兰多赫·达哈大人与米瓦尔什·法兹渡了过来。米瓦尔什强作镇定，却尽量骑近尾巴，一手捏着钱袋里几味克蛇的药草，嘴唇急急地向他众神祷告。上岸后他们谢过鳄鱼，与它道别，快步穿林而去。米瓦尔什像新出狱的囚犯，轻步走在前面，又唱又捻指作响。

此后三四天，他们在山麓间曲折前行；随后在齐亚谷、峡沟之上住了四十天。这里河谷展宽为一片平底圆场，瘦削的石灰岩峭壁四面顶天。南面高处，卧在巨大灰色冰碛之上，齐亚冰川——皱背隆起，像上古混沌里活下来的一条龙——把吻伸进谷中。年轻的大河从它的冰洞里轰雷般涌出，扬起水沫，晴日里虹霓在沫上徘徊。冰川上吹来的风凛冽，高山花木饱餐阳光。

他们在那里储备了充足的食物。每天清晨日出之前起身登山，先练熟身手，再去碰那些更大的峰。他们踏遍了特特拉赫南普夫与伊斯拉尔金各条支脉，把那些峰本身也踏遍；踏遍了俯瞰巴维南的下努安纳山脉的岩峰；伊斯拉尔金以东的雪峰：阿夫塞克、基乌尔姆苏尔、缪尔苏、贝尔什纳尔金，与全脉最高的博尔赫·梅赫普塔尔斯克——沿它各条棱都走过，在福阿纳高地谷上方的梅赫普塔尔斯克冰川碛上宿了一星期；还有西边布尔贾扎尔沙的白云岩群与希拉克大墙。

===Original===

Now were their muscles by these exercises grown like bands of iron, and they hardy as mountain bears and sure of foot as mountain goats. So on the ninth day of May they crossed the Zia Pass and camped on the rocks under the south wall of Tetrachnampf nan Tshark. The sun went down, like blood, in a cloudless sky. On either hand and before them, the snows stretched blue and silent. The air of those high snowfields was bitter cold. A league and more to the south a line of black cliffs bounded the glacier-basin. Over that black wall, twelve miles away, Koshtra Belorn and Koshtra Pivrarcha towered against an opal heaven.

While they supped in the fading light, Juss said, “The wall thou seest is called the Barriers of Emshir. Though over it lieth the straight way to Koshtra Pivrarcha, yet is it not our way, but an ill way. For, first, that barrier hath till now been held unclimbable, and so proven even by half-gods that alone assayed it.”

“I await not thy second reason,” said Brandoch Daha. “Thou hast had thy way until now, and now thou shalt give me mine in this, to come with me tomorrow and show how thou and I make of such barriers a puff of smoke if they stand in the path between us and our fixed ends.”

“Were it only this,” answered Juss, “I would not gainsay thee. But not senseless rocks alone are we set to deal with if we take this road. Seest thou where the Barriers end in the east against yonder monstrous pyramid of tumbled crags and hanging glaciers that shuts out our prospect eastaway? Menksur men call it, but in heaven it hath a more dreadful name: Ela Mantissera, which is to say, the Bed of the Mantichores. O Brandoch Daha, I will climb with thee what unscaled cliff thou list, and I will fight with thee against the most grisfullest beasts that ever grazed by the Tartarian streams. But both these things in one moment of time, that were a rash part and a foolish.”

But Brandoch Daha laughed, and answered him, “To nought else may I liken thee, O Juss, but to the sparrow-camel. To whom they said, ‘Fly,’ and it answered, ‘I cannot, for I am a camel’; and when they said, ‘Carry,’ it answered, ‘I cannot, for I am a bird.’ ”

“Wilt thou egg me on so much?” said Juss.

“Ay,” said Brandoch Daha, “if thou wilt be assish.”

“Wilt thou quarrel?” said Juss.

“Thou knowest me,” said Brandoch Daha.

===Chinese===

经这些操练，他们的筋肉如今硬如铁条，悍如山熊，脚踏实地如山羊。五月九日，他们越过齐亚隘口，在特特拉赫南普夫·南·恰尔克南墙下的乱石上扎营。太阳在无云的天空里落下，红得像血。左右与面前，雪原铺展，青蓝而沉默。那些高山雪原的空气苦寒。南面一里格开外，一道黑岩的线围着冰川盆地。越过那道黑墙，十二英里外，科什特拉·贝洛恩与科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡顶着一片蛋白石色的天。

他们在渐暗的光里用晚饭时，朱斯说：「你看见的那道墙，叫埃姆希尔壁垒。越过它虽是去科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡的正路，却不是我们的路，是条歹路。第一，那道壁垒迄今被公认为不可攀，连半神独自尝试过，也都证实了。」

「我等不及你的第二条理由了，」布兰多赫·达哈说。「到如今都是你拿主意；这一回你得让我拿我的：明天跟我来，看看你我怎样把挡在我们与既定目标之间的这种壁垒，变成一缕烟。」

「若只是这个，」朱斯答，「我不驳你。可走这条路，要对付的就不只是无知的岩石了。看见没有，壁垒在东端尽头，抵着那边一座乱岩与悬冰川垒成的巨大金字塔，把我们的东望堵死了？人叫它门克苏尔，天上有名字却更可怕：埃拉·曼蒂塞拉，意思是，曼提克之床。布兰多赫·达哈啊，你要爬哪座没爬过的崖，我都陪你去；你要斗鞑靼溪边吃草的最凶恶的兽，我都陪你打。可两样事挤在同一刻，就是鲁莽，就是愚蠢。」

布兰多赫·达哈却大笑，答道：「朱斯，我只能把你比作雀骆驼。人对它说『飞』，它答『我不能，我是骆驼』；对它说『驮』，它答『我不能，我是鸟』。」

「你这样撺掇我？」朱斯说。

「是，」布兰多赫·达哈说，「如果你要蠢。」

「你要吵架？」朱斯说。

「你知道我，」布兰多赫·达哈说。

===Original===

“Well,” said Juss, “thy counsel hath been right once and saved us, for nine times that it hath been wrong, and my counsel saved thee from an evil end. If ill behap us, it shall be set down that it had from thy peevish will original.” And they wrapped them in their cloaks and slept.

On the morrow they rose betimes and set forth south across the snows that were crisp and hard for the frosts of the night. The Barriers, as it were but a stone’s-throw removed, stood black before them; starlight swallowed up size and distance that showed only by walking, as still they walked and still that wall seemed no nearer nor no larger. Twice and thrice they dipped into a valley or crossed a raised-up fold of the glacier; till they stood at break of day below the smooth blank wall frozen and bleak, with never a ledge in sight great enough to bear snow, barring their passage southward.

They halted and ate and scanned the wall before them. And ill to do with it seemed. So they searched for an ascent, and found at last a spot where the glacier swelled higher, a mile or less from the western shoulder of Ela Mantissera. Here the cliff was but four or five hundred feet high; yet smooth enow and ill enow to look on; yet their likeliest choice.

Some while it was ere they might get a footing on that wall, but at length Brandoch Daha, standing on Juss’s shoulder, found him a hold where no hold showed from below, and with great travail fought a passage up the rock to a stance some hundred feet above them, whence sitting sure on a broad ledge great enough to hold six or seven folk at a time he played up Lord Juss on the rope and after him Mivarsh. An hour and a half it cost them for that short climb.

“The northeast buttress of Ill Stack was children’s gruel to this,” said Lord Juss.

“There’s more aloft,” said Lord Brandoch Daha, lying back against the precipice, his hands clasped behind his head, his feet a-dangle over the ledge. “In thine ear, Juss: I would not go first on the rope again on such a pitch for all the wealth of Impland.”

“Wilt repent and return?” said Juss.

“If thou’lt be last down,” he answered. “If not, I’d liever risk what waits untried above us. If it prove worse, I am confirmed atheist.”

===Chinese===

「好吧，」朱斯说，「你的主意对过一回、救过我们，错的时候倒有九回，是我的主意救你脱了恶终。若我们遭了殃，记下账来：根子在你这乖戾的性子。」他们裹上大氅睡了。

次日他们早早起来，南行穿过被夜寒冻得脆硬的雪原。壁垒仿佛只隔一掷之遥，黑黑地立在面前；星光吞掉了大小与距离，只有走才知道远近——他们走着走着，那墙仿佛总不见近、不见大。他们两度三度下到洼地、翻过冰川隆起的褶；到破晓时分，站在了那平整光秃、冻结荒凉的墙下，眼前看不见一条容得下雪的岩台，堵死了南行之路。

他们停下进食，端详面前的墙。难办。他们找路，最后找到一处冰川隆得较高的地方，在埃拉·曼蒂塞拉西肩一英里不到处。这里崖高只有四五百英尺；却足够平滑、足够难看；但这是他们最可行的选择。

好一阵他们才在这墙上立足；末了布兰多赫·达哈踩上朱斯的肩，在下面看不见把手的地方找到一个把手，费尽力气攀上一段岩，到了他们上方百来英尺的一处立足点，稳坐在一条宽台上——台宽得一次能站六七人——把朱斯大人用绳拉上去，再拉米瓦尔什。这短短一爬花了他们一个半钟头。

「伊利斯塔克的东北扶壁比起这个是小儿科的稀粥，」朱斯大人说。

「上面还有更妙的，」布兰多赫·达哈大人仰靠着绝壁说，双手枕在脑后，脚在岩台上晃荡。「朱斯，附耳过来：这样的坡度，把整个妖国的财富都给我，我也不再打头绳了。」

「你悔了，要回去？」朱斯说。

「只要你最后下，」他答。「不然，我宁肯赌一赌上面没试过的。要是更糟，我就成了坚定的无神论者。」

===Original===

Lord Juss leaned out, holding by the rock with his right hand, scanning the wall beside and above them. An instant he hung so, then drew back. His square jaw was set, and his teeth glinted under his dark moustachios something fiercely, as a thunder-beam betwixt dark sky and sea in a night of thunder. His nostrils widened, as of a warhorse at the call of battle; his eyes were like the violet levin-brand, and all his body hardened like a bowstring drawn as he grasped his sharp sword and pulled it forth grating and singing from its sheath.

Brandoch Daha sprang afoot and drew his sword, Zeldornius’s loom. “What stirreth?” he cried. “Thou look’st ghastly. That look thou hadst when thou tookest the helm and our prows swung westward toward Kartadza Sound, and the fate of Demonland and all the world beside hung in thine hand for wail or bliss.”

“There’s little sword-room,” said Juss. And again he looked forth eastward and upward along the cliff. Brandoch Daha looked over his shoulder. Mivarsh took his bow and set an arrow on the string.

“It hath scented us down the wind,” said Brandoch Daha.

Small time was there to ponder. Swinging from hold to hold across the dizzy precipice, as an ape swingeth from bough to bough, the beast drew near. The shape of it was as a lion, but bigger and taller, the colour a dull red, and it had prickles lancing out behind, as of a porcupine; its face a man’s face, if aught so hideous might be conceived of human kind, with staring eyeballs, low wrinkled brow, elephant ears, some wispy mangy likeness of a lion’s mane, huge bony chaps, brown bloodstained gubber-tushes grinning betwixt bristly lips. Straight for the ledge it made, and as they braced them to receive it, with a great swing heaved a man’s height above them and leaped down upon their ledge from aloft betwixt Juss and Brandoch Daha ere they were well aware of its changed course. Brandoch Daha smote at it a great swashing blow and cut off its scorpion tail; but it clawed Juss’s shoulder, smote down Mivarsh, and charged like a lion upon Brandoch Daha, who, missing his footing on the narrow edge of rock, fell backwards a great fall, clear of the cliff, down to the snow an hundred feet beneath them.

===Chinese===

朱斯大人探身出去，右手扒着岩，细看旁边与上面的壁。他那样悬了一瞬，收回来。他的方颌咬紧，黑髭下牙齿凶狠地闪光，像雷雨之夜里黑天与海之间的一道雷光。他鼻孔张开，像战马听见战号；眼睛像紫色的雷火；他握住利剑，从鞘里铮铮唱着拔出来时，全身绷紧如拉满的弓弦。

布兰多赫·达哈跳起来拔剑——泽尔多尼厄斯的那柄。「什么动了？」他喊，「你脸色吓人。你那神色，就是你掌舵、我们的船首转向卡尔塔扎水道那一天的神色——魔国与全世界的命运，是祸是福，都悬在你手里。」

「这里没有多少使剑的余地，」朱斯说。他又朝东、朝上沿崖望。布兰多赫·达哈从他肩上望去。米瓦尔什取弓搭箭。

「它顺风闻到我们了，」布兰多赫·达哈说。

没有工夫细想。那兽在令人目眩的绝壁间把手换把手地荡过来，像猿在树枝间荡。它的形像如狮，却更高更大，颜色暗红，身后放出箭刺，如豪猪；脸是人的脸——若人脸竟能设想得那样狰狞：暴突的眼球，低皱的额，象耳，几缕癞痢似的鬃毛，巨大的骨颚，龇在硬唇间的棕色带血獠牙。它直奔岩台而来；他们刚摆好架势接它，它却猛一荡，荡到他们一人高之上，趁他们未察觉它换了路线，从高处直跳落在朱斯与布兰多赫·达哈之间的岩台上。布兰多赫·达哈抡剑猛劈，斩掉它的蝎尾；它却抓伤朱斯的肩，扑倒米瓦尔什，又像狮子一样直扑布兰多赫·达哈；他在窄窄的岩棱上失足，仰面直跌下崖，落在他们下方一百英尺的雪上。

===Original===

As it craned over, minded to follow and make an end of him, Juss smote it in the hinder parts and on the ham, shearing away the flesh from the thigh bone, and his sword came with a clank against the brazen claws of its foot. So with a horrid bellow it turned on Juss, rearing like a horse; and it was three heads greater than a tall man in stature when it reared aloft, and the breadth of its chest like the chest of a bear. The stench of its breath choked Juss’s mouth and his senses sickened, but he slashed it athwart the belly, a great round-armed blow, cutting open its belly so that the guts fell out. Again he hewed at it, but missed, and his sword came against the rock, and was shivered into pieces. So when that noisome vermin fell forward on him roaring like a thousand lions, Juss grappled with it, running in beneath its body and clasping it and thrusting his arms into its inward parts, to rip out its vitals if so he might. So close he grappled it that it might not reach him with its murthering teeth, but its claws sliced off the flesh from his left knee downward to the ankle bone, and it fell on him and crushed him on the rock, breaking in the bones of his breast. And Juss, for all his bitter pain and torment, and for all he was well nigh stifled by the sore stink of the creature’s breath and the stink of its blood and puddings blubbering about his face and breast, yet by his great strength wrastled with that fell and filthy man-eater. And ever he thrust his right hand, armed with the hilt and stump of his broken sword, yet deeper into its belly until he searched out its heart and did his will upon it, slicing the heart asunder like a lemon and severing and tearing all the great vessels about the heart until the blood gushed about him like a spring. And like a caterpillar the beast curled up and straightened out in its death spasms, and it rolled and fell from that ledge, a great fall, and lay by Brandoch Daha, the foulest beside the fairest of all earthly beings, reddening the pure snow with its blood. And the spines that grew on the hinder parts of the beast went out and in like the sting of a new-dead wasp that goes out and in continually. It fell not clean to the snow, as by the care of heaven was fallen Brandoch Daha, but smote an edge of rock near the bottom, and that strook out its brains. There it lay in its blood, gaping to the sky.

===Chinese===

它探身向下，想跟下去结果了他；朱斯砍中它的后身与腿弯，把肉从股骨上削下来，剑当的一声磕在它脚上的铜爪上。它发出可怖的吼声，转过身来对付朱斯，像马一样人立而起；它人立起来比高个子男人还高出三个头，胸膛宽得像熊。它呼吸的恶臭呛满朱斯的口，他的感官发昏；但他抡圆臂膀横斩它的肚腹，开膛破肚，肠子流了出来。他再一剑砍去，砍空了，剑磕在岩上，碎成几段。于是当那肮脏的害虫像千狮齐吼般向他扑倒时，朱斯抱住它，钻到它身子底下，搂住它，把双臂捅进它的脏腑，想掏出它的命。他贴得那样近，它杀人的牙够不着他，可它的爪把他左膝到踝骨的肉一条条削下来；它压倒他，把他压在岩石上，压断了他的胸骨。朱斯忍着剧痛与折磨，几乎被那东西呼吸、血污与糊在他脸上胸上的脏器的恶臭闷死，仍凭他伟大的膂力与那凶暴污秽的食人兽搏斗。他的右手握着断剑的柄与残刃，一直往它肚里捅得更深，直到摸着它的心，对它任意施为：把心像柠檬一样切开，把心周围的大血管一一割断撕裂，直到血像泉水一样涌他一身。那兽像毛虫一样在死的痉挛里蜷起又伸直，翻滚着从那岩台上跌下去，跌了老高，躺在布兰多赫·达哈旁边——地上万物中最污秽的挨着最美好的——用它的血染红纯洁的雪。它后身的箭刺像新死黄蜂的毒刺那样不停地伸出缩进。它不像布兰多赫·达哈——天照应着叫他不偏不倚落在雪上——那样干净落地，而是磕在近底的岩棱上，磕出了脑浆。它躺在血泊里，朝天张着口。

===Original===

Now was Juss stretched face downward as one dead, on that giddy edge of rock. Mivarsh had saved him, seizing him by the foot and drawing him back to safety when the beast fell. A sight of terror he was, clotted from head to toe with the beast’s blood and his own. Mivarsh bound his wounds and laid him tenderly as he might back against the cliff, then peered down a long while to know if the beast were dead indeed.

When he had gazed downward earnestly so long that his eyes watered with the strain, and still the beast stirred not, Mivarsh prostrated himself and made supplication saying aloud, “O Shlimphli, Shlamphi, and Shebamri, gods of my father and my father’s fathers, have pity of your child, if as I dearly trow your power extendeth over this far and forbidden country no less than over Impland, where your child hath ever worshipped you in your holy places, and taught my sons and my daughters to revere your holy names, and made an altar in mine house, pointed by the stars in manner ordained from of old, and offered up my seventh-born son and was minded to offer up my seventh-born daughter thereon, in meekness and righteousness according to your holy will; but this I might not do, since you vouchsafed me not a seventh daughter, but six only. Wherefore I beseech you, of your holy names’ sake, strengthen my hand to let down this my companion safely by the rope, and thereafter bring me safely down from this rock, howsoever he be a devil and an unbeliever; O save his life, save both their lives. For I am sure that if these be not saved alive, never shall your child return, but in this far land starve and die like an insect that dureth but for a day.”

===Chinese===

朱斯面朝下摊在那令人目眩的岩沿上，像死人一般。是米瓦尔什救了他：兽跌下去时，米瓦尔什抓住他的脚，把他拖回安全处。他那样子骇人：从头到脚结满兽血与人血的痂。米瓦尔什包扎好他的伤口，尽力轻柔地让他靠壁躺好，然后朝下望了很久，看那兽是不是真死了。

他凝神下望得眼睛都酸出泪水，那兽仍一动不动；米瓦尔什伏倒在地，大声祷告说：「什林弗利、什兰菲、谢巴姆里啊——我父与我列祖的神——怜恤你们的孩子！我深信你们的能力既盖妖国，也盖这遥远禁地，一如往昔；你们的孩子在妖国圣地一向敬拜你们，教我的儿女敬畏你们的圣名，在我家中设一座坛，照亘古规定的那样以星定向，献上过我第七个儿子，还想把第七个女儿也献在上面，温柔而公义地遵你们的圣意；只是这事我没能作成，因为你们没有赐我第七个女儿，只赐了六个。所以我求你们，为你们圣名的缘故，坚固我的手，叫我用绳把我这位同伴平安放下去；然后再把我自己从这岩上平安放下去——尽管他是魔鬼、是不信的人。哦，救他的命，救他们两个的命。因为我确知：他们两个若不能活着得救，你们的孩子就永远回不去了，必在这远方像朝生暮死的虫豸一样饿死。」

===Original===

So prayed Mivarsh. And belike the high Gods were moved to pity of his innocence, hearing him so cry for help unto his mumbo-jumbos, where no help was; and belike they were not minded that those lords of Demonland should there die evilly before their time, unhonoured, unsung. Howsoever, Mivarsh arose and made fast the rope about Lord Juss, knotting it cunningly beneath the arms that it might not tighten in the lowering and crush his breast and ribs, and so with much ado lowered him down to the foot of the cliff. Thereafter came Mivarsh himself down that perilous wall, and albeit for many a time he thought his bane was upon him, yet by good cragsmanship spurred by cold necessity he gat him down at last. Being down, he delayed not to minister to his companions, who came to themselves with heavy groaning. But when Lord Juss was come to himself he did his healing art both on himself and on Lord Brandoch Daha, so that in a while they were able to stand upon their feet, albeit something stiff and weary and like to vomit. And it was by then the third hour past noon.

While they rested, beholding where the beast mantichora lay in his blood, Juss spake and said, “It is to be said of thee, O Brandoch Daha, that thou today hast done both the worst and the best. The worst, when thou wast so stubborn set to fare upon this climb which hath come within a little of spilling both thee and me. The best, whenas thou didst smite off his tail. Was that by policy or by chance?”

“Why,” said he, “I was never so poor a man of my hands that I need turn braggart. ’Twas handiest to my sword, and it disliked me to see it wagging. Did aught lie on it?”

“The sting of his tail,” answered Juss, “were competent for thine or my destruction, and it grazed but our little finger.”

“Thou speakest like a book,” said Brandoch Daha. “Else might I scarce know thee for my noble friend, being berayed with blood as a buffalo with mire. Be not angry with me, if I am most at ease to windward of thee.”

===Chinese===

米瓦尔什这样祷告了。大约高天的众神怜他那无辜，听见他向他的偶像们——那里其实无甚可求——这样哭喊求助；也大约他们不愿魔国诸大人就在那里、未到时辰、无声无息地横死。无论如何，米瓦尔什起身，把绳在朱斯大人身上系牢，臂下打了个巧结，免得下放时勒紧他的胸肋；然后费了大劲把他缒到崖脚。随后米瓦尔什自己也下了那险墙，虽然好几次他都觉得死到临头，终究凭着寒苦逼出来的好岩技下来了。一到下面，他马上救护同伴；两人沉沉呻吟着苏醒过来。朱斯大人一醒，便对自己与布兰多赫·达哈大人施行医术，不多时两人便能站起来了，虽然又僵又乏、直想呕吐。那时已过午后三点。

他们歇着，望着那曼提克躺在血泊里；朱斯开言道：「布兰多赫·达哈，今天你可说又干了最糟的、又干了最好的。最糟，是你固执非要来爬这一趟，差一点把你我两人的命都送掉；最好，是你一剑斩了它的尾。那是出于算计，还是出于碰巧？」

「这有什么，」他说，「我从来不是手上功夫差到要吹牛的人。它离我的剑最近，我又看不惯它摇来摆去。那上面有什么讲究？」

「它尾上的毒刺，」朱斯答，「足够要你或我的命；我们却只蹭破了小指头。」

「你说得像本书，」布兰多赫·达哈说。「不然我真认不出你这高贵的朋友——糊满血，像水牛糊满泥。别怪我站你上风口最舒服。」

===Original===

Juss laughed. “If thou be not too nice,” he said, “go to the beast and dabble thyself too with the blood of his bowels. Nay, I mock not; it is most needful. These be enemies not of mankind only, but each of other: walking every one by himself, loathing every one his kind living or dead, so that in all the world there abideth nought loathlier unto them than the blood of their own kind, the least smell whereof they do abhor as a mad dog abhorreth water. And ’tis a clinging smell. So are we after this encounter most sure against them.”

---

That night they camped at the foot of a spur of Avsek, and set forth at dawn down the long valley eastward. All day they heard the roaring of mantichores from the desolate flanks of Ela Mantissera that showed now no longer as a pyramid but as a long-backed screen, making the southern rampart of that valley. It was ill going, and they somewhat shaken. Day was nigh gone when beyond the eastern slopes of Ela they came where the white waters of the river they followed thundered together with a black water rushing down from the southwest. Below, the river ran east in a wide valley dropping afar to tree-clad depths. In the fork above the watersmeet the rocks enclosed a high green knoll, like some fragment of a kindlier clime that over-lived into an age of ruin.

“Here, too,” said Juss, “my dream walked with me. And if it be ill crossing there where this stream breaketh into a dozen branching cataracts a little above the watersmeet, yet well I think ’tis our only crossing.” So, ere the light should fade, they crossed that perilous edge above the waterfalls, and slept on the green knoll.

That knoll Juss named Throstlegarth, after a thrush that waked them next morning, singing in a little wind-stunted mountain thorn that grew among the rocks. Strangely sounded that homely song on the cold mountain side, under the unhallowed heights of Ela, close to the confines of those enchanted snows which guard Koshtra Belorn.

===Chinese===

朱斯大笑。「你若不嫌腌臜，」他说，「到那畜生那儿去，也拿它的脏血抹一抹自己。不，我不是取笑；这是最要紧的。这些家伙不但是人类的仇敌，也彼此为仇：各自独来独往，憎恶一切同类，死的活的都憎；所以全世界对它们来说，再没有比它们自己同类的血更可憎的东西，那气味它们避之如疯狗避水。而这气味经久不散。这一场遭遇之后，我们从此不怕它们了。」

---

当夜他们在阿夫塞克一条支脉脚下扎营，黎明出发沿长谷东行。整日他们都听得见埃拉·曼蒂塞拉荒凉山坡上曼提克的吼声；它如今显出的不再是金字塔，而是一道长背的屏风，作那山谷的南墙。路难走，人也有些震伤。天将尽时，在埃拉东坡之外，他们来到一处：他们所循的那条白水，与一条从西南奔下的黑水轰然相汇。再往下，河在宽谷中东流，远远落向覆林的深处。合水口上方的岔口里，岩石围着一座高高的绿丘，像一片更温柔气候的残片，幸存进了这残毁的世代。

「这里，」朱斯说，「我的梦也陪我走过。这道溪在合水口上方一点碎成十几股分支瀑布，渡过去虽难，我却深信那是我们惟一的渡口。」于是趁光未灭，他们越过瀑布上方那道险棱，在绿丘上过夜。

那丘，朱斯名之为斯罗斯尔加斯，因第二天早晨一只鸫鸟叫醒他们，在一丛风摧矮小的山山楂里歌唱，山楂长在岩石间。那家常的歌在冷山坡上、在埃拉不洁的高地下、紧挨着守卫科什特拉·贝洛恩的魔法雪原边上，响得奇异。

===Original===

No sight of the high mountains had they from Throstlegarth, nor, for a long while, from the bed of that straight steep glen of the black waters up which now their journey lay. Rugged spurs and buttresses shut them in. High on the left bank above the cataracts they made their way, buffeted by the wind that leaped and charged among the crags, their ears sated with the roaring sound of waters, their eyes filled with the spray blown upward. And Mivarsh followed after them. Silent they fared, for the way was steep and in such a wind and such a noise of torrents a man must shout lustily if he would be heard. Very desolate was that valley, having a dark aspect and a ghastful, such as a man might look for in the infernal glens of Pyriphlegethon or Acheron. No living thing they saw, save at whiles high above them an eagle sailing down the wind, and once a beast’s form running in the hollow mountain side. This stood at gaze, lifting up its foul human platter-face with glittering eyes bloody and great as saucers; scented its fellow’s blood, started, and fled among the crags.

So fared they for the space of three hours, and so, coming suddenly round a shoulder of the hill, stood on the upper threshold of that glen at the gates of a flat upland valley. Here they beheld a sight to darken all earth’s glories and strike dumb all her singers with its grandeur. Framed in the crags of the hillsides, canopied by blue heaven, Koshtra Pivrarcha stood before them. So huge he was that even here at six miles’ distance the eye might not at a glance behold him, but must sweep back and forth as over a broad landscape from the ponderous roots of the mountain where they sprang black and sheer from the glacier, up the vast face, where buttress was piled upon buttress and tower upon tower in a blinding radiance of ice-hung precipice and snow-filled gully, to the lone heights where like spears menacing high heaven the white teeth of the summit-ridge cleft the sky. From right to left he filled nigh a quarter of the heavens, from the graceful peak of Ailinon looking over his western shoulder, to where on the east the snowy slopes of Jalchi shut in the prospect, hiding Koshtra Belorn.

===Chinese===

从斯罗斯尔加斯望不见高山；此后许久，沿着他们如今上行的黑水那笔直陡峭的谷床，也望不见。嶙峋的支脉与扶壁围困着他们。他们在瀑布上方高的左岸行进，被在岩间腾跃冲锋的风撞着，耳朵灌满水吼，眼里满是扬上来的飞沫。米瓦尔什跟在他们后面。他们默默而行：路陡，这样的风这样的涛声里，人要叫人听见非得放声喊不可。那谷荒凉已极，面目阴黑可怖，像人在皮里弗勒格通或阿克隆的地狱润谷里所能指望见到的那样。活物一个不见，只偶尔有鹰高高地乘风滑下；又有一次，一只兽的形影在空谷坡里奔跑。那兽站住张望，抬起它那张肮脏的人盘子脸，眼睛血红、亮而大如茶碟；它嗅出同类的血，一惊，逃进乱岩里去了。

他们这样走了三个钟头，忽然绕过一道山肩，站在那谷的上门槛、一片平坦高山谷的门口。他们在这里看见一副景象，足以叫大地上一切荣光失色，叫一切歌人哑口于它的宏伟：科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡立在面前，嵌在山坡的乱岩间，罩着蓝天。它如此巨大，即便在此六英里之外，眼睛也不能一眼收尽它，只能像扫视一片广阔的风景那样来回扫视：从山沉重的根——它们从冰川里又黑又陡地拔起——向上，到那浩大的脸面——那里扶壁叠着扶壁、塔叠着塔，在冰悬的绝壁与积雪的沟壑的一片炫目光辉里——直到孤高的高处，顶峰山脊的白牙如矛一样逼指高天，劈开天空。从右到左，它占了将近四分之一的天：从俯在它西肩的艾利农那优雅的峰，到东面亚尔奇的雪坡封住视野、藏起科什特拉·贝洛恩。

===Original===

They camped that evening on the left moraine of the High Glacier of Temarm. Long spidery streamers of cloud, filmy as the gauze of a lady’s veil, blew eastward from the spires on the ridge, signs of wild weather aloft.

Juss said, “Glassy clear is the air. That forerunneth not fair weather.”

“Well, time shall wait for us if need be,” said Brandoch Daha. “So mightily my desire crieth unto me from those horns of ice that, having once looked on them, I had as lief die as leave them unclimbed. But of thee, O Juss, I make some marvel. Thou wast bidden inquire in Koshtra Belorn, and sure she were easier won than Koshtra Pivrarcha, going behind Jalchi by the snowfields and so avoiding her great western cliffs.”

“There is a saw in Impland,” answered Juss, “ ‘Ware of a tall wife.’ Even so there lieth a curse on any that shall attempt Koshtra Belorn that hath not first looked down upon her; and he shall have his death or ever he have his will. And from one point only of earth may a man look down on Koshtra Belorn; and ’tis from yonder unascended tooth of ice where thou seest the last beam burn. For that is the topmost pinnacle of Koshtra Pivrarcha. And it is the highest point of the stablished earth.”

They were silent a minute’s space. Then Juss spake: “Thou wast ever greatest amongst us as a mountaineer. Which way likes thee best for our climbing up him?”

“O Juss,” said Brandoch Daha, “on ice and snow thou art my master. Therefore give me thy rede. For mine own choice and pleasure, I have settled it this hour and more: namely to ascend into the gap between the two mountains, and thence turn westward up the east ridge of Pivrarcha.”

“It is the fearsomest climb to look on,” said Juss, “and belike the grandest, and for both counts I had wagered it thy choice. That gap hight the Gates of Zimiamvia. It, and the Koshtra glacier that runneth up to it, lieth under the weird I told thee of. It were our death to adventure there ere we had looked down upon Koshtra Belorn; which done, the charm is broke for us, and from that time forth it needeth but our own might and skill and a high heart to accomplish whatsoever we desire.”

“Why then, the great north buttress,” cried Brandoch Daha. “So shall she not behold us as we climb, until we come forth on the highest tooth and overlook her and tame her to our will.”

===Chinese===

当晚他们在特马姆高冰川的左侧冰碛上扎营。细长的蛛丝般的云旗，薄如贵妇面纱的绢，从山脊的尖塔上向东飘——高空将有狂风的征兆。

朱斯说：「空气玻璃般的清。那可不是好天气的先兆。」

「也好，需要的话，时间会等我们，」布兰多赫·达哈说。「那些冰角这样向我高声呼喊，我一见它们，宁可死也不肯丢下不爬。倒是你，朱斯，叫我有点诧异。你受命到科什特拉·贝洛恩去问；她当然比皮弗拉尔卡好登：走亚尔奇后面的雪原，就避开她的大西壁了。」

「妖国有句谚语，」朱斯答，「『当心高个子的老婆。』凡不曾先俯瞰过她就径直去攀科什特拉·贝洛恩的人，都带着咒：他要死，还死在如愿之前。而全地只有一处能叫人俯瞰科什特拉·贝洛恩：就是你看见最后一抹光在烧的那颗未登的冰齿。因为那是科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡最高的塔尖，是立定的大地的至高点。」

他们沉默了一分钟。朱斯又说：「论登山，你从来是我们中间最强的。你看我们该从哪边爬它？」

「朱斯，」布兰多赫·达哈说，「冰和雪上你是我的师父。所以还是你拿主意。至于我自己的拣选与喜欢，一个多钟头前我已定下：先登上两山之间的隘口，从那里转向西，沿皮弗拉尔卡的东山脊往上。」

「那是看上去最骇人的一登，」朱斯说，「多半也是最宏大的一登；为这两条，我就料到你会挑它。那隘口名叫齐米亚姆维亚之门。它，和通往它的科什特拉冰川，都在我说过的那咒之下。没俯瞰过科什特拉·贝洛恩之前闯那里，就是我们的死；俯瞰之后，咒对我们破了，从那时起，只需要我们自己的膂力、技艺与一颗高心，便能成全我们所愿的一切。」

「那就走大北扶壁，」布兰多赫·达哈喊道。「这样我们爬的时候她就看不见我们，直到我们登上最高的冰齿、俯瞰她、把她驯服在我们意志之下。」

===Original===

So they supped and slept. But the wind cried among the crags all night long, and in the morning snow and sleet blotted out the mountains. All day the storm held, and in a lull they struck camp and came down again to Throstlegarth, and there abode nine days and nine nights in wind and rain and battering hail.

On the tenth day the weather abated, and they went up and crossed the glacier and lodged them in a cave in the rock at the foot of the great north buttress of Koshtra Pivrarcha. At dawn Juss and Brandoch Daha went forth to survey the prospect. They crossed the mouth of the steep snow-choked valley that ran up to the main ridge betwixt Ashnilan on the west and Koshtra Pivrarcha on the east, rounded the base of Ailinon, and climbed from the west to a snow saddle some three thousand feet up the ridge of that mountain, whence they might view the buttress and choose their way for their attempt.

“ ’Tis a two days’ journey to the top,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “If night on the ridge freeze us not to death, I dread no other hindrance. That black rib that riseth half a mile above our camp, shall take us clean up to the crest of the buttress, striking it above the great tower at the northern end. If the rocks be like those we camped on, hard as diamond and rough as a sponge, they shall not fail us but by our own neglect. As I live, I ne’er saw their like for climbing.”

“So far, well,” said Juss.

“Above,” said Brandoch Daha, “I’d drive thee a chariot until we come to the first great kick o’ the ridge. That must we round, or ne’er go further, and on this side it showeth ill enough, for the rocks shelve outward. If they be iced, there’s work indeed. Beyond that, I’ll prophesy nought, O Juss, for I can see nought clear save that the ridge is hacked into clefts and steeples. How we may overcome them must be put to the proof. It is too high and too far to know. This only: where we would go, there have we gone until now. And by that ridge lieth, if any way there lieth, the way to this mountain top that we crossed the world to climb.”

---

===Chinese===

于是他们吃了睡。风整夜在岩间哭号；早晨，雪与雨雪把群山抹没了。风暴整日不歇；趁一阵间歇，他们拔营，又下到斯罗斯尔加斯，在那里挨了九天九夜的风、雨与冰雹的敲打。

第十天天气平息，他们上去过了冰川，宿进科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡大北扶壁脚下一个岩洞里。黎明，朱斯与布兰多赫·达哈出去察看形势。他们越过那陡峻的、被雪壅塞的谷口——它向西通到阿什尼兰与科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡之间的主山脊——绕过艾利农的山根，从西面爬上那山山脊上约三千英尺高的一处雪鞍，从那里可以观察扶壁、选定进攻的路线。

「到顶是两天的路，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「只要夜里在山脊上不把我们冻死，别的阻碍我不怕。我们营地上头半英里拔起的那道黑棱，可以一直把我们送上扶壁的顶，在北端那大塔上方与顶相接。若岩石都同我们扎营这些一样——硬得像金刚石，糙得像海绵——那它们必不负我们，除非我们自己疏忽。我敢说，攀岩我从未见过这样的好货。」

「到目前为止，都好，」朱斯说。

「再往上，」布兰多赫·达哈说，「我可以替你赶车，一直赶到山脊第一大坎。那道坎我们必须绕过去，不然就别想再往前；从这边看它够呛，岩石都向外倾。要是结了冰，那就有活干了。再往上，朱斯，我什么也不预言，因为我什么都看不清，只看清山脊被劈成一裂裂、一尖尖。怎样克服它们，得试了才知道。太高太远，看不见。只有一条：我们要去的地方，到现在为止我们都到了。而沿着那条山脊——若还有路的话——就躺着通往这座山顶的路；我们漂洋过海，为的就是爬它。」

---

===Original===

Next day with the first paling of the skies they arose all three and set forth southward over the crisp snows. They roped at the foot of the glacier that came down from the saddle, some five thousand feet above them, where the main ridge dips between Ashnilan and Koshtra Pivrarcha. Ere the brighter stars were swallowed in the light of morning they were cutting their way among the labyrinthine towers and chasms of the icefall. Soon the new daylight flooded the snowfields of the High Glacier of Temarm, dyeing them green and saffron and palest rose. The snows of Islargyn glowed far away in the north to the right of the white dome of Emshir. Ela Mantissera blocked the view northeastward. The buttress that bounded their valley on the east plunged it in shadow blue as a summer sea. High on the other side the great twin peaks of Ailinon and Ashnilan, roused by the warm beams out of their frozen silence of the night, growled at whiles with avalanches and falling stones.

Juss was their leader in the icefall, guiding them now along high knife-edges that fell away on either hand to unsounded depths, now within the very lips of those chasms, along the bases of the ice-towers. These, five times a man’s height, some square, some pinnacled, some shattered or piled with the ruins of their kind, leaned above the path, as ready to fall and overwhelm the climbers and dash their bones forever down to those blue-green secret places of frost and silence where the chips of ice chinked hollow as Juss pressed onward, cutting his steps with Mivarsh’s axe. At length the slope eased and they walked out on the unbroken surface of the glacier, and passing by a snow-bridge over the great rift betwixt the glacier and the mountain side came two hours before noon to the foot of the rock-rib that they had scanned from Ailinon.

===Chinese===

次日，天刚发白，三人起身，南行踏过硬脆的雪。他们在冰川脚下结了绳——那冰川从他们上方约五千英尺、主山脊在阿什尼兰与科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡之间的低伏处流下。晨光还没吞没亮星，他们已在冰瀑迷宫般的塔与渊之间开路。不久，新昼的光灌满特马姆高冰川的雪原，把它们染成绿、藏红与最淡的玫瑰。伊斯拉尔金的雪在北方远处发亮，在埃姆希尔白色圆顶的右边。埃拉·曼蒂塞拉挡住了东北望。围住他们山谷东面的扶壁把谷浸在影里，蓝得像夏日的海。另一面高处，艾利农与阿什尼兰这对孪生巨峰，被暖光从夜的冻结沉默里唤醒，时时以雪崩与落石低吼。

冰瀑里由朱斯领路：时而领他们走又高又薄的雪刃——两边都是不可测的深渊——时而领他们在那些裂罅的唇边走，沿冰塔的根。这些冰塔五倍于人的高度，或方或尖，或碎裂，或堆着同类的残骸，俯在路的上空，随时要倒下来压住登山者，把他们的骨头永远砸下去，砸进那些青绿、隐秘的霜与寂静之域——朱斯向前开路、用米瓦尔什的斧砍出步级时，冰屑在那里空洞地叮当。末了坡度放缓，他们走出到冰川未破的面上，经一座雪桥过了冰川与山腰间的大裂谷，午前两小时到了他们从艾利农上观察过的那道石棱脚下。

===Original===

Now was Brandoch Daha to lead them. They climbed face to the rock, slowly and without rest, for sound and firm as the rocks were the holds were small and few and the cliffs steep. Here and there a chimney gave them passage upward, but the climb was mainly by cracks and open faces of rock, a trial of main strength and endurance such as few might sustain for a short while only: but this wall was three thousand feet in height. By noon they gained the crest, and there rested on the rocks too weary to speak, looking across the avalanche-swept face of Koshtra Pivrarcha to the corniced parapet that ended against the western precipices of Koshtra Belorn.

For some way the ridge of the buttress was broad and level. Then it narrowed suddenly to the width of a horse’s back, and sprang skyward two thousand feet and more. Brandoch Daha went forward and climbed a few feet up the cliff. It bulged out above him, smooth and holdless. He tried it once and again, then came down saying, “Nought without wings.”

Then he went to the left. Here hanging glaciers overlooked the face from on high, and while he gazed an avalanche of ice-blocks roared down it. Then he went to the right, and here the rocks sloped outward, and the sloping ledges were piled with rubbish and the rocks rotten and slippery with snow and ice. So having gone a little way he returned, and, “O Juss,” he said, “wilt take it right forth, and that must be by flying, for hold there is none: or wilt go east and dodge the avalanche: or west, where all is rotten and slither and a slip were our destruction?”

So they debated, and at length decided on the eastern road. It was an ill step round the jutting corner of the tower, for little hold there was, and the rocks were undercut below, so that a stone or a man loosed from that place must fall clear at a bound three or four thousand feet to the Koshtra glacier and there be dashed in pieces. Beyond, wide ledges gave them passage along the wall of the tower, that now swept inward, facing south. Far overhead, dazzling white in the sunshine, the broken glacier-edges and splinters jutted against the blue, and icicles greater than a man hung glittering from every ledge: a sight heavenly fair, whereof they yet had little joy, hastening as they had not hastened in their lives before to be out of the danger of that ice-swept face.

===Chinese===

现在由布兰多赫·达哈领路。他们脸贴着岩向上爬，缓慢而不歇：岩石虽坚实牢固，把手却又小又少，崖又陡。这里那里一道岩缝给他们上行之路，但主要靠裂隙与光面岩：那是纯粹膂力与耐力的考验，少有人能支持多久——而这道墙高三千英尺。正午他们登上棱顶，在岩石上歇下，累得说不出话，隔着科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡雪崩横扫的脸，望向那以科什特拉·贝洛恩西绝壁为尽头的雪檐栏墙。

扶壁的山脊起初有一段又宽又平。随后骤然收窄到马背那么宽，又向天空拔起两千多英尺。布兰多赫·达哈上前，往崖上爬了几英尺。头顶上岩壁凸出，平滑无把手。他试了一次又一次，下来道：「没有翅膀不行。」

他又到左边。那里悬冰川高高俯瞰着崖面；他正看，一阵冰块的雪崩轰然扫下崖面。他又到右边；那里岩石外倾，斜台堆满碎石，岩又酥又挂着冰雪打滑。他走了一小段便回来：「朱斯，你是要正面硬上——那非飞不可，因为毫无把手：还是走东边躲雪崩：还是走西边，那边一切又酥又滑，一滑我们就完？」

他们计议了一番，最后决定走东路。绕过那塔凸出的角，是一步险棋：把手几乎没有，岩石下切，从那里松脱的一块石头或一个人，必一跃直下三四千英尺，落上科什特拉冰川，摔得粉碎。过去之后，宽宽的岩台引他们沿塔壁行进；塔壁这时向内弯，面朝南。头顶高处，碎裂的冰川棱与冰刺在蓝天上白得炫目，比人还长的冰锥从每道岩台上垂下闪亮：天国般美的景象，他们却无心领受——生平从未这样赶路，急着逃出那面扫冰之壁的危险。

===Original===

Suddenly was a noise above them like the crack of a giant whip, and looking up they beheld against the sky a dark mass which opened like a flower and spread into a hundred fragments. The Demons and Mivarsh hugged the cliffs where they stood, but there was little cover. All the air was filled with the shrieking of the stones, as they swept downwards like fiends returning to the pit, and with the crash of them as they dashed against the cliffs and burst in pieces. The echoes rolled and reverberated from cliff to distant cliff, and the limbs of the mountain seemed to writhe as under a scourge. When it was done, Mivarsh was groaning for pain of his left wrist sore hurt with a stone. The others were scatheless.

Juss said to Brandoch Daha, “Back, howsoever it dislike thee.”

Back they went; and an avalanche of ice crashed down the face which must have destroyed them had they proceeded. “Thou dost misjudge me,” said Brandoch Daha, laughing. “Give me where my life lieth on mine own might and main; then is danger meat and drink to me, and nought shall turn me back. But here on this cursed cliff, on the ledges whereof a cripple might walk at ease, we be the toys of chance. And it were pure folly to abide upon it a moment longer.”

“Two ways be left us,” said Juss. “To turn back, and that were our shame forever; and to essay the western traverse.”

“And that should be the bane of any save of me and thee,” said Brandoch Daha. “And if our bane, why, we shall sleep sound.”

“Mivarsh,” said Juss, “is nought so bounden to this adventure. He hath bravely held by us, and bravely stood our friend. Yet here we be come to such a pass, I sore misdoubt me if it were less danger of his life to come with us than seek safety alone.”

But Mivarsh put on a hardy face. Never a word he spake, but nodded his head, as who should say, “Forward.”

“First I must be thy leech,” said Juss. And he bound up Mivarsh’s wrist. And because the day was now far spent, they camped under the great tower, hoping next day to reach the top of Koshtra Pivrarcha that stood unseen some six thousand feet above them.

---

===Chinese===

忽然头顶上一声巨响，像巨人挥鞭；抬头看，天幕上一团黑块绽开如花，散成百块碎片。魔人们与米瓦尔什贴住身处的崖壁，可遮蔽极少。满空是石块的尖叫，像返回魔窟的恶鬼那样扫下来，砸上崖壁迸碎。回声从崖滚到远崖，山的肢体像受鞭刑一样抽搐。一停，米瓦尔什正呻吟：左腕被石头砸得重伤。其余两人无恙。

朱斯对布兰多赫·达哈说：「退回去，不管你多不情愿。」

他们退了；一阵冰的雪崩轰然扫下崖面——若他们先前前行，必被它毁灭。「你错看我了，」布兰多赫·达哈笑着说。「把性命握在我自己膂力里的地方给我；那样，危险于我就是酒食，什么也不能叫我回头。可在这道受咒的崖上、在瘸子都能闲步的岩台上，我们是运气的玩物。再在这里多待一刻，就是纯粹的愚妄。」

「剩两条路，」朱斯说。「退回去，那是我们永远的耻辱；要么试试西面横切。」

「那对任何人都是绝路，除了你和我，」布兰多赫·达哈说。「若是我们的绝路——那正好，我们睡得香。」

「米瓦尔什，」朱斯说，「并不这样受这条冒险的捆绑。他勇敢地跟了我们，勇敢地作了我们的朋友。可如今到了这个地步，我实在疑心：他跟着我们，未必比独自寻活路更险。」

米瓦尔什却摆出硬汉的脸。一句话不说，只点点头，像是说：「前进。」

「先让我作你的医生，」朱斯说。他给米瓦尔什包扎了腕。因为白日已深，他们在大塔下扎营，指望次日登上在他们上方约六千英尺、看不见的科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡之顶。

---

===Original===

Next morning, when it was light enough to climb, they set forth. For two hours’ space on that traverse not a moment passed but they were in instant peril of death. They were not roped, for on those slabbery rocks one man had dragged a dozen to perdition had he made a slip. The ledges sloped outward; they were piled with broken rock and mud; the soft red rock broke away at a hand’s touch and plunged at a leap to the glacier below. Down and up and along, and down and up and up again they wound their way, rounding the base of that great tower, and came at last by a rotten gully safe to the ridge above it.

While they climbed, white wispy clouds which had gathered in the high gullies of Ailinon in the morning had grown to a mass of blackness that hid all the mountains to the west. Great streamers ran from it across the gulf below, joined and boiled upward, lifting and sinking like a full-tided sea, rising at last to the high ridge where the Demons stood and wrapping them in a cloak of vapour with a chill wind in its folds, and darkness in broad noonday. They halted, for they might not see the rocks before them. The wind grew boisterous, shouting among the splintered towers. Snow swept powdery and keen across the ridge. The cloud lifted and plunged again like some great bird shadowing them with its wings. From its bosom the lightning flared above and below. Thunder crashed on the heels of the lightning, sending the echoes rolling among the distant cliffs. Their weapons, planted in the snow, sizzled with blue flame; Juss had counselled laying them aside lest they should perish holding them. Crouched in a hollow of the snow among the rocks of that high ridge of Koshtra Pivrarcha, Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha and Mivarsh Faz weathered that night of terror. When night came they knew not, for the storm brought darkness on them hours before sundown. Blinding snow and sleet and fire and thunder, and wild winds shrieking in the gullies till the firm mountain seemed to rock, kept them awake. They were near frozen, and scarce desired aught but death, which might bring them ease from that hellish roundelay.

===Chinese===

次日晨光够攀爬时，他们出发。那道横切上两个钟头里，没有一刻不是在死亡的即时危险中。他们没有结绳：在那样的滑石上，一个人失足会把一打人拖进地狱。岩台向外倾；堆着碎石与泥；酥红的岩一手一碰就崩落，一跃跳到下面的冰川。下、上、平走，又下、又上、又上，他们绕着那大塔的根蜿蜒而行，末了从一道酥碎的冲沟安全上到塔顶的山脊。

他们攀爬时，早晨聚在艾利农高沟里的白云絮，已长成一团黑云，把西面群山尽数遮没。大片的云旗从它上面横过下面的深渊，聚拢、沸腾着向上，像满潮的海起伏，末了升到魔人们站立的高脊，把他们裹进一件寒风藏在褶里的雾氅，正午成了黑夜。他们停下，因为看不见面前的岩石。风狂了，在碎塔间呼啸。雪粉又冷又利地扫过山脊。云像一只巨鸟，起落之间以翼影罩他们。电光在它怀中上下闪。雷紧跟着闪电炸开，回声在远崖间滚。他们插在雪里的兵刃嗤嗤地冒蓝火；朱斯早就叫他们放下兵刃，惟恐握着丧命。朱斯大人、布兰多赫·达哈大人与米瓦尔什·法兹蜷在科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡高脊岩石间的一个雪窝里，熬过了那恐怖之夜。夜几时来的他们不知道，因为风暴在日落前几个小时就把黑暗压给了他们。迷眼的雪、雨雪、火与雷，还有在沟壑里尖叫的狂风——吹得坚固的山都像在摇——叫他们彻夜无眠。他们几乎冻僵，什么都不想，只想死，好从那地狱轮舞里解脱。

白昼以虚弱的灰光破晓，风暴息了。朱斯站起身，累得说不出话。米瓦尔什说：「你们是魔鬼；可连我自己都惊奇。我这辈子都住在雪山边，知道许多大风雪里被困雪山上的人。被找到的那些，没有一个是冻死的。我说的是被找到的。许多没被找到——鬼把她们吃了。」

布兰多赫·达哈大人闻言大笑：「米瓦尔什啊，我怕你不过是条没出息的狗。瞧瞧他——论吃苦耐劳、火烧冰冻之下的坚持，他超过我，正像我超过你——却是三人里最乏的。想知道为什么？我告诉你：他整夜在斗严寒，不光摩擦他自己，还摩擦我与你，救我们免于冻伤。放心，没有别的能救下你这条命。」

那时雾更淡了些，他们看得见山脊向前伸去一百步或更远：每一座尖塔衬着后面一座更朦胧的尖塔，影影绰绰地立着。隔着雾，那些尖塔显得异样巨大，身量如峰。

===Original===

Day broke with a weak gray light, and the storm died down. Juss stood up weary beyond speech. Mivarsh said, “Ye be devils, but of myself I marvel. For I have dwelt by snow mountains all my days, and many I wot of that have been benighted on the snows in wild weather. And not one but was starved by reason of the cold. I speak of them that were found. Many were not found, for the spirits devoured them.”

Whereat Lord Brandoch Daha laughed aloud, saying, “O Mivarsh, I fear me that in thee I have but a graceless dog. Look on him, that in hardihood and bodily endurance against all hardships of frost or fire surpasseth me as greatly as I surpass thee. Yet is he weariest of the three. Wouldst know why? I’ll tell thee: all night he hath striven against the cold, chafing not himself only but me and thee to save us from frostbite. And be sure nought else had saved thy carcase.”

By then was the mist grown lighter, so that they might see the ridge for an hundred paces or more where it went up before them, each pinnacle standing out shadowy and unsubstantial against the next succeeding one more shadowy still. And the pinnacles showed monstrous huge through the mist, like mountain peaks in stature.

They roped and set forth, scaling the towers or turning them, now on this side now on that; sometimes standing on teeth of rock that seemed cut off from all earth else, solitary in a sea of shifting vapour; sometimes descending into a deep gash in the ridge with a blank wall rearing aloft on the further side and empty air yawning to left and right. The rocks were firm and good, like those they had first climbed from the glacier. But they went but a slow pace, for the climbing was difficult and made dangerous by new snow and by the ice that glazed the rocks.

As the day wore the wind was fallen, and all was still when they stood at length before a ridge of hard ice that shot steeply up before them like the edge of a sword. The east side of it on their left was almost sheer, ending in a blank precipice that dropped out of sight without a break. The western slope, scarcely less steep, ran down in a white even sheet of frozen snow till the clouds engulfed it.

Brandoch Daha waited on the last blunt tooth of rock at the foot of the ice-ridge. “The rest is thine,” he cried to Lord Juss. “I would not that any save thou should tread him first, for he is thy mountain.”

===Chinese===

他们结绳出发：或登上那些塔，或绕过它们，忽左忽右；有时立在一颗仿佛与大地其余一切割断的岩齿上，孤悬于流雾之海；有时下到山脊一道深剁里，对面一堵光墙高高竖起，左右张着空的深渊。岩石坚实良好，同他们最初从冰川上爬的那些一样。可他们走得慢：攀爬艰难，新雪与挂在岩上的冰更添凶险。

日暮时分风已止息；他们终于立在一道坚冰的山脊前，它像剑锋一样陡然向上挺出。左边它的东面近乎垂直，尽在一堵不见中断、直落视界之外的绝壁上。西坡稍缓些也缓不了多少，一整幅冰冻的白雪平平地泻下去，直到云把它吞没。

布兰多赫·达哈在冰脊脚最后一颗钝岩齿上等着。「剩下的是你的了，」他向朱斯大人喊。「我不愿除你之外的任何人第一个踏它，因为它是你的山。」

「没有你我根本上不到这里，」朱斯答；「首登之荣归我，而主功是你的，不合适。你先行。」

「我不，」布兰多赫·达哈大人说。「也不是这么回事。」

于是朱斯上前，在山脊西面、脊骨稍下处用斧砍出大步级；布兰多赫·达哈大人与米瓦尔什·法兹踏着步级跟上。

不一会，一阵风从天空看不见的空阔里起来，像撕一件烂衣裳似的撕开雾。阳光的矛从裂缝里射进来。南边不可想象的深处，遥远的、洒满阳光的大地闪着微光，在一道深渊之外巨墙的顶上望过去：一道黑岩扶壁的屏风，割着一千条亮雪的沟壑，顶上如城堞般排着一列山峰，形貌蛮野剽悍，亮得叫人眨眼：那是科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡顶峰山脊的瘦削尖塔。这些魔人们仰望了这么久、以为远在天上的塔，如今都躺在了他们脚下。只有他们正登的这座峰还耸在上方，如今清晰而近：东北面是一堵光秃的危崖，崖顶悬着一道雪檐。朱斯看中那雪檐，回身继续砍步级；云破之后半小时，他站上了那颗从未有人登过的塔尖，全大地都在他脚下。

---

===Original===

“Without thee I had never won up hither,” answered Juss; “and it is not fitting that I should have that glory to stand first upon the peak when thine was the main achievement. Go thou before.”

“I will not,” said Lord Brandoch Daha. “And it is not so.”

So Juss went forward, smiting with his axe great steps just below the backbone of the ridge on the western side, and Lord Brandoch Daha and Mivarsh Faz followed in the steps.

Presently a wind arose in the unseen spaces of the sky, and tore the mist like a rotten garment. Spears of sunlight blazed through the rifts. Distant sunny lands shimmered in the unimaginable depths to the southward, seen over the crest of a tremendous wall that stood beyond the abyss: a screen of black rock buttresses seamed with a thousand gullies of glistening snow, and crowned as with battlements with a row of mountain peaks, savage and fierce of form, that made the eye blink for their brightness: the lean spires of the summit-ridge of Koshtra Pivrarcha. These, that the Demons had so long looked up to as in distant heaven, now lay beneath their feet. Only the peak they climbed still reared itself above them, clear now and near to view, showing a bare beetling cliff on the northeast, overhung by a cornice of snow. Juss marked the cornice, turned him again to his step-cutting, and in half an hour from the breaking of the clouds stood on that unascended pinnacle, with all earth beneath him.

---

They went down a few feet on the southern side and sat on some rocks. A fair lake studded with islands lay bosomed in wooded and crag-girt hills at the foot of a deep-cut valley which ran down from the Gates of Zimiamvia. Ailinon and Ashnilan rose near by in the west, with the delicate white peak of Akra Garsh showing between them. Beyond, mountain beyond mountain like the sea.

===Chinese===

他们下到南面几英尺，坐在几块岩石上。一座点缀着岛屿的美湖，偎在林木与危岩环抱的群山里，在一条从齐米亚姆维亚之门延伸下来的深谷脚下。艾利农与阿什尼兰在近处西边耸起，两山之间露出阿克拉·加什纤秀的白峰。再往外，山外是山，像海。

朱斯望向南方：蓝色的陆地一层一层铺展成绵延的丘原，柔而朦胧，终于化进天里。「你我，」他说，「人类的孩子中头两个，如今用活眼看见了传说中的齐米亚姆维亚之地。哲人们讲的关于那幸运之国的话，你想是真的么：凡人的脚不能踏它，蒙福的魂——已故死者中的那些——住在那里，就是那些生前在地上伟大、行过大事业、不轻看大地及其欢愉与荣光、却又行公义、不作懦夫也不作暴君的人？」

「谁知道呢？」布兰多赫·达哈说，手支着下巴，像梦中一样望着南方。「谁敢说他知道？」

他们沉默了一阵。朱斯又开口：「我的朋友，你我若终久到了那里，还会记得魔国么？」他不答，朱斯便说：「我宁在夏夜的星下到月湖上划船，也不作全齐米亚姆维亚的王。我宁看斯卡夫山上的日出，也不愿在科什特拉·贝洛恩之下、那魔法拉瓦里湖的岛上欢欢乐乐住一辈子。」

===Original===

Juss looked southward where the blue land stretched in fold upon fold of rolling country, soft and misty, till it melted in the sky. “Thou and I,” said he, “first of the children of men, now behold with living eyes the fabled land of Zimiamvia. Is that true, thinkest thou, which philosophers tell us of that fortunate land: that no mortal foot may tread it, but the blessed souls do inhabit it of the dead that be departed, even they that were great upon earth and did great deeds when they were living, that scorned not earth and the delights and the glories thereof, and yet did justly and were not dastards nor yet oppressors?”

“Who knoweth?” said Brandoch Daha, resting his chin in his hand and gazing south as in a dream. “Who shall say he knoweth?”

They were silent awhile. Then Juss spake saying, “If thou and I come thither at last, O my friend, shall we remember Demonland?” And when he answered him not, Juss said, “I had rather row on Moonmere under the stars of a summer’s night, than be a King of all the land of Zimiamvia. And I had rather watch the sunrise on the Scarf, than dwell in gladness all my days on an island of that enchanted Lake of Ravary, under Koshtra Belorn.”

Now the curtain of cloud that had hung till now about the eastern heights was rent into shreds, and Koshtra Belorn stood like a bride before them, two or three miles to eastward, facing the slanting rays of the sun. On all her vast precipices scarce a rock showed bare, so encrusted were they with a dazzling robe of snow. More lovely she seemed and more graceful in her airy poise than they had yet beheld her. Juss and Brandoch Daha rose up, as men arise to greet a queen in her majesty. In silence they looked on her for some minutes.

Then Brandoch Daha spake, saying, “Behold thy bride, O Juss.”

===Chinese===

这时，一直挂在东面高地的云幕裂成碎片，科什特拉·贝洛恩像一位新娘立在他们面前，在东边两三英里处，迎着太阳斜射的光。她全部浩大的绝壁上几乎不见一块裸岩，密密裹着一件炫目的雪袍。她那空灵的仪态，显得比他们迄今所见的更可爱、更优雅。朱斯与布兰多赫·达哈站起来，像人们起立迎接御座上的王后。他们默默看了她几分钟。

布兰多赫·达哈开口说：「看哪，朱斯，你的新娘。」

## XIII / XIII
===Original===

Koshtra Belorn

How the Lord Juss accomplished at length his dream’s behest, to inquire in Koshtra Belorn; and what manner of answer he received.

That night they spent safely, by favour of the Gods, under the highest crags of Koshtra Pivrarcha, in a sheltered hollow piled round with snow. Dawn came like a lily, saffron-hued, smirched with smoke-gray streaks that slanted from the north. The great peaks stood as islands above a main of level cloud, out of which the sun walked flaming, a ball of red-gold fire. An hour before his face appeared, the Demons and Mivarsh were roped and started on their eastward journey. Ill to do with as was the crest of the great north buttress by which they had climbed the mountain, seven times worse was this eastern ridge, leading to Koshtra Belorn. Leaner of back it was, flanked by more profound abysses, deeplier gashed, too treacherous and too sudden in its changes from sure rock to rotten and perilous: piled with tottering crags, hung about with cornices of uncertain snow, girt with cliffs smooth and holdless as a castle wall. Small marvel that it cost them thirteen hours to come down that ridge. The sun wheeled towards the west when they reached at length that frozen edge, sharp as a sickle, that was in the Gates of Zimiamvia. Weary they were, and ropeless; for by no means else might they come down from the last great tower save by the rope made fast from above. A fierce northeaster had swept the ridges all day, bringing snowstorms on its wings. Their fingers were numbed with cold, and the beards of Lord Brandoch Daha and Mivarsh Faz stiff with ice.

Too weary to halt, they set forth again, Juss leading. It was many hundred paces along that ice-edge, and the sun was near setting when they stood at last within a stone’s throw of the cliffs of Koshtra Belorn. Since before noon avalanches had thundered ceaselessly down those cliffs. Now, in the cool of the evening, all was still. The wind was fallen. The deep blue sky was without a cloud. The fires of sunset crept down the vast white precipices before them till every ledge and fold and frozen pinnacle glowed pink colour, and every shadow became an emerald. The shadow of Koshtra Pivrarcha lay cold across the lower stretches of the face on the Zimiamvian side. The edge of that shadow was as the division betwixt the living and the dead.

===Chinese===

科什特拉·贝洛恩

记朱斯大人终于如何遵梦的命，往科什特拉·贝洛恩问讯；及他所得的是怎样一个回答。

那夜，托诸神的护佑，他们在科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡（Koshtra Pivrarcha）最高的峭壁下一个避风的雪窝里平安过夜。黎明像一朵藏红色的百合来了，抹着几道从北面斜过来的烟灰条纹。群峰如岛屿立在一平如镜的云海之上，太阳从云海里走出，一团红金的火。在它露面之前一个钟头，魔族众人和米瓦尔什已系好绳索，踏上去程科什特拉·贝洛恩（Koshtra Belorn）的东行路。他们上山时所靠的大北麓的顶已是难缠的了，这条通往科什特拉·贝洛恩的东山脊却还要糟七倍：背更瘦，两侧渊壑更深，割裂更甚，从坚实的岩石到酥烂凶险的岩体变换得又诡又骤：堆积着摇摇欲坠的岩塔，悬挂着靠不住的雪檐，围着如城堡墙面般光平无握的峭壁。花了十三个钟头才下完这条山脊，毫不奇怪。他们终于踏上那如镰刀般锋利的冰棱——齐米亚姆维亚（Zimiamvia）门户上的那道——时，太阳已转向西天。他们疲惫不堪，绳子也没有了：离开最后一座巨塔时，绳子系在上头，无法带上，否则别无下法。一整天，狂暴的东北风扫着山脊，带来一阵阵暴雪。他们的手指冻僵了，布兰多赫·达哈大人和米瓦尔什·法兹的胡须冻得硬如冰凌。

累得停不下脚，他们又上路了，朱斯领路。沿着那道冰棱走了几百步；当他们终于站到离科什特拉·贝洛恩的崖壁一石之遥时，太阳将落。自正午前起，雪崩就在那些崖壁上隆隆不息。此刻，晚凉之中，万籁俱寂。风停了。深蓝的天空无云。落日的火沿着眼前那大片雪白的高崖缓缓爬下，直到每一条岩棱、每一道褶皱、每一座冰封的尖顶都燃成粉色，每一道阴影都变成翡翠色。科什特拉·皮弗拉尔卡的影子冷冷地横过面向齐米亚姆维亚那面山壁的下段。那影子的边，就像生者与死者之间的分界。

===Original===

“What dost think on?” said Juss to Brandoch Daha, that leaned upon his sword surveying that glory.

Brandoch Daha started and looked on him. “Why,” said he, “on this: that it is likely thy dream was but a lure, sent thee by the King to tempt us on to mighty actions reserved for our destruction. On this side at least ’tis very certain there lieth no way up Koshtra Belorn.”

“What of the little martlet,” said Juss, “who, whiles we were yet a great way off, flew out of the south to greet us with a gracious message?”

“Well if it were not a devil of his,” said Brandoch Daha.

“I will not turn back,” said Juss. “Thou needest not to come with me.” And he turned again to look on those frozen cliffs.

“No?” said Brandoch Daha. “Nor thou with me. Thou’lt make me angry if thou wilt so vilely wrest my words. Only fare not too securely; and let that axe still be ready in thine hand, as is my sword, for kindlier work than step-cutting. And if thou embrace the hope to climb her by this wall before us, then hath the King’s enchantery made thee fey.”

By then was the sun gone down. Under the wings of night uplifted from the east, the unfathomable heights of air turned a richer blue; and here and there, most dim and hard to see, throbbed a tiny point of light: the greater stars opening their eyelids to the gathering dark. Gloom crept upward, brimming the valleys far below like a rising tide of the sea. Frost and stillness waited on the eternal night to resume her reign. The solemn cliffs of Koshtra Belorn stood in tremendous silence, death-pale against the sky.

Juss came backward a step along the ridge, and laying his hand on Brandoch Daha’s, “Be still,” he said, “and behold this marvel.” A little up the face of the mountain on the Zimiamvian side, it was as if some leavings of the afterglow had been entangled among the crags and frozen curtains of snow. As the gloom deepened, that glow brightened and spread, filling a rift that seemed to go into the mountain.

“It is because of us,” said Juss, in a low voice. “She is afire with expectation of us.”

===Chinese===

「你在想什么？」朱斯问倚剑眺望那壮景的布兰多赫·达哈。

布兰多赫·达哈一怔，看着他。「想这个，」他说，「你的梦很可能不过是个诱饵，是王上打发来引我们去干那注定毁灭我们的伟业的。至少这一面，千真万确，没有上科什特拉·贝洛恩的路。」

「那小无足燕（martlet）怎么说？」朱斯说，「我们还在老远的地方，它就从南边飞来迎接我们，带着慈爱的口信。」

「最好不是他的一个魔鬼。」布兰多赫·达哈说。

「我不回头。」朱斯说。「你不必随我来。」他又转身去看那些冰封的崖壁。

「是么？」布兰多赫·达哈说。「你也别随我走。你若这样歪曲我的话，我可要生气了。只是别走得太放心；让那把斧头仍旧在手里随时待命，像我的剑一样，好干比砍台阶更杀气的活儿。你要是指望从我们面前这面墙上爬上她，那王上的妖术已经把你也迷了。」

此时日已沉。在从东方扬起的夜的羽翼下，深不可测的高天转成更浓的蓝；这儿那儿，最暗最难以辨清的地方，怞动着细小的光点：大些的星辰正向渐浓的黑暗睁开眼睑。晦暗向上爬，像上涨的海潮，渐渐淹满下方深谷。严寒与静默等候永恒之夜恢复她的统治。科什特拉·贝洛恩庄严的崖壁立在可怕的寂静中，映着天色，死一般苍白。

朱斯沿山脊向后退了一步，把手搭在布兰多赫·达哈手上：「别动，」他说，「看这个奇景。」山壁齐米亚姆维亚那一面稍高处，仿佛有几绕晚霞的余烬缠在岩塔和冻雪的帷幕间。晦暗越深，那光越亮越广，注满了一道似乎通进山体里的裂缝。

「这是为我们而设的，」朱斯低声说。「她在为等候我们而燃烧。」

===Original===

No sound was there save of their breath coming and going, and of the strokes of Juss’s axe, and of the chips of ice chinking downwards into silence as he cut their way along the ridge. And ever brighter, as night fell, burned that strange sunset light above them. Perilous climbing it was for fifty feet or more from the ridge, for they had no rope, the way was hard to see, and the rocks were steep and iced and every ledge deep in snow. Yet came they safe at length up by a steep short gully to the gully’s head where it widened to that rift of the wondrous light. Here might two walk abreast, and Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha took their weapons and entered abreast into the rift. Mivarsh was fain to call to them, but he was speechless. He came after, close at their heels like a dog.

For some way the bed of the cave ran upwards, then dipped at a gentle slope deep into the mountain. The air was cold, yet warm after the frozen air without. The rose-red light shone warm on the walls and floor of that passage, but none might say whence it shone. Strange sculptures glimmered overhead, bullheaded men, stags with human faces, mammoths, and behemoths of the flood: vast forms and uncertain carved in the living rock. For hours Juss and his companions pursued their way, winding downward, losing all sense of north and south. Little by little the light faded, and after an hour or two they went in darkness: yet not in utter darkness, but as of a starless night in summer where all night long twilight lingers. They went a soft pace, for fear of pitfalls in the way.

After a while Juss halted and sniffed the air. “I smell new-mown hay,” he said, “and flower-scents. Is this my fantasy, or canst thou smell them too?”

“Ay, and have smelt it this half-hour past,” answered Brandoch Daha; “also the passage wideneth before us, and the roof of it goeth higher as we journey.”

“This,” said Juss, “is a great wonder.”

===Chinese===

除了他们的呼吸一起一伏、朱斯挥斧开路的声音和冰屑坠落无声的脆响，再无别的声音。而夜色越落，他们头顶那道奇异的落日之光烧得越亮。从山脊上去那五十多尺爬得惊险：没有绳，路难辨认，岩石陡峭挂冰，每个台阶都深埋在雪里。但他们终于平安地从一条陡短的山沟爬上沟头，沟头在那里展开成那道奇光的裂缝。这里可容两人并行；朱斯大人和布兰多赫·达哈大人拿起兵器，并肩进入裂缝。米瓦尔什想喊他们，却喊不出声。他跟在后面，紧贴着他们的脚跟，像一条狗。

洞道起初向上走了一段，然后以平缓的坡度深深探入山腹。空气冷，可比外面的冰冻空气又算暖了。玫瑰红的光暖暖地照在通道的四壁和地上，可谁也说不出光从何处来。头顶隐隐约约是些奇异的雕像：牛首人身、人面牝鹿、猛犸、洪荒巨兽：都是雕在原生岩里的庞大而模糊的形。朱斯和同伴们走了几个钟头，蜿蜒而下，失去了南北的方向感。光一点一点淡下去，一两个钟头后他们走在黑暗里：却不是全然的黑，而像夏日无星之夜，暮色彻夜不散。他们放慢脚步，怕路上有陷坑。

过了一阵，朱斯停下，嗅了嗅空气。「我闻到新割的干草味，」他说，「还有花香。是我的幻觉么，还是你也闻得到？」

「闻到，这半个钟头都在闻，」布兰多赫·达哈答；「还有，通道在前头宽起来，我们一路走，洞顶也一路高起来。」

「这个，」朱斯说，「是一大奇观。」

===Original===

They fared onward, and in a while the slope slackened, and they felt loose stones and grit beneath their feet, and in a while soft earth. They bent down and touched the earth, and there was grass growing, and night-dew on the grass, and daisies folded up asleep. A brook tinkled on the right. So they crossed that meadow in the dark, until they stood below a shadowy mass that bulked big above them. In a blind wall so high the top was swallowed up in the darkness a gate stood open. They crossed that threshold and passed through a paved court that clanked under their tread. Before them a flight of steps went up to folding doors under an archway.

Lord Brandoch Daha felt Mivarsh pluck him by the sleeve. The little man’s teeth were chattering together in his head for terror. Brandoch Daha smiled and put an arm about him. Juss had his foot on the lowest step.

===Chinese===

他们继续前行，过了一阵，坡度缓了，脚下踩到碎石和砂砺，再过一阵，踩到软土。他们俯身摸地，地上长着草，草上有夜露，雏菊收拢花瓣睡着。右边有溪水淙淙。他们就这样在黑暗中穿过那片草甸，直到立在一团黑影之下——那东西黑压压地高踞在他们头顶。一道盲墙高得不见顶，墙上开着一扇门。他们跨过门槛，穿过一个石铺的庭院，脚步铿然。前面一道台阶，通向拱门下的对开大门。

布兰多赫·达哈大人觉出来瓦尔什在拽他的衣袖。小个子吓得牙齿在脑袋里捉对儿打颤。布兰多赫·达哈一笑，搂住他的肩。朱斯一脚已踏上了最下一级台阶。

===Original===

In that instant came a sound of music playing, but of what instruments they might not guess. Great thundering chords began it, like trumpets calling to battle, first high, then low, then shuddering down to silence; then that great call again, sounding defiance. Then the keys took new voices, groping in darkness, rising to passionate lament, hovering and dying away on the wind, until nought remained but a roll as of muffled thunder, long, low, quiet, but menacing ill. And now out of the darkness of that induction burst a mighty form, three ponderous blows, as of breakers that plunge and strike on a desolate shore; a pause; those blows again; a grinding pause; a rushing of wings, as of Furies steaming up from the pit; another flight of them dreadful in its deliberation; then a wild rush upward and a swooping again; confusion of hell, raging serpents blazing through night sky. Then on a sudden out of a distant key, a sweet melody, long-drawn and clear, like a blaze of low sunshine piercing the dust-clouds above a battlefield. This was but an interlude to the terror of the great main theme that came in tumultuous strides up again from the deeps, storming to a grand climacteric of fury and passing away into silence. Now came a majestic figure, stately and calm, born of that terror, leading to it again: battlings of these themes in many keys, and at last the great triple blow, thundering in new strength, crushing all joy and sweetness as with a mace of iron, battering the roots of life into a general ruin. But even in the main stride of its outrage and terror, that great power seemed to shrivel. The thunder-blasts crashed weaklier, the harsh blows rattled awry, and the vast frame of conquest and destroying violence sank down panting, tottered and rumbled ingloriously into silence.

===Chinese===

就在这一瞬，乐声响起，却猜不出是什么乐器。开篇是雷鸣般的巨大和弦，如号角吹响战斗的召唤，先高，后低，继而颤抖着沉入寂静；然后那伟大的召唤再来，声声挑战。随后琴键换上新声，在黑暗中摸索，升华为炽烈的悲怆，徘徊着随风消逝，末了只余一阕如闷雷的滚动，长、低、静，却威胁着不祥。接着，从那前奏的黑暗中迸出一个雄浑的乐句：三记沉重的打击，像巨浪扑打荒凉的海岸；一停；又是那三击；一阵磨牙般的停顿；一阵振翅之声，如复仇女神从深渊蒸腾而上；又一波振翅，从容不迫，愈发可怖；随即疯狂上冲，又猛然俯掠；地狱般的混乱，狂怒的群蛇烧穿夜空。突然，从遥远的调性里转出一支甜美的旋律，悠长而清朗，如一线低斜的阳光穿透战场上空的尘云。而这不过是间奏，那恐怖的大主题正踏着骚乱的步伐从深处再度踏上来，直冲向狂怒的大高潮，又逝入寂静。随后来了一个庄严的乐句，华贵而平静，生于那恐怖，又引回那恐怖：这些主题在多个调性上厮杀，最后是那伟大的三连击，以新的力量轰鸣，像铁锤一样碾碎一切喜悦与甜美，把生命的根砸成一片齑粉。可就在它肆虐与恐怖的极盛处，那股大力量仿佛枯萎了。雷霆的爆发一声弱过一声，粗暴的敲击打得歪斜零落，那征服与毁灭之暴力的庞大骨架喘息着塌落，踉跄着，碌碌地滚入寂静。

===Original===

Like men held in a trance those lords of Demonland listened to the last echoes of the great sad chord where that music had breathed out its heart, as if the very heart of wrath were broken. But this was not the end. Cold and serene as some chaste virgin vowed to the Gods, with clear eyes which see nought below high heaven, a quiet melody rose from that grave of terror. Weak it seemed at first, a little thing after that cataclysm; a little thing, like spring’s first bud peeping after the blasting reign of cold and ice. Yet it walked undismayed, gathering as it went beauty and power. And on a sudden the folding doors swung open, shedding a flood of radiance down the stairs.

Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha watched, as men watch for a star to rise, that radiant portal. And like a star indeed, or like the tranquil moon appearing, they beheld after a while one crowned like a Queen with a diadem of little clouds that seemed stolen from the mountain sunset, scattering soft beams of rosy brightness. She stood alone under that mighty portico with its vast shadowy forms of winged lions in shining stone black as jet. Youthful she seemed, as one that hath but just bidden adieu to childhood, with grave sweet lips and grave black eyes and hair like the night. Little black martlets perched on her either shoulder, and a dozen more skimmed the air above her head, so swift of wing that scarcely the eye might follow them. Meantime, that delicate and simple melody mounted from height to height, until in a while it burned with all the fires of summer, burned as summer to the uttermost ember, fierce and compulsive in its riot of love and beauty. So that, before the last triumphant chords died down in silence, that music had brought back to Juss all the glories of the mountains, the sunset fires on Koshtra Belorn, the first great revelation of the peaks from Morna Moruna; and over all these, as the spirit of that music to the eye made manifest, the image of that Queen so blessed-fair in her youth and her clear brow’s sweet solemn respect and promise: in every line and pose of her fair form, virginal dainty as a flower, and kindled from withinward as never flower was with that divinity before the face of which speech and song fall silent and men may but catch their breath and worship.

===Chinese===

魔国两位大人像中了梦廘的人，听那音乐倾尽心脏吐出的最后一个悲怆和弦的余音——仿佛愤怒的心本身已经碎了。但这还不是终曲。清冷而安详，如一位献身诸神的贞洁处子，眼里只望得见高天，一支安静的旋律从那恐怖的坟里升起。起初它显得弱小，在那场大灾变后不过一桩小东西；一桩小东西，像严寒冰雪的暴政之后探出头来的春之第一颗蓓蕾。然而它毫不气馁地走着，一路收集美与力量。突然，对开的大门敞开，一片光华倾泻下台阶。

朱斯大人和布兰多赫·达哈大人守望着那光华的门，如人们守候一颗星升起。而确乎像一颗星，或像安详的月亮显现，过了一会儿，他们看见一位加冕的女子，冠冕由朵朵小云织成，仿佛偷自山间的落日，散着玫瑰色柔光。她独自立在那巨大的门廊下，门廊两侧闪黑玉般光泽的石头上，雕着生翼巨狮的庞大暗影。她看似年轻，像刚与童年道别的人，有庄严甜美的唇、庄严的黑眼睛和夜一样的头发。两只小黑无足燕栖在她双肩，另有十来只在头顶掠飞，翅快得眼睛几乎追不上。与此同时，那细腻而单纯的旋律一层层升上去，不一刻便燃起夏日全部的火，如夏日烧到最后的余烬，在爱与美的狂欢中炽烈而不可抗拒。于是，在最后凯旋的和弦沉入寂静之前，那音乐已把群山的全部荣光带回给朱斯：科什特拉·贝洛恩上的落日之火，从莫尔纳·莫鲁纳初见群峰的大启示；而这一切之上，如同那音乐的灵魂显了形，是那位女王的形象——她青春年少，光洁的额头上有一种甜美的庄重与应许，有福地美好：她美好身形的每一线条每一姿态，如花般纯洁精巧，又由内而外燃着一种花从未有过的神性——在那神性面前，言语与歌都沉默，人只能屏住呼吸，敬拜。

===Original===

When she spoke, it was with a voice like crystal: “Thanks be and praise to the blessed Gods. For lo, the years depart, and the fated years bring forth as the Gods ordain. And ye be those that were for to come.”

Surely those great lords of Demonland stood like little boys before her. She said again, “Are not ye Lord Juss and Lord Brandoch Daha of Demonland, come up to me by the way banned to all mortals else, come up into Koshtra Belorn?”

Then answered Lord Juss for them both and said, “Surely, O Queen Sophonisba, we be they thou namest.”

Now the Queen carried them into her palace, and into a great hall where was her throne and state. The pillars of the hall were as vast towers, and there were galleries above them, tier upon tier, rising higher than sight could reach or the light of the gentle lamps in their stands that lighted the tables and the floor. The walls and the pillars were of a sombre stone unpolished, and on the walls strange portraitures: lions, dragons, nickers of the sea, spread-eagles, elephants, swans, unicorns, and other, lively made and richly set forth with curious colours of painting: all of giant size beyond the experience of human kind, so that to be in that hall was as it were to shelter in a small spot of light and life, canopied, vaulted, and embraced by the circumambient unknown.

The Queen sate on her throne that was bright like the face of a river ruffled with wind under a silver moon. Save for those little martlets she was unattended. She made those lords of Demonland sit down before her face, and there were brought forth by the agency of unseen hands tables before them and precious dishes filled with unknown viands. And there played a soft music, made in the air by what unseen art they knew not.

The Queen said, “Behold, ambrosia which the Gods do eat and nectar which they drink; on which meat and wine myself do feed, by the bounty of the blessed Gods. And the savour thereof wearieth not, and the glow thereof and the perfume thereof dieth not forever.”

So they tasted of the ambrosia, that was white to look on and crisp to the tooth and sweet, and being eaten revived strength in the body more than a surfeit of bullock’s flesh, and of the nectar that was all afoam and coloured like the inmost fires of sunset. Surely somewhat of the peace of the Gods was in that nectar divine.

The Queen said, “Tell me, why are ye come?”

===Chinese===

她开口了，声音如水晶：「感谢称颂蒙福的诸神。看哪，岁月流逝，命定的岁月照诸神的安排结出果实。你们就是那将要来的人。」

魔国两位大人在她面前，确乎立得像两个小男孩。她又问：「你们不就是魔国的朱斯大人和布兰多赫·达哈大人么？从对一切凡人都禁绝的路上来到我这里，上到科什特拉·贝洛恩来了？」

朱斯大人代表两人答道：「正是，索芙妮丝芭女王（Queen Sophonisba），我们就是你说的那两个人。」

于是女王引他们入她的宫殿，进到设着宝座和仪仗的大厅。厅中的柱如巨塔，柱上一层层回廊，叠得比目光所及更高，也比那些立在座上、照着桌与地面的柔和灯光更高。四壁和柱子是末磨的暗色石头，墙上绘着奇异的图像：狮子、龙、海中马头怪、展翅鹰、象、天鹅、独角兽，还有别的，画得生动，着色古艳：全是巨人般的尺寸，超出人类的经验；置身那厅中，便如栖身在一小片光与生的孤点上，被四围的未知所覆罩、所拱卫、所拥抱。

女王坐在宝座上，宝座亮得像银月之下被风皱起的一条河面。除那些小无足燕外，她无人侍奉。她命魔国两位大人在她面前坐下；看不见的手在他们面前摆开桌子，摆上盛满无名肴馔的珍馐器皿。又有轻柔的音乐奏起，在空气中奏成，用的什么隐秘技艺，他们不知道。

女王说：「看，这是诸神吃的仙食、诸神饮的琼浆；我自己也靠这酒食滋养，蒙蒙福诸神的恩赐。它的滋味永不令人生厌，它的暖意与芳香永不消亡。」

于是他们尝了那仙食——色白，入口脆而甜，吃下去，身体里恢复的气力比饱餐一顿牛肉还多；又尝了那琼浆——满杯的泡沫，色如落日最内里的火。那神圣的琼浆里，确乎有诸神的一份安宁。

女王说：「告诉我，你们为何而来？」

===Original===

Juss answered, “Surely there was a dream sent me, O Queen Sophonisba, through the gate of horn, and it bade me inquire hither after him I most desire, for want of whom my whole soul languisheth in sorrow this year gone by: even after my dear brother, the Lord Goldry Bluszco.”

His words ceased in his throat. For with the speaking of that name the firm fabric of that palace quivered like the leaves of a forest under a sudden squall. Colour went from the scene, like the blood chased from a man’s face by fear, and all was of a pallid hue, like the landscape which one beholds of a bright summer day after lying with eyes closed for a space face-upward under the blazing sun: all gray and cold, the warm colours burnt to ashes. Withal, followed the appearance of hateful little creatures issuing from the joints of the paving stones and the great blocks of the walls and pillars: some like grasshoppers with human heads and wings of flies, some like fishes with stings in their tails, some fat like toads, some like eels a-wriggling with puppy-dogs’ heads and asses’ ears: loathly ones, exiles of glory, scaly and obscene.

The horror passed. Colour returned. The Queen sat like a graven statue, her lips parted. After a while she said with a shaken voice, low and with downcast eyes, “Sirs, you demand of me a very strange matter, such as wherewith never hitherto I have been acquainted. As you are noble, I beseech you speak not that name again. In the name of the blessed Gods, speak it not again.”

Lord Juss was silent. Nought good were his thoughts within him.

In due time a little martlet by the Queen’s command brought them to their bedchambers. And there in great beds soft and fragrant they went to rest.

===Chinese===

朱斯答道：「确曾有一个梦送来给我，索芙妮丝芭女王，从兽角之门来；它嘱咐我到这里来寻访我最渴望的人——没有他，我这一整年全灵魂都在悲伤中憔悴——就是我的爱弟，戈尔德里·布卢斯科大人（Lord Goldry Bluszco）。」

话在他喉中停住了。因为那名字一出口，整座宫殿的坚固架构便如森林的叶子遇上一阵骤风般簌簌颤抖。色彩从景物中退去，如恐惧把血从人脸上赶走，一切都成了一片死灰，像人在烈日下仰面闭目躺过一阵后再看盛夏的白昼风景：一片灰冷，暖色尽成死灰。随之，可憎的小东西从铺路石的缝隙和墙壁巨石的接缝里钻出来：有的像长着人首蝇翅的蚱蜢，有的像尾带毒刺的鱼，有的肥得像蟾蜍，有的像顶着小狗头、长着驴耳朵的蜿蜒鳗鱼：一派污秽之物，荣耀的流放者，鳞光闪而淫。

恐怖过去了。色彩回来了。女王像一尊雕像般坐着，唇微启。过了一会儿，她声音发颤地、低低地垂目说道：「两位大人，你们问了我一件极奇怪的事，我从不曾与闻。看在你们高贵身份的份上，求你们别再说那个名字。看蒙福诸神的份上，别再说了。」

朱斯大人沉默了。他心里想的不是好事。

到时辰，一只小无足燕奉女王之命领他们去寝宫。他们在柔软芬芳的大床上安歇。

===Original===

Juss waked long in the doubtful light, troubled at heart. At length he fell into a troubled sleep. The glimmer of the lamps mingled with his dreams and his dreams with it, so that scarce he wist whether asleep or waking he beheld the walls of the bedchamber dispart in sunder, disclosing a prospect of vast paths of moonlight, and a solitary mountain peak standing naked out of a sea of cloud that gleamed white beneath the moon. It seemed to him that the power of flight was upon him, and that he flew to that mountain and hung in air beholding it near at hand, and a circle as the appearance of fire round about it, and on the summit of the mountain the likeness of a burg or citadel of brass that was green with eld and surface-battered by the frosts and winds of ages. On the battlements was the appearance of a great company both men and women, never still, now walking on the wall with hands lifted up as in supplication to the crystal lamps of heaven, now flinging themselves on their knees or leaning against the brazen battlements to bury their faces in their hands, or standing at gaze as nightwalkers gazing into the void. Some seemed men of war, and some great courtiers by their costly apparel, rulers and kings and kings’ daughters, grave bearded counsellors, youths and maidens and crowned queens. And when they went, and when they stood, and when they seemed to cry aloud bitterly, all was noiseless even as the tomb, and the faces of those mourners pallid as a dead corpse is pallid.

===Chinese===

朱斯在那明暗不定的光里久久醒着，心中愁烦。终于他坠入烦乱的睡眠。灯的微光混进他的梦，他的梦又混进灯光，他几乎分不清自己是睡着还是醒着——只见寝宫的墙向两边分开，露出一幅景象：大片月光铺成的路，一座孤峰从云海中裸出，云在月下泛着白。他觉得飞翔之力降临到他身上，他飞向那山，悬在空中就近看它：一圈如火焰的外观绕着它，山顶上有如一座青铜的堡或塞，铜色绿老，表皮被亘古的风霜打得坑坑洼洼。雉埞上有许多人影，男女都有，永不安宁：一会儿在墙上行走，双手举起，像向天上的水晶灯祈求；一会儿跪倒，或伏在铜雉埞上把脸埋进手里；或如梦游者般站定，凝望虚空。有的看似武士，有的凭服饰看似显赫的廷臣、君长、君王和君王之女、肃穆的须髯重臣、少年少女和戴冠的王后。他们行走时、站立时、似在惨痛呼号时，全都无声，寂静如坟墓；那些哀恸者的脸，苍白得像死人的脸。

===Original===

Then it seemed to Juss that he beheld a keep of brass flat-roofed standing on the right, a little higher than the walls, with battlements about the roof. He strove to cry aloud, but it was as if some devil gripped his throat stifling him, for no sound came. For in the midst of the roof, as it were on a bench of stone, was the appearance of one reclining; his chin resting in his great right hand, his elbow on an arm of the bench, his cloak about him gorgeous with cloth of gold, his ponderous two-handed sword beside him with its heart-shaped ruby pommel darkly resplendent in the moonlight. Nought otherwise looked he than when Juss last beheld him, on their ship before the darkness swallowed them; only the ruddy hues of life seemed departed from him, and his brow seemed clouded with sorrow. His eye met his brother’s, but with no look of recognition, gazing as if on some far point in the deeps beyond the star-shine. It seemed to Juss that even so would he have looked to find his brother Goldry as he now found him; his head unbent for all the tyranny of those dark powers that held him in captivity: keeping like a God his patient vigil, heedless alike of the laments of them that shared his prison and of the menace of the houseless night about him.

The vision passed; and Lord Juss perceived himself in his bed again, the cold morning light stealing between the hangings of the windows and dimming the soft radiance of the lamps.

---

Now for seven days they dwelt in that palace. No living thing they encountered save only the Queen and her little martlets, but all things desirous were ministered unto them by unseen hands and all royal entertainment. Yet was Lord Juss heavy at heart, for as often as he would question the Queen of Goldry, so she would ever put him by, praying him earnestly not a second time to pronounce that name of terror. At last, walking with her alone in the cool of the evening on a trodden path of a meadow where asphodel grew and other holy flowers beside a quiet stream, he said, “So it is, O Queen Sophonisba, that when first I came hither and spake with thee I well thought that by thee my matter should be well sped. And didst not thou then promise me thy goodness and grace from thee thereafter?”

“This is very true,” said the Queen.

===Chinese===

然后朱斯仿佛看见右面立着一座平顶的铜碉楼，比城墙略高，屋顶围着雉埞。他竭力想喊，却像有魔鬼扼住他的喉咙令他空息，发不出一点声音。因为屋顶正中，像在一张石凳上，斜倚着一个人：下巴搁在右大手里，肘抵在凳臂上，身上的斗篷华贵，织金锦缎，沉重的双手巨剑放在身旁，心形红宝石的剑首在月光下幽幽生辉。他的样子同朱斯最后一次见到他时毫无二致——在他们的船上，黑暗吞没他们之前；只是生命红润的颜色似乎已离他而去，眉宇间似乎罩着悲伤。他的眼与兄弟的眼相遇，却没有相识的神色，仿佛凝望着星辰光辉之外深渊里的某个远点。朱斯觉得，如今这样找到弟弟戈尔德里，同他料想中将要找到的完全一样：那拘禁他的黑暗权势再暴虐，他的头也不曾低下：他像一位神，守着他坚忍的夜更，既不理会同囚者的悲叹，也不理会四围无家之夜的威胁。

幻象过去了；朱斯大人发觉自己又在床上，清冷的晨光从窗帘间溜进来，暗了灯的柔光。

---

他们在那宫殿里住了七天。除女王和她的小无足燕，他们没遇见一个活物；但一切想要的东西都有看不见的手供给，一切王家的款待齐备。只是朱斯大人心中沉重：每当他想向女王问起戈尔德里，她总是把他岔开，恳切求他不要第二次念出那恐怖的名字。末了，一日晚凉，他同她单独走在草甸上一条践踏出的小径上，旁边一条静静的溪水流着，溪畔长着日影兰和其他圣花。他说：「事情是这样的，索芙妮丝芭女王：我初来此地同你说话时，满以为靠你我的事必能顺遂。你不是当场就应许我，此后必有你的恩典和善意么？」

「这确是真的。」女王说。

===Original===

“Then why,” said he, “when I would question thee of that I make most store of, wilt thou always daff me and put me by?”

She was silent, hanging her head. He looked sidelong for a minute at her sweet profile, the grave clear lines of her mouth and chin. “Of whom must I inquire,” he said, “if not of thee, which art Queen in Koshtra Belorn and must know this thing?”

She stopped and faced him with dark eyes that were like a child’s for innocence and like a God’s for splendour. “My lord, that I have put thee off, ascribe it not to evil intent. That were an unnatural part indeed in me unto you of Demonland who have fulfilled the weird and set me free again to visit again the world of men which I so much desire, despite all my sorrows I there fulfilled in elder time. Or shall I forget you are at enmity with the wicked house of Witchland, and therefore doubly pledged my friends?”

“That the event must prove, O Queen,” said Lord Juss.

“O saw ye Morna Moruna?” cried she. “Saw ye it in the wilderness?” And when he looked on her still dark and mistrustful, she said, “Is this forgot? And methought it should be mention and remembrance made thereof unto the end of the world. I pray thee, my lord, what age art thou?”

“I have looked upon this world,” answered Lord Juss, “for thrice ten years.”

“And I,” said the Queen, “but seventeen summers. Yet that same age had I when thou wast born, and thy grandsire before thee, and his before him. For the Gods gave me youth forever more, when they brought me hither after the realm-rape that befell our house, and lodged me in this mountain.”

===Chinese===

「那么，」他说，「当我要向你问起我最珍视的事，你为什么总是掦塞我、岔开我？」

她沉默了，垂着头。他侧目看了一分钟她那甜美的侧影，她唇颚清朗庄严的线条。「我不问你问谁，」他说，「你是科什特拉·贝洛恩的女王，必然知道这件事。」

她站住，面对他，黑眼睛像孩子的眼一样无邪，又像神的眼一样辉煌。「大人，我把你推托了，请不要归罪于恶意。那于我对你们魔国人倒是真正反常的了——你们应了命运，使我能重访我如此渴望的人间，尽管我古时在那里 fulfilled 了一切悲伤。难道我忘了你们与巫国那个邪恶王族为敌？他们因此更是我加倍立誓的朋友。」

「这要等事实来证明了，女王。」朱斯大人说。

「哦，你们见过了莫尔纳·莫鲁纳么？」她喊道。「在荒原上见过了么？」见他仍然面色阴沉、满腹疑虑，她又说：「这难道也忘了？我还以为这事要被传讲记念到世界末日呢。请你告诉我，大人，你多大年纪？」

「我在这世上，」朱斯大人答，「已看了三个十年。」

「而我，」女王说，「只有十七个夏天。可你出生时我就这个年纪了，你祖父出生时也是，他祖父之前也是。因为诸神给了我永远的青春——在他们把我们家遭劫之后带我来这里，安顿在这座山里的时候。」

===Original===

She paused, and stood motionless, her hands clasped lightly before her, her head bent, her face turned a little away so that he saw only the white curve of her neck and her cheek’s soft outline. All the air was full of sunset, though no sun was there, but a scattered splendour only, shed from the high roof of rock that was like a sky above them self-effulgent. Very softly she began again to speak, the crystal accents of her voice sounding like the faint notes of a bell borne from a great way off on the quiet air of a summer evening. “Surely time past is gone by like a shadow since those days, when I was Queen in Morna Moruna, dwelling there with my lady mother and the princes my cousins in peace and joy. Until Gorice III came out of the north, the great King of Witchland, desiring to explore these mountains, for his pride sake and his insolent heart; which cost him dear. ’Twas on an evening of early summer we beheld him and his folk ride over the flowering meadows of the Moruna. Nobly was he entertained by us, and when we knew what way he meant to go, we counselled him turn back, and the mantichores must tear him if he went. But he mocked at our advisoes, and on the morrow departed, he and his, by way of Omprenne Edge. And never again were they seen of living man.

===Chinese===

她停住，静立不动，双手轻轻交握在身前，头微俯，脸略偏向一旁，他只看得见她颈项雪白的曲线和脸颊柔美的轮廓。空气里满是落日的颜色，虽然没有太阳，只有一片散射的光辉，从高处的岩顶透下——那岩顶像一轮自明的天，覆在他们头顶。她重新开口时声音极轻，水晶般的音色像远处传来的一声钟磬，乘着夏晚静谧的空气：「自从那些日子以来，逝去的时光真像影子一般过去了——那时我是莫尔纳·莫鲁纳的女王，同我的母亲和各位堂兄弟一起，平安喜乐地住在那里。直到戈里斯三世（Gorice III）从北方来——巫国的大王，为着他的骄傲和倡狂的心要来探索这些山，付出了惨重的代价。那是初夏的一个傍晚，我们看见他和他的人马驰过莫鲁纳开花的草甸。我们体面地款待了他；得知他要去哪条路，我们力劝他回头，说若去，吃人的曼提克兽必撕碎他。他却嗤笑我们的忠告，次日便带着他的人取道奥姆普伦尼缘崖去了。活人从此再没见过他们。

===Original===

“That had been small loss; but hereof there befell a great and horrible mischief. For in the spring of the year came Gorice IV with a great army out of waterish Witchland, saying with open mouth of defamation that we were the dead King’s murtherers: we that were peaceful folk, and would not entertain an action should call us villain for all the wealth of Impland. In the night they came, when all we save the sentinels upon the walls were in our beds secure in a quiet conscience. They took the princes my cousins and all our men, and before our eyes most cruelly murthered them. So that my mother seeing these things fell suddenly into deadly swoonings and was presently dead. And the King commanded them burn the house with fire, and he brake down the holy altars of the Gods, and defiled their high places. And unto me that was young and fair to look on he gave this choice, to go with him and be his slave, other else to be cast down from the Edge and all my bones be broken. Surely I chose this rather. But the Gods, that do help every rightful true cause, made light my fall, and guided me hither safe through all perils of height and cold and ravening beasts, granting me youth and peaceful days forever, here on the borderland between the living and the dead.

“And the Gods blew upon all the land of the Moruna in the fire of their wrath, to make it desolate, and man and beast cut off therefrom, for a witness of the wicked deeds of Gorice the King, even as Gorice the King made desolate our little castle and our pleasant places. The face of the land was lifted up to high airs where frosts do dwell, so that the cliffs of Omprenne Edge down which ye came are ten times the height they were when Gorice III came down them. So was an end of flowers on the Moruna, and an end there of spring and of summer days forever.”

The Queen ceased speaking, and Lord Juss was silent for a space, greatly marvelling.

===Chinese===

「那本算不得什么损失；可随后却生出一场大而可怕的衲殃。因为那年春天，戈里斯四世（Gorice IV）率大军出了水乡巫国，公然造谣中偒，说我们是那死去君王的凶手：我们是爱好和平的人，妖国的全部财富堆给我们，我们也不屑打一场会叫我们背上恶名的官司。他们夜里来，那时除了墙上的哨兵，我们都睡在床上，凭著清白的良心高枕。他们抓住我各位堂兄弟和我们所有的男子，当着我们的面把他们残杀了。我母亲眼见这一切，登时陷入死一般的昏厥，很快便死了。王又命人放火烧了宅子，捣毁诸神的圣坛，玷污了他们的高处。至于我，年轻而容貌姣好，他给了我这个选择：跟他走，做他的女奴；不然就从缘崖上抛下去，摔得骨头尽断。我当然选了后者。但诸神——他们助一切正义真正的事业——使我的坠落变得轻盈，引我平安越过高处、严寒与猛兽的一切凶险，到了这里，赐我青春与永世的安宁日子，在这生者与死者的边地上。

「诸神又以怒火吹遍整个莫鲁纳之地，使它荒芜，人畜断绝，作为戈里斯王恶行的见证，正如戈里斯王荒芜了我们的小城堡和我们欢乐的家园。大地的脸被抬升到冰霜所居的高空，所以你们下来的奥姆普伦尼缘崖的峭壁，比戈里斯三世下来时高了十倍。莫鲁纳的花就此绝了，春天和夏日的时光在那里就此永远绝了。」

女王住了口，朱斯大人沉默了一阵，惊叹不已。

===Original===

“Judge now,” said she, “if your foes be not my foes. It is not hidden from me, my lord, that you deem me but a lukewarm friend and no helper at all in your enterprise. Yet have I ceased not since ye were here to search and to inquire, and sent my little martlets west and east and south and north after tidings of him thou namedst. They are swift, even as wingy thoughts circling the stablished world; and they returned to me on weary wings, yet with never a word of thy great kinsman.”

Juss looked at her eyes that were moist with tears. Truth sat in them like an angel. “O Queen,” he cried, “why need thy little minions scour the world, when my brother is here in Koshtra Belorn?”

She shook her head, saying, “This I will swear to thee, there hath no mortal come up into Koshtra Belorn save only thee and thy companions these two hundred years.”

But Juss said again, “My brother is here in Koshtra Belorn. Mine eyes beheld him that first night, hedged about with fires. And he is held captive on a tower of brass on a peak of a mountain.”

“There be no mountains here,” said she, “save this in whose womb we have our dwelling.”
