德卡拉贾乌斯把他一把推开，对科里尼厄斯说：「别理我兄弟，他嘴快心直；他是酒后说话，酒就是另一个人。可是再真不过的是，科里尼厄斯啊——这一点，我父亲公爵和我们全体，都可以照你所要的最重的誓言对你起誓——加兰德斯图谋擅权，只为一样：把我们全军卖给敌人。也正只为这个，科苏斯才杀了他。」

「那是彻头彻尾的谎，」拉克苏斯说。

格罗轻轻一笑。

科里尼厄斯的剑却已半出鞘，他向科苏斯父子跨前一步。「同我说话，要称王的名，」他向他们沉下脸说。「你们科苏斯的儿子们，别当我是给你们捅鸟的竿子、供你们使唤的。还有你，」他狠狠瞪着科苏斯，「最好乖乖地走，别同我斗嘴。你这傻子！你以为我是加兰德斯又回来了？你杀得了他，杀不了我。还是你以为，我把你从你自己那愚妄乖戾织成的罗网里解出来，是为了再容你在这里作威作福、再凭你那不安分的歹毒把一切搅坏？卫队就在这里，送你们上船。算你走运，我没一剑削下你的脑袋。」

科苏斯父子一时立着，心里嘀咕：是拔刀扑向科里尼厄斯、把身家性命押在奥尔斯威克大厅一场恶战上好，还是拥抱这不得已、下船去好。后一条他们觉得更妥：对面立着科里尼厄斯、拉克苏斯和他们的人，科苏斯自己这边可靠死党寥寥无几，真打起来未必靠得住；何况就算势均力敌，他们也不愿同科里尼厄斯交手。于是末了，他们怀着满腔怒愤，屈从了他的意志；就在当夜，拉克苏斯把他们送上那条船，渡过湾去斯卡拉姆西。

他们在那里安全得像磨坊里的老鼠：那条船的船长是卡达鲁斯——拉克苏斯大人信得过的封臣，船员个个忠于科里尼厄斯与拉克苏斯。船在岛背风处停泊过夜，待黎明第一线光，便顺湾而下，载着科苏斯父子离开魔国，回乡去了。

## XXI / XXI
===Original===

The Parley Before Krothering

Wherein is shown how warlike policy and a picture painted drew the war westward: and how the Lord Gro went on an embassage to Krothering Gates, and of the answer he gat there.

Now it is to be said of Zigg that he failed not to fulfil Spitfire’s behest, but gathered hastily an army of more than fifteen hundred horse and foot out of the northern dales and the habitations about Shalgreth Heath and the pasture-lands of Kelialand and Switchwater Way and the region of Rammerick, and came in haste over the Stile. But when Corinius knew of this faring from the west, he marched three thousand strong to meet them above Moonmere Head, to deny them the way to Galing. But Zigg, being yet in the upper defiles of Breakingdale, now for the first time had advertisement of the great slaughter at Thremnir’s Heugh, and how the forces of Spitfire and Volle were broken and scattered and themselves fled up into the mountains; and so deeming it small gain with so little an army to give battle to Corinius, he turned back without more ado and returned hastily over the Stile whence he came. Corinius sent light forces to harry his retreat, but being not minded as then to follow them into the west country, let build a burg in the throat of the pass in a place of vantage, and stationed there sufficient men to ward it, and so came again to Owlswick.

===Chinese===

克罗瑟林城下的谈判

本章可见兵略与一幅画像如何把战事引向西；及格罗勋爵如何出使克罗瑟林城门，与他在那里所得的回答。

如今要说齐格：他没有辜负斯皮特法厄的嘱托，从北面诸谷和沙尔格雷斯荒原周围的村落、凯利亚兰牧场、斯维奇沃特路和拉默里克一带，急速聚起一支一千五百多人的马步军，匆勿过了斯泰尔隘口。可科里尼厄斯得报这一西来的行动，率三千人上穆恩米尔高地迎击，堵他们去加灵的路。但齐格还在布雷金谷上段的隘道里，这时才初次听到斯雷姆尼尔崖那场大屠戮的消息——斯皮特法厄和沃尔的部队被击溃驱散，他们自己也逃上山去了；他想，凭这么点人马同科里尼厄斯交战捞不到便宜，便不再逗留，掉头照原路匆勿退过斯泰尔。科里尼厄斯派轻兵骚扰他的退路，却无意于此时追入西乡，只叫人在隘口咽喉的险要处筑起一座堡，留足人马驻守，然后回师奥尔斯威克。

===Original===

They that were with Corinius in Demonland numbered now more than five thousand fighting men: a great and redoubtable army. With these, the weather being fine and open, he in a short time laid under him all eastern Demonland, save Galing alone. Bremery of Shaws with but seventy men held Galing for Lord Juss against all assaults. So that Corinius, thinking this fruit should ripen later and drop into his hand when the rest had been gathered, resolved at winter’s end to march with his main army into the west country, leaving a small force to hold down the eastlands and contain Bremery in Galing. To this determination he was led by all arguments of sound soldiership, most happily seconding his own inclinations. For besides this of warlike policy two scarce weaker lodestones drew him westward: first the old cankered malice he bare in his heart against the Lord Brandoch Daha, that made Krothering his dearest prey; and next, his own lustful desires most outrageously burning for the Lady Mevrian. And this only for the sight of her picture, found by him in Spitfire’s closet among his pens and inkstands and other trinkets, which once looked on he swore that with Heaven’s will (ay, or without if so it must be) she should be his paramour.

So on the fourteenth day of March, of a bright frosty morn, he with his main army marched up Breakingdale and over the Stile, by that same road that Lord Juss fared by and Lord Brandoch Daha, that summer’s day when they went to take counsel in Krothering before the Impland expedition. So came the Witches down to the watersmeet and turned aside to Many Bushes. There they found not Zigg nor his lady wife nor any of his folk, but found the house desolate. So they robbed and burned and went their way. And a famous castle of Juss’s they sacked and burned in the confines of Kelialand, and another on Switchwater Way, and a summer palace of Spitfire’s on a little hill above Rammerick Mere. In such wise they marched victoriously down Switchwater Way, and there was none to dispute their progress but all fled at the approach of that great army and hid themselves in the secret places of the mountains, avoiding death and fate.

===Chinese===

这时，随科里尼厄斯在魔国的人马已超过五千战斗人员：一支庞大可畏的军队。趁天气晴好，他在短期内平定了魔国全部东部，独剩加灵。布雷梅里·奥夫·肖斯只带七十人替朱斯大人守加灵，御住了一切攻击。于是科里尼厄斯想着这颗果子留待后熟、等其余的收尽自会落进他手心，决定在冬末亲率主力开入西乡，留少量部队弹压东地、困住加灵的布雷梅里。促成他这个决断的，是一切正派的兵法道理，而那些道理又最称他的私心。因为在这兵略之外，还有两块几乎同样有力的磁石吸他向西：一是他对布兰多赫·达哈大人怀有的那股陈年宿怨，那使他视克罗瑟林为最珍贵的猎物；二是他自己对梅夫里安夫人（Mevrian）燃烧得无法无天的欲念。而这一层，只因他见过她的画像——在斯皮特法厄存放笔砚和小摆设的私室里发现的；只看了一眼，他就立誓：凭上天意愿（哼，必要时没有也得有），她必得做他的情妇。

于是三月十四日，一个明亮的霜晨，他率主力沿布雷金谷而上，越过斯泰尔——正是当年朱斯大人和布兰多赫·达哈大人妖国远征前、那个夏日去克罗瑟林议事所走的同一条路。巫国人就这样下到两水汇流处，折向曼尼布舍斯。在那里他们没找到齐格、他夫人或他任何一个族人，只见宅子空无一人。于是他们抢掠一空，放火烧了，继续前进。他们又劫掠焚毁了朱斯的一座名堡，在凯利亚兰边境上；还有斯维奇沃特路上的另一座；以及斯皮特法厄在拉默里克湖畔小山上的一座夏宫。他们就这样一路奏凯，沿斯维奇沃特路开进；没有人出来阻挡他们的兵锋，那支大军所到之处人人逃遁，藏进大山的隐秘处，躲避死亡与劫数。

===Original===

When he was come through the straits of Gashterndale up on to Krothering Side, Corinius let pitch his camp under Erngate End, at the foot of the scree-strewn slopes that rise steeply to the high western face of the mountain, where the lean embattled crags far aloft stand like a wall against high heaven.

Corinius came to Lord Gro and said to him, “To thee will I entrust mine embassage to this Mevrian. Thou shalt go with a flag of truce to gain thee entry to the castle; or if they will not admit thee, then bid her parley with thee without the wall. Then shalt thou use what fantastic courtier’s jargon nature and thine invention shall lightliest counsel thee, and say, ‘Corinius, by the grace of the great King and the might of his own hand king of Demonland, sitteth as thou well mayst see in power invincible before this castle. But he willed me let thee know that he is not come for to make war against ladies and damosels, and be thou of this sure, that neither to thee nor to none of thy fortress he will nought say nor hurt. Only this honour he proffereth thee, to wed thee in sweet marriage and make thee his queen in Demonland.’ Whereto if she say yea, well and good, and we will go up peaceably into Krothering and possess it and the woman. But if she deny me this, then shalt thou say unto her right fiercely that I will set on against the castle like a lion, and neither rest nor give over until I have beaten it all to a ruin about her ears and slain the folk with the edge of the sword. And that which she refuseth me to have in peaceful love and kindness I will have of my own violent deed, that she and her stiff-necked Demons may know that I am their king, and master of all that is theirs, and their own bodies but chattels to serve my pleasure.”

Gro said, “My Lord Corinius, choose I pray thee another who shall be fitter than I to do this errand for thee;” and so for a long time most earnestly besought him. But Corinius, the more he perceived the duty hateful to Gro, the firmer became his resolution that none but Gro should undertake it. So that in the end Gro perforce consented, and in the same hour went with eleven up to the gates of Krothering, and a white flag of truce was borne before him.

===Chinese===

科里尼厄斯穿过加什特恩谷的隘道、登上克罗瑟林山麓时，在恩盖特崖下扎了营；营地背靠碎石累累的陡坡，坡直上山的西面高处，那里嶙峋的带堞危岩高踞半天，像一堵抵着高天的墙。

科里尼厄斯来到格罗跟前，对他说：「出使这位梅夫里安的差使，我托给你。你打着休战旗去，争取进城堡；他们若不放你进去，就请她出墙来同你会谈。然后，凭你的天性和急智给你出的最顺口的主意，用那些花哨的廷臣腔调说话，说：『科里尼厄斯，蒙大王恩准、凭自己手掌之力，已为魔国之王，正携不可战胜的威势坐困此城之前，你亲眼看得见。但他嘱我告诉你：他不是来同夫人小姐们打仗的；你尽可放心，他对你、对你的堡垒里任何人，一无所求，一无伤害。他只向你奉献这份体面：与你缔结甜蜜的婚姻，立你为魔国的王后。』她若答允，好极了，我们就安安稳稳上克罗瑟林去，接收城堡和这个女人。可她若拒绝，你就恶狠狠地对她说：我要像狮子一样扑向这座城堡，不打到它塌在她头顶上、不把里面的人用剑刃杀尽，我决不歇手、决不罢休。她在恩爱和睦里不肯给我的，我就用暴力自取；叫她和她的那群倨傲的魔族知道：我才是他们的王，是他们一切财物的主人，连他们自己的身体，也不过是供我取乐的物件。」

格罗说：「科里尼厄斯大人，求你另挑一个比我更合适的人办这趟差吧；」接着又恳求了许久。可科里尼厄斯越是看出这差使叫格罗憎恶，越认定非格罗去不可。末了格罗只得应承，当即带上十一人上克罗瑟林城门去，前面打着一面白休战旗。

===Original===

He sent his herald up to the gate to desire speech of the Lady Mevrian. And in a while the gates were opened, and she came down attended to meet Lord Gro in the open garden before the bridge-gate. It was by then late afternoon, and the burning sun swam low amid streaked level clouds incarnadine, setting aflame the waters of Thunderfirth with the reflection of his beams. From the horizon, high beyond the pine-clad hills of Westmark, a range of clouds reared themselves, solid and of an iron hue; so hard-edged against the vapoury sky of sunset, that they seemed substantial mountains, not clouds: unearthly mountains (a man might fancy) divinely raised up for Demonland, for whom not all her ancient hills gave any longer refuge against her enemies. Here, in Krothering gates, wintersweet and the little purple daphne bush that blooms before the leaf breathed fragrance abroad. Yet was it not this sweetness in the air that troubled the Lord Gro, nor that western glory burning that dazzled his eyes; but to look upon that lady standing in the gate, white-skinned and dark, like the divine Huntress, tall and proud and lovely.

Mevrian, seeing him speechless, said at last, “My lord, I heard thou hadst some errand to declare unto me. And seeing a great camp of war gathered under Erngate End, and having heard of robbers and evildoers rife about the land these many moons, I look not for soft speech. Take heart, therefore, and declare plainly what ill thou meanest.”

Gro answered and said, “Tell me first if thou that speakest art in truth the Lady Mevrian, that I may know whether to human kind I speak or to some Goddess come down from the shining floor of heaven.”

She answered, “Of thy compliments I have nought to do. I am she thou namest.”

“Madam,” said Lord Gro, “I would not have brought your highness this message nor delivered it, but that I know full well that did I refuse it another should bear it thee full speedily, and with less compliment and less sorrow than I.”

She nodded gravely, as who should say, Proceed. So, with what countenance he might, he rehearsed his message, saying when it was ended, “Thus, madam, saith Corinius the king: and thus he charged me deliver it unto your highness.”

===Chinese===

他派传令官上城门，求见梅夫里安夫人。过了一会儿，城门开了，她在侍从的簇拥下下来，在桥门前的开阔园地里会见格罗勋爵。这时已是傍晚，西沉的太阳游在带状的绛红层云间，波光映着落日，把雷霆湾的水面烧成一片火海。地平线上，在西马克松林覆盖的群山之后，一带云山拔地而起，沉实如铁；衬着落日水汽的天空，轮廓那样硬朝，与其说是云，不如说是实体的大山：不像人间的山——人们会恍惚觉得——那是诸神为魔国从天上升起的大山，因为她自古的群山已庇护不了她抵御仇敌了。在克罗瑟林城门口，腊梅和先叶开花的紫色瑞香小灌木吐着芬芳。可叫格罗勋爵心绪不宁的，不是空气里的这份甜香，也不是烧着他眼睛的那片西方的辉煌，而是看着立在门中的那位夫人：肌肤雪白，头发深黑，像神圣的狩猎女神，高挑、倡傲、可爱。

梅夫里安见他一言不发，终于说：「大人，听说你有话要传给我。我看见恩盖特崖下扎起了大战营，这许多月又听说盗匪恶徒在乡里横行；我不指望什么软话。所以放大胆，直说你要怎样作恶。」

格罗答道：「先告诉我，说话的可是梅夫里安夫人本人，好叫我知道我是在同人类说话，还是同一位从天庭光明之境降下来的女神。」

她答：「你的恭维话我无福消受。我就是你说的那个人。」

「夫人，」格罗勋爵说，「若不是我知道得很清楚——我若推了这差，立刻另有人来传话，而且传得比我不客气、也比我少些遗懁——我本不愿向您陛下传这个口信，也不愿开口。」

她庄重地点头，意思像说：讲吧。于是他摆出尽可能摆出的脸色，把口信一字字传了；说完时道：「夫人，科里尼厄斯王如此说；他嘱咐我如此向你陛下传达。」

===Original===

Mevrian heard him attentively with head erect. When he had done she was silent a little, still studying him. Then she spake: “Methinks I know thee now. Thou art Lord Gro of Goblinland that bearest me this message.”

Gro answered, “Madam, he thou namest went years ago from this earth. I am Lord Gro of Witchland.”

“So it seemeth, from thy talk,” said she; and was silent again.

The steady contemplation from that lady’s eyes was like a knife scraping his tender skin, so that he was ill at ease well nigh past bearing.

After a little she said, “I remember thee, my lord. Let me stir thy memory. Eleven years ago, my brother went to war in Goblinland against the Witches, and overcame them on Lormeron field. There slew he the great King of Witchland in single combat, Gorice X, that until that day was held for the mightiest man-at-arms in all the world. My brother was as then but eighteen winters old, and that was the first blazing up of his great fame and glory. So King Gaslark made great feasting and great rejoicing in Zajë Zaculo because of the ridding of his land of the oppressors. I was at those revels. I saw thee there, my lord; and being but a little maid of eleven summers, sat on thy knee in Gaslark’s halls. Thou didst show me books, with pictures in strange colours of gold and green and scarlet, of birds and beasts and distant countries and wonders of the world. And I, being a little harmless maid, thought thee good and kind of heart, and loved thee.”

She ceased, and Gro, like a man hath taken some drowsy drug, stood looking on her confounded.

“Tell me,” said she, “of this Corinius. Is he such a fighter as men say?”

“He is,” said Gro, “one of the most famousest captains that ever was. That might not his worst enemies gainsay.”

Mevrian said, “A likely consort, think’st thou, for a lady of Demonland? Remember, I have said nay to crowned kings. I would know thy mind, for doubtless he is thy very familiar friend, since he made thee his go-between.”

Gro saw that she mocked, and he was troubled at heart. “Madam,” said he, and his voice shook somewhat, “take not in too great scorn this vile part in me. Verily this I brought thee is the most shamefullest message, and flatly against my will did I deliver it unto thee. Yet with such constraint upon me, how could I choose but strike my forehead into dauntless marble and word by word deliver my charge?”

===Chinese===

梅夫里安昂着头专心听。他讲究之后，她沉默了片刻，仍在打量他。然后她开口：「我想我现在认出你了。你是哥布林国的格罗勋爵，替我传这个口信的人。」

格罗答：「夫人，你说的那个人多年前已离开人世。我是巫国的格罗勋爵。」

「听你的谈吐，像是如此。」她说；又沉默了。

那位夫人目光沉稳的凝视像一把刀刮着他娇嫩的皮肤，使他难受到几乎撑不住。

过了一会儿她说：「我记得你，大人。让我来挑动你的记忆。十一年前，我兄长去哥布林国同巫国人作战，在洛尔梅隆战场击败了他们。他在单挑中杀了巫国的大王——戈里斯十世，直到那天为止全世界公认的最强武士。我兄长那时不过十八岁，那是他伟大名声与荣光的第一次腾焰。加斯拉克王因为国土上除去了压迫者，在扎伊·扎库洛大摆筵席、大庆特庆。我在那些欢宴上。我见过你，大人；我那时是个十一岁的小丫头，坐在你膝上，在加斯拉克的殿堂里。你给我看书，书上有金、绿、朱红奇色的图画，画着鸟兽、远国和世界的奇观。我呢，一个不知人心险恶的小丫头，只当你心肠好，爱着你。」

她住了口；格罗像服了什么昏沉的药，站在那里望着她，神志恍惚。

「告诉我，」她说，「这个科里尼厄斯，他真像人们说的是那样的战将么？」

「他是，」格罗说，「古往今来最出名的统帅之一。这一点连他最大的仇人也否认不了。」

梅夫里安说：「那么，你想，这像一个配魔国贵妇的夫君么？记住，戴王冠的君王我也回绝过。我想听听你的意见；他既然派你做媒，想必是你极亲近的朋友。」

格罗看出她在讥诮，心里难受。「夫人，」他说，声音有些发抖，「不要太鄙薄我扮演的这个卑劣角色。我带给你的这个口信实在是最无耻的口信，我传给你也是全然被迫。可我受着那样的拘束，除了把额头撞成无畏的大理石、一字一句传达我的差使，还有什么可挑的呢？」

===Original===

“Thy tongue,” said Mevrian, “hath struck hot irons in my face. Go back to thy master. If he look for an answer, tell him he may read it in letters of gold above the gates.”

“Thy noble brother, madam,” said Gro, “is not here to make good that answer.” And he came near to her, saying in a low voice so that only they two should hear it, “Be not deceived. This Corinius is a naughty, wicked, and luxurious youth, that will use thee without any respect if once he break in by force into Krothering Castle. It were wiselier carried to make some open show to receive him; so by fair words and putting of him off thou mayst yet escape.”

But Mevrian said, “Thou hast mine answer. I have no ears to his request. Say too that my cousin the Lord Spitfire hath healed his wounds, and hath an army afoot shall whip these Witches from my gates ere many days be passed by.”

So saying she returned in great scorn within the castle.

But the Lord Gro returned again to the camp and to Corinius, who asked him how he had sped.

He answered, she did utterly refuse it.

“So,” said Corinius; “doth the puss thump me off? Then pause my hot desires an instant, only the more thunderingly to clap it on. For I will have her. And this coyness and pert rejection hath the more fixedly confirmed me.”

===Chinese===

「你的舌头，」梅夫里安说，「是烙在我脸上的烧红的铁。回你主人那里去。他若要回答，告诉他：城门上方金字里写着呢。」

「夫人，你那位高贵的兄长可不在城里践行这回答。」格罗说。他凑近她，压低声音，只叫他们两人听见：「别受骗。这个科里尼厄斯是个下流、邪恶、荒淫的少年；他一旦强破克罗瑟林城，对你不会有半分敬惜。作出一些开门延纳的样子才是上策；用甜话拖住他、磨着他，你或许还能脱身。」

梅夫里安却说：「你已经得到我的回答了。他的请求我没有耳朵听。再告诉他：我堂兄斯皮特法厄大人伤已痊愈，手上已有一支大军，不出几天就要把这些巫国人从我的城门前抽走。」

说完，她满怀鄙夷地回城去了。

格罗勋爵也回营见科里尼厄斯；科里尼厄斯问他办得怎样。

他答，她断然拒绝了。

「哦，」科里尼厄斯说；「小猫儿敢掊我的面子？那叫我火热欲念歇一口气，只为攒足了更响亮的一记。我非要她不可。这一番假撇清和俏皮的回绝，只把我钉得更牢。」

## XXII / 二十二
===Original===

Aurwath and Switchwater

How the Lady Mevrian beheld from Krothering walls the Witchland army and the captains thereof: and of the tidings brought her there of the war in the west country, of Aurwath Field and the great slaughter on Switchwater Way.

The fourth day after these doings aforewrit, the Lady Mevrian walked on the battlements of Krothering keep. A blustering wind blew from the northwest. The sky was cloudless: clear blue overhead, all else pearl-gray, and the air a little misty. Her old steward, stalwart and soldier-like, greaved and helmed and clad in a plated jerkin of bull’s hide, walked with her.

“The hour should be about striking,” said she. “ ’Tis today or tomorrow my Lord Zigg named to me when they were here a-guesting. If but Goblinland keep tryst it were the prettiest feat, to take them so pat.”

“As your ladyship might clap a gnat ’twixt the palms of your two hands,” said the old man; and he gazed again southward over the sea.

Mevrian set her gaze in the same quarter. “Nothing but mist and spray,” she said after a few minutes’ searching. “I’m glad I sent Lord Spitfire those two hundred horse. He must have every man can be scraped up, for such a day. How thinkest thou, Ravnor: if King Gaslark come not, hath Lord Spitfire force enow to cope them alone?”

Ravnor chuckled in his beard. “I think and my lord your brother were here he should tell your highness ‘ay’ to that. Since first I bowled a hoop, they taught me a Demon was under-matched against five Witches.”

She looked at him a little wistfully. “Ah,” she said, “were he at home. And were Juss at home.” Then on a sudden she faced round northward, pointing to the camp. “Were they at home,” she cried, “thou shouldst not see outlanders insulting in arms on Krothering Side, sending me shameful offers, caging me like a bird in this castle. Have such things been in Demonland, until now?”

Now came a boy running along the battlements from the far side of the tower, crying that ships were hove in sight sailing from the south and east, “And they make for the firth.”

“Of what land?” said Mevrian, while they hastened back to look.

“What but Goblinland?” said Ravnor.

“O say not so too hastily!” cried she. They came round the turret wall, and the sea and Stropardon Firth opened wide and void before them. “I see nought,” she said; “or is yon flight of sea-mews the fleet thou sawest?”

===Chinese===

奥沃斯与斯维奇沃特

述梅夫里安（Mevrian）小姐如何从克罗瑟林城头望见巫国大军及其诸统帅；并在那里向她报来的西境战事的消息：奥沃斯田野之战与斯维奇沃特道上的大屠杀。

上述事件之后的第四天，梅夫里安小姐在克罗瑟林（Krothering）主堡的垛口上散步。西北风呼呼地吹。天无云：头顶澄蓝，四外珍珠灰，空气微带雾意。她的老管家陪她走着：健壮如兵，绑腿戴盔，穿一件牛皮镶片紧身衣。

「钟点大约要敲了，」她说。「齐格大人来这里做客时同我定的，就是今天或明天。只要哥布林国（Goblinland）践约，那真是再漂亮不过的一手：正正好好撞上他们。」

「就像小姐您两只手掌一拍，夹住一只蚊子，」老人说着，又向海上南方望去。

梅夫里安把目光投向同一方向。「除了雾和浪沫什么也没有，」她搜寻了几分钟，说。「幸亏我把那两百骑兵派给了斯皮特法厄（Spitfire）大人。这样的日子，能抓罗的人他都得带上。拉夫诺尔，你看：加斯拉克王若不来，斯皮特法厄大人独力对付得了他们么？」

拉夫诺尔胡子里咕哝一笑。「我想，要是你哥哥大人在家，他会回您一声『能』。从我还是滚铁环的娃娃起，人家就教我：一个魔人抵五个巫人还绰绰。」

她有点怅然地看他。「唉，」她说，「他要在家里。朱斯也要在家里。」忽然她转身向北，指着敌营。「他们要在家里，」她喊道，「你就看不见外乡人持兵在克罗瑟林坡上横行，给我送来可耻的提议，把我像鸟一样关在这座城堡里！魔国从古到今，何曾有过这样的事？」

这时一个少年沿垛口从塔那头跑来，喊着：望见船了，从南边东边驶来，「他们朝湾口开。」

「哪国的？」梅夫里安边往回走边问。

「不是哥布林国还能是哪儿？」拉夫诺尔说。

「哦，别说得这样急！」她喊道。他们绕过塔墙，海与斯特罗帕顿湾在眼前敞开、空荡荡的。「我什么也看不见，」她说；「难道你望见的舰队，是那边那群海鸥？」

===Original===

“He meaneth Thunderfirth,” said Ravnor, who had gone on ahead, pointing to the west. “They shape their course toward Aurwath. ’Tis King Gaslark for sure. Mark but the blue and gold of his sails.”

Mevrian watched them, her gloved hand drumming nervously on the marble battlement. Very stately she seemed, muffled in a flowing cloak of white watered silk collared and lined with ermine. “Eighteen ships!” she said. “I dreamed not Goblinland might make so great a force.”

They were silent for a time, watching the ships sail in to the mouth of the firth and make land at Aurwath. “Dear heavens,” she said, “were I a man to help them. Will Spitfire be there in time? The Witches be in great force.”

“Your ladyship may see,” said Ravnor, walking back along the wall, “whether the Witchlanders have slept while these ships sailed to port.”

She followed and looked. Great stir there was in the Witchland army, marshalling before the camp; there was coming and going and leaping on horseback, and faintly on the wind their trumpets’ blare was borne to Mevrian’s ears as she beheld them from her high watchtower. The host moved forth down the meadows, all orderly, a-glitter with bronze and steel. Southward they came, passing at length through the home-meads of Krothering, so near that each man was plainly seen from the battlements, as they rode beneath.

Mevrian leaned forward in an embrasure, one hand on either battlement at her left and right. “I would know their names,” said she. “Thou, that hast oft fared to the wars, mayst teach me. Gro I know, with a long beard; and heart-heaviness it is to see a lord of Goblinland in such a fellowship. What’s he beside him, yon bearded gallant, with a winged helm and a diadem about it, like a king’s, and beareth a glaive crimson-hafted? He looketh a proud one.”

The old man answered, “Laxus of Witchland: the same that was admiral of their fleet against the Ghouls.”

“ ’Tis a brave man to look on, and worthy a better cause. What’s he rideth now below us, heading their horse: ruddy and swarthy and light of build, hath a brow like the thundercloud, and weareth armour from neck to toe?”

Ravnor answered, “Highness, I know him not certainly, the sons of Corund so favour one another. But methinks ’tis the young prince Heming.”

Mevrian laughed. “Prince quotha?”

===Chinese===

「他指的怕是雷湾，」走在前头的拉夫诺尔说，指向西面。「他们朝奥沃斯去。必是加斯拉克王无疑。看他帆上那蓝与金。」

梅夫里安望着，戴手套的手指紧张地敲着大理石垛口。她裹着一件飘垂的白罗纹绸斗篷，貂皮领衬，显得十分雍容。「十八条船！」她说。「我做梦也想不到哥布林国能出这样大的军。」

他们静了一阵，看那些船驶进湾口，在奥沃斯靠岸。「老天爷，」她说，「我要是个男人，好去帮他们。斯皮特法厄能赶上么？巫人（Witchland）人多势众。」

「小姐您看，」拉夫诺尔沿墙往回走说，「巫国人可没趁这些船进港时睡觉。」

她跟过去看。巫国军营前大乱，正在集结；人来人往，纷纷上马；她在高高的瞭望塔上，风里隐隐送来喇叭声。大军开拔下草甸，秩序井然，铜铁生光。他们向南来，末了从克罗瑟林的家牧场中穿过，近得垛口上每个人物都看得清清楚楚，就从下面驰过。

梅夫里安在垛口里探身向前，左右两手各按着一方垛口。「我想知道他们的名字，」她说。「你常出征，可以教我。格罗（Gro）我认得，长胡子；一位哥布林国的大人混在这样的队伍里，看着叫人心沉。他旁边那个是谁？那个有须的华丽人物，盔上带翼、翼间一道王冠似的箍，提一柄猩红柄的大刀？看去是个傲家伙。」

老人答：「巫国的拉克苏斯（Laxus）：对食尸鬼那回他们舰队的提督。」

「看去是条好汉，可惜所事非主。现在从我们下面走过的这位、领他们骑兵的，又是谁：红黑的脸，身量轻捷，眉头像雷雨云，从颈到脚一身甲？」

拉夫诺尔答：「殿下，我说不准：科伦德（Corund）的儿子们彼此太像。可我想是那位少年王子赫明。」

梅夫里安笑了。「王子，好个王子！」

===Original===

“So moveth the world, your highness. Since Gorice set Corund in kingdom in Impland﻿—”

Said Mevrian, “Name him prithee Heming Faz: I warrant they trap them now with barbarous additions. Heming Faz, good lack! lording it now in Demonland.

“The prime huff-cap of all,” said she after a little, “holdeth aback it seemeth. O here he comes. Sweet heaven, what furious horsemanship! Troth, and he can sit a horse, Ravnor, and hath the great figure of an athlete. Look where he gallopeth bareheaded down the line. I ween he’ll need more than golden curls to keep his head whole ere he have done with Gaslark, ay, and our own folk gathering from the north. I see he beareth his helm at the saddlebow. To ape us so!” she cried as he drew nearer. “All silks and silver. Thou’dst have sworn none but a Demon went to battle so costly apparelled. O, for a scissors to cut his comb withal!”

So speaking she leaned forward all she might, to watch him. And he, galloping by below, looked up; and marking her so watching, reined mightily his great chestnut horse, throwing him with the check well nigh on his haunches. And while the horse plunged and reared, Corinius hailed her in a great voice, crying, “Mistress, good-morrow!” crying, “Wish me victory, and swift to thine arms!”

So near below was he a-riding, she might scan the very lineaments of his face and read it as he looked up and shouted to her that greeting. He saluted with his sword, and spurred onward to overtake Gro and Laxus in the van.

As if sickened on a sudden, or as if she had been ready to tread on a deadly stinging adder, the Lady Mevrian leaned against the marble of the battlements. Ravnor stepped towards her: “Is your ladyship ill? Why, what’s the matter?”

“A silly qualm,” said Mevrian faintly. “If thou’dst medicine it, show me the sheen of Spitfire’s spears to the northward. The blank land dazzles me.”

---

===Chinese===

「世道就这样，殿下。自从戈里斯把科伦德立在妖国为王——」

梅夫里安说：「那就请你称他『赫明·法兹』吧：我担保他们如今拿野蛮的尊号互相笼络了。赫明·法兹，好家伙！如今倒来魔国（Demonland）作威作福了。」

「头号的大傲公，」她过了一会儿说，「看来到现在还缀在后头。哦，他来了。老天爷，好凶的骑术！真的，拉夫诺尔，他很能坐住马，又有一副大力士的身材。看他光着头沿阵线驰下来。我看他要保住脑袋囫囵，光凭金色鬈发还不够呢——等他对上加斯拉克，还有我们北方汇聚的人马。瞧他把盔挂在鞍桥上。学我们学成这样！」他驰近时她喊道。「绫罗绸缎、银装铠裹。你赌咒也只当是个魔人才这样盛装上阵。哦，给我一把剪子，铰了他的鸡冠！」

她说着，把身子尽量探出去看他。他驰过下面，抬起头；见她这样望着，猛勒他那匹大栗马，一勒之下几乎把马勒得坐在后胯上。趁着那马腾跃直立，科里尼厄斯（Corinius）放声向她呼喊：「小姐，早上好！」喊着：「祝我凯旋，我快快投入你的怀抱！」

他骑得那样近，她连他脸上的眉目都看得清清楚楚，连他仰面高呼那声招呼时脸上的意思都读得出。他以剑行礼，一夹马，赶上前队的格罗与拉克苏斯去了。

梅夫里安小姐像突然恶心，又像一脚差点踩上剧毒的蝰蛇，倚在大理石垛口上。拉夫诺尔向她跨近一步：「小姐您不舒服？怎么了？」

「一阵无名的恶心，」梅夫里安虚弱地说。「你要医它，就指给我看北边斯皮特法厄矛尖的闪光。这片空荡荡的陆晃得我眼花。」

---

===Original===

So wore the afternoon. Twice and thrice Mevrian went upon the walls, but could see nought save the sea and the firths and the mountain-bosomed plain fair and peaceful in the springtime: no sign of men or of war’s alarums, save only the masts of Gaslark’s ships seen over the land’s brow three miles or more to the southwest. Yet she knew surely that near those ships beside Aurwath harbour must be desperate fighting toward, Gaslark the king engaged at heavy odds against Laxus and Corinius and the spears of Witchland. And the sun wheeled low over the dark pines of Westmark, and still no sign from the north.

“Thou didst send one forth for tidings?” she said to Ravnor, the third time she went on the wall.

He answered, “Betimes this morning, your highness. But ’tis slow faring until a be a mile or twain clear of the castle, for a must elude their small bands that go up and down guarding the countryside.”

“Bring him to me o’ the instant of his return,” said she.

With a foot on the stair, she turned back. “Ravnor,” she said.

He came to her.

“Thou,” she said, “hast been years enow my brother’s steward in Krothering, and our father’s before him, to know what mind and spirit dwelleth in them of our line. Tell me, truly and sadly, what thou makest of this. Lord Spitfire is too late: other else, Goblinland too sudden-early (and that was his fault from of old). What seest thou in it? Speak to me as thou shouldst to my Lord Brandoch Daha were it he that asked thee.”

“Highness,” said the old man Ravnor, “I will answer you my very thought: and it is, woe to Goblinland. Since my Lord Spitfire cometh not yet from the north, only the deathless Gods descending out of heaven can save the king. The Witches number at an humble reckoning twice his strength; and man to man you were as well pit a hound against a bear, as against Witches Goblins. For all that these be fierce and full of fiery courage, the bear hath it at the last.”

Mevrian listened, looking on him with sorrowful steady eyes. “And he so generous-noble flown to comfort Demonland in the blackness of her days,” she said at last. “Can fate be so ungallant? O Ravnor, the shame of it! First La Fireez, now Gaslark. How shall any love us any more? The shame of it, Ravnor!”

===Chinese===

下午就这样磨过去。梅夫里安两三度上城墙，只看见海与两湾与群山环抱的平原，春光里安宁静美：没有人影，没有战尘，只有加斯拉克船队的桅杆，在西南三英里开外的地棱上露着。可她确知，那些船旁、奥沃斯港边，此刻必正打着殊死的恶仗：加斯拉克王以悬殊之势，敌着拉克苏斯、科里尼厄斯与巫国的矛阵。太阳在西马克黑黢黢的松林上转低了，北边仍无消息。

「你派人出去打听了？」她第三次上墙时问拉夫诺尔。

他答：「一早派了，殿下。只是出城堡一两英里之前走得很慢：他得避开他们四乡巡逻的小队。」

「他一回来，立刻带到我这里，」她说。

她一脚已踏上楼梯，又回过头。「拉夫诺尔，」她说。

他走到她跟前。

「你，」她说，「给我哥哥、也给先父当克罗瑟林管家当了这么多年，该知道我们这一族人的心性魂魄。告诉我，照实、也不必留情：这事你怎么看。斯皮特法厄大人迟了；要不然，就是哥布林国来得太早——那也是他的老毛病。你看这是什么兆头？像对我哥哥布兰多赫·达哈大人那样对我说。」

「殿下，」老人拉夫诺尔说，「我把心里话答您：是哥布林国之祸。斯皮特法厄大人既还没从北边到，除非不死的神们从天而降，救不了那位王了。巫人以最保守的算法也是他两倍的人；而且以一对一而论，叫哥布林人抵巫人，就像叫猎犬抵熊：哥布林人尽管剽悍、满腔火勇，末了还是熊赢。」

梅夫里安听着，用悲定定的眼睛看他。「而这样一位高贵的仁人，飞驰来给魔国黑暗的日子雪中送炭，」她末了说。「命运就这样无礼么？哦拉夫诺尔，这羞耻！先是拉·菲里兹，如今又是加斯拉克。往后还有谁敢爱我们？这羞耻，拉夫诺尔！」

===Original===

“I would not have your highness,” said Ravnor, “too hasty to blame us. If their plan and compact have gone amiss, ’tis likelier King Gaslark’s misprision than Lord Spitfire’s. We know not for sure which day was set for this landing.”

While he so spake, he was looking past her seaward, a little south of the reddest part of the sunset. His eyes widened. He touched her arm and pointed. Sails were hoisted among the masts at Aurwath. Smoke, as of burning, reeked up against the sky. As they watched, the most part of the ships moved out to sea. From those that remained, some five or six, fire leaped and black clouds of smoke. The rest as they came out of the lee of the land, made southward for the open sea under oar and sail.

Neither spake; and the Lady Mevrian leaning her elbows on the parapet of the wall hid her face in her hands.

---

Now came Ravnor’s messenger at length back from his faring, and the old man brought him in to Mevrian in her bower in the south part of Krothering. The messenger said, “Highness, I bring no writing, since that were too perilous had I fallen in my way among Witches. But I had audience of my Lord Spitfire and my Lord Zigg in the gates of Gashterndale. And thus their lordships commanded me deliver it unto you, that your highness should be at ease and secure, seeing that they do in such sort hold all the ways to Krothering, that the Witchland army cannot escape out of this countryside that is betwixt Thunderfirth and Stropardon Firth and the sea, but and if they will give battle unto their lordships. But if they choose rather to abide here by Krothering, then may our armies close on them and oppress them, since our forces do exceed theirs by near a thousand spears. Which tomorrow will be done whate’er betide, since that is the day appointed for Gaslark the king to land with a force at Aurwath.”

Mevrian said, “They know nought then of this direful miscarriage, and Gaslark here already before his time and thrown back into the sea?” And she said, “We must apprise them on’t, and that hastily and tonight.”

When the man understood this, he answered, “Ten minutes for a bite and a stirrup-cup, and I am at your ladyship’s service.”

===Chinese===

「殿下也不必太急着怪我们，」拉夫诺尔说。「他们的计划与约定若出了岔，多半是加斯拉克王的失算，不是斯皮特法厄大人的。我们并不确知约定登陆的是哪一天。」

他正说着，目光越过她望向海上、落日最红处偏南一点。他的眼睛睁大了。他碰碰她的手臂，指过去：奥沃斯的桅杆间升起了帆。烟，像焚烧的烟，向天蒸起。他们看着，船队的大部驶出了海。留在后面的五六艘，火舌腾起，黑烟滚滚。其余的出了陆地的背风，桨帆并用，向南往开阔的大海去了。

两人都不说话；梅夫里安小姐两肘支在女墙上，把脸埋进手里。

---

拉夫诺尔的信使终于回来了，老人把他带到克罗瑟林南面内室的梅夫里安面前。信使说：「殿下，我没有带书信：半路落在巫人手里，那太危险。但我在加什特恩谷城门得了斯皮特法厄大人和齐格大人的接见。两位大人命我传给您的意思是：请殿下宽心安稳，因为他们已把通克罗瑟林的一切道路握在手中，巫国的大军逃不出雷湾、斯特罗帕顿湾与海之间的这片乡野，除非肯同两位大人一战。而他们若宁肯守在克罗瑟林这里，我们的两军就能合围痛歼：我们的兵力比他们多出近一千支矛。这事明日无论如何要办：因为明日正是加斯拉克王按约在奥沃斯登陆的日子。」

梅夫里安说：「那么他们对这场惨败一无所知，不知道加斯拉克提前来了、又被赶回了海里？」她说：「必须通知他们，今夜，火速。」

那人明白了，答：「给我十分钟吃口东西、喝杯上马酒，我听候小姐差遣。」

===Original===

And in a short while, that man went forth again secretly out of Krothering in the dusk of night to bring word to Lord Spitfire of what was befallen. And the watchmen watching in the night from Krothering walls beheld northward under Erngate End the campfires of the Witches like the stars.

---

Night passed and day dawned, and the camp of the Witches showed empty as an empty shell.

Mevrian said, “They have moved in the night.”

“Then shall your highness hear great tidings ere long,” said Ravnor.

“ ’Tis like we may have guests in Krothering tonight,” said Mevrian. And she gave order for all to be made ready against their coming, and the choicest bedchambers for Spitfire and Zigg to welcome them. So, with busy preparations, the day went by. But as evening came, and still no riding from the north, some shadows of impatience and anxious doubt crept with night’s shades creeping across heaven across their eager expectancy in Krothering. For Mevrian’s messenger returned not. Late to rest went the Lady Mevrian; and with the first peeping light she was abroad, muffled in her great mantle of velvet and swansdown against the eager winds of morning. Up to the battlements she went, and with old Ravnor searched the blank prospect. For pale morning rose on an empty landscape; and so all day until the evening: watching, and waiting, and questioning in their hearts.

So went they at length to supper on this third night after Aurwath field. And ere supper was half done was a stir in the outer courts, and the rattle of the bridge let down, and a clatter of horse-hooves on the bridge and the jasper pavements. Mevrian sate erect and expectant. She nodded to Ravnor who wanting no further sign went hastily out, and returned in an instant hastily and with heavy brow. He spake in her ear, “News, my Lady. It were well you bade him to private audience. Drink this cup first,” pouring out some wine for her.

She rose up, saying to the steward, “Come thou, and bring him with thee.”

As they went he whispered her, “Astar of Rettray, sent by the Lord Zigg with matter of urgent import for your highness’s ear.”

===Chinese===

不多时，那人便趁夜色悄悄出了克罗瑟林，去把变故报给斯皮特法厄大人。夜里守望的人在克罗瑟林墙上望见北方厄恩盖特恩德下巫人的营火，像星。

---

夜过天明，巫人的营地空了，像一只空壳。

梅夫里安说：「他们夜里拔营了。」

「那殿下不久必听见大消息，」拉夫诺尔说。

「今晚克罗瑟林怕要有客，」梅夫里安说。她下令为来客备齐一切，为斯皮特法厄和齐格备下最好的寝宫迎候。就这样，一天在忙渌的预备中过去。可到了傍晚，北边仍无驰马来，随着夜的暗影爬过天空，一片焦灼与疑虑的暗影也爬上了克罗瑟林人热切的等待。因为梅夫里安的信使没有回来。梅夫里安小姐很晚才歇；天刚露光她已起身，裹上丝绒天鹅绒的大氅，抵着清晨凛冽的风。她上到垛口，同老拉夫诺尔一起搜索那片空白的远景。因为苍白的早晨升在一片空荡的山水上；随后一整天直到入夜，都是这样：望着，等着，心里嘀咕。

奥沃斯之战后的第三夜，他们末了去用晚饭。晚饭未半，外面庭院一阵骚动：吊桥放下的响声，马蹄敲过桥面与碧玉铺地的聒噪。梅夫里安端坐期待。她朝拉夫诺尔一点头；他不等第二下便匆匆出去，又立刻匆匆回来，眉头沉重。他附她耳边说：「消息，小姐。您最好单独接见他。先饮了这杯，」给她斟了些酒。

她起身对管家说：「你来，带他同来。」

走时他悄声对她说：「雷特雷的阿斯塔尔，齐格大人差来的，有急务面禀殿下。」

===Original===

The Lady Mevrian sat in her ivory chair cushioned with rich stuffed silks of Beshtria, with little golden birds and strawberry leaves with the flowers and rich red fruits all figured thereon in gorgeous colours of needlework. She reached out her hand to Astar who stood before her in his battle harness, muddy and bebloodied from head to foot. He bowed and kissed her hand: then stood silent. He held his head high and looked her in the face, but his eyes were bloodshed and his look was ghastly like a messenger of ill.

“Sir,” said Mevrian, “stand not in doubt, but declare all. Thou knowest it is not in our blood to quail under dangers and misfortune.”

Astar said, “Zigg, my brother-in-law, gave me this in charge, madam, to tell thee all truly.”

“Proceed,” said she. “Thou knowest our last news. Hour by hour since then, we watched on victory. I have no mean welcome feast prepared against your coming.”

Astar groaned. “My Lady Mevrian,” said he, “you must now prepare a sword, not a banquet. You did send a runner to Lord Spitfire.”

“Ay,” said she.

“He brought us advertisement that night,” said Astar, “of Gaslark’s overthrow. Alas, that Goblinland was a day too soon, and so bare alone the brunt. Yet was vengeance ready to our hand, as we supposed. For every pass and way was guarded, and ours the greater force. So for that night we waited, seeing Corinius’s fires alight in his camp on Krothering Side, meaning to smite him at dawn of day. Now in the night were mists abroad, and the moon early sunken. And true it is as ill it is, that the whole Witchland army marched away past us in the dark.”

“What?” cried Mevrian, “and slept ye all to let them by?”

“In the middle night,” answered he, “we had sure tidings he was afoot, and the fires yet burning in his camp a show to mock us withal. By all sure signs, we might know he was broke forth northwestward, where he must take the upper road into Mealand over Brocksty Hause. Zigg with seven hundred horse galloped to Heathby to head him off, whiles our main force fared their swiftest up Little Ravendale. Thou seest, madam, Corinius must march along the bow and we along the bowstring.”

“Yes,” said Mevrian. “Ye had but to check him with the horse at Heathby, and he must fight or fall back toward Justdale where he was like to lose half his folk in Memmery Moss. Outlanders shall scarce find a firm way there in a dark night.”

===Chinese===

梅夫里安小姐坐在她的象牙椅里，椅垫是贝什特里亚的厚绸，上面用绚烂的彩线绣着小小的金雀、草莓叶，开着花、结着殷红的果。她向阿斯塔尔伸出手；他一身战装立在她面前，从头到脚泥血斑斑。他躬身吻她的手，随后默默立着。他昂着头直视她的脸，可他两眼充血，神色像报丧的使者。

「先生，」梅夫里安说，「不必踌躇，全说出来。你知道，危难与厄运之下不皱眉，不是我们的血统里没有的东西。」

阿斯塔尔说：「小姐，我的连襟齐格把话交给我，叫我原原本本告诉你。」

「讲吧，」她说。「你知道我们最后得到的消息。自那以后，我们时时刻刻守望的是胜利。为迎接你们，我备下的可不是简单的接风宴。」

阿斯塔尔呻吟了一声。「梅夫里安小姐，」他说，「您如今须备的是剑，不是宴席。您曾派飞毛腿去见斯皮特法厄大人。」

「是，」她说。

「他那夜把加斯拉克败没的消息带到了，」阿斯塔尔说。「可惜哥布林国早到了一天，独自顶了那阵锋。但报仇眼看已在我们手里，我们当时这样想：因为每条隘路都守住了，我们的兵又多。所以那一夜我们按兵不动，望着科里尼厄斯在克罗瑟林坡上营里的火，打算天一亮就打他个粉碎。偏偏夜里起了雾，月亮又落得早。而事情就坏在这里：巫国全军在黑暗里从我们旁边开过去了。」

「什么？」梅夫里安喊道，「你们全睡着了，由他们过去？」

「午夜，」他答，「我们得到确实消息说他动了；营里的火还烧着，是嘲弄我们的一出假戏。种种确凿迹象，都指他已向西北突围，必走布罗克斯蒂山口上米亚兰的高路。齐格带七百骑飞驰希思比去堵他，我们的主力则尽力速行，上小雷文谷。小姐您明白：科里尼厄斯走的是弓，我们走的是弦。」

「是，」梅夫里安说。「你们只消在希思比用骑兵一拦，他就得要么接战、要么退向贾斯特谷——黑夜里，外地人很难在那边门默里沼里找到硬路，他多半要在那里折损一半人马。」

===Original===

“Certain it is we should have had him,” said Astar. “Yet certain it is he doubled like a hare and fooled us all to the top of our bent: turned in his tracks, as later we concluded, somewhere by Goosesand, and with all his army slipped back eastward under our rear. And that was the wonderfullest feat heard tell of in all chronicles of war.”

“Tush, noble Astar,” said Mevrian. “Labour not Witchland’s praises, nor imagine not I’ll deem less of Spitfire’s nor Zigg’s generalship because Corinius, by art or fortune’s favour, dodged ’em in the dark.”

“Dear Lady,” said he, “even look for the worst and prepare yourself for the same.”

Her gray eyes steadily beheld him. “Certain intelligence,” said he, “was brought us of their faring with all speed they might eastaway past Switchwater; and ere the sun looked well over Gemsar Edge we were hot on the track of them, knowing our force the stronger and our only hope to bring them to battle ere they reached the Stile, where they have made a fortress of great strength we might scarce hope to howster them out from if they should win thither.”

He paused. “Well,” said she.

“Madam,” he said, “that we of Demonland are great and invincible in war, ’tis most certain. But in these days fight we as a man that fighteth hobbled, or with half his gear laid by, or as a man half roused from sleep. For we be reft of our greatest. Bereft of these, such sorrows befall us and such doom as at Thremnir’s Heugh last autumn shattered our strength in pieces, and now this very day yet more terribly hath put us down on Switchwater Way.”

Mevrian’s cheek turned white, but she said no word, waiting.

===Chinese===

「那样我们原是拿稳了他的，」阿斯塔尔说。「可他偏偏像野兔一样折返，把我们个个骗到了十足：后来我们推断，他是在古斯桑德附近什么地方掉头的，全军从我们背后溜回了东面。那是历代兵史上闻所未闻的一手。」

「嘘，高贵的阿斯塔尔，」梅夫里安说。「别替巫国卖力夸赞；也别以为科里尼厄斯靠诡道或运气的照应，在黑地里闪过了他们，我就会看低斯皮特法厄和齐格的用兵。」

「亲爱的小姐，」他说，「还是作最坏的打算，并且先备好承受它。」

她灰色的眼睛定定地望着他。「我们得了确报，」他说，「他们全速东去，过斯维奇沃特；太阳还没完全跃出格姆萨尔崖，我们已衔尾疾追，知道我们兵多，惟一的指望是在他们退到斯泰尔山口之前缠住他们决战——他们在那里筑了一座坚固堡垒，一旦叫他们退进去，我们就未必啃得动。」

他停了停。「怎么样？」她说。

「小姐，」他说，「魔国之人战争伟大、战无不胜，这是千真万确。可这些日子，我们打的是绑着腿的仗，或是搁下一半行装的仗，或是睡到一半被人拖起来的仗。因为我们被夺去了我们最伟大的人。失了他们，这样的祸事就落到我们头上：去年秋天，斯雷姆尼尔崖把我们的力量打得粉碎；而就在今天，斯维奇沃特道上，又更惨地把我军掀翻在地。」

梅夫里安的脸白了，但她一言不发，只等着。

===Original===

“We were eager in the chase,” said Astar. “I have told thee why, madam. Thou knowest how near to the mountains runneth the road past Switchwater, and the shores of the lake hem in the way for miles against the mountain spurs, and woods clothe the lower slopes, and dells and gorges run up betwixt the spurs into the mountain side. The day was misty, and the mists hung by the shores of Switchwater. When we had marched so far that our van was about over against the stead of Highbank that stands on the farther shore, the battle began: greatly to their advantage, since Corinius had placed strong forces in the hills on our right flank, and so ambushed us and took us at unawares. Not to grieve thee with a woeful tale, madam, we were most bloodily overthrown, and our army merely brought to not-being. And in the mid rout, Zigg stole an instant to charge me by my love for him ride to Krothering as if my life lay on it and the weal of all of us, and bid you fly hence to Westmark or the isles or whither you will, ere the Witches come again and here entrap you. Since save for these walls and these few brave soldiers you have to ward them, no help standeth any more ’twixt you and these devilish Witches.”

Still she was silent. He said, “Let me not be too hateful to you, most gracious Lady, for this rude tale of disaster. The suddenness of the times bar any pleasant glozing. And indeed I thought I should satisfy you more with plainness, than should opinion of I know not what false courtliness bind me to show you comfort where comfort is not.”

The Lady Mevrian stood up and took him by both hands. Surely the light of that lady’s eyes was like the new light of morning glancing through mists on the gray still surface of a mountain tarn, and the accent of her voice sweet as the voices of the morning as she said, “O Astar, think me not so unhandsome, nor yet so foolish. Thanks, gentle Astar. But thou hast not supped, and sure in a great soldier battle and swift far riding should breed hunger, how ill soever the news he beareth. Thy welcome shall not be the colder because we looked for more than thee, alas, and for far other tidings. A chamber is prepared for thee. Eat and drink; and when night is done is time enough to speak more of these things.”

“Madam,” he said, “you must come now or ’tis too late.”

===Chinese===

「我们追得急，」阿斯塔尔说，「缘由我已告诉过您了。您知道斯维奇沃特道傍山多近：湖岸把路夹在山嘴间好几英里，坡下全是林，山嘴之间沟壑峡峪直插山腹。那天有雾，雾卧在斯维奇沃特湖岸。我们的前锋行到差不多正对对岸海班克庄园时，仗打起来了：于他们大占便宜，因为科里尼厄斯在我们右翼山里伏了重兵，打了我们一个措手不及。不再拿悲惨的细账折磨您了，小姐：我们被血腥地击溃，全军差不多不复存在。乱军之中，齐格偷出一息，凭他对我的情分嘱我：拿命一样赶去克罗瑟林，为着我们大家的存亡，请小姐赶在巫人回来、困住您之前，逃去西马克、或群岛、或任何地方。因为除了这几堵墙、和守卫它们的这几位勇士，再没有任何东西立在你和这些恶魔般的巫人中间了。」

她仍沉默。他说：「别因为这番粗直的噩耗太恨我，最仁慈的小姐。时局的急迫容不得涂脂抹粉。而且我想，坦白直陈比那种不知所谓的虚假客套更对得起您：那会逼我在无安慰处献安慰。」

梅夫里安小姐站起来，双手握住他的手。那位小姐眼里的光，真像晨光初透雾霭、照在高山湖灰静静的水面上；她的语声温柔如清晨的众声：「哦阿斯塔尔，别把我想得那样丑，也别想得那样傻。谢谢你，好阿斯塔尔。可你还没有用晚饭；一个军人在大战与疾驰之后，无论带来多坏的消息，必定饿了的。你的欢迎不会因此变冷，虽然我们等的是别人，唉，等的也是全然别的消息。已为你备好了房间。吃吧喝吧；等天亮了，再细谈这些事也尽来得及。」

「小姐，」他说，「您必须现在就走，不然来不及了。」

===Original===

But she answered him, “No, noble Astar. This is my brother’s house. So long as I may keep it for him against his coming home I will not creep out of Krothering like a rat, but stand to my watch. And this is certain, I shall not open Krothering gates to Witches whiles I and my folk yet live to bar them against them.”

---

So she made him go to supper; but herself sat late that night alone in the Chamber of the Moon, that was in the donjon keep above the inner court in Krothering. This was Lord Brandoch Daha’s banquet chamber, devised and furnished by him in years gone by; and here he and she commonly sat at meat, using not the banquet hall across the court save when great company was present. Round was that chamber, following the round walls of the tower that held it. All the pillars and the walls and the vaulted roof were of a strange stone, white and smooth, and yielding such a glistering show of pallid gold in it as was like the golden sheen of the full moon of a warm night in midsummer. Lamps that were milky opals self-effulgent filled all the chamber with a soft radiance, in which the bas-reliefs of the high dado, delicately carved, portraying those immortal blooms of amaranth and nepenthe and moly and Elysian asphodel, were seen in all their delicate beauty, and the fair painted pictures of the Lord of Krothering and his lady sister, and of Lord Juss above the great open fireplace with Goldry and Spitfire on his left and right. A few other pictures there were, smaller than these: the Princess Armelline of Goblinland, Zigg and his lady wife, and others; wondrous beautiful.

Here a long while sat the Lady Mevrian. She had a little lute wrought of sweet sandalwood and ivory inlaid with gems. While she sat a-thinking, her fingers strayed idly on the strings, and she sang in a low sweet voice:

“There were three ravens sat on a tree,

They were as black as they might be.

*With a downe, derrie down.*

The one of them said to his make,

Where shall we our breakefast take?

Downe in yonder greene field,

There lies a knight slain under his shield.

His hounds they lie downe at his feete,

So well they can their master keepe.

His haukes they flie so eagerly,

There’s no fowle dare him come nie.

Downe there comes a fallow doe

As great with yong as she might goe.

She lift up his bloudy hed,

And kist his wounds that were so red.

===Chinese===

她却答他：「不，高贵的阿斯塔尔。这是我哥哥的家。只要我还能为他守着它、等他回家，我就绝不作耗子溜出克罗瑟林，而要守我的岗。而且这是定的：只要我和我的人还活着能拦，我就绝不对巫人开克罗瑟林的门。」

---

于是她叫他先去用饭；自己却独坐在月亮之室里，坐到夜深：那是克罗瑟林内院上方主堡里的房间。那是布兰多赫·达哈大人（Lord Brandoch Daha）的便宴之室，多年前由他亲自擘画布置；他和她平日用饭就在这里，除非宾客众多，才用院对面的大宴厅。那间屋子是圆的，随着承托它的圆塔墙。柱、墙、拱顶都是一种奇石，白而温润，泛着一层淡金的辉光，像仲夏暖夜的满月金辉。乳白的自放光欧泊灯把满室照得柔亮；高墙裙上精雕的浮雕，刻着不朽的花：千日红、忘忧草、魔草、极乐水仙，纤毫毕美；还有克罗瑟林之主与他妹妹的美丽画像，以及大壁炉上方的朱斯大人像，左戈尔德里、右斯皮特法厄。另有几幅小些的：哥布林国的阿梅琳公主，齐格与他的夫人，等等；美不胜收。

梅夫里安小姐在这里坐了许久。她有一把小琉特琴，檀香木与象牙制成，嵌着宝石。她坐着出神，手指闲闲地在弦上游走，用低柔的声音唱起来：

「三只渡鸦栖在树上，
黑得不能再黑。
*嘀当，德里当。*
一只对它的伴儿说：
咱们的早餐哪里去寻？
「远处那片绿野里，
躺着一位盾下丧身的骑士。
他的猎犬卧在他脚边，
守主人守得这样稳。
他的鹰飞得那样猛，
没有飞禽敢近他身。」
那边走来一头扁角母鹿，
怀着孕，走得步履沉沉。
她抬起他血染的头，
吻他伤口那样红。

===Original===

She gat him up upon her backe,

And carried him to earthen lake.

She buried him before the prime;

She was dead herselfe ere evensong time.

God send every gentleman

Such haukes, such hounds, and such a leman.

*With a downe, derrie down.*”

With the last sighing sweetness trembling from the strings, she laid aside the lute, saying, “The discord of my thoughts, my lute, doth ill agree with the harmonies of thy strings. Put it by.”

She fell to gazing on her brother’s picture, the Lord Brandoch Daha, standing in his jewelled hauberk laced about with gold, his hand upon his sword. And that lazy laughter-loving yet imperious look of the eyes which in life he had was there, wondrous lively caught by the painter’s art, and the lovely lines of his brow and lip and jaw, where power and masterful determination slumbered, as brazen Ares might slumber in the arms of the Queen of Love.

A long while Mevrian looked on that picture, musing. Then, burying her face in the cushions of the long low seat she sat on, she burst into a great passion of tears.

===Chinese===

她驮他上背，
载他到黄土的湖滨。
她赶在晨祷前把他埋葬；
晚祷未到，她自己已殒命。
上帝赐每个好儿郎
这样的鹰、这样的犬、这样的爱人。
*嘀当，德里当。」

最后一声叹息似的余颤还在弦上颤动，她把琴搁下，说：「我心绪的乱音，我的琴，同你弦上的和声不合。收起来吧。」

她开始凝望她哥哥的画像：布兰多赫·达哈大人，穿着金绳系扎的镶宝锁子甲，手按着剑。他生前眼中那种慵懒、爱笑、却又威严的神气，被画师的技艺活生生捕在画上；还有他眉、唇、颔那些可爱的线条，力量与主见在那里沉睡，像青铜的阿瑞斯睡在爱之女王的臂弯里。

梅夫里安对着那画像看了许久，沉思着。随后，她把脸埋进她所坐的低长沙发的软垫里，放声大哭起来。

## XXIII / XXIII
===Original===

The Weird Begun of Ishnain Nemartra

Of the counsel taken by the witches touching the conduct of the war: whereafter in the fifth assault the castle of Lord Brandoch Daha was made a prey unto Corinius.

Now was little time for debate or conjecture, but with the morrow’s morn came the Witchland army once more before Krothering, and a herald sent by Corinius to bid Mevrian yield up the castle and her own proper person lest a worse thing befall them. Which she stoutly refusing, Corinius let straight assault the castle, but won it not. And in the next three days following he thrice assaulted Krothering, and, failing with some loss of men to win an entry, closely invested it.

And now summoned he those other lords of Witchland to talk with him. “How say ye? Or what rede shall we take? They be few only within to man the walls; and great shame it is to us and to all Witchland if we get not this hold taken, so many as we be here gone up against it, and so great captains.”

Laxus said, “Thou art king in Demonland. Thine it is to take order what shall be done. But if thou desire my rede, then shall I give it thee.”

“I desire each one of you,” said Corinius, “to show forth to me frankly and freely his rede. And well ye know I strive for nought else but for Witchland’s glory and to make firm our conquest here.”

“Well,” said Laxus, “I told thee once already my counsel, and thou wast angry with me. Thou madest a mighty victory on Switchwater Way; which had we followed up, pushing home the sword of our advantage till the hilts came clap against the breastplate of our adversary, we might now have exterminated from the land the whole nest of them, Spitfire, Zigg, and Volle. But now are they gotten away the devil knows whither, for the preparing of fresh thorns to prick our sides withal.”

Corinius said, “Claim not wisdom after the event, my lord. ’Twas not so thou didst advise. Thou didst bid me let go Krothering: a thing I will not do, once I have set mine hand to it.”

Laxus answered him, “Not only did I so advise thee as I have said, but Heming was by, and will bear me out, that I did offer that he or I with a small force should keep this comfit-box shut for thee till thou shouldst have done the main business.”

“ ’Tis so,” said Heming.

===Chinese===

伊斯内恩·内马尔特拉之兆开始应验

记巫国众人关于战局的合议；其后在第五次强攻中，布兰多赫·达哈大人的城堡如何落入科里尼厄斯之手。

已没有时间争论猜测；次日一早，巫国大军又开到克罗瑟林城下，科里尼厄斯派传令官叫梅夫里安献出城堡和她本人，免遭更糟的下场。她断然拒绝；科里尼厄斯立即强攻城堡，没有得手。此后三天他又三攻克罗瑟林，都折损了人马而不得入，便把城堡紧紧围死。

这时他召巫国其他几位勋贵来议事。「你们怎么说？咱们拿什么主意？城里守墙的只有寥寥几个人；咱们这么多人、这么多名将围它，要是拿不下这座堡，是我们和整个巫国的奇耻大辱。」

拉克苏斯说：「你是魔国的王。该拿什么主意，由你定。可你若要我出主意，我就给你。」

「我要你们每一位，」科里尼厄斯说，「都向我坦率、公开地出主意。你们知道得很清楚，我奋斗的无非是巫国的光荣，是把我们在这里的征服坐牢。」

「好，」拉克苏斯说，「我的主意我早已给过你一次，你还对我发火。你在斯维奇沃特路赢了一场大胜；若乘胜追击，把优势之剑直捅到剑柄磕上敌人的胸甲，我们现在早把那一窝——斯皮特法厄、齐格、沃尔——从这片土地上根除了。可如今他们都逃到天知道哪里去了，正在磨新的荆棘来扎我们的腰眼。」

科里尼厄斯说：「别当事后诸葛亮，大人。你当时可不是这么谏的。你叫我撇开克罗瑟林：这事我既然动了手，就绝不撒手。」

拉克苏斯答：「我不但如我所说谏过你，赫明当时也在场，可以作证：我还主动提出，由他或我带一小支人马替你看死这个糖果盒，等你办完大事再说。」

「确是如此。」赫明说。

===Original===

But Corinius said, “ ’Tis not so, Heming. And were it so, ’tis easily seen why he or thou shouldst hanker for first suck at this luscious fruit. Yet not so easy to see why I should yield it you.”

“That,” said Laxus, “is very ill said. I see thy memory needs jogging, and thou art sliding into ingratitude. How many suchlike fruits hast thou enjoyed since we came out hither, that we had all the pains and plucking of?”

“O cry thee mercy, my lord,” said Corinius, “I should have remembered, dreams of Sriva’s moist lips keep thee from straying. But enough of this fooling: to the matter.”

Lord Laxus flushed. “By my faith,” said he, “this is very much to the matter. ’Twere well, Corinius, if thy loose thoughts were kept from straying. Spend men on a fortress? Better assay Galing, then: that were a prize worth more to our safety and our lordship here.”

“Ay,” said Heming. “Seek out the enemy. ’Tis therefore we came hither: not to find women for thee.”

Thereupon the Lord Corinius struck him across the table a great buffet in the face. Heming, mad wroth, snatched out a dagger; but Gro and Laxus catching him one by either hand restrained him. Gro said, “My lords, my lords, you must not word it so dangerous ill. We have but one heart and mind here, to magnify our Lord the King and his glory. Thou, Heming, forget not the King hath put authority in the hand of Corinius, so that thy dagger set against him setteth most treasonably against the King’s majesty. And thou, my lord, I pray be temperate in thy power. Sure, for want of open war it is that our hands be so ready for these private brawls.”

When by fair words this stew was cooled again, Corinius bade Gro say forth his mind, what he thought lay next to do. Gro answered, “My lord, I am of Laxus’s opinion. Abiding here by Krothering, we fare as idle cooks toying with sweetmeats while the roast spoils. We should seek out power and destroy it where still it fareth free, lest it swell again to a growth may danger us: wheresoever these lords be fled, think not they’ll be slack to prepare a mischief for us.”

“I see,” said Corinius, “ye be all three of an accord against me. But there is no one beam of these thoughts your discourse hath planted in me, but is able to discern a greater cloud than you do go in.”

“It is very true,” said Laxus, “that we do think somewhat scornfully of this war against women.”

===Chinese===

科里尼厄斯却说：「不是这么回事，赫明。就算这么回事，他或你为什么喏喏惦记着先吮这颗甜果，倒也不难明白；难明白的是我为什么该让给你们。」

「这话，」拉克苏斯说，「说得太难听了。我看你的记性得敲打敲打，你正在滑向忘恩负义。咱们出来到现在，这样的果子你吃了多少？哪一颗不是我们辛苦摘的？」

「哦，恕罪，大人，」科里尼厄斯说，「我本该记得，丝莉瓦湿润嘴唇的梦拴着你，不叫你乱跑。可这种玩笑够了：说正事。」

拉克苏斯大人涨红了脸。「说真的，」他说，「这正是正事。科里尼厄斯，倒是你那闲散的心思该拴住不叫乱跑。在一座堡垒上耗人马？要攻就攻加灵：那才是对我们在这里的安全与统治更值钱的战利品。」

「对，」赫明说，「去找敌军决战。咱们是为这个来的：不是来给你找女人的。」

科里尼厄斯大人闻言隔着桌子一拳挥在赫明脸上。赫明狂怒，拔出匕首；格罗和拉克苏斯一人抓住他一只手，拦住了。格罗说：「大人们，大人们，话不能说得这么凶。我们在这里只有一条心：光大王上、光大他的荣光。赫明，别忘了王上把权柄交在了科里尼厄斯手里；你的匕首指着他，就是最叛逆地指着王的威严。大人您呢，也请有节制地使用权柄。说真的，正因为没有堂堂之敌可打，我们的手才这么容易痒到私斗上。」

好话把这锅滚汤又晾凉之后，科里尼厄斯叫格罗说说想法，看下一步怎么办。格罗答：「大人，我同拉克苏斯的意见一致。守在克罗瑟林城下，我们就像偷懒的厨子，摆弄甜点心，任烤肉馊掉。我们该去寻找敌军，趁它还在自由游荡时把它打掉，免得它再长成危害我们的东西：这几位大人无论逃到哪里，别以为他们会闲着不给我们准备灾祸。」

「我明白了，」科里尼厄斯说，「你们三个串通一气对付我。可你们这套议论插进我脑子里的每一根梁，都望得见比你们行进中更大的乌云。」

「一点不假，」拉克苏斯说，「我们确实有点看不上这场对女人的战争。」

“Ay, there’s the cover off the dish!” said Corinius, “and a pretty mess within. Y’are woman-mad, every jack of you, and this blears your eyes to think me sick o’ the same folly. Thou and thy little dark-eyed baggage, that I dare swear hath months ago forgot thee for another. Heming here and I know not what sweet maid his young heart doteth on. Gro, ha! ha!” and he fell a-laughing. “Wherefore the King saddled me with this Goblin, he only knoweth, and his secretary the Devil: not I. By Satan, thou hast a starved look i’ the eyes giveth me to think the errand I sent thee to Krothering gates did thee no good. My cat’s leering look showeth me that my cat goeth a catterwawing. Dost now find the raven’s wing a seemlier hue in a wench’s hair to set thy cold blood a-leaping than tawny red? Or dost think this one hath a softer breast than thy Queen’s to cushion thy perfumed locks?”

With that word spoken, all three of them leaped from their seats. Gro, with a face ashen gray, said, “At me thou mayst spit what filth thou wilt. I am schooled to bear with it for Witchland’s sake and until thine own venom choke thee. But this shalt thou not do whiles I live, thou or any other: to let thy bawdy tongue meddle with Queen Prezmyra’s name.”

Corinius sat still in his chair in a posture of studied ease, but his sword was ready. His great jowl was set, his insolent blue eyes scornfully looked from one to another of those lords where they stood menacing him. “Pshaw!” said he, at last. “Who brought her name into it but thyself, my Lord Gro? not I.”

“Thou wert best not bring it in again, Corinius,” said Heming. “Have we not well followed thee and upheld thee? And so shall we do henceforth. But remember, I am King Corund’s son. And if thou speak this wicked lie again, it shall cost thee thy life if I may.”

Corinius threw out his arms and laughed. “Come,” said he, standing up, with much show of jolly friendliness, “ ’twas but a jest; and, I freely acknowledge, an ill jest. I’m sorry for it, my lords.

「哈，盘子的盖子揭开了！」科里尼厄斯说，「里头好一锅粥！你们一个个全是女人迷，还因此眼花，以为我也害同样的痴病。你和你那黑眼睛的小包袱——我敢打赌她几个月前早为别的男人把你忘了。赫明这里，和他那颗年轻心宠着的哪位甜小姐。格罗，哈！哈！」他大笑起来。「王上为什么把这个哥布林鞍配给我，只有他知道，还有他的文书魔鬼知道；我不知道。凭撒旦起誓，你眼里那副飢相告诉我，我派你去克罗瑟林城门那趟差没给你什么好处。我家猫儿那副斜眼告诉我，我家猫儿在外面偷了腥。你现在是不是觉得，姑娘头发里那翅膀似的黑色，比你那位王后的赤褐色更能叫你冷血跳跃？还是你觉得这一位的胸脯，比你王后的更软和，更配垫你那熏香的卷发？」

这话一出口，三个人都从座位上跳了起来。格罗脸色灰白如死灰，说：「冲我，你尽可以随意吐你嘴里的脏水。为了巫国，也为了等你自己的毒汁嗆死你自己，我受惯了。可这一件，只要我一息尚存，你和任何人都休想：让你那淫舌头碰普雷兹米拉王后的名字。」

科里尼厄斯端坐椅中，摆出一副从容的架势，剑却已就手。他的大颚绷紧了，倡傲的蓝眼睛轻蔑地从一位扫到另一位——他们站在那里威胁他。「咄！」他终于说，「是谁先把她的名字扯进来的，格罗大人？不是我。」

「你最好别再扯进来，科里尼厄斯，」赫明说。「我们不是好好追随着你、扶助着你么？往后也一样。可记住：我是科伦德王的儿子。你再把这种恶毒的谎说一遍，只要我做得到，就叫你拿命来抵。」

科里尼厄斯摊开双臂，笑了。「来，」他说，站起身，满脸亲热的快活，「不过是句玩笑；而且我痛快承认，是句坏玩笑。对不住，诸位大人。」

===Original===

“And now,” said he, “come we again to the matter. Krothering Castle will I not forgo, since ’tis not my way to turn back for any man on earth, no not for the Gods almighty, once I have ta’en my course. But I will make a bargain with you, and this it is: that we tomorrow do assault the hold a last time, using all our men and all our might. And if, as I think is most unlikely and most shameful, we get it not, then shall we fare away and do according to thy counsel, O Laxus.”

“ ’Tis now four days lost,” said Laxus. “Thou canst not retrieve them. Howso, be it as thou wilt.”

So brake up their council. But the mind and heart of the Lord Gro was nought peaceful within him, but tumultuous with manifold imaginings of hopes and fears and old desires, that intertwined like serpents twisting and contending. So that nought was clear to him save the unclear trouble of his discontent; and it was as if the conscience of a secret grant his inward mind made had suddenly cast a vail betwixt his thoughts and him that he durst not pluck aside.

---

Betimes on the morrow Corinius let fare against Krothering with all his host, Laxus from the south, Heming and Cargo from the east against the main gates, and himself from the west where the walls and towers showed strongest but the natural strength of the place weaker than elsewhere. Now they within were few, because of Mevrian’s sending of those two hundred horse to follow Zigg and those came not back after Switchwater; and as the day wore, and still the battle went forward, and still were wounds given and taken, the odds swung yet heavier against them of Demonland, and more and more must the castle hold of its own strength only, for there were not whole men left enow to man the walls. And now had Corinius well nigh won the castle, faring up on the walls west of the donjon tower where he and his fell to clearing the battlements, rushing on like wolves. But Astar of Rettray stayed him there with so great a sword-stroke on the helm that he overthrew him all astonied down without the wall and into the ditch; but his men drew him forth and saved him. So was the Lord Corinius put out of the fight; but greatly still he egged on his men. And about the fifth hour after noon the sons of Corund gat the main gate.

===Chinese===

「现在，」他说，「回到正事。克罗瑟林城我不放弃：我这人就是这样，一旦定了道，世上任何人也不能叫我回头——全能的诸神也不能。但我同你们做个交易，是这样：明天我们倾全部人马、全部气力，最后一次强攻此堡。万一——我想这最不可能、也最丢脸——攻不下来，我们就撤围，照你的主意办，拉克苏斯。」

「已经白白丢了四天。」拉克苏斯说。「你捞不回来了。也罢，随你便。」

会议就这样散了。可格罗勋爵的心里并不平静，翻腾着希望、恐惧和旧日欲念的种种臆想，它们像群蛇一样绞缠争斗。结果除了那搅不清的不安之外，他什么都看不清；仿佛他内心偷偷作下的一个允诺的良心，突然在他和他的思想之间垂下一道帷幕，他不敢去掀。

---

次日一早，科里尼厄斯全军进击克罗瑟林：拉克苏斯攻南面，赫明和卡尔戈攻东面正对大门，他亲自攻西面——那里城墙和塔楼看去最坚，地势的天然之险却弱于别处。城内人少，因为梅夫里安派了两百骑去追齐格，斯维奇沃特一役后一去不返；战事越拖，伤亡越积，魔国这边的劣势越来越重，城堡越来越只能靠本身的坚厚撑着——守墙的健全人手已不敷用了。有一阵科里尼厄斯几乎得手，攻上了主碉楼以西的城墙，同他的人像狼群般冲扫雉埞。可是雷特雷的阿斯塔尔一剑狠击在他的头盔上，把他打得晕头转向翻下墙外、跌进壕沟；他的人把他拖出来救了。科里尼厄斯大人就这样退出了战阵，但仍在拼命督战。午后五时左右，科伦德的儿子们攻破了正门。

===Original===

Lady Mevrian bare in that hour with her own hand a stoup of wine to Astar in a lull of the battle. While he drank, she said, “Astar, the hour demandeth that I pledge thee to obedience, even as I pledged mine own folk and Ravnor that here commandeth my garrison in Krothering.”

“My Lady Mevrian,” answered he, “under your safety, I shall obey you.”

She said, “No conditions, sir. Harken and know. First I will thank thee and these valiant men that so mightily warded us and golden Krothering against our enemies. This was my mind, to ward it unto the last, because it is my dear brother’s house, and I count it unworthy Corinius should stable his horses in our chambers, and carousing amid his drunkards do hurt to our fair banquet hall. But now, by hard necessity of disastrous war, hath this thing come to pass, and all fallen into his hand save only this keep alone.”

“Alas, madam,” said he, “to our shame I may not deny it.”

“O trample out any thought of shame,” said she. “A score of them against every one of us: the glory of our defence shall be forever. But now ’tis for me mainly he still beareth against Krothering so great and peisant strokes as thick as rain falleth from the sky. And now must ye obey me and do my commandment; else must we perish, for even this tower we are not enough to hold against him many days.”

“Divine Lady,” said Astar, “but once shall one pass the cruel pass of death. I and your folk will defend you unto that end.”

“Sir,” said she, standing like a queen before him, “I shall now defend myself and our precious things in Krothering more certainly than ye men of war may do.” And she showed him shortly that this was her design, to yield up the keep unto Corinius under promise of a safe conduct for Astar and Ravnor and all her men.

“And submit thee to this Corinius?” said Astar. But she answered, “Thy sword hath likely cut his claws for awhile. I fear him not.”

「梅夫里安夫人，」他答，「只要不逾您的安全，我必服从您。」

她说：「不许讲条件，先生。听好。首先我谢谢你和谐位勇士，这样神勇地护卫了我们和金色的克罗瑟林抵御仇敌。我本来的心意，就是守它到最后，因为它是我亲爱的兄长的家宅；我一想到科里尼厄斯要在我们的厅堂里饮马、在他那群醉鬼中间酗酒作乐、糟蹋我们美丽的大宴厅，就觉得于理不容。可如今，惨祸之战的严酷必然，把这变成了现实；除了这最后一座主楼，一切都已落入他手。」

「唉，夫人，」他说，「这是我们的耻辱，我无法否认。」

「哦，把羞耻的念头踩灭吧。」她说。「他们二十个对我们一个：我们这场守卫的荣光将是永远的。可如今，主要就是为我，他还向克罗瑟林下这样重、这样密的死手，密得像天落的雨。现在你们必须服从我、行我的命令；不然我们都得毁灭：就连这座塔，我们的人手也撑不了他几天。」

「神圣的夫人，」阿斯塔尔说，「人死那道残酷的关，谁也只过一次。我和您的人将保卫您到那一步。」

「先生，」她说，像王后一样立在他面前，「我将用比你们这些武人更稳当的法子，保卫我自己和克罗瑟林的珍宝。」她简单向他说明，她的打算就是以保障阿斯塔尔、拉夫诺尔和她全部人手安全撤离为条件，把主楼交给科里尼厄斯。

「向这个科里尼厄斯低头？」阿斯塔尔说。她却答：「你的剑大概已经把他的爪子砍钝了一阵。我不怕他。」

===Original===

Of all this would Astar at first have nought to do, and the old steward withal was well nigh mutinous. But so firm of purpose was she, and withal showed them so plainly that this was the only hope to save herself and Krothering, and the Witches must else sack the house of Krothering and in a few days win the keep, “and then, snaky despair; and the fault on’t not in fortune but in ourselves, that could not frame ourselves to our fortune”; that at last with heavy hearts they consented to do her bidding.

Without more ado, was a parley called, Mevrian speaking for herself from a high window opening on the court and Gro for Corinius. In which parley it was articled that she should render up the tower; and that the fighting men which were within should have peace and safe passage whither they would; and that there should be no scathe nor outrage done to Krothering neither to the lands thereof; and that all this should be writ down and sealed under the hands of Corinius, Gro, and Laxus, and the gates opened to the Witches and all keys delivered up within an half hour of the giving of the sealed writing into Mevrian’s hand.

Now was all this performed accordingly, and Krothering keep rendered to the Lord Corinius. Astar and Ravnor and their men would have abided as prisoners for Mevrian’s sake, but Corinius would not suffer it, vowing with bloody imprecations that he would let slay out of hand any man of them he should take after an hour’s space within three miles of Krothering. So, under Mevrian’s strait commands, they departed.

===Chinese===

这些安排，阿斯塔尔起初一概不肯；老管家也几乎要抗命。可她的意志那样坚定，又把话向他们说得那样明白：这是救她自己和克罗瑟林唯一的希望；不然巫国人必洗劫克罗瑟林，不出几日拿下主楼，「到那时，就是蛇一样的绝望；而咎不在命运，在我们自己，我们没能顺应自己的命运」——他们终于怀着沉重的心，遵命而行。

随即举行会谈：梅夫里安从一扇开向庭院的高窗亲自陈词，格罗代表科里尼厄斯。会谈订立条款：她交出塔楼；塔内战斗人员得享和平与安全通行，去留随愿；克罗瑟林及其土地不得有任何毁损凌辱；以上各条由科里尼厄斯、格罗、拉克苏斯亲手签署用印，文书交到梅夫里安手中后半个时辰之内，向巫国人开城并交出全部钥匙。

这一切都照约办妥，克罗瑟林主楼移交给了科里尼厄斯大人。阿斯塔尔、拉夫诺尔和他们的人本愿为梅夫里安留下为囚，科里尼厄斯却不许，赌着血咒发誓：他们中任何人，一小时后若还在克罗瑟林三里之内，他立刻叫人格杀勿论。于是，在梅夫里安的严令之下，他们离去了。

## XXIV / XXIV
===Original===

A King in Krothering

How the Lord Corinius would take unto himself a queen in Demonland, and made him a bridal feast thereto: wherein is a notable instance how unto them which the gods do love helpers are raised up and comforters even in the midst of their enemies.

That same evening Corinius let dight a banquet in the Chamber of the Moon for some two score of his chiefest men, a very pompous and kingly entertainment; and conceiving that he might now very well avail to accomplish his pleasure touching the Lady Mevrian, he sent her word by one of his gentlemen that she should attend him there. And she sending answer to tell him gently all else in the castle was at his service, but for herself she was quite fordone and greatly desired rest and sleep that night, he fell a-laughing immoderately and saying, “A most unseasonable desire, and one that smacketh besides of mockery, since well she knoweth what this night I do intend. Wish her to repair to us, and that right swiftly, lest I fetch her.”

To that message sent her came she in a short while herself to answer, dressed all in funereal black, her gown and close-fitting bodice of black sendal slashed with black sarcenett, and about her throat a chain of sapphires darkly lustrous. Very nobly she carried her head. Framed with the piled and braided masses of her night-dark hair, her face showed pale indeed, but unruffled and undismayed.

All at her coming in stood up to greet her; and Corinius said, “Lady, thou didst change thy mind quickly since thou didst first affirm thou never wouldst yield up Krothering unto me.”

“As quickly as I might, my lord,” said she, “for I saw I was wrong.”

He abode silent a minute, his eyes like amorous surfeiters overrunning her fair form. Then said he, “Thou didst wish to purchase safety for thy friends?”

She answered, “Yes.”

“For thine own self,” said Corinius, “it had made no jot of difference. Be witness unto me the omnisciency of the Gods, whereunto is nothing concealable, I mean thee only good.”

“My lord,” said she, “I embrace the comfort of that word. And know that good to me is mine own freedom: not conditions of any man’s choosing.”

===Chinese===

克罗瑟林之王

记科里尼厄斯大人如何在魔国为自己迎立一位王后，并为此设婚宴；其中有一明证：诸神所爱的人，即便身处仇敌中间，也有救助者与安慰者被兴起来。

当晚，科里尼厄斯命人在月厅为他的四十来位首要人物备下筵席，一场极尽奢华、王者气派的款待；他自觉如今大可趁愿把梅夫里安夫人的事办了，便差一名侍从传话，叫她到那里伺候。她回话说：堡中其余一切都听凭他取用，只是她自己已困乏不堪，今夜极想安睡。他听了纵声大笑，说：「不合时宜的欲望，还带着讥诮的味道——她心里明明白白，我今夜图的是什么。叫她到我们这里来，快些，免得我亲自去拿。」

口信送去不久，她便亲自出来回话：一身丧服似的黑，裙衫和紧身胸衣都是黑闪绸，开黑绦口，喉咙上一串蓝宝石链，幽幽生光。她把头抬得极高贵。一头夜色般的黑发堆叠编织，衬出那张脸：苍白，却平静无惯，不露惧色。

她进来时，众人一齐起身相迎；科里尼厄斯说：「夫人，你先前一口咬定永不把克罗瑟林交给我，如今倒变得真快。」

「能多快就多快，大人，」她说，「因为我明白我错了。」

他默然看了她一分钟，一双眼睛像好色的饕餮客，在她姣好的身段上逡巡。然后他说：「你想为你的朋友们买平安？」

她答：「是。」

「至于你自己，」科里尼厄斯说，「那原无半点分别。请诸神的全知作证于我——诸神面前无可隐藏——我对你就图个『好』字。」

「大人，」她说，「这话里的安慰我领了。也请你告诉知道：于我的好，是我自己的自由——不是任何人开出的条件。」

===Original===

Whereto he, being well tippled with wine, framing the most lovely countenance he might, made answer, “I doubt not but tonight, madam, thou shalt be well advised to choose that highest condition, and till today unknown, which I shall proffer thee: to be Queen of Demonland.”

She thanked him in her best manner, but said she was minded to forgo that supposedly pleasing eminence.

“How?” said he. “Is it too little a thing for thee? Or is it as I think, that thou laughest?”

She said, “My lord, it should little beseem me that am of the seed of men of war since long generations to trap my mind with the false shows of a greatness that is gone. Yet I pray you forget not this: the dominion of the Demons hath used to soar a pitch above common royalty, and like the eye of day regarded kings from above. And for this style of Queen thou offerest me, I say unto thee it is an addition I desire not, who am sister unto him that writ that writing above the gate that all ye had tasted the truth thereof had he been here to meet with you.”

Corinius said, “True it is, some have out-bragged the world, yet I ere this have used them like knaves. My jackboot hath known things in Carcë, madam, I’ll not gall thy heart to tell thee of.” But perceiving a great lowe of disdainful anger blaze in Mevrian’s eye, “Cry you mercy,” said he, “incomparable lady; this was beside the mark. I would not sully our new friendship with memories of﻿—Ho there! a chair beside me for the Queen.”

But Mevrian made them set it on the far side of the board, and there sat her down, saying, “I pray thee, my Lord Corinius, unsay that word. Thou knowest it dislikes me.”

He looked on her in silence for a minute, leaned forward across the board, his lips parted a little and between them his breath coming and going thick and swift. “Well,” he said, “sit there, and it like thee, madam, and manage my delights by stages. Last year the wide world betwixt us: this year the mountains: yestereve Krothering walls: tonight a table’s breadth: and ere night be done, not so much as﻿—”

Gro saw the wild-deer look in Lady Mevrian’s eyes. She said, “This is talk I have not learned to understand, my lord.”

“I shall learn it thee,” said Corinius, his face aflame. “Lovers live by love as larks by leeks. By Satan, I do love thee as thou wert the heart out of my body.”

他已灌饱了酒，摆出他能摆出的最可爱的脸色，答道：「夫人，我毫不怀疑，今夜你必会明智地选中那最高的、直到今日还未示人的条件，我要奉献给你的：魔国王后之位。」

她以她最周全的礼数道了谢，却说这份想当然的美妙尊荣，她有意辞谢。

「怎么？」他说。「嫌小了？还是如我所想，你在笑？」

她说：「大人，我生于世代武人之家，拿一个早已烟消云散的伟大之虚假幻影来迷困自己的心，很不相宜。但也请你别忘：魔国人的治权，向来翱翔在寻常王权之上一头，如白昼之眼自上俯瞰君王们。至于你开的『王后』这个尊号，我告诉你：我不要这个加封——写城门上方那行字的，正是我的兄长；他若在家迎着你们，你们早已个个尝到那话的滋味了。」

科里尼厄斯说：「不错，有人夸口夸遍了天下，可我早就把他们当无赖收拾过。我的马靴在喀尔刻见识过的事，夫人，我不忍细讲给你听，免得伤你的心。」但瞥见梅夫里安眼中蹿起一团轻蔑怒火的烈焰，「恕罪，」他说，「无双的夫人；这话扯远了。我不愿拿旧事的记忆——嗐，来人！给王后设座，就在我旁边。」

梅夫里安却叫他们把椅子摆在桌子最远的一头，在那里坐下，说：「科里尼厄斯大人，求你把那句话收回去。你知道我不爱听。」

他默默看了她一分钟，隔着桌子前倾过身，嘴唇微张，呼吸又粗又急。「好，」他说，「随你坐哪儿，夫人，一步步地经营我的欢喜吧。去年，隔着大半个世界：今年，隔着群山：前夜，隔着克罗瑟林的城墙：今晚，隔着一张桌子的宽：等今夜过完，连这一——」

格罗看见梅夫里安夫人眼里那头野鹿的神色。她说：「这种话，大人，我没有学过怎么听懂。」

「我教你。」科里尼厄斯说，满脸着了火。「情人靠爱情活，就像云雀靠葱。凭撒旦，我爱你，爱得像你是我心口挖出来的心。」

===Original===

“My Lord Corinius,” said she, “we ladies of the north have little stomach for these fashions, howe’er they commend them in waterish Witchland. If thou’lt have my friendship, bring me service therefor, and that in season. This is no fit table-talk.”

“Why there,” said he, “we’re in fast agreement. I’ll blithely show thee all this, and a quainter thing beside, in thine own chamber. But ’twas beyond my hopes thou’dst grant me that so suddenly. Are we so happy?”

In great shame and anger the Lady Mevrian stood up from the table. Corinius, something unsteadily, leaped to his feet. For all his bigness, so tall she was she looked him level in the eye. And he, as when in the face of a night-ranging beast suddenly a man brandishes a bright light, stood stupid under that gaze, the springs of action strangely frozen in him on a sudden, and said sullenly, “Madam, I am a soldier. Truly mine affection standeth not upon compliment. That I am impatient, put the wite on thy beauty not on me. Pray you, be seated.”

But Mevrian answered, “Thy language, my lord, is too bold and vicious. Come to me tomorrow if thou wilt; but I’ll have thee know, patience only and courtesy shall get good of me.”

She turned to the door. He, as if with the turning away of that lady’s eyes the spell was broke, cried loudly upon his folk to stay her. But there was none stirred. Therewith he, as one that cannot command his own indecent appetites, o’ersetting bench and board in eager haste to lay hands on her, it so betided that he tripped up with one of these and fell a-sprawling. And ere he was gotten again on his feet, the Lady Mevrian was gone from the hall.

He rose up painfully, proffering from his lips a mud-spring of barbarous and filthy imprecations; so that Laxus who helped raise him up was fain to chide him, saying, “My lord, unman not thyself by such a bestial transformation. Are not we yet with harness on our backs in a kingdom newly gained, the old lords thereof discomfited indeed but not yet ta’en nor slain, studying belike to raise new powers against us? And above such and so many affairs wilt thou make place for the allurements of love?”

===Chinese===

「科里尼厄斯大人，」她说，「我们北地的女子，对这一套没什么胃口，任凭水乡巫国把它夸上天。你要我的友谊，就拿效劳来换，还得看准时节。这不是席上该说的话。」

「瞧，这上头咱们倒是一致。」他说，「这一切我都乐意表演给你看，还有更古怪的，就在你自己的寝房里。只是你答应得这样痛快，倒出手我的意料。咱们这就这般快活了么？」

梅夫里安夫人又羞又怒，从席上站起。科里尼厄斯晃晃悠悠地跳起来。别看他块头大，她却高得同他平视对眼。而他，就像人在夜行的猛兽面前忽然挥起一盏明灯，在那凝视之下呆立当场，行动的机簧莫名地冻住了，瓮声瓮气地说：「夫人，我是个当兵的。说实在的，我的感情不讲客套。我不耐烦，怪你的美，别怪我。请您坐。」

梅夫里安答道：「大人，你的语言太粗野、太下流。愿意的话，明天再来见我；可你要知道，唯有忍耐和礼敬能从我这里得到好处。」

她转身向门。他，仿佛那位夫人目光一转，咒就破了，大呼下人拦住她。可谁也没动。于是他，像个管不住自己下流食欲的人，急切地掀翻长凳和桌板要抓她，偏偏叫其中一件绊住，摔了个四脚朝天。等他爬起来，梅夫里安夫人早已出了大厅。

他痛苦地爬起来，嘴里涌出一股野蛮污秽的咒骂的泥泉；扶他起来的拉克苏斯忍不住训他：「大人，别叫自己这样畜生变形、丢掉人样。我们不是还甲在身上、坐守在一个新得的王国里么？这里的老主人虽败，可还没被擒、没被杀，多半正在筹划纠起新的力量对付我们。这么多的大事压在头上，你倒要给爱的诱惑腾位子？」

===Original===

“Ay!” answered he. “Nor shall such a sapless ninny as thou avail to cross me therein. Ask thy little gamesome Sriva, when thou comest home to wed her, if I be not better able than thou to please a woman. She’ll tell thee! I’ the mean season meddle not in matters that be too high for such as thou.”

Both Gro and the sons of Corund were by and heard those words. The Lord Laxus schooled himself to laugh. He turned toward Gro, saying, “The general is far gone in wine.”

Gro, marking Laxus’s face flushed red to the ears for all his studied carelessness, answered him softly, “ ’Tis so, my lord. And in wine is truth.”

Now Corinius, bethinking him that it was yet early and the feast barely well begun, let set a guard on all the passages which led to Mevrian’s lodgings, to the end that she might not issue therefrom but there wait on his pleasure. That done, he bade renew their feasting.

No stint of luscious meats and wines was there, and the lords of Witchland sat them down again right eagerly to the good banquet. Laxus spoke secretly to Gro: “I wot well thou takest in very ill part these doings. Let it stand firm in thy mind that if thou shouldst deem it fitting to play him a trick and steal the lady from him, I’ll not stand i’ the way on’t.”

“In a bunch of cards,” said Gro, “knaves wait upon the kings. It were not so ill done and we made it so here. I heard a bird sing lately thou hadst a quarrel to him.”

“Thou must not think so,” answered Laxus. “I’ll give thee still a Roland for thine Oliver, and tell thee ’tis most apparent thyself dost love this lady.”

Gro said, “Thou chargest me with a sweet folly is foreign to my nature, being a grave scholar that if ever I did frequent such toys have long eschewed them. Only meseems ’tis an ill thing if she must be given over unto him against her will. Thou knowest him of a rough and mere soldierly mind, besides his dissolute company with other women.”

“Tush,” said Laxus, “he may go his gate for me, and be as close as a butterfly with the lady. But out of policy, ’twere best rid her hence. I’d not be seen in’t. That provided, I’ll second thee all ways. If he lie here the summer long in amorous dalliance, justly might the King abraid us that midst o’ the day’s sport we gave his good hawk a gorge, and so lost him the game.”

===Chinese===

「要！」他答。「你也别指望你这个没脈水的傻瓜拦得住。等你回家娶你那小把戏丝莉瓦时，问她：讨女人欢心，我是不是比你强。她会告诉你的！眼下，别来掺和你这种人够不着的事。」

格罗和科伦德的儿子们都在场，听见了这些话。拉克苏斯大人强笑着，转向格罗：「统帅酒醉得深了。」

格罗看出他尽管装得不在乎、耳朵却红到了耳根，轻轻答道：「是这样，大人。酒里有真言。」

这时科里尼厄斯想起时候还早、宴席才开了个头，便派人把守通往梅夫里安住处的每一条过道，叫她不得出来，只在那里等他的兴致。办妥之后，他命继续欢宴。

肥甘的酒肉无穷无尽，巫国众勋贵重新落座，放开大啖。拉克苏斯悄悄对格罗说：「我很清楚，你把这些勾当看得很不堪。你只管把这话立在心里：你若觉得该同他玩一手、把那位夫人从他手里偷走，我不会拦。」

「一副纸牌里，」格罗说，「无赖伺候着王。咱们在这里也照这么办，不算坏事。近来我听见一只鸟儿唱，说你同他有一段过节。」

「你可别这么想，」拉克苏斯答。「你有一手，我必还一手；告诉你，最明显不过的是，你自己倒爱上了这位夫人。」

格罗说：「你指控我的这个甜蜜的愚蠢，与我的天性无缘：我是个严肃的学者，纵然玩过那些玩意，也早已戒了。只是我心想：她若违背自己的意愿被交给他，总是件坏事。你知道他这个人，一身粗直的大兵心肠，还加上同别的女人那一段放荡的历史。」

「咄，」拉克苏斯说，「他爱怎么走随他，同那位夫人蝶恋蜂黏都由他。只是为方略计，最好把她弄走。我不愿沾手。这一条定了，我一切配合。他若在这里一夏天躺着谈情说爱，王上怪罪下来，怪我们白天正行猎时给他的好鹰喂饱了嗦子、丢了他的猎物——那可是师出有名。」

===Original===

“I see,” said Gro, smiling in himself, “thou art a man of sober government and understanding, and thinkest first of Witchland. And that is both just and right.”

Now went the feast forward with great surfeiting and swigging of wine. Mevrian’s women that were there, much against their own good will, to serve the banquet, set ever fresh dishes before the feasters and poured forth fresh wines, golden and tawny and ruby-red, in the goblets of jade and crystal and hammered gold. The air in the fair chamber was thick with the steam of bake-meats and the vinous breath of the feasters, so that the lustre of the opal lamps burned coppery, and about each lamp was a bush of coppery beams like the beams about a torch that burns in a fog. Great was the clatter of cups, and great the clinking of glass as in their drunkenness the Witches cast down the priceless beakers on the floor, smashing them in shivers. And huge din there was of laughter and song; and amidst of it, women’s voices singing, albeit near drowned in the hurly burly. For they constrained Mevrian’s damosels in Krothering to sing and dance before them, howsoever woeful at heart. And to other entertainment than this of dance and song was many a black-bearded reveller willing to constrain them; and sought occasion thereto, but this by stealth only, and out of eyeshot of their general. For heavily enow was his wrath fallen on some who rashly flaunted in his face their light disports, presuming to hunt in such fields while their lord went still a-fasting.

After a while Heming, who sat next to Gro, began to say to him in a whisper, “This is an ill banquet.”

“Meseems rather ’tis a very good banquet,” said Gro.

“Would I saw some other issue thereof,” said Heming, “than that he purposeth. Or how thinkest thou?”

“I scarce can blame him,” answered Gro. “ ’Tis a most lovesome lady.”

“Is not the man a most horrible open swine? And is it to be endured that he should work his lewd purpose on so sweet a lady?”

“What have I to do with it?” said Gro.

“What less than I?” said Heming.

“It dislikes thee?” said Gro.

“Art thou a man?” said Heming. “And she that hateth him besides as bloody Atropos!”

「我明白了，」格罗心里暗笑，「你是个稳重有谋的人，想的是巫国第一。这既公正，又正当。」

宴席这样往前推去，纵饮大嚼。梅夫里安的侍女们——满不情愿地被拉来伺候筵席——不断给宾客上新菜，斟新酒：金的、赤褐的、宝石红的，斟进玉杯、水晶杯和金锤杯。华厅的空气被烤肉的蒸汽和饮者的酒气熏得浓稠，蛋白石灯的光晕烧成了铜色，每盏灯四围一丛铜色的光束，像雾中火炬的光芒。杯盘震响，玻璃脆鸣——巫国人喝醉了，把无价的杯盏摔在地上，砸得粉碎。大笑与歌唱的喧声震天；闹声中间，还有女子的歌声，虽几乎被喧吵淹没。因为他们逼着梅夫里安留在克罗瑟林的侍女们为他们唱歌跳舞，任凭她们心里悲苦。而比这歌舞更进一步的消遣，许多黑胡子的酒色之徒也乐意强求；只等机会——但只能偷偷地，避开统帅的视线。因为已有几个胆敢在他面前放肆轻儇的，被他的怒火砸得不轻——主子还在饿着，他们竟敢先去那样的猎场行猎。

过了一阵，坐在格罗旁边的赫明开始对他耳语：「这是场坏宴席。」

「我看倒是场好得很的宴席。」格罗说。

「但愿我看到另一个结局，」赫明说，「别是他打算的那样。你怎么想？」

「我很难怪他，」格罗答。「这是位最可爱的夫人。」

「这人是不是一头最不堪的敞着门的猪？他要对这样一位甜美的夫人行他那淫邪的目的，能容么？」

「与我何干？」格罗说。

「与我何干又差多少？」赫明说。

「你不喜欢这事？」格罗说。

「你还是不是个男人？」赫明说。「何况她恨他，恨得像血腥的阿特罗波斯！」

Gro looked him a swift searching look in the eye. Then he whispered, his head bowed over some raisins he was a-picking: “If this is thy mind, ’tis well.” And speaking softly, with here and there some snatch of louder discourse or jest between whiles lest he should seem too earnestly engaged in secret talk, he taught Heming orderly and clearly what he had to do, discovering to him that Laxus also, being bit with jealousy, was of their accord. “Thy brother Cargo is aptest for this. He standeth about her height, and by reason of his youth is yet beardless. Go find him out. Rehearse unto him word by word all this talking that hath been between me and thee. Corinius holdeth me too deep suspect to suffer me out of his eye tonight. Unto you sons of Corund therefore is the task; and I biding at his elbow may avail to hold him here i’ the hall till it be performed. Go; and wise counsel and good speed wait on your attempts.”

The Lady Mevrian, being escaped to her own chamber in the south tower, sat by an eastern window that looked across the gardens and the lake, past the sea-lochs of Stropardon and the dark hills of Eastmark, to the stately ranges afar which overhang in midair Mosedale and Murkdale and Swartriverdale and the inland sea of Throwater. The last lights of day still lingered on their loftier summits: on Ironbeak, on the gaunt wall of Skarta, and on the distant twin towers of Dina seen beyond the lower Mosedale range in the depression of Neverdale Hause. Behind them rolled up the ascent of heaven the wheels of quiet Night: holy Night, mother of the Gods, mother of sleep, tender nurse of all little birds and beasts that dwell in the field and all tired hearts and weary: mother besides of strange children, affrights, and rapes, and midnight murders bold.

Mevrian sat there till all the earth was blurred in darkness and the sky a-throb with starlight, for it was yet an hour until the rising of the moon. And she prayed to Lady Artemis, calling her by her secret names and saying, “Goddess and Maiden chaste and holy; triune Goddess, Which in heaven art, and on the earth Huntress divine, and also hast in the veiled sunless places below earth Thy dwelling, viewing the large stations of the dead: save me and keep me that am Thy maiden still.”

格罗飞快地、探查地看了他一眼。然后低头拾着葡萄干，悄声说：「你既存此心，甚好。」他软声细语，中间不时夹两句高声的谈笑，免得显出密谈的样子——把赫明该做的事，条分缕析地教给了他，并告诉他：拉克苏斯也因妒火中烧，同他们一条心。「你弟弟卡尔戈干这差最合适。他个子同她相仿，又因年轻还没留须。去找他。把我同你这番话一字一句传给他。科里尼厄斯疑我疑得太深，今夜绝不放我离开他的眼睛。所以这差事落在你们科伦德诸子身上；我守在他肘边，可以设法把他拖在大厅里，等事成。去吧；愿智谋与顺遂随你们的行动。」
